children.translated_text: // Now begins the first <s>ullāsa</s> (chapter). //
At the commencement of the work, the author invokes the appropriate chosen deity for the removal of obstacles.
Free from the constraints imposed by <s>niyati</s> (fate), consisting solely of delight, not dependent on anything else,
Beautiful with the nine <s>rasas</s> (aesthetic sentiments), producing creation — the <s>Bhāratī</s> (speech/literary art) of the poet is triumphant. // 1 //

children.text: niyatiśaktyā niyatarūpā sukhaduḥkhamohakhabhāvā paramāṇvādyupādānakarmādisahakārikāraṇaparatantrā ṣaḍrasā na ca hṛdyaiva taiḥ, tādṛśī brahyaṇo nirmitirnirmāṇam /
children.translated_text: The creation of <s>Brahman</s> has a fixed form determined by the power of <s>niyati</s> (fate), consists of pleasure, pain, and delusion, is dependent on material causes such as atoms and cooperative causes such as <s>karma</s> (action), has six <s>rasas</s> (tastes), and is not pleasing to the heart through those alone — such is the creation, the making, of <s>Brahman</s>.
But the creation of the poet's speech is different from this.
Therefore it is triumphant.

children.text: jayatyarthena ca namaskāra ākṣipyate, iti tāṃ pratyasmi praṇata iti labhyate //
children.translated_text: By the word 'jayati' (is triumphant), a salutation is implied, thus it is understood: 'I am bowed before her.' //
Now he states the subject matter along with its purpose:
<s>Kāvya</s> (poetry) serves for fame, for wealth, for knowledge of worldly conduct, for warding off what is inauspicious,
For immediate supreme bliss, and for instruction in the manner of a beloved. // 2 //

children.text: kālidāsānādīnāmiva yaśaḥ śrīharṣāderdhāvakādīnāmiva dhanam rājādigatocitācāraparijñānam ādityādermayūrādīnāmivānarthanivāraṇam sakalaprayojanamaulibhūtaṃ samanantarameva rasāsvādanasamudbhūrta vigalidavedyāntaramānandam prabhusaṃmitaśabdapradhānavedādiśāstrebhyaḥ suhṛtsaṃmitārthatātparyavatpurāṇādītihāsebhyaśva śabdārthayorguṇabhāvena rasāṅgabhūtavyāpārapravaṇatayā vilakṣaṇaṃ yat kāvyaṃ lokottaravarṇanānipuṇakavikarma tat kānteva sarasatāpādanenābhimukhīkṛtya rāmādivadvartitavyaṃ na rāvaṇādivadityupadeśaṃ ca yathāyogaṃ kaveḥ sahṛdayasya ca karotīti sarvathā tatra yatanīyam //
children.translated_text: Fame like that of <s>Kālidāsa</s> and others; wealth like that of <s>Śrīharṣa</s> and others through plays and similar works; knowledge of proper conduct learned from kings and others; warding off misfortune like that of <s>Āditya</s>, <s>Mayūra</s> and others; the supreme purpose of all — the bliss that arises immediately from the relishing of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment), in which awareness of everything else dissolves — distinct from the <s>Vedas</s> and other <s>śāstras</s> (treatises) which are like a master, with words being predominant, and from the <s>Purāṇas</s> and <s>Itihāsas</s> (epics) which are like a friend, with emphasis on meaning; that <s>kāvya</s> (poetry), the work of a poet skilled in extraordinary description, which through the predominance of activity that is an element of <s>rasa</s>, with words and meanings being in the relation of quality and substance, makes one receptive through imparting charm, like a beloved, and instructs that one should conduct oneself like <s>Rāma</s> and not like <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, appropriately both to the poet and the sympathetic reader — therefore one should strive in every way regarding it. //
Having thus stated its purpose, he states the cause:
<s>Śakti</s> (innate talent), <s>nipuṇatā</s> (proficiency) from the study of the world, <s>śāstras</s> (sciences), <s>kāvya</s> (poetry) and so forth,
And practice through the instruction of those learned in <s>kāvya</s> — these are the causes for its production. // 3 //

children.text:
śaktiḥ kavitvabījarūpaḥ saṃskāraviśeṣaḥ, yāṃ vinā kāvyaṃ na prasaret, prasṛtaṃ vā, upahasanīyaṃ syāt /
lokasya sthāvarajaṅgamātmakalokavṛttasya /

children.translated_text: 'Of <s>śāstras</s>' — of treatises on <s>chandas</s> (prosody), <s>vyākaraṇa</s> (grammar), <s>abhidhāna</s> (lexicography), <s>kośa</s> (dictionaries), <s>kalā</s> (arts), the four aims of life, and works on the characteristics of elephants, horses, swords, and the like.
And of <s>kāvyas</s> (literary works) belonging to great poets.
By the word 'ādi' (and so forth), of <s>itihāsas</s> (epics) as well — from the examination of these comes <s>vyutpatti</s> (learned proficiency).

children.text: kāvyaṃ kartuṃ vicārayituṃ ca ye jānanti tadupadeśena karaṇe yojane ca paunaḥpunyena pravṛttiriti trayaḥ samuditāḥ, na cu vyastāstasya kāvyasyodbhave nirmāṇe samullāse ca heturna tu hetavaḥ //
children.translated_text: Those who know how to compose and critically evaluate <s>kāvya</s> (poetry) — through their instruction, repeated engagement in composition and practice — these three combined, not separately, are the cause, not causes, of the production, creation, and flourishing of that poetry. //

<s>Śakti</s> (innate talent) is a special <s>saṃskāra</s> (mental impression) in the form of the seed of poetic genius, without which poetry would not flow forth, or if it did, would be laughable. 'Of the world' — of the world consisting of the animate and inanimate, of worldly affairs.
Having thus stated the cause, he states its essential nature (sūtra 1):

That which is free from <s>doṣa</s> (defects), consisting of <s>śabda</s> (word) and <s>artha</s> (meaning), endowed with <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), and not devoid of <s>alaṃkāra</s> (ornamentation) — and yet in some cases:
<s>Doṣa</s> (defects), <s>guṇa</s> (qualities), and <s>alaṃkāra</s> (ornaments) will be discussed.

children.text: kvāpītyanenaitadāha yat sarvatra sālaṃkārau, kvacittu sphuṭālaṃkāravirahe 'pi na kāvyatvahāniḥ /
children.translated_text: By the word 'kvāpi' (in some cases), he states this: that everywhere they should be ornamented, but occasionally even in the absence of manifest <s>alaṃkāra</s> (ornament), the status of <s>kāvya</s> (poetry) is not lost.

children.text: yathā yaḥ kaumāraharaḥ sa eva hi varastā eva caitrakṣapā- ste conmīlitamālatīsurabhayaḥ prauḍhāḥ kadambānilāḥ /
children.translated_text: For example: He who stole my maidenhood is indeed the bridegroom; those same nights of the month of <s>Caitra</s>,

children.text: sā caivāsmi tathāpi tatra suratavyāpāralīlāvidhau revārodhasi vetasītarutale cetaḥ samutkaṇṭhate //1//
children.translated_text: Those same <s>mālatī</s>-fragrant, full-blown <s>kadamba</s> breezes — and I am the same woman; yet in the matter of love-play on the banks of the <s>Revā</s>, beneath the <s>vetasī</s> tree, my heart is filled with longing. //1//

children.text:
atra sphuṭo na kaśvidalaṃkāraḥ /
rasasya ca prādhānyānnālaṃkāratā /
tadbhedān krameṇāha (sū- 2)
children.translated_text: Here there is no manifest <s>alaṃkāra</s> (ornament). And because of the predominance of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment), it does not constitute mere ornamentation. He states the distinctions of that in order (sūtra 2):
This is the highest kind — when the suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) surpasses the expressed meaning (<s>vācya</s>), the learned call it <s>dhvani</s> (resonance). // 4 //

children.text: budhairvaiyākaraṇaiḥ pradhānabhūtasphoṭarūpavyaṅgyavyañjakasya śabdasya dhvaniriti vyavahāraḥ kṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: By the learned — the grammarians — the term <s>dhvani</s> has been applied to sound (<s>śabda</s>) which suggests the <s>vyaṅgya</s> (suggested meaning) in the form of <s>sphoṭa</s> (the meaning-bearing linguistic unit) as the principal element.

Then by others following that doctrine as well, it is applied to the combination of word and meaning capable of suggestion, where the expressed meaning (<s>vācya</s>) is subordinated to the suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgya</s>).

children.text: yathā niḥśeṣacyutacandanaṃ stanataṭaṃ nirmṛṣṭarāgo 'dharo netre dūramanañjane pulakitā tanvī taveyaṃ tanuḥ /
children.translated_text: For example: Your breast-surface is completely devoid of sandal paste, the color of your lips is wiped clean, your eyes are far from having collyrium, your slender body is covered with goosebumps —

children.text: mithyāvādini dūti bāndhavajanasyājñātapīḍāgame vāpīṃ snātumito gatāsi na punastasyādhamasyāntikam //2//
children.translated_text: O deceitful messenger-woman! When the kinsmen came bearing unknown sorrow, you went to bathe at the pond, and certainly not to the presence of that vile man! //2//
'This' refers to <s>kāvya</s> (poetry).

children.text: atra tadantikameva rantuṃ gatāsīti prādhānyenādhamapadena vyajyate //
children.translated_text: Here, the suggested meaning — that she went precisely to his presence for love-making — is primarily conveyed through the word 'adhama' (vile man). //
(sūtra 3)
When the suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) is not surpassing, it is <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (subordinated suggestion) — this is the middle type.
'Not surpassing' means not surpassing the expressed meaning (<s>vācya</s>).
For example: The young woman, seeing the young village <s>vañjula</s> tree laden with fresh clusters of blossoms, held in the hands —
Her facial complexion becomes increasingly pale. //3//

children.text: atra bañjulalatāgṛhe dattasaṃketā nāgateti vyaṅgyaṃ guṇībhūtaṃ tadapekṣayā vācyasyaiva camatkāritvāt //
children.translated_text: Here the suggested meaning — that the one who had arranged a rendezvous at the bower of the <s>bañjula</s> creeper did not come — is subordinated, because the expressed meaning itself is more striking in comparison to it. //
(sūtra 4)
<s>Śabdacitra</s> (verbal ornamentation) and <s>vācyacitra</s> (sense ornamentation) without suggestion are considered the lowest type. // 5 //
'Without suggestion' means devoid of a clearly apprehended implied meaning.
'<s>Avara</s>' means the lowest.
For example: May the <s>Mandākinī</s>, whose streaming waters, escaping from the hollows of the cascading rocks, dispel the darkness of all other waters,
Whose waves of mighty pride, arising from the intoxication of the great sage's delight in the sacred bath performed as a daily rite, be slow for you! //4//
'<s>Citra</s>' means endowed with <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) and <s>alaṃkāras</s> (ornaments).
Having heard by chance that <s>Māna</s> (pride) has departed from her own abode, she becomes —
<s>Amarāvatī</s> (the city of the gods), with bolts hastily dropped by <s>Indra</s> in alarm, appears as if with eyes shut in fear. //5//

children.text: iti kāvyaprakāse kāvyasya prayojanakāraṇasvarūpaviśeṣanirṇayo nāma prathama ullāsaḥ // 1. //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first <s>ullāsa</s> (chapter) of the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>, entitled the determination of the purpose, cause, and essential nature of <s>kāvya</s> (poetry). // 1. //
// Now begins the second <s>ullāsa</s> (chapter). //
He states in order the essential nature of <s>śabda</s> (word) and <s>artha</s> (meaning) — (sūtra 5)
In this context, <s>śabda</s> (word) is threefold: <s>vācaka</s> (denotative), <s>lākṣaṇika</s> (indicatory), and <s>vyañjaka</s> (suggestive).
'Here' means in <s>kāvya</s> (poetry).
The nature of these will be discussed. //
(sūtra 6)
The meanings corresponding to those are <s>vācya</s> (expressed), <s>lakṣya</s> (indicated), and <s>vyaṅgya</s> (suggested). //
<s>Vācya</s> (expressed), <s>lakṣya</s> (indicated), and <s>vyaṅgya</s> (suggested). //
(sūtra 7)
According to some, the <s>tātparyārtha</s> (purport meaning) is also a type of meaning. // 6 //

children.text: ākāhkṣāyogyatāsaṃnidhivaśādvakṣyamāṇasvarūṃpāṇāṃ padārthānāṃ samanvaye tātparyārtho viśeṣavapurapadārtho 'pi vākyārthaḥ samullasatītyabhihinānvayavādināṃ matam //
children.translated_text: When the meanings of words whose nature will be described are synthesized through <s>ākāṅkṣā</s> (expectancy), <s>yogyatā</s> (compatibility), and <s>sannidhi</s> (proximity), the <s>tātparyārtha</s> (purport meaning), a special meaning that is not a mere word-meaning, also manifests as sentence-meaning — this is the view of the <s>abhihitānvayavādins</s> (proponents of the theory of post-expressional connection).
The <s>anvitābhidhānavādins</s> (proponents of the theory of connected denotation) hold that the expressed meaning alone is the sentence-meaning. //
(sūtra 8)
It is accepted that generally all meanings also have the capacity for suggestion (<s>vyañjakatva</s>).
Of the expressed meaning (<s>vācya</s>), for example:

children.text: māe gharovaaraṇaṃ ajja hu ṇatthi tti sāhiaṃ tumae /
children.translated_text: 'My lady, today there is truly no one guarding the house' — so you have told me.

children.text: tā bhaṇa kiṃ karaṇijjaṃ emea ṇa vāsaro ṭhāi //6//
children.translated_text: 'Then tell me, what should be done? The day does not remain still for me!' //6//
Here, 'she desires free amorous enjoyment' is suggested.

children.text: lakṣyasya yathā sāhentī sahi suhaaṃ khaṇe khaṇe dūmmiāsi majjhakae /
children.translated_text: Of the indicated meaning (<s>lakṣya</s>), for example: 'O friend, bearing pleasant friendship moment by moment, you have become hostile to me,
Though what you have done is worthy of one's natural affection — for the time being, you have shown aversion.' //7//

children.text: atra matpriyaṃ ramayantyā tvayā śatrutvamācaritamiti lakṣyam, tena ca kāmukaviṣayaṃ sāparādhatvaprakāśanaṃ vyaṅgyam /
children.translated_text: Here, the indicated meaning is 'you, while pleasing my beloved, have acted as an enemy toward me'; and through that, the suggested meaning is the revelation of the lover's sense of guilt.

children.text: vyaṅgyasya yathā ua ṇiccalaṇippaṃdā bhisiṇīpattammi rehai balāā /
children.translated_text: Of the suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgya</s>), for example: 'Motionless and still, the crane rests on the lotus leaf,
Like a conch-shell ornament set upon a spotless emerald platform.' //8//

children.text: atra niṣpandatvena, āśvastatvam, tena ca janarahitatvam, ataḥ saṃketasthānametaditi kayācit kaṃcitpratyucyate /
children.translated_text: Here, through the motionlessness, the sense of security is indicated; through that, the absence of people is inferred; therefore 'this is a place for a rendezvous' — thus one woman says to another regarding some man.

children.text: athavā mithyā vadasi na tvamatrāgato 'bhūriti vyajyate //
children.translated_text: Or alternatively, what is suggested is: 'You speak falsely — you were not not present here.' //
He states the nature of <s>vācaka</s> (denotative word) and the others in order (sūtra 9):
That which expresses a directly conventionally designated meaning is <s>vācaka</s> (denotative). // 7 //

children.text:
ihāgṛhītasaṃketasya śabdasyārthapratīterabhāvātsaṃketasahāya eva śabdo 'rthaviśeṣaṃ pratipādayatīti yasya yatrāvyavadhānena saṃketo gṛhyate sa tasya vācakaḥ /
(sū- 10)
children.translated_text: Since a word whose convention has not been grasped cannot produce cognition of meaning, a word aided by convention alone conveys a particular meaning; thus, the word for which convention is directly grasped in relation to a particular object is its <s>vācaka</s> (denotative word). (sūtra 10)
The conventionally designated meaning is fourfold — <s>jāti</s> (universal) and others — or <s>jāti</s> (universal) alone.

children.text:
yadyapyarthakriyākāritayā pravṛttinivṛttiyogyā vyaktireva, tayāpyānantyāvdyabhicārācca tatra saṃketaḥ kartuṃ na yujyate, iti gauḥ śuklaśvalo ḍittha ityādīnāṃ viṣayavibhāgo na prāpnotīti ca tadupādhāveva saṃketaḥ /
upādhiśva dvividhaḥ--vastudharmo vaktṛyadṛcchāsaṃniveśitaśva /
vastudharmo 'pi dvividhaḥ--siddhaḥ sādhyaśva /
siddho 'pi dvividhaḥ--padārthasya prāṇaprado viśeṣādhānahetuśva /
tatrādyo jātiḥ uktaṃ hi vākyapadīye " na hi gauḥ svarūpeṇa gaurnāpyagauḥ, gotvābhisaṃbhandhāttu gauḥ" iti /
dvitīyo gumaḥ /
śuklādinā hi labdhasattārka vastu viśiṣyate /
sādhyaḥ pūrvāparībhūtāvayavaḥ kriyārūpaḥ /
ḍitthādiśabdānāmantyabuddhinirgrāhyaṃ saṃhṛtakramaṃ svarūpaṃ vaktrā yadṛcchayā ḍitthādiṣvartheṣūpādhitvena saṃniveśyata iti so 'yaṃ saṃjñārūpo yadṛcchātmaka iti /
"gauḥśuklaśvalo ḍittha ityādau catuṣṭayī śabdānāṃ pravṛttiḥ" iti mahābhāṣyakāraḥ /
paramāṇvādīnāṃ tu guṇamadhyapāṭhāt pāribhāṣikaṃ guṇatvam /
guṇakriyāyadṛcchānāṃ vastuta ekarūpāṇāmapyāśrayabhedādbheda iva lakṣyate /
yathaikasya mukhasya khaḍgamukuratailādyālambanabhedāt /
himapayaḥśaṅkhādyāśrayeṣu paramārthato bhinneṣu śuklādiṣu yadvaśena śuklaḥ śukla ityādyabhinnābhidhānapratyayotpattistat śuklatvādi sāmānyam /
children.translated_text: In the case of substrata like snow, milk, conch, and the like, which are in ultimate reality distinct, that on account of which there arises an undifferentiated cognition and designation 'white, white' — that is the universal such as <s>śuklatva</s> (whiteness).
Similarly, in the cooking of jaggery, rice, and the like — that is the universal such as <s>pākatva</s> (cookedness).

children.text: bālavṛddhaśukādyudīriteṣu ḍitthādiśabdeṣu ca pratikṣaṇaṃ bhidyamāneṣu ḍitthādyartheṣu vā ḍitthatvādyastīti sarveṣāṃ śabdānāṃ jātireva pravṛttinimittamityanye /
children.translated_text: In the words '<s>Ḍittha</s>' and the like uttered by children, old persons, and parrots, and in the referents '<s>Ḍittha</s>' and the like which are constantly changing — there exists something like <s>Ḍitthatva</s> (Ḍittha-ness); thus some hold that <s>jāti</s> (universal) alone is the ground of application for all words.

children.text: tadvān apoho vā śabdārthaḥ kaiśvidukta iti granthagauravabhayāt prakṛtānupayogācca na darśitam //
children.translated_text: Others have said that what possesses that, or <s>apoha</s> (exclusion), is the meaning of words — but this has not been shown here, out of fear of prolixity and because it is not relevant to the present topic. //

Although it is the particular (<s>vyakti</s>) alone that is capable of practical activity and thus fit for engagement and disengagement, since particulars are infinite and there would be error in applying convention to them, the division of domains for words like 'gauḥ' (cow), 'śukla' (white), 'caṭ' (walking), and '<s>Ḍittha</s>' would not be possible — therefore convention is established only in relation to the limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>). The limiting condition is of two kinds: a real property of the object, and one arbitrarily imposed by the speaker. The real property is also of two kinds: established and to-be-established. The established is also of two kinds: that which gives existence to the referent, and that which serves as the basis for differentiation. Of these, the first is <s>jāti</s> (universal) — as stated in the <s>Vākyapadīya</s>: 'A cow is not a cow by its own form, nor is it a non-cow; it is a cow through its connection with <s>gotva</s> (cowness).' The second is <s>guṇa</s> (quality) — for a thing whose existence is already established is further distinguished by whiteness and the like. The to-be-established has parts that are prior and posterior, and is in the nature of <s>kriyā</s> (action). The own-form of words like '<s>Ḍittha</s>' is grasped by the final cognition, with its sequence collapsed, and is arbitrarily assigned by the speaker as a limiting condition for the referents '<s>Ḍittha</s>' and the like — thus this is of the nature of a proper name, and is arbitrary. 'In the case of gauḥ (cow), śukla (white), caṭ (walking), and <s>Ḍittha</s>, the application of words is fourfold' — so says the author of the <s>Mahābhāṣya</s>. For atoms and the like, however, the quality-status is technical, since they are listed in the middle of qualities. Though quality, action, and arbitrary designation are in reality of one form, their distinction appears due to the difference in their substrata — just as with one face reflected in a sword, mirror, oil, and so forth.
(sūtra 11)
That is the primary meaning; and the primary function of the word with respect to it is called <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation). // 8 //
'That' refers to what is directly conventionally designated.
'Of this' refers to the word. //
(sūtra 12)
When the primary meaning is obstructed, through connection with it, either from established usage or from purposive intention,
Another meaning is indicated — the function so attributed is called <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication). // 9 //

children.text:
"karmaṇi kuśalaḥ'; ityādau darbhagrahaṇādyayogāt "gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣaḥ'; ityādau ca gaṅgādīnāṃ ghoṣādyādhāratvāsaṃbhavot mukhyārthasya bādhe vivecakatvādau sāmīpye ca saṃbandhe rūḍhitaḥ prasiddheḥ, tathā gaṅgātaṭe ghoṣa ityādeḥ prayogāt yeṣāṃ na tathā pratipattiḥ, teṣāṃ pāvanatvādīnāṃ dharmāṇāṃ tathāpratipādanātmanaḥ prayojanācca mukhyena amukhyo 'rtho lakṣyate yat sa āropitaḥ śabdavyāpāraḥ sāntarārthaniṣṭho lakṣaṇā /
(sū- 13)
children.translated_text: In expressions like '<s>karmaṇi kuśalaḥ</s>' (skilled in action) and the like, where there is inapplicability of the primary meaning of grasping <s>darbha</s> grass and the like; and in '<s>gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣaḥ</s>' (the hamlet on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>) and the like, where there is impossibility of <s>Gaṅgā</s> and such being a substratum for a hamlet — when there is obstruction of the primary meaning, through the relation of proximity and the like as the distinguishing factor, from established usage (<s>rūḍhi</s>), that is, from convention, and for those who do not have such understanding from the mere usage of '<s>gaṅgātaṭe ghoṣaḥ</s>' (the hamlet on the bank of the Gaṅgā), from the purposive intention of conveying properties like sanctity and the like — a non-primary meaning is indicated by means of the primary meaning; that word-function which rests upon an intermediate meaning is <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication). (sūtra 13)
The drawing in of another for one's own establishment, and the surrendering of oneself for another's purpose —

children.text: upādānaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ cetyuktā śuddhaiva sā dvidhā // 10 //
children.translated_text: These are called <s>upādāna</s> (inclusion) and <s>lakṣaṇa</s> (indication); thus pure <s>lakṣaṇā</s> is said to be of two kinds. // 10 //

children.text:
"kuntāḥ praviśanti'; "yaṣṭayaḥ praviśanti'; ityādau kuntādibhirātmanaḥ praveśasiddhyarthaṃ svasaṃyoginaḥ puruṣā ākṣipyante /
tata upādāneneyaṃ lakṣaṇā /
"gauranubandhyaḥ" ityādau śruticoditamanubandhanaṃ kathaṃ me syāditi jātyā vyaktirākṣipyate na tu śabdenocyate "viśeṣyaṃ nābhidhā gacchet śrīṇaśaktirviśepaṇe" iti nyāyādityupādānalakṣaṇā tu nodāhartavyā /
na hyatra prayojanamasti na vā ruḍhiriyam /
vyaktyavinābhāvitvāttu jātyā vyaktirākṣipyate /
yathā kriyatāmityatra kartā /
kurvityatra karma /
praviśa piṇḍīmityādau gṛhaṃ bhakṣayetyādi ca /
"pīno devadatto divā nabhuṅkte'; ityatra ca rātribhojanaṃ na lakṣyate śrutārthāpatterarthāpattervā tasya viṣayatvāt /
"gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣaḥ'; ityatra taṭasya ghoṣādhikaraṇatvasiddhaye gaṅgāśabdaḥ svārthamarpayati, ityevamādau lakṣaṇenaiṣā lakṣaṇā /
ubhayarupā ceyaṃ śuddhā /

children.translated_text: because it is unmixed with <s>upacāra</s> (figurative usage).

children.text: anayorlakṣyasya lakṣakasya ca na bhedarūpaṃ tāṭasthayam /
children.translated_text: In these two, the distinction between the indicated meaning and the indicator is not one of mere external relation.

children.text: taṭādīnāṃ gaṅgādiśabdaiḥ pratipādane tacvapratipattau hi pratipipādayiṣitaprayojanasaṃpratyayaḥ /
children.translated_text: For when things like the bank are conveyed by words like <s>Gaṅgā</s>, and when there is comprehension of that, there arises the understanding of the intended purpose.

children.text: gahgāsaṃbandhamātraprātītau tu gaṅgātaṭe ghoṣa iti mukhyaśabdābhidhānāllakṣaṇāyāḥ ko bhedaḥ //
children.translated_text: But if only the relation with <s>Gaṅgā</s> were understood, then what difference would there be from <s>lakṣaṇā</s>, since the primary word denotes in 'a settlement on the bank of <s>Gaṅgā</s>'?

In examples like 'the spears enter' and 'the staffs enter,' the persons associated with the spears and so forth are implied for the purpose of accomplishing the act of entering.
Therefore this is <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification) through inclusion.
In examples like '<s>gauḥ</s> (cow) is to be tied for sacrifice,' the individual is implied by the universal for the purpose of fulfilling the Vedic injunction 'how shall the binding apply to me' — but it is not denoted by the word, according to the principle that 'the qualified cannot be reached by denotation when the power of the qualifier is in the qualifier.' Therefore <s>lakṣaṇā</s> by inclusion need not be illustrated separately.
For here there is no purpose for it, nor is this a conventional usage.
Because the universal is inseparable from the individual, the individual is implied by the universal,
just as the agent is implied in 'let it be done,'
the object in 'do it,'
and in expressions like 'enter the hall' implying a house, or 'eat' implying food.
In 'Fat <s>Devadatta</s> does not eat during the day,' eating at night is not the secondary meaning, because it is the domain of either <s>śrutārthāpatti</s> (implication from what is heard) or <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption).
In '<s>Gaṅgā</s> has a settlement,' the word <s>Gaṅgā</s> yields its own meaning for the purpose of establishing the bank as the substratum of the settlement — in such cases, this is <s>lakṣaṇā</s> through indication.
And this is of both kinds, being pure,
(<s>sūtra</s> 14)
The other [type of <s>lakṣaṇā</s>] is <s>sāropā</s> (with superimposition), where the superimposed and the locus of superimposition are stated as such.

children.text: āropyamāṇaḥ, āropaviṣayaśva yatrānapahnutabhedau sāmānādhikaraṇyena nirdiśyete sā lakṣaṇā sāropā //
children.translated_text: Where the superimposed and the locus of superimposition are expressed in grammatical co-reference without negation of their difference, that <s>lakṣaṇā</s> is called <s>sāropā</s> (with superimposition).
(<s>sūtra</s> 15)
When the other [i.e., the locus of superimposition] is absorbed within the superimposed, that is called <s>sādhyavasānikā</s> (determinative). // 11 //

children.text: viṣayiṇāropyamāṇenāntaḥkṛte nigīrṇe, anyasminnāropaviṣaye sati sādhyavasānā syāt //
children.translated_text: When the other, the locus of superimposition, is absorbed — that is, engulfed — by the superimposed, that is <s>sādhyavasānā</s> (determination).
(<s>sūtra</s> 16)

children.text:
bhedāvimau ca sādṛśyātsaṃbandhāntaratastathā /
gauṇau śuddhau ca vijñeyau
children.translated_text: And these two varieties are to be known as <s>gauṇa</s> (figurative) and <s>śuddha</s> (pure), based on similarity and based on other relations respectively.

children.text:
imāvāropādhyavasānarūpau sādṛśyahetū bhedau "gaurvāhīkaḥ'; ityatra "gaurayam'; ityatra ca /
atra hi svārthasahacāriṇo guṇā jāḍyamāndyādayo lakṣyamāṇā api gośabdasya parārthābhidhāne pravṛttinimittetvamupayānti, iti kecit /
svārthasahacāriguṇābhedena parārthagatā guṇā eva lakṣyante na parārtho 'bhidhīyate, ityanye /
sādhāraṇaguṇāśrayatvena parārtha eva lakṣyate, ityapare /
uktaṃ cānyatra "abhidheyāvinābhūtapratītirlakṣaṇocyate /
lakṣyamāṇaguṇairyogādvṛtteriṣṭā tu gauṇatā" iti /
avinābhāvo 'tra saṃbandhamātraṃ na tu nāntarīyakatvam /
tecve hi mañcāḥ krośanti'; ityādau na lakṣaṇā syāt /
avanābhāve cākṣepeṇaiva siddherlakṣaṇāyā nopayoga ityuktam /
"āyurgṛtam'; "āyurevedam'; ityādo ca sādṛśyādanyat kāryakāraṇabāvādi saṃbandhāntaram /
evamādau ca kāryakāraṇabhāvādilakṣaṇapūrve, āropādhyavasāne /
atra gauṇabhedayorbhede 'pi tādrūpyapratītiḥ sarvathaivābhedāvagamaśva prayojanam /
śuddhabhedayostvanyavailakṣaṇyenāvyabhicāreṇa ca kāryakāritvādi /
kvacit tādartyādupacāraḥ /
yathā, indrārthā sthūṇā, indraḥ /
kvacanatama svasvāmibhāvāt /
yathā, rājakīyaḥ puruṣo rājā /

children.translated_text: Sometimes it is due to the relation of part and whole.
For example, in '<s>agrahasta</s>' (tip-hand), the word 'hand' refers to the tip alone, which is a part.
Sometimes it is due to the relation of function.
For example, one who is not a carpenter is called a carpenter.

These two, in the form of superimposition and determination, are the varieties based on similarity as their cause — as in 'he is an ox-like person' and 'this one is an ox.'
Here some hold that the qualities co-occurring with the primary meaning — such as stupidity and slowness — though indicated, serve as the ground for the word 'cow' being applied to another object.
Others say that through non-difference from the qualities co-occurring with the primary meaning, only the qualities present in the secondary object are indicated, not the secondary object itself denoted.
Still others hold that the secondary object itself is indicated through being the locus of the common qualities.
And it has been stated elsewhere: 'The cognition that is inseparable from the denoted meaning is called <s>lakṣaṇā</s>; the figurativeness of usage is accepted due to connection with the indicated qualities.'
Here 'inseparability' means mere relation, not invariable concomitance,
for otherwise in cases like 'the platforms are crying,' there would be no <s>lakṣaṇā</s>.
And when there is inseparability, since the purpose is accomplished by implication alone, <s>lakṣaṇā</s> has no role — as was stated.
In examples like '<s>ghṛta</s> (ghee) is life' and 'this indeed is life,' there is another relation beyond similarity, such as cause-and-effect.
In such cases, superimposition and determination are preceded by <s>lakṣaṇā</s> based on cause-and-effect relation.
Here, though the two figurative varieties differ, the cognition of identity and the complete apprehension of non-difference is the purpose.
But for the two pure varieties, it is the production of effect through distinctness from others and non-deviation.
Sometimes the figurative usage is due to purpose-relation;
for example, a post for <s>Indra</s>'s purpose is called '<s>Indra</s>.'
Sometimes it is due to the relation of owned and owner;
for example, a royal servant is called 'the king.'
(<s>sūtra</s> 17)
<s>Lakṣaṇā</s> is thus sixfold. // 12 //
Together with the first two varieties.
And that (<s>sūtra</s> 18)

children.text: vyaṅgyena rahitā rūḍhau sahitā tu prayojane /
children.translated_text: When devoid of suggested meaning, it is <s>rūḍhi</s> (conventional); when accompanied [by suggested meaning], it is purposeful.
For the purpose is indeed that which is apprehended through the operation of <s>vyañjanā</s> (suggestion).
(<s>sūtra</s> 19)
And that [suggested meaning] may be concealed or unconcealed.
'That' refers to the suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgya</s>).

children.text: gūḍhaṃ yathā mukhaṃ vikasitasmitaṃ vaśitavakrima prekṣitaṃ samucchalitavibhramā gatirapāstasaṃśthā matiḥ /
children.translated_text: An example of the concealed: 'The face has a blossoming smile, the glance has a controlled curvature, the gait has surging grace, the mind has abandoned its composure,

children.text: uro mukulitastanaṃ jaghanamaṃsabandhoddhuraṃ batenduvadanātanau taruṇimodgamo modate //9//
children.translated_text: the chest has budding breasts, the hips are heavy with flesh — alas, in the body of the moon-faced one, the rising of youth delights!' // 9 //

children.text: agūḍhaṃ yathā śrīparicayājjaḍā api bhavantyabhijñā vidagdhacaritānām /
children.translated_text: An example of the unconcealed: 'Through familiarity with beauty, even the dull become knowledgeable of the ways of the sophisticated.
The intoxication of youth itself teaches young women the arts of love.' // 10 //
Here 'teaches' [is the key word indicating the unconcealed suggestion].
(<s>sūtra</s> 20)
Thus this [<s>lakṣaṇā</s>] has been described as threefold. // 13 //
Without suggested meaning, with concealed suggested meaning, and with unconcealed suggested meaning.
(<s>sūtra</s> 21)
A word based on that [<s>lakṣaṇā</s>]
'Word' is to be connected [with the preceding].
That which is based on it, that which has it as its foundation.
(<s>sūtra</s> 22)
There the operation is of the nature of <s>vyañjanā</s> (suggestion).
Why? He says: (<s>sūtra</s> 23)
That whose cognition <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification) is employed to establish — // 14 //
when the result is accessible through the word alone, there is no operation other than <s>vyañjanā</s> (suggestion).

children.text: prayojanapratipipādayiṣayā yatra lakṣaṇayā śabdaprayogastatra nānyatastatpratītirapi tu tasmādeva sabdāt /
children.translated_text: Where a word is used with <s>lakṣaṇā</s> for the purpose of conveying the intended meaning, there the cognition [of that meaning] comes from that very word alone and from nothing else.
And here there is no other operation apart from <s>vyañjanā</s> (suggestion).
For instance: (<s>sūtra</s> 24)
<s>Abhidhā</s> (denotation) [cannot account for it] due to the absence of convention.

children.text: gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣa ityādau ye pāvanatvādayo dharmāstaṭādau pratīyante na tatra gaṅgādiśabdāḥ saṃketitāḥ //
children.translated_text: In examples like 'a settlement on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,' the qualities such as purifying power that are cognized in the bank and so forth — for those, words like <s>Gaṅgā</s> have not been conventionally assigned.
(<s>sūtra</s> 25)
Nor is it <s>lakṣaṇā</s>, due to the absence of its cause. // 15 //
The cause is the triad beginning with obstruction of the primary meaning.
And further: (<s>sūtra</s> 26)

children.text: lakṣyaṃ na mukhyaṃ nāpyatra bādho yogaḥ phalena no /
children.translated_text: The indicated meaning is not primary, nor is there obstruction here, nor connection with the result,

children.text: na prayojanametasmin na ca śabdaḥ skhaladgatiḥ // 16 //
children.translated_text: nor is there a purpose in this, nor does the word stumble [in its function]. // 16 //

children.text:
yathā gaṅgāśabdaḥ srotasi sabādha iti taṭaṃ lakṣayati tadvat yadi taṭe 'pi sabādhaḥ syāt tat prayojanaṃ lakṣayet /
na ca taṭaṃ mukhyo 'rthaḥ /

children.translated_text: Nor is there any obstruction here.

children.text: na ca gaṅgāśabdārthasya taṭasya pāvanatvādyairlakṣaṇīyaiḥ saṃbandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Nor is there any relation between the meaning of the word <s>Gaṅgā</s>, i.e., the bank, and the qualities to be indicated such as purifying power.
Nor is there any purpose in the indicated purpose.
Nor is the word <s>Gaṅgā</s> incapable of conveying the purpose in the way it conveys the bank.

Just as the word <s>Gaṅgā</s> indicates the bank because there is obstruction [of primary meaning] in the stream, similarly if there were obstruction in the bank too, it would indicate the purpose.
But the bank is not the primary meaning.
(<s>sūtra</s> 27)
Even so, there would be an infinite regress that would destroy the root [meaning].

children.text: evamapi prayojanaṃ cellakṣyate tat prayojanāntareṇeti tadapi prayojanāntareṇeti prakṛtāpratītikṛt anavasthā bhavet //
children.translated_text: Even if the purpose were indicated, then that too would require another purpose, and that too another purpose — thus there would be an infinite regress that prevents the cognition of the original [meaning].

children.text:
nanu pāvanatvādidharmayuktameva taṭaṃ lakṣyate /
"gaṅgāyāstaṭe ghoṣaḥ'; ityato 'dhikasyārthasya pratītiśva pyojanamiti viśiṣṭe lakṣaṇā ttkiṃ vyañjanayetyāha /
(sū- 28)
children.translated_text:
Objection: The bank itself is indicated as endowed with qualities such as purifying power. And the cognition of a meaning beyond what is in 'a settlement on the bank of <s>Gaṅgā</s>' is the purpose, so there is <s>lakṣaṇā</s> for the qualified [meaning] — why then posit <s>vyañjanā</s>? To this he says:
(<s>sūtra</s> 28)
It is not proper that the indicated meaning be combined with the purpose. // 17 //
Why? He says: (<s>sūtra</s> 29)
The object of cognition is one thing; the result is stated to be another.
The object of perception and so forth is blue and the like; but the result is manifestation or awareness.
(<s>sūtra</s> 30)
<s>Lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification) for the qualified [meaning] is not thus [possible].
This has been explained.
(<s>sūtra</s> 31)
But the particular qualities would belong to the indicated [meaning]. // 18 //

children.text: taṭādau ye viṣeṣāḥ pāvanatvādayaste cābhidhātātparyalakṣaṇābhyo vyāpārāntareṇa gamyāḥ /
children.translated_text: The particular qualities such as purifying power that belong to the bank and so forth — those are to be apprehended through an operation different from <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation), <s>tātparya</s> (purport), and <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification).
And that [operation], designated by words such as <s>vyañjana</s> (suggestion), <s>dhvanana</s> (resonance), and <s>dyotana</s> (illumination), must necessarily be accepted.
Thus the suggestive power based on <s>lakṣaṇā</s> has been established.

Now he states the suggestive power based on <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation):
(<s>sūtra</s> 32)
When the denotative power of a word having multiple meanings is restricted,
the operation that produces the cognition of a non-denoted meaning through <s>saṃyoga</s> (association) and other [factors] is <s>vyañjana</s> (suggestion). // 19 //
'<s>Saṃyoga</s> (association), <s>viprayoga</s> (dissociation), <s>sāhacarya</s> (co-occurrence), <s>virodhitā</s> (opposition),
<s>artha</s> (meaning), <s>prakaraṇa</s> (context), <s>liṅga</s> (gender/indication), proximity of another word,
<s>sāmarthya</s> (capability), <s>aucitī</s> (propriety), <s>deśa</s> (place), <s>kāla</s> (time), <s>vyakti</s> (person), <s>svara</s> (accent) and so forth —
these are the causes for recollecting the specific [meaning] when the meaning of the word is undetermined.'

children.text:
ityuktadiśā saśaṅkhacakro hariḥ aśaṅkhacakro harirityacyute /
rāmalakṣmaṇāviti dāśarathau /
rāmārjunagatistayoriti bhārgavakārtavīryayoḥ /
sthāṇuṃ bhaja bhavacchide, iti hara /
sarvaṃ jānāti deva iti yuṣmadarthe /
kupito makaradhvaja iti kāme /
devasya purārāderiti saṃbhau /
madhunā mattaḥ kokila iti vasante /
pātu vo dayitāmukhamiti sāṃmukhye /
bhātyatra parameśvara iti rājadhānīrūpāt deśādrājani /
citrabānurvibhātīti dine ravau rātrau vahnau /
mitraṃ bhātīti suhṛdi, mitro bhātīti ravau /
children.translated_text: '<s>Mitra</s> shines' — [refers to] a friend; '<s>Mitra</s> shines' — [refers to] the sun.

children.text: indraśatrurityādau vete eva, na kāvye, svero viśeṣapratītikṛt /
children.translated_text: In compounds like '<s>Indraśatru</s>' and the like, these very [factors] — not in poetry — accent is what produces the specific cognition.
And by the inclusion of 'and so forth': 'So much is this distance, so much by these auspicious ones,
so much is this situation, so much by these days.' // 11 //

In the manner stated [above]: '<s>Hari</s> with conch and discus' — [refers to] <s>Hari</s> [as <s>Viṣṇu</s>]; '<s>Hari</s> without conch and discus' — [refers to] <s>Acyuta</s>.
'<s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>' — the sons of <s>Daśaratha</s>.
'The course of <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Arjuna</s>' — of <s>Bhārgava</s> and <s>Kārtavīrya</s>.
'Worship <s>Sthāṇu</s> for the destruction of worldly existence' — [refers to] <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>).
'The lord knows everything' — in the sense of 'you.'
'The banner-of-<s>Makara</s> is angry' — [refers to] <s>Kāma</s> (the god of love).
'Of the god, the destroyer of <s>Pura</s>' — [refers to] <s>Śambhu</s> (<s>Śiva</s>).
'Intoxicated by honey, the cuckoo' — [refers to] spring.
'May the face of the beloved protect you' — in the sense of facing.
'The supreme lord shines here' — from the place in the form of a capital city, [refers to] the king.
'<s>Citrabānu</s> shines' — during the day [refers to] the sun, at night [refers to] fire.

children.text:
ityādāvabhinayādayaḥ /
itthaṃ saṃyogādibhirardhāntarābhidhāyakatve nivārite 'pyanekārthasya śabdasya yat kvacidarthāntarapratipādanaṃ tatra nābhidhā niyamanāttasyāḥ /

children.translated_text: Nor is it <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification), due to the absence of obstruction of primary meaning and the rest.
Rather, <s>vyañjana</s> (suggestion) alone is the operation.
For example: 'Of the noble one, difficult to mount, broad, elevated in lineage, one who has gathered arrows,
whose gait is unimpeded — of that great elephant, the trunk was always beautified by the streaming waters of <s>dāna</s> (rut-fluid).' // 12 //

In such cases, dramatic gestures and the like [serve as determinants].
Thus, even when the denotation of other meanings is prevented by association and other factors for a word with multiple meanings, wherever there is the conveyance of yet another meaning, there <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation) does not operate, because it has been restricted.
(<s>sūtra</s> 33)
A word endowed with that is suggestive.
Endowed with that — endowed with <s>vyañjana</s> (suggestion). (<s>sūtra</s> 34)
When that [word] is connected with another meaning, likewise
the meaning too is regarded as suggestive in that case, in the capacity of an auxiliary. // 20 //
'Likewise' means 'suggestive.'

children.text: iti kāvyaprakāśe śabdārthasvarūpanirṇayo nāma dvitīya ullāsaḥ // 2 //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second <s>ullāsa</s> (chapter), named 'Determination of the Nature of Word and Meaning,' in the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>. // 2 //
// Now begins the third <s>ullāsa</s> (chapter). //
(<s>sūtra</s> 35)
The meanings have been previously stated; of those,
the meanings — the denoted, the indicated, and the suggested.
Of those — of the denoting, the indicating, and the suggesting [words].
(<s>sūtra</s> 36)
The suggestive power of meaning is now stated.
Of what kind? He says: (<s>sūtra</s> 37)
Through the speaker, the addressee, the <s>kāku</s> (tone of voice), the sentence, the proximity of another denoted meaning, // 21 //
through the distinctiveness of the occasion, place, time and so forth, for those endowed with <s>pratibhā</s> (intuitive insight),
that operation of a meaning which causes the cognition of another meaning — that alone is <s>vyakti</s> (manifestation/suggestion). // 22 //
Of meaning — that which is of the nature of the denoted, indicated, and suggested.
Examples [will be given] in order.

children.text: aipihulaṃ jalakuṃbhaṃ ghettūṇa samāgadahni sahi turiam /
children.translated_text: 'Taking a large water-pot, having come together on that day with my friend,
with the companion of equal water-fetching, I rest for a moment.' // 13 //

<s>Boddhavya</s> means 'that which is to be communicated.'
<s>Kāku</s> is a modification of sound.
<s>Prastāva</s> means context.
Here the concealment of a secret love affair is suggested.
'Listlessness, weakness, anxiety, lethargy, drowsiness —

children.text: maha maṃdabhāiṇīe keraṃ sahi tuha vi ahaha parihavai //14//
children.translated_text: O friend, all these qualities of my slow-speaking one, alas, now afflict you too.' // 14 //
Here the messenger-woman's enjoyment with her [friend's] lover is suggested.

children.text: tathābhūtāṃ dṛṣṭvā nṛpasadasi pāñjālatanayāṃ vane vyādhaiḥ sārdhaṃ suciramuṣitaṃ valkaladharaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Having seen the daughter of <s>Pāñcāla</s> in such a state in the king's assembly, having dwelt long in the forest with hunters wearing bark garments,

children.text: virāṭasyāvāse sthitamanucitārambhanibhṛtaṃ guruḥ khedaṃ khinne mayi bhajati nādyāpi kuruṣu //15//
children.translated_text: having stayed in the house of <s>Virāṭa</s> restrained in undertaking improper tasks — my elder [<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>] does not even now feel distress toward the <s>Kurus</s>, though I am distressed. // 15 //

children.text: atra mayi na yogyaḥ khedaḥ kuruṣu tu yogya iti kākvā prakāśyate /
na ca vācyasiddhayaṅgamatra kākuriti guṇībhūtavyaṅgyatvaṃ śaṅkyam /
children.translated_text: And one should not suspect that the <s>kāku</s> here is merely an accessory to the denoted meaning, making this a case of subordinated suggestion (<s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>),
because the <s>kāku</s> comes to rest even in the mere question [itself].

children.text: taiā maha gaṃḍatthalaṇimiaṃ diṭhṭhiṃ ṇa ṇesi aṇṇatto /
children.translated_text: 'Do not cast that glance, resting on my cheek, elsewhere,

children.text: eṇhiṃ saccea ahaṃ te a kavālā ṇa sā diṭhṭhī //16//
children.translated_text: 'Come here; truly I am yours, and that glance is not for her.' // 16 //
Here, through <s>kāku</s> (tone), it is revealed: 'distress is not appropriate for me, but it is appropriate toward the <s>Kurus</s>.'

children.text: atra matsakhīṃ kapolapratibimbitāṃ paśyataste dṛṣṭiranyaivābhūt calitāyāṃ tu tasyāmanyaiva jātetyaho pracchannakāmukatvaṃ te, iti vyajyate /
children.translated_text: Here it is suggested: "Look at my friend reflected on [his] cheek — his gaze became something else entirely; and when she moved away, it became yet another — oh, what a secret lover you are!"
This is that place on the <s>Narmadā</s>, surpassing in beauty the rows of lush <s>kadalī</s> (plantain) trees, where the delightful charm of the bower-groves has sprouted forth,

children.text: kiṃ caitasmin suratasudṛdastanvi de vānti vātā yeṣāmagre sarati kalitākāṇjakopo manobhūḥ //17//
children.translated_text: Moreover, in this place, O slender one, winds blow that are firmly steeped in passion, before which <s>Manobhū</s> (the god of love) advances with his quiver of arrows readied. //17//
Here the suggested meaning is "she enters for the purpose of lovemaking."
Devoted to household duties, not paying attention to herself,

children.text: khaṇamettaṃ jai saṃjhāi hoi ṇa va hoi vīsāmo //18//
children.translated_text: If for even a moment there is twilight, there may or may not be rest. //18//

children.text: atra saṃdhyā saṃketakāra iti taṭasthaṃ prati kayāciddayotyate /
children.translated_text: Here, the fact that twilight is the appointed time for a rendezvous is conveyed by someone to an onlooker.

children.text: suvvaha samāgamissadi tujjha pio ajja paharametteṇa /
children.translated_text: "Your beloved will arrive today within a short while, dear friend,"

children.text: eme a kitti ciṭhṭhasi tā sahi sajjesu karaṇijjam //19//
children.translated_text: "Why do you stand here? So, friend, prepare what needs to be done." //19//

children.text: atropapatiṃ pratyabhisartuṃ prastutā na yuktamiti kayācinnivāryate /
children.translated_text: Here, one who has set out to go to meet a secret lover is restrained by someone saying "this is not proper."

children.text: anyatra yūyaṃ kusumāvacāyaṃ kurudhvamatrāsmi karomi sakhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: "You all go elsewhere to gather flowers; I shall do so here, friends,

children.text: nāhaṃ hi dūraṃ bhramituṃ samarthā prasīdatāyaṃ racito 'ñjalirvaḥ //20//
children.translated_text: for I am not able to wander far — please be gracious, this is my folded-hands entreaty to you." //20//

children.text: atra vivikto 'yaṃ deśa iti pracchannakāmukastvayābhisāryatāmiti, āśvastāṃ prati kayācinnivedyate /
children.translated_text: Here, to one who has been reassured, someone conveys: "This is a secluded place; the secret lover should be invited here for a rendezvous."

children.text: guruaṇaparavasa pia kiṃ bhaṇāmi tui maṃdabhāiṇī ahakam /
children.translated_text: "Dear one, subject to the authority of elders — what shall I, an ill-fated woman, say to you?

children.text: ajja pavāsaṃ vaccasi vacca saaṃ jevva suṇasi karaṇijjam //21//
children.translated_text: Today you go away on a journey; go then, you yourself will hear what must be done." //21//

children.text:
atrādya madhusamaye yadi vrajasi tadāhaṃ tāvat na bavāmi tava tu na jānāmi gatimiti vyajyate /
ādigrahaṇācceṣṭādeḥ /
children.translated_text:
Here it is suggested: "If today, in the spring season, you depart, then I at least will not survive, but of your fate I do not know."
The word <s>ādi</s> (etc.) includes gesture and so forth.

children.text: tatra ceṣṭāyā yathā dvāropāntanirantare mayi tayā saundaryasāraśriyā prollāsyoruyugaṃ parasparasamāsaktaṃ samāsāditam /
children.translated_text: There, regarding gesture, for example: "When I stood near the doorway, she — the essence of all beauty — brought her pair of thighs closely pressed together before me;

children.text: ānītaṃ purataḥ śiroṃ'śukamadhaḥ kṣipte cale locane vācastatra nivāritaṃ prasaraṇaṃ saṃkocite dorlate //22//
children.translated_text: She brought the edge of her garment before her face, when [my] eyes fell downward and wavered, the movement of speech was restrained there, and her creeper-like arms contracted." //22//
Here, through gesture, a particular intention regarding the secretly beloved one is suggested.
For the sake of complete understanding without residual expectancy, and because the occasion has arrived, examples are given again and again.
In the mutual combination of speech and other elements, through the distinctions of pairs and so forth.
By this method, the suggestive function of the perceptible suggested meaning should also be illustrated.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 38)
A meaning known through verbal testimony, inasmuch as it suggests another meaning,
in the suggestive capacity of meaning, that [function] of the word is merely an auxiliary role. //23//
Regarding "<s>śabda</s>" (word) —
Indeed, a meaning known through other means of knowledge is not a suggestive element.
Thus ends the third <s>ullāsa</s> (chapter), named "Determination of the Suggestive Capacity of Meaning" in the glorious <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>. //3//
// Now begins the fourth <s>ullāsa</s> (chapter) //

children.text:
yadyapi śabdārthayornirṇaye kṛte doṣaguṇālaṃkārāṇāṃ svarūpamabhidhānīyam tathāpi dharmiṇi pradarśite dharmāṇāṃ hermāṇāṃ heyopādeyatā jñāyata iti prathamaṃ kāvyabhedān āha /
(sū- 39)
children.translated_text:
Although, once the nature of word and meaning has been determined, the essential nature of <s>doṣa</s> (faults), <s>guṇa</s> (qualities), and <s>alaṃkāra</s> (figures of speech) should be discussed, nevertheless, since the acceptability and rejectability of qualities becomes known when the qualified entity is first demonstrated, he first states the types of <s>kāvya</s> (poetry).
(<s>Sūtra</s> 39)
That [poetry] in which the literal meaning is not intended — therein the literal meaning, in <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion),
is either transferred to another meaning, or entirely concealed. //24//

children.text: lakṣaṇāmūlagūḍhavyaṅgyaprādhānye satyeva, avivakṣitaṃ vācyaṃ yatra sa "dhvanau'; ityanuvādāt dhvaniriti jñeyaḥ /
children.translated_text: When there is predominance of the hidden suggested meaning based on <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification), that in which the literal meaning is not intended is to be understood as <s>dhvani</s> — this is indicated by the resumptive particle.
And therein, the literal meaning in some cases is transformed into another meaning because it serves no purpose [in its literal sense].

children.text: yathā tvāmasmi vacmi viduṣāṃ samavāyo 'tra tiṣṭhati /
children.translated_text: For example: "I am telling you — an assembly of learned ones stands here;
Therefore, relying on your own judgment, establish your conduct here accordingly." //23//
Here, the act of speaking and so forth is transformed into the form of instruction and so forth.
In some cases, because [the literal meaning] is untenable, it is entirely concealed.

children.text: yathā upakṛtaṃ bahu tatra kimucyate sujanatā prathitā bhavatā param /
children.translated_text: For example: "You have rendered great help — what more can be said? Your goodness, O sir, is widely renowned;

children.text: vidadhadīdṛśameva sadā sakhe sukhitamāssva tataḥ śaradāṃ śatam //24//
children.translated_text: Always acting in just this manner, O friend, may you live happily for a hundred autumns." //24//
This is spoken by someone toward an offender through <s>viparītalakṣaṇā</s> (ironic secondary signification).
(<s>Sūtra</s> 40)
And that [poetry] in which the literal meaning is intended but subordinate to something else — that other [type of <s>dhvani</s>] is:
"Subordinate to something else" means having the suggested meaning as its chief purport.
And this [type] — (<s>Sūtra</s> 41)
is of two kinds: one where the process of suggestion is imperceptible, and another where it is perceptible. //25//
Regarding "imperceptible" —
It is not the case that <s>rasa</s> arises from <s>vibhāva</s> (determinants), <s>anubhāva</s> (consequents), and <s>vyabhicārin</s> (transitory emotions) alone;
rather, <s>rasa</s> [is manifested] by means of them — thus there is a [logical] sequence.
But that sequence is not perceptible due to its subtlety.
Here — (<s>Sūtra</s> 42)
<s>Rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s> (emotion), their semblances (<s>tadābhāsa</s>), <s>bhāvaśānti</s> (quiescence of emotion), and so forth — the imperceptible [type of <s>dhvani</s>]
is distinct from <s>rasa</s> and other <s>alaṃkāras</s> (figures), being established as that which is to be ornamented. //26//
The word <s>ādi</s> (etc.) includes <s>bhāvodaya</s> (arising of emotion), <s>bhāvasaṃdhi</s> (juncture of emotions), and <s>bhāvaśabalatva</s> (mixture of emotions).
Where <s>rasa</s> and so forth are established with predominance, there they are the <s>alaṃkārya</s> (that which is to be ornamented), as will be illustrated.

children.text: anyatra tu pradhāne vākyārthe yatrāṅgabhūto rasādistatra guṇībhūtavyaṅgaye rasavatpreyaūrjasvisamāhitādayo 'laṃkārāḥ /
children.translated_text: But elsewhere, where <s>rasa</s> and so forth are subordinate elements to the predominant sentence-meaning, there they constitute <s>alaṃkāras</s> (figures) such as <s>rasavat</s>, <s>preyas</s>, <s>ūrjasvin</s>, <s>samāhita</s>, and so forth, within <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (subordinated suggestion).
And these will be illustrated in the section on <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (subordinated suggestion).
Therein, he states the essential nature of <s>rasa</s> — (<s>Sūtra</s> 43)
Those that are causes, effects, and accompanying factors
of the enduring emotion (<s>sthāyin</s>) such as <s>rati</s> (love) and so forth in the world — those same, in drama and poetry, //27//
are called <s>vibhāva</s> (determinants), <s>anubhāva</s> (consequents), and <s>vyabhicārin</s> (transitory emotions);

children.text: vyaktaḥ sa tairvibhāvādyaiḥ sthāyī bhāvo rasaḥ smṛtaḥ // 28 //
children.translated_text: the <s>sthāyibhāva</s> (enduring emotion) manifested by those <s>vibhāvas</s> and so forth is designated as <s>rasa</s>. //28//
This they explain [as follows]:

children.text: "vibhāvairlalanodyānādi bhirālambanoddīpanakāraṇaiḥ, ratyādiko bhāvo janitaḥ, anubhāvaiḥ kaṭākṣabhujākṣepaprabhṛtibhiḥ kāryaiḥ pratītiyogyaḥ kṛtaḥ, vyabhicārimirnirvedādibhiḥ sahakārimirupacito mukhyayā vṛcyā rāmādāvanukārye tadrūpatasaṃdhānānnartake 'pi pratīyamāno rasaḥ" iti bhaṭṭalollaṭaprabhṛtayaḥ /
children.translated_text: "The emotional state such as <s>rati</s> (love), generated by <s>vibhāvas</s> — the foundational and stimulating causes such as a beautiful woman, a garden, and so forth — made fit for apprehension through <s>anubhāvas</s> — effects such as sidelong glances, arm gestures, and so forth — and intensified by <s>vyabhicārins</s> — auxiliary emotions such as <s>nirveda</s> (world-weariness) and so forth — is <s>rasa</s> when apprehended in the actor as well, through the contemplation in the mode of the character being imitated such as <s>Rāma</s>, by means of the primary [literal] function" — thus say <s>Bhaṭṭa Lollaṭa</s> and others.

children.text: rāma evāyam ayameva rāma iti "na rāmo 'yam'; ityauttarakālike bādhe rāmo 'yamiti rāmaḥ syādvā na vāyamiti rāmasadṛśo 'yamiti ca samyaṅbhithyāsaṃśayasādṛśyapratītibhyo vilakṣaṇayā citraturagādinyāyena rāmo 'yamiti pratipacyā grāhye naṭe "seyaṃ mamāṅgeṣu sudhārasacchaṭā supūrakarpūraśalākikā dṛśoḥ /
children.translated_text: "This is <s>Rāma</s> himself, this very one is <s>Rāma</s>" — through a cognition distinct from the later sublation "this is not <s>Rāma</s>," and distinct from valid cognition, error, doubt, and similarity — "this one is <s>Rāma</s>" or "perhaps this is not <s>Rāma</s>" or "this one resembles <s>Rāma</s>" — through a cognition like the principle of the painted horse, by which the actor is apprehended as "this is <s>Rāma</s>" — [as in the verse:] "This very nectar-stream upon my limbs, this camphor-stick for the eyes,
this embodied splendor of desire for the heart — my lord of life has come within the range of sight" //25//
For <s>Bharata</s> has stated: "From the conjunction of <s>vibhāva</s>, <s>anubhāva</s>, and <s>vyabhicārin</s>, <s>rasa</s> arises."
"By fate, today I am separated from her of the long, restless eyes,
and this season of dense, dark, swaying rain-clouds has arrived" //26//

children.text:
ityādikāvyānusaṃdhānabalācchikṣābhyāsanirvartitasvakāyraprakaṭanena ca naṭenaiva prakāśitaiḥ kāraṇakāryasahakāribhiḥ kṛtrimairapi tathānabhimanyamānairvibhāvādiśabdavyapadeśyaiḥ "saṃyogāt'; gamyagamakabhāvarūpāt anumīyamāno 'pi vastusaundaryabalādrasanīyatvenānyānumīyamānavilakṣaṇaḥ sthāyitvena saṃbhāvyamāno ratyādirbhāvastatrāsannapi sāmājikānāṃ vāsanayā carvyamāṇo rasa iti śrīśaṅkukaḥ /
na tāṭasthyena nātmagatatvena rasaḥ pratīyate notpadyate nāmivyajyate, api tu kāvye nāṭye cābhidhāto dvitīyenana vibhāvādisādhāraṇīkaraṇātmanā bhāvakatvavyāpāreṇa bhāvyamānaḥ sthāyī sacvodrekaprakāśānandamayasaṃvidviśrāntisatacvena bhogena bhujyate, iti bhaṭṭanāyakaḥ /
loke pramadimiḥ sthāyyanumāne 'bhyāsapāṭavavatāṃ kāvye nāṭye ca taireva kāraṇatvādiparihāreṇa vibhāvanādivyāpāravcvādalaukikavibhāvādiśabdavyavahāyairrmamaivaite śatrorevaite taṭasthasyaivaite na mamaivaite na śatrorevaite na taṭasthasyaivaite, iti saṃbandhaviśeṣasvīkāraparihāraniyamānadhyavasāyāt sādhāraṇyena pratītairabhivyaktaḥ sāmājikānāṃ vāsanātmatayā sthitaḥ sthāyī ratyādiko niyatapramātṛgatatvena sthito 'pi sādhāraṇopāyabalāt tatkālavigalitaparimitapramātṛbhāvavaśonmiṣitavedyāntarasaṃparkaśūnyāparimitabhāvena pramātrā sakalasahṛdayasaṃvādabhājā sādhāraṇyena svākāra ivābhinno 'pi gocarīkṛtaśvarvyamāṇataikaprāṇo vibhāvādijīvitāvadhiḥ pānakarasanyāyena carvyamāṇaḥ pura iva parisphuran hṛdayamiva praviśan sarvāṅgīṇamivāliṅgan anyat sarvamiva tirodadhat brahnāsvādamivānubāvayan alaukikacamatkārakārī śṛṅgārādiko rasaḥ /
sa ca na kāryaḥ /
vibhāvādivināśe 'pi tasya saṃbhavaprasaṅgāt /
nāpi jñāpyaḥ siddhasya tasyāsaṃbhavāt /
api tu vibhāvādibhirvyajjitaśvarvaṇīyaḥ /
kārakajñāpakābhyāmanyat kva dṛṣṭamiti cet, na kvaciddṛṣṭamityalaukikasiddherbhūṣaṇametanna dūṣaṇam /
carvaṇāniṣpacyā tasya niṣpattirupacariteti kāryo 'pyucyatām /

children.translated_text: It is the object of extraordinary self-cognition — distinct from the knowledge of ordinary perception and other detached means of knowledge, free from contact with any other object such as that known by the limited consciousness of a yogin, and confined to oneself alone, distinct from the limited cognition of other yogins — thus it may also be called a cognition.
And its apprehension is not indeterminate (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>), because it is predominantly characterized by the consideration of <s>vibhāvas</s> and so forth.
Nor is it determinate (<s>savikalpaka</s>), because the extraordinary blissful [<s>rasa</s>] being savored is established through self-cognition.

children.text: ubhayābhāvasvarūpasya co bhayātmakatvamapi pūrvavallokottaratāmeva gamayati na tu virodhamiti śrīmadācāryābhinavaguptapādāḥ //
children.translated_text: And the fact that its nature partakes of both [indeterminate and determinate] — being of the nature of the absence of both — likewise indicates only its extraordinary character, not any contradiction. Thus [say] the feet of the glorious master <s>Abhinavagupta</s>.

— thus, through the power of poetic contemplation and through the actor's own manifestation of his body perfected by training and practice, <s>rasa</s> is the enduring emotion such as <s>rati</s> and so forth — inferred through the relationship of suggested and suggestor from the conjunction of causes, effects, and auxiliary factors — even though artificial, not being regarded as such — designated by the terms <s>vibhāva</s> and so forth — inferred yet distinct from other inferences by virtue of the power of the beauty of the subject matter — regarded as enduring — and relished by the spectators through their latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) even though not directly their own. Thus says <s>Śrī Śaṅkuka</s>.
<s>Bhaṭṭa Nāyaka</s> [holds]: <s>Rasa</s> is neither cognized with detachment nor as belonging to oneself; it is neither produced nor merely manifested. Rather, in poetry and drama, through the operation of <s>bhāvakatva</s> (the power to evoke emotion) — a second function beyond denotation, whose nature is the universalization (<s>sādhāraṇīkaraṇa</s>) of <s>vibhāvas</s> and so forth — the <s>sthāyin</s> (enduring emotion) thus evoked is enjoyed through <s>bhoga</s> (direct experience), which has the nature of repose in a state of consciousness that is full of heightened manifestation and bliss.
The glorious master <s>Abhinavagupta</s> [holds]: In the world, the enduring emotions are [known] through ordinary cognition and other means of knowledge; for those proficient through practice, in poetry and drama, through the very same [emotions] — but freed from the condition of being causes and so forth, and designated by the extraordinary terms <s>vibhāva</s> and so forth through the operation of universalization — cognized universally, without the determination to accept or reject a specific relationship such as "these belong to me alone," "these belong to the enemy alone," "these belong to the onlooker alone," "these do not belong to me," "these do not belong to the enemy," "these do not belong to the onlooker" — thus manifested, the enduring emotion such as <s>rati</s>, existing in the form of latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) in the spectators, though established in a specific cognizer, by the power of universalization, at that moment transcending the limited state of the individual cognizer, experienced by the awakened cognizer in an unlimited mode free from contact with any other object of knowledge — as if identical with one's own form, though not truly undifferentiated — having relish as its very life-breath, having <s>vibhāvas</s> and so forth as its vital limit — being savored like the <s>pānakarasa</s> (the flavor of a blended drink) — as if shining forth as before, as if entering the heart, as if embracing all the limbs, as if concealing everything else, as if making one experience the bliss of <s>Brahman</s> — causing extraordinary wonder — this is <s>rasa</s> such as <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic) and so forth.
And it is not an effect [to be produced],
for if <s>vibhāvas</s> and so forth were destroyed, [<s>rasa</s>] would absurdly still arise.
Nor is it something to be merely made known, since it does not exist as already established.
Rather, it is to be manifested and relished through <s>vibhāvas</s> and so forth.
If one asks, "Where else is something seen that is neither a product nor something to be made known?" — the answer is: "That it has never been seen elsewhere is the ornament of its extraordinary nature, not a defect."
Since its arising is through relishing, it may also be figuratively called an effect.

children.text: vyāghrādayo vibhāvā bhayānakasyeva vīrādbhutaraudrāṇām aśrupātādayo 'nubhāvāḥ śṛṅgārasyeva karuṇabhayānakayoḥ, cintādayo vyabhicāriṇaḥ śṛṅgārasyeva vīrakaruṇabhayānakānāmiti pṛthaganaikāntikatvāt sūtre militā nirdiṣṭāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Vibhāvas</s> (determinants) such as tigers and so forth belong to <s>bhayānaka</s> (the terrible) as well as to <s>vīra</s> (the heroic), <s>adbhuta</s> (the marvelous), and <s>raudra</s> (the furious); <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents) such as shedding of tears belong to <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic) as well as to <s>karuṇa</s> (the pathetic) and <s>bhayānaka</s> (the terrible); <s>vyabhicārins</s> (transitory emotions) such as anxiety belong to <s>śṛṅgāra</s> as well as to <s>vīra</s>, <s>karuṇa</s>, and <s>bhayānaka</s> — since individually they are not invariably [connected to one rasa], they are stated collectively in the <s>sūtra</s>.
The sky [is filled] with clouds bearing dark-streaked waters, the beauty of the directions resounds with the humming of bees and the cooing of <s>kokila</s> birds,
the earth is marked with fresh sprouts — O innocent one, be gracious to your beloved who bows before you! //27//

children.text: ityādau parimṛditamṛṇālīmlānamaṅgaṃ pravṛttiḥ kathamapi parivāraprārthanābhiḥ kriyāsu /

<s>Nirveda</s> (despondency) is also a <s>sthāyibhāva</s> (permanent emotional state); there is also a ninth <s>rasa</s> — <s>śānta</s> (tranquil).
