children.text: kiṃ vakṣyantyapakalmaṣāḥ kṛtadhiyaḥ svapne 'pi sā durlabhā cetaḥ svāsthayamupaihi kaḥ khalu yuvā dhanyo 'dharaṃ dhāsyati // 53 //
children.translated_text: What will the purified, wise ones say? Even in a dream she is unattainable — O heart, attain composure! What fortunate youth will indeed place his lips upon hers?' (53)

Here there is an intermixture (<s>śabalatā</s>) of <s>vitarka</s> (deliberation), <s>autsukyam</s> (eagerness), <s>ati-smaraṇa</s> (excessive recollection), <s>śaṅkā</s> (apprehension), <s>dainya</s> (wretchedness), <s>dhṛti</s> (contentment), and <s>cintā</s> (anxiety).
The stable state of <s>bhāva</s> has been stated and illustrated.
(sūtra 51)
Even in the principal <s>rasa</s>, these sometimes attain the status of a subordinate element (<s>aṅga</s>).
Those [are] the quiescence and other states of <s>bhāva</s>.
The status of being a subordinate element is like that of a servant engaged in the wedding procession of a king.
(sūtra 52)
That which has the state of suggestion (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) in the form of reverberation (<s>anuraṇana</s>), unperceived in its stages, (37)
Is called <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion) of three kinds, arising from the power of word, meaning, or both.

Threefold: that whose suggested meaning is in the form of reverberation based on word-power, that whose suggested meaning is in the form of reverberation based on meaning-power, and that whose suggested meaning is in the form of reverberation based on both powers.
Among these,
Where an <s>alaṃkāra</s> (figure of speech) or a mere fact (<s>vastu</s>) is manifested from the word and so forth — (38)
(sūtra 53)

children.text: pradhānatvena sa jñeyaḥ śabdaśaktyudbha vo dvidhā /
children.translated_text: That, arising from word-power with predominance, should be known as twofold.
'Mere fact' means plain content without a figure of speech.

children.text: ādyo yathā ullāsya kālakaravālamahāmbuvāhaṃ devena yena jaraṭhorjitagarjitena /
children.translated_text: The first type, as in: 'Having roused the great cloud dark as the locks of Death, by the god whose aged, overpowering thunder —

children.text: nirvāpitaḥ sakala eva raṇe ripūṇāṃ dhārājalaistrijagati jvalitaḥ pratāpaḥ // 54 //
children.translated_text: In battle, the blazing valor of all enemies in the three worlds was extinguished by streams of water.' (54)

children.text: atra vākyasyāsaṃbaddhārthābidhāyakatvaṃ mā prasāṅkṣīditi prākaraṇikāprākaraṇikayorupamānopameyabhāvaḥ kalpanīya ityatropamālaṃkāro vyaṅgyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, lest the sentence be deemed one conveying an incoherent meaning, the relation of comparison between the contextual and the non-contextual must be construed — thus the suggested meaning here is the figure of <s>upamā</s> (simile).
'Of surpassing splendor, O Lord, dispeller of the moon's distress, of charming grace,
Of conduct that honors the intellect, foremost in every proposition's side — you shine.' (55)
Here, the double meaning of each word being applicable to two subjects constitutes <s>virodhābhāsa</s> (semblance of contradiction).
'O joy-giver, Lord, by the excellences attained from those who are boundless yet assembled,
You are harmful to the wicked yet allied with the virtuous, famed for righteous glory.' (56)
Here also there is <s>virodhābhāsa</s> (semblance of contradiction).
'Without material cause, upon no wall at all, he paints
The wondrous universe — salutations to that <s>Śūlin</s> (<s>Śiva</s>, the trident-bearer), praiseworthy in his arts.' (57)
Here the figure is <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast/distinction).
Even the object of ornamentation (<s>alaṃkārya</s>) can become an ornament (<s>alaṃkāra</s>), by the maxim of 'a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> becoming a servant.'

children.text: vastumātraṃ yathā paṃthia ṇa ettha sattharamatthi maṇaṃ pattharatthale gāme /
children.translated_text: An example of mere fact (<s>vastu</s>): 'There is no traveler here; there is a resting house in the village at the end of the road;

children.text: uṇṇaapaoharaṃ pekhkhiūṇa jai vasasi tā vasasu // 58 //
children.translated_text: Having seen one who removes weariness and distress — if you wish to stay, then stay.' (58)
Here it is suggested: 'If you are capable of enjoyment, then abide.'

children.text: śaniraśaniśva tamuccairnihanti kupyasi narendra yasmai tvam /
children.translated_text: 'Lightning and thunderbolt strike him high whom you, O king, are angered at;
And he upon whom you are pleased shines — both noble and ignoble.' (59)

children.text:
tra aviruddhāvapi tvadanuvartanārthamekaṃ kāryaṃ kuruta iti dhvanyate /
(sū- 54)
children.translated_text:
here, even though they are not opposed [to each other], it is suggested that 'for the purpose of following you, they perform a single action.'
(Sūtra 54)
That which is born from the power of meaning, yet is itself a meaning, is the suggestor (<s>vyañjaka</s>); it may be naturally occurring, //39//
or established merely by the poet's bold expression (<s>prauḍhokti</s>), or by the poet's creative fashioning;
it suggests either a thing (<s>vastu</s>) or a figure of speech (<s>alaṃkṛti</s>) — thus it has six varieties. //40//
A thing (<s>vastu</s>) or a figure of speech (<s>alaṃkāra</s>), and so this [<s>dhvani</s>] has twelve forms.

children.text:
svataḥsaṃbhavī na kevalaṃ bhaṇitimātraniṣpanno yāvabdahirapyaucityena saṃbhāvyamānaḥ /
kavinā pratibhāṇamātreṇa bahirasannapi nirmitaḥ kavinibaddhena vaktreti vā dvividho 'para iti trividhaḥ /
vastu vālaṃkāro vāsāviti ṣoḍhā vyañjakaḥ /
tasya vastu vālaṃkāro vā byaṅgya iti dvādaśabhaṅedor /
children.translated_text: Its suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) is either a thing (<s>vastu</s>) or a figure of speech (<s>alaṃkāra</s>) — thus there are twelve varieties.
This is <s>dhvani</s> born from the power of meaning (<s>arthaśaktyudbhava</s>).

children.text: krameṇodāharaṇam-- alasaśiropaṇi dhuttāṇaṃ aggimo putti dhaṇasamiddhimao /
children.translated_text: Examples in order — "On the lazy one's head, O daughter, the rogue's first [act] is from the prosperity of wealth;
when this was spoken, the young woman became wide-eyed." //60//

The naturally occurring [suggestor] is not merely one produced by the statement alone, but one that is plausibly conceived even externally through propriety (<s>aucitya</s>). The one created by the poet through mere imaginative power (<s>pratibhā</s>), though not existing externally, [is of two kinds:] fashioned by the poet or by the speaker — thus the latter is of two kinds, making three in total. The suggestor is sixfold: [each of these three] suggesting either a thing (<s>vastu</s>) or a figure of speech (<s>alaṃkāra</s>).

children.text: atra mamaivopabhogya iti vastunā vastu vyajyate /
children.translated_text: Here, through a thing (<s>vastu</s>), namely 'this is for my enjoyment alone,' another thing (<s>vastu</s>) is suggested.

children.text: dhanyāsi yā kathayasi priyasaṃgame 'ri visrabdhacāṭukaśatāni ratāntareṣu /
children.translated_text: "Fortunate are you who speak of intimate meetings with your beloved, O friend, hundreds of confident flatteries during the intervals of lovemaking;

children.text: nīvīṃ prati praṇihite tu kare priyeṇa sakhyaḥ śapāmi yadi kiṃcidapi smarāmi // 61 //
children.translated_text: but when my beloved placed his hand toward my garment-knot, O friends, I swear I remember nothing at all." //61//

children.text: atra tvamadhanyā, ahaṃ tu dhanyeti vyatirekālaṃkāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, [the suggested meaning is] 'you are unfortunate, but I am fortunate' — this is the figure <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast).
"Smeared with the thick blood flowing from striking the frontal globes of elephants blinded by the pride of rut,

children.text: vīrairvyaloki yudhi kopakaṣāyakāntiḥ kālīkaṭākṣa iva yasya kare kṛpāṇaḥ // 62 //
children.translated_text: the sword in whose hand was seen in battle, its luster reddened with the hue of wrath — like the sidelong glance of <s>Kālī</s>." //62//

children.text: atropamālaṃkāreṇa sakalaripubalakṣayaḥ kṣaṇāt kariṣyate, iti vastu /
children.translated_text: Here, through the figure of <s>upamā</s> (simile), [the suggested thing is:] 'the destruction of the entire enemy army will be accomplished in an instant' — this is the thing (<s>vastu</s>).
"He who [caused] the distress of the enemy's women from the pain of deep bite-marks left by their lovers,
releasing the ruby-like petals of their lips — he, in battle, furiously bit his own lower lip." //63//

children.text: atra virodhālaṃkāreṇādharanirdaśanasamakālameva śatravo vyāpāditā iti tulyayogitā mama kṣatyāpyanyasya kṣatirnivartatāmiti tadbuddhirutprekṣyate, ityutprekṣā ca /
children.translated_text: Here, through the figure of <s>virodha</s> (contradiction): simultaneously with the biting of his own lip, the enemies were slain — this is <s>tulyayogitā</s> (equal conjunction). 'Even though I am wounded, may the wounding of others cease' — such a thought is imagined, thus it is <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) as well.
In these [examples], the suggestor is naturally occurring.

children.text: kailāsasya prathamaśikhare veṇusaṃmūrchanābhiḥ śrutvā kīrtiṃ vibudharamaṇīgīyamānāṃ yadīyām /
children.translated_text: "On the first peak of <s>Kailāsa</s>, having heard through the melodies of the flute his fame being sung by the <s>Apsaras</s> (divine nymphs),
the elephants of the quarters, with drooping glances, suspecting it to be a succulent lotus stalk, curl their trunks at the sandy bank near their ears." //64//

children.text: atra vastunā yeṣāmapyarthādhigamo nāsti teṣāmapyevamādibuddhijananena camatkāraṃ karoti tvatkīrtiriti vastu dhvanyate /
children.translated_text: Here, through a thing (<s>vastu</s>), even for those who have no comprehension of its meaning, by generating such cognitions, your fame produces wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>) — thus a thing (<s>vastu</s>) is suggested.

children.text: kesesu balāmoḍia teṇa a samarammi jaasirī gahiā /
children.translated_text: "Having seized [the enemy] by the hair, by him in battle the glory of victory was grasped;

children.text: jaha kandarāhiṃ vihurā tassa daḍhaṃ kaṃṭhaammi saṃṭhaviā // 65 //
children.translated_text: as if disturbed by the caves, it was firmly placed upon his neck." //65//

children.text: atra keśagrahaṇāvalokanoddīpitamadanā iva kandarāstadvidhurān kaṇṭhe gṛhṇanti, ityutprekṣā /
ekatra saṃgrāme vijayadarśanāttasyārayaḥ palāyya guhāsu tiṣṭhantīti kāvyaheturalaṃkāraḥ /
children.translated_text: In a single battle, having seen his victory, his enemies fled and remain in caves — this is the figure <s>kāvyahetu</s> (poetic causation).

children.text: na parāyya gatāstadvairiṇo 'pi tu tataḥ parābhavaṃ saṃbhāvya tān kandarā na tyajantītyapahnutiśva /
children.translated_text: His enemies have not fled and gone away; rather, anticipating defeat from him, the caves do not release them — this is <s>apahṇuti</s> (concealment).
"When straightened in the secret of tight embrace, O beloved, she quickly approaches;
the pride of proud women, as if from fear of being crushed, [retreats] from their hearts." //66//
Here, as if the caves (<s>kandarā</s>), their passion aroused by witnessing the hair-grasping, seize those distressed ones by the neck — this is <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy).

children.text: atrotprekṣayā pratyāliṅganādi tatra vijṛmbhate, iti vastu /
children.translated_text: Here, through <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy), reciprocal embrace and such [responses] manifest there — this is a thing (<s>vastu</s>).
"She who, as if laughing at the old, having arranged herself in the abode of lotuses of detachment,

children.text: dāvei bhuaṇamaṃḍalamaṇṇaṃ via jaai sā vāṇī // 67 //
children.translated_text: displays the world-sphere as if it were another — that is <s>Vāṇī</s> (Speech/Sarasvatī)." //67//

children.text: atrotprekṣayā camatkāraikakāraṇaṃ navaṃ navaṃ jagat ajaḍāsanasthā nirmimīte, iti vyatirekaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, through <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy), the sole cause of wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>) [is that] she, seated on the seat of consciousness, creates an ever-new world — this is <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast).
In these [examples], the suggestor is one whose body is established merely by the poet's bold expression (<s>prauḍhokti</s>).

children.text: je laṃkāgirimehalāsu khaliā saṃbhogakhiṇṇoraī-- phārupphullaphaṇāvalīkavalaṇe pattā dariddattaṇam /
children.translated_text: "Those who, exhausted from lovemaking on the girdle-like ridges of <s>Laṅkā</s>'s mountain, had fallen into wretchedness in swallowing the expanded hoods of serpents —

children.text: te eṅṇiṃ malaānilā virahiṇīṇīsāsasaṃpakkiṇo jādā jhatti sisuttaṇe vi bahalā tāruṇṇapuṇṇā via // 68 //
children.translated_text: those <s>Malaya</s> winds, now infused with the sighs of women in separation, have suddenly become, even in winter, thick as if full of youthfulness." //68//

children.text: atra niḥśvāsaiḥ prāptaiśvaryā vāyavaḥ kiṃ kiṃ na kurvantīti vastunā vastu vyajyate /
children.translated_text: Here, through a thing (<s>vastu</s>), [the meaning is:] 'the winds that have attained power through the sighs [of separated women] — what will they not do?' — thus a thing (<s>vastu</s>) is suggested.

children.text: sahi viraiūṇa māṇassa majjha dhīrattaṇeṇa āsāsam /
children.translated_text: "O friend, through my firmness (<s>dhīratva</s>), give hope to the pride of my beloved in separation;
at the moment of faltering from the agitation of seeing my beloved, he suddenly withdrew." //69//

children.text: atra vastunākṛte 'pi prārthane prasanneti vibhāvanā priyadarśanasya saubhāgyabalaṃ dhairyeṇa soḍhuṃ na śakyate, ityutprekṣā vā /
children.translated_text: Here, through a thing (<s>vastu</s>), [she] is gracious even without being entreated — this is <s>vibhāvanā</s> (extraordinary causation). Or: the power of the beloved's beauty cannot be endured with firmness — this is <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy).
"With the tips of your trembling, agitated hands, you have given to my eyes

children.text: rattaṃsuaṃ paāo koveṇa puṇo ime ṇa akkamiā // 70 //
children.translated_text: a gift of red rays; out of anger, these [eyes] have not transgressed again." //70//

children.text: atra kimiti locane kupite vahasi, iti, uttarālaṃkāreṇa na kevalamārdranakhakṣatāni gopāyasi yāvatteṣāmahaṃ prasādapātraṃ jāteti vastu /
children.translated_text: Here, [the suggested meaning is:] 'why do you bear anger in your eyes?' Through the figure of <s>uttara</s> (reply): 'you are not merely concealing the fresh nail-scratch marks, but I have become a worthy vessel of their grace' — this is a thing (<s>vastu</s>).

children.text: mahilāsahassabharie tuha hiae suhaa sā amāantī /
children.translated_text: "In your heart, O fortunate one, filled with thousands of women, she who does not fit
daily performs unprecedented deeds, making even a slender body more slender." //71//

children.text: atra hetvalaṃkāreṇa "tanostanūkaraṇe 'pi tava hṛdaye na vartate'; iti viśeṣoktiḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, through the figure of <s>hetu</s> (causation): 'even in making the body thinner, [the rival] does not exist in your heart' — this is <s>viśeṣokti</s> (particular statement).
In these [examples], the suggestor has its body established merely through the bold expression of a speaker created by the poet.
Thus there are twelve varieties.
(Sūtra 55)
A word-meaning is one that is manifold in its fearful [suggestive power].
For example: "Adorned with the unwearied moon, having aroused <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love),

children.text: tārakātaralā śyāmā sānandaṃ na karoti kam // 72 //
children.translated_text: with trembling stars, the dark [night] — whom does it not delight?" //72//
Here <s>upamā</s> (simile) is the suggested meaning.
(Sūtra 56)
Its varieties are eighteen. //41//
'Its' means of <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion).

Now, since <s>rasa</s> and other [suggested meanings] have many varieties, how can there be [only] eighteen? To this he says:
(Sūtra 57)
Since <s>rasa</s> and the rest are infinite, [each] is counted as a single variety.

children.text:
anantatvāditi /
tathāhi-nava rasāḥ /
tatra śṛhgārasya dvau bhedau /
saṃbhogo vipralambhaśva /
saṃbhogasyāpi parasparāvalokanāliṅganaparicumbanādikusumoccayajalakelisūryāṃstamayacandrodayaṣaḍṛtuvarṇanādayo bahavo bhedāḥ /
vipralambhasyābhilāṣādaya uktāḥ /
tayorapi vibhāvānubhāvavyabhicārivaicitryam /

children.translated_text: Within that, there is further the classification of heroes and heroines as having superior, middling, and inferior natures.
Within that too, there are distinctions of place, time, condition, and so forth — thus even a single <s>rasa</s> is infinite.
What need is there to count the others?

children.text: asaṃlakṣyakramatvaṃ tu sāmānyamāśritya rasādidhvanibheda eka eva gaṇyate //
children.translated_text: But since the imperceptible gradation (<s>asaṃlakṣyakramatva</s>) is based on the general [category], the variety of <s>dhvani</s> comprising <s>rasa</s> and the rest is counted as one only.

'Since they are infinite' — namely: there are nine <s>rasas</s>. Of these, <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic sentiment) has two varieties: <s>saṃbhoga</s> (union) and <s>vipralambha</s> (separation). <s>Saṃbhoga</s> itself has many varieties such as mutual gazing, embracing, kissing, flower-gathering, water-sport, sunset, moonrise, descriptions of the six seasons, and so forth. <s>Vipralambha</s> has the subdivisions beginning with <s>abhilāṣa</s> (longing), as previously stated. Both of these further have diversity in <s>vibhāva</s> (determinants), <s>anubhāva</s> (consequents), and <s>vyabhicārin</s> (transitory emotions).
(Sūtra 58)
In a sentence, [<s>dhvani</s>] arises from both.
'From both' means rooted in the power of both word and meaning.
(Sūtra 59)
In a word also, [there are] others.
By the word 'also,' [it is implied that these occur] in a sentence too.

children.text: ekāvayavasthitena bhūṣaṇena kāminīva padadyotyena vyaṅgyena vākyavyaṅgyāpi bhāratī bhāsate /
children.translated_text: Like a beautiful woman adorned with an ornament placed on a single limb, <s>Bhāratī</s> (Speech) shines even with sentence-level suggestion through word-level suggestive meaning.

children.text: tatra padaprakāśyatve krameṇodāharaṇāni-- yasya mitrāṇi mitrāṇi śatravaḥ śatravastathā /
children.translated_text: Now, examples in order for word-level manifestation — "He whose friends are [truly] friends, whose enemies are [truly] enemies,

children.text: anukampyo 'nukampyaśva sa jātaḥ sa ca jīvati // 73 //
children.translated_text: who is [truly] an object of compassion — he alone is [truly] born, and he alone [truly] lives." //73//

(1) Here, the second occurrence of words like 'friends' and so on have their denotative meaning transferred to [connotations such as] trustworthiness, being worthy of restraint, being a vessel of affection, and so forth.

children.text: khalavavahārā dīsanti dāruṇā jahavi tahavi dhīrāṇam /
children.translated_text: "The ways of the wicked appear cruel; nevertheless, of the steadfast,
whose hearts are rich in the descent of inner feeling, their resolves do not waver." //74//
(2) Here, 'they are not deluded' [is the meaning].
"That gracefulness, that radiance, that beauty, that flow of speech —
then it was an abode of nectar, but now it is a great fever." //75//
Here, through words like 'that' and so on, meanings accessible only through direct experience are revealed.

children.text: yathā vā mugdhe mugdhatayaiva netumakhilaḥ kālaḥ kimārabhyate mānaṃ dhatsva dhṛtiṃ badhāna ṛjutāṃ dūre kuru preyasi /
children.translated_text: As also: "O innocent one, is the entire time to be spent merely in your innocence? Maintain your pride, hold firm your resolve, keep simplicity far away, O dear one.

children.text: sakhyaivaṃ śaṃsa hṛdi sthito hi nanu me prāṇeśvaraḥ śroṣyati // 76 //
children.translated_text: O friend, speak thus [to me softly], for my lord and master is indeed stationed in my heart — he will hear!" //76//
For by this, the propriety of speaking softly is understood.

children.text: bhāvādīnāṃ padaprakāśyatve 'dhikaṃ na vaicitryamiti na tadudāhriyate /
children.translated_text: Regarding the word-level manifestation of <s>bhāva</s> (emotions) and the rest, there is no further variety, so examples of those are not given.
"With arms like iron bars, terrifying and beautiful, [his] sword adorned with the streaming flow of blood,
with forehead marked by a sudden frown — O king, you shine like <s>Bhīma</s>." //77//
(3) Here, [she means] 'speak with a frightened face.'
(4) Here, the fearsome <s>Bhīmasena</s> is the standard of comparison (<s>upamāna</s>).
"Devoted to commanding solitary practice for worldly enjoyment and liberation,
whose arrival does not produce a flood of bliss?" //78//
(5) A certain woman conveys [a message] to the one who has given the signal for a rendezvous, through the primary meaning of the words.
"The evening bath has been performed, the body anointed with the great sacrifice, the sun-jewel has gone to the crest of the western mountain; come here confidently.

children.text: āśvaryaṃ tava saukumāryamabhitaḥ klāntāsi yenādhunā netradvandvamamīlanavyatikaraṃ śakroti te nāsitum // 79 //
children.translated_text: It is a wonder — your delicacy is such that you are now exhausted, and the pair of your eyes cannot manage to refrain from closing." //79//

children.text: (6) atra vastunā kṛtapuruṣaparicayā klāntāsīti vastu, adhunāpadadyotyaṃ vyajyate /
children.translated_text: (6) Here, through a thing (<s>vastu</s>), [the suggestion is that] she has had intimate acquaintance with a man, 'you are exhausted' is a thing (<s>vastu</s>); the word 'now' (<s>adhunā</s>) has word-level suggestive meaning.
"All sins dissolved by the great sorrow of not attaining Him,
and the accumulated merit exhausted by the vast joy of contemplating Him, //80//
contemplating the creator of the universe, who is of the nature of the supreme <s>Brahman</s>,
another <s>gopakanyakā</s> (cowherd maiden) attained <s>mukti</s> (liberation) by becoming breathless." //81//

(7) Here it is stated that the fruits of merit and demerit, which would [normally] have to be experienced over thousands of births, were experienced through the sorrow of separation and the joy of contemplation.
And thus, through the word-level suggestion of 'all' and 'accumulated' (<s>aśeṣacaya</s>), this is <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole).
"Night became not-night, the forest became not-forest, misfortune became not-misfortune;

children.text: bata vīra tava dviṣatāṃ parāhnukhe tvayi paraṅbhukhaṃ sarvam // 82 //
children.translated_text: Alas, O hero, for your enemies — when you turn away, everything turns away." //82//

(8) Here, through the figure of <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroboration) with the subsidiary element of <s>virodha</s> (contradiction) rooted in word-power, 'even fate follows you' — this is a thing (<s>vastu</s>) suggested by the word 'all' (<s>sarva</s>).

children.text: tuha vallahassa gosammi āsi aharo milāṇakamaladalo /
children.translated_text: "In the pasture of your beloved, the day was [like] a lotus petal that had wilted;

children.text: ia ṇavavahuā soūṇa kuṇai vaaṇaṃ mahisaṃmuham // 83 //
children.translated_text: hearing this, the new bride makes a face turned toward her co-wife." //83//

children.text: (9) atra rūpakeṇa tvayāsya muhurmuhuḥ paricumbanaṃ tathā kṛtam yena mlānatvamiti milāṇādipadadyotyaṃ kāvyaliṅgam /
children.translated_text: (9) Here, through the figure of <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor), [the suggestion is:] 'you have kissed him repeatedly so much that he became wilted' — the word-level suggestion from 'wilted' (<s>milāṇa</s>) and so on is <s>kāvyaliṅga</s> (poetic reason).
In these [examples], the suggestor is naturally occurring.
"On nights white as the moon, gracefully yawning, he who [produces] a canopy,
as if creating a single parasol — he manifests, the sovereignty of the world." //84//

children.text: (10) atra vastunā yeṣāṃ kāmināmasau rājā smarastebhyo na kaśvidapi tadādeśaparāṅbhukha iti jāgradbhirupabhogaparaireva tairniśātivāhyate, iti bhuaṇarajjapadadyotyaṃ vastu prakāśyate /
children.translated_text: (10) Here, through a thing (<s>vastu</s>): for those lovers whose king he is, there is no one who turns away from his command; thus by those who are awake and devoted to enjoyment, the night is passed — this is a thing (<s>vastu</s>) suggested by the word-level meaning of 'sovereignty of the world' (<s>bhuvanarājya</s>).
"<s>Anaṅga</s> (the bodiless god of love) places his army with arrow-sharp intent upon the glance of the beautiful woman, O friend,

children.text: diśi nipatati yatra sā ca tatra vyatikarametya samunmiṣantyavasthāḥ // 85 //
children.translated_text: and wherever her gaze falls, there mutual states arise and blossom." //85//

children.text: (11) atravastunā yugapadavasthāḥ parasparaviruddhā api prabhavantīti vyatikarapadadyotyo virodhaḥ /
children.translated_text: (11) Here, through a thing (<s>vastu</s>): even mutually contradictory states arise simultaneously — the word-level suggestion of 'encounter' (<s>vyatikara</s>) is <s>virodha</s> (contradiction).
"Even when restrained, again with a heart desirous of running forth,

children.text: thaṇaharavaassaeṇa visuddhajāī ṇa calai se hāro // 86 //
children.translated_text: because of [its] pure lineage, that necklace of hers does not move from the support of her breasts." //86//

children.text: (12) atra viśuddhajātitvalakṣaṇahetvalaṃkāreṇa hāro 'navarataṃ ampamāna evāste, iti ṇa calaipadadyotyaṃ vastu /
children.translated_text: (12) Here, through the figure of <s>hetu</s> (causation) characterized by pure birth: the necklace remains constantly moving [between her breasts] — the word-level suggestion of 'does not move' (<s>na calai</s>) is a thing (<s>vastu</s>).
"That soft and slightly darkened braid of hair, its body delightful with playful looseness,

children.text: tīe khaṃdhāhi balaṃ gahia saro suraasaṃgare jaai // 87 //
children.translated_text: having seized strength from her shoulders, goes forth like an arrow in the battle of love." //87//

children.text: (13) atra rūpakeṇa muddurmuhurākarṣaṇena tathā keśapāśaḥ skandhayoḥ prāptaḥ, yathā rativiratāvapyanivṛttābhilāṣaḥ kāmuko 'bhūditi khaṃdhapadadyotyā vibhāvanā /
children.translated_text: (13) Here, through <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor): the tress of hair, through repeated pulling, reached the shoulders — so that even after the cessation of lovemaking, the lover's desire remained unappeased — the word-level suggestion from 'shoulders' (<s>khaṃdha</s>) is <s>vibhāvanā</s> (extraordinary causation).
In these [examples], the suggestor has its body established merely through the poet's bold expression.

children.text: ṇavapuṇṇimāmiaṃkassa suhaa ko ttaṃ si bhaṇasu maha saccam /
children.translated_text: "O beloved, who are you, with the mark of the new full moon? Tell me the truth."

children.text: kā sohaggasamagga paosaraaṇi vva tuha ajja // 88 //
children.translated_text: What joyful union can compare to yours today? // 88 //

children.text: (14) atra vastunā mayīvānyasyāmapi prathamamanuktastvaṃ na tata iti ṇavetyādipaosetyādipadadyotyaṃ vastu vyajyate /
children.translated_text: (14) Here, by the substance—whether in me or in another woman, you who were first unspoken of are not so—the substance suggested by the words beginning with 'ṇave' ('new') and 'paose' ('affection') is revealed.
Dear friend, when the tight embrace of the arm-garland was upon the fresh, young, and unequal body,

children.text: hāro ṇivārio via uccheranto tado kahaṃ ramiam // 89 //
children.translated_text: The necklace, as if forced away, rose up—then how was the pleasure? // 89 //

children.text: (15) atra vastunā hāracchedānantaramanyadeva ratamavaśyamabhūt tatkathaya kīdṛgiti vyatirekaḥ kahaṃpadagamyaḥ /
children.translated_text: (15) Here, by the substance—immediately after the breaking of the necklace, something else (lovemaking) must certainly have occurred; tell me, what was it like—the <s>vyatireka</s> (distinction) is to be understood from the word 'katham' ('how').
As she entered the doorway of the house, with face turned away, looking at the path,

children.text: khaṃdhe ghettūṇa ghaḍaṃ hā hā ṇaṭhṭhotti ruasi sahi kiṃ ti // 90 //
children.translated_text: Carrying the pot on her shoulder—'Alas, alas, it slipped!'—friend, why do you weep? // 90 //

children.text: atra hetvalaṃkāreṇa saṃketaniketanaṃ gacchantaṃ dṛṣṭvā yadi tatra gantumicchasi tadā, aparaṃ ghaṭaṃ gṛhītvā gaccheti vastu kiṃtipadadyotyam /
children.translated_text: Here, through the figure <s>hetvalaṃkāra</s> (causation), having seen someone going to the rendezvous house, if you wish to go there, then—'take another pot and go'—the substance is suggested by the word 'kiṃ' ('why').

children.text: yathā vā vihalaṃkhalaṃ tumaṃ sahi daṭṭhūṇa kuḍheṇa taralataradiṭṭhim /
children.translated_text: Or, for example: Friend, seeing you moving about freely with agitated, restless glances,

children.text: vārapphaṃsamiseṇa a appā guruotti pāḍia vihiṇṇo // 91 //
children.translated_text: With the pretext of a doorway touch, self as elder—thus struck, he was shattered. // 91 //

children.text: (16) atra nadīkūle latāgahane kṛtasaṃketamaprāptaṃ gṛhapraveśāvasare pasvādāgataṃ dṛṣṭvā punarnadīgamanāya dvāropaghātavyājena buddhipūrvaṃ vyākulatayā tvayā ghaṭaḥ sphoṭita iti mayā cintitam tatkimiti nāśvasiṣi tatsamīhitasiddhaye vraja, ahaṃ te śvaśrūnikaṭe sarvaṃ samarthayiṣye, iti dvārasparśanavyājenetyapahnutyā vastu /
children.translated_text: (16) Here—having made a rendezvous at a vine-thicket on the riverbank, when he did not come and was seen arriving later at the time of entering the house, [she] deliberately, under the pretext of agitation for going again to the river, broke the pot at the doorstep—thus I understood; so why do you not breathe easy? Go for the fulfillment of that desire; I shall justify everything before your mother-in-law—thus, through <s>apahṇuti</s> (concealment) under the pretext of touching the door, the substance is revealed.
With the sweetness of youth, pale with weeping and anxious longing, she—

children.text: buḍḍhā vi ṇavoḍhavvia paravahuā ahaha harai tuha hiaam // 92 //
children.translated_text: Even though old, like a new bride, another man's wife—alas!—steals your heart. // 92 //

children.text:
(17) atra kāvyaliṅgena vṛddhāṃ paravadhūṃ tvamasmānujjhitvābhitaṣasīti tvadīyamācaritaṃ vaktuṃ na śakyamityākṣepaḥ paravahūpadaprakāśyaḥ /
eṣu kavinibaddhavaktṛprauḍhoktimātraniṣpannaśarīraḥ /
vākyaprakāśye tu pūrvamudāhṛtam śabdārthobhayaśaktyudbhavastu padaprakāśyo na bhavatīti pañcatriṃśadbhedāḥ /
(sū- 60)
children.translated_text:
(17) Here, through <s>kāvyaliṅga</s> (poetic reason), 'you desire another man's wife, abandoning us'—your conduct cannot be spoken of—thus the <s>ākṣepa</s> (reproach) is revealed by the word 'paravadhū' ('another's wife').
Among these, the body is produced solely through the skilled utterance of the poet-created speaker.
In sentence-level suggestion, what was previously illustrated—suggestion born from the power of word, meaning, or both—does not arise at the word level; thus there are thirty-five varieties.
(Sūtra 60)
In a <s>prabandha</s> (extended composition) too, [suggestion] arises from the power of meaning. //42//
As in the dialogue between the vulture and the jackal:
Enough of staying in this cremation ground, crowded with vultures and jackals,
Terrible with abundant skeletons, frightening to all living beings. // 93 //
And no one here who has lived has escaped the law of death;

children.text: priyo vā yadi vā dveṣyaḥ prāṇināṃ gatirīdṛśī // 94 //
children.translated_text: Whether dear or hateful—such is the destiny of living beings. // 94 //

children.text: iti divā prabhavato gṛdhrasya puruṣavisarjanaparamidaṃ vacanam /
children.translated_text: Thus, this is the speech of the vulture, who prevails by day, directed toward the dismissal of people.

children.text: ādityo 'yaṃ sthito mūḍhāḥ snehaṃ kuruta sāṃpratam /
children.translated_text: This sun is standing still, O fools—now show affection!
This moment is full of obstacles; perhaps one may even survive. // 95 //
This youth, golden-complexioned, who has not yet attained manhood—
On account of the vulture's words, O fools, abandon him without hesitation! // 96 //

children.text: iti niśi vijṛmbhamāṇasya gomāyorjanavyāvartananiṣṭhaṃ ca vacanamiti prabandha eva prathate /
children.translated_text: Thus, this is the speech of the jackal, who is active at night, aimed at turning people away—and so the suggestion operates precisely in the <s>prabandha</s> (extended narrative).

children.text: anye tvekādaśa bhedā grandhavistarabhayānnodāhṛtāḥ svayaṃ tu lakṣaṇato 'nusartavyāḥ /
children.translated_text: The other eleven varieties are not illustrated due to fear of excessive length of the treatise; they should be understood by oneself from the definitions.
By the word 'api' ('also'), [suggestion occurs] in words and sentences.
(Sūtra 61)
<s>Rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) and the rest [arise] even in word-parts, compositional arrangement, and individual syllables.
In that regard, by nature, as [in the verse]: Of him whose new young [body] is obstructed by sprout-like hands clinging in love-play,
Of him who is restrained—the new young [beauty], kissed by the mountain, arises. // 97 //

children.text: atha jayatīti na tu śobhate, ityādi /
children.translated_text: Now, 'jayati' means 'is victorious,' not merely 'is beautiful,' and so forth.

children.text: samāne 'pi hi sthaganavyāpāre lokottareṇaiva vyāpāreṇāsya pidhānamiti tadevotkṛṣṭam /
children.translated_text: For even though the act of concealing is the same, its covering is accomplished by a transcendent act—therefore that alone is superior.

children.text: yathā vā preyān so 'yamapākṛtaḥ saśapathaṃ pādānataḥ kāntayā dvitrāṇyeva padāni vāsabhavanādyāvanna yātyunmanāḥ /
children.translated_text: Or, for example: That dear one was rejected; with an oath he fell at the feet of his beloved; scarcely had he gone two or three steps from the dwelling, his mind uplifted,

children.text: tāvatpratyuta pāṇisaṃpuṭagalannīvīnibandhaṃ dhṛto dhāvitveva kṛtapraṇāmakamaho premṇo vicitrā gatiḥ // 98 //
children.translated_text: When she, running after him, held the knot of her waistband slipping from her cupped hands, and bowed to him—ah, wondrous is the course of love! // 98 //
Here, 'padāni' means 'steps,' not 'doors.'

children.text: tiṅsuporyathā pathi pathi śukacañcūcārupābhāṅkurāṇāṃ diśi diśi pavamāno vīrudhāṃ lāsakaśva /
children.translated_text: Regarding verbal and nominal endings, as [in the verse]: On every path, sprouts beautiful as parrot-beak hues; in every direction, the wind is a dancer of creepers;

children.text: nari nari kirati drāk sāyakān puṣpadhanbā puri puri vinivṛttā māninīmānacarcā // 99 //
children.translated_text: On every woman, the flower-bow quickly scatters arrows; in every city, the pride-quarrel of haughty women has ceased. // 99 //

children.text: atra kiratīti kiraṇasya sādhyamānatvam nivṛtteti nivartanasya siddhatvaṃ tiṅā supā ca tatrāpi ktapratyayenātītatvaṃ dyotyate /
children.translated_text: Here, 'kirati' ('scatters') indicates the action as being accomplished, and 'nivṛttā' ('ceased') indicates the completion of cessation—through verbal endings and nominal endings, and there too through the <s>kta</s>-suffix, the past tense is suggested.

children.text: yathā vā likhannāste bhūmiṃ bahiravanataḥ prāṇadayitaḥ nirāhārāḥ sakhyaḥ satataruditocchūnanayanāḥ /
children.translated_text: Or, for example: Your beloved, head bowed, sits scratching the ground outside; your friends, without food, their eyes swollen from constant weeping;

children.text: parityaktaṃ sarvaṃ hasitapaṭhitaṃ pañjaraśukaiḥ tavāvasthā ceyaṃ visṛja kaṭhine mānamadhunā // 100 //
children.translated_text: All laughter and recitation has been abandoned by the cage-parrots—and such is your condition; O hard-hearted one, now abandon your pride! // 100 //

children.text: atra likhanniti na tu likhatīti tathā, āste, iti na tu, āsita iti, api tu prasādaparyantamāste, iti, bhūmimiti na tu bhūmāviti na hi buddhipūrvakamaparaṃ kiṃcillikhatīti tiṅsubvibhaktīnāṃ vyaṅgyam /
children.translated_text: Here, 'likhann' ('scratching') and not 'likhati' ('he scratches'); likewise 'āste' ('sits') and not 'āsita' ('was seated'), but rather 'he sits until reconciliation'; 'bhūmim' ('the ground,' accusative) and not 'bhūmāu' ('on the ground,' locative)—for he does not deliberately draw something else—thus the suggestive meaning of verbal and nominal case endings is [demonstrated].

children.text: saṃbandhasya yathā gāmāruhammi gāme vasāmi ṇaaraṭhṭhiiṃ ṇa jāṇāmi /
children.translated_text: Regarding syntactic relation, as [in the verse]: I go to the village, I dwell in the village, I do not know city ways;

children.text: ṇāariāṇaṃ paiṇo haremi jā homi sā homi // 101 //
children.translated_text: I carry the husbands of the village women—whatever I am, that I am. // 101 //
'The <s>Kṣatriya</s> prince was handsome'—this is [an example] of tense.

children.text: eṣā hi bhagnamaheśvarakārmukaṃ dāśarathiṃ prati kupitasya bhārgavasyoktiḥ /
children.translated_text: For this is the speech of <s>Bhārgava</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>), who was angry toward the son of <s>Daśaratha</s> (<s>Rāma</s>) who had broken the bow of <s>Maheśvara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>).

children.text: vacanasya yathā tāṇaṃ guṇaggahaṇāṇaṃ tāṇukkaṃṭhāṇaṃ tassa pemmassa /
children.translated_text: Regarding utterance, as [in the verse]: Of those appreciations of virtues, of those longings, of that love—
Of those words, O beautiful one, such has been the final outcome. // 102 //
Here, 'nāgarikāṇām' ('of the city-dwellers') employs the genitive case.
Here, the plurality of the appreciation of virtues and so forth, and the singularity of love, are suggested.

children.text: puruṣavyatyayasya yathā re re cañcalalocanāñcitaruce cetaḥ pramucya sthira- premāṇaṃ mahimānameṇanayamānālokya kiṃ nṛtyasi /
children.translated_text: Regarding interchange of person, as [in the verse]: O you of flickering-eyed, curved splendor—O heart, abandoning firm love, beholding the greatness that leads astray, why do you dance?

children.text: kiṃ manye vihariṣyase bata hatāṃ muñcāntarāśāmimām eṣā kaṇṭhataṭe kṛtā khalu śilā saṃsāravārāṃnidhau // 103 //
children.translated_text: What do I think—you will sport? Alas! Abandon this inner hope for the slain—for this stone has indeed been placed at the throat-bank in the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence). // 103 //
Here, this is a <s>prahāsa</s> (farce/jest).

children.text: pūrvanipātasya yathā yeṣāṃ dorbalameva durbalatayā te saṃmatāstairapi prāyaḥ kevalanītirītiśaraṇaiḥ kāryaṃ kimurvīśvaraiḥ /
children.translated_text: Regarding precedence [of words], as [in the verse]: Those whose arm-strength alone is considered weakness by the weak, and by those who mostly take refuge in mere policy and conduct—what can such kings accomplish?

children.text: ye kṣyāśakra punaḥ parākramanayasvīkārakāntakramā- ste syurnaiva bhavādṛśāstrijagati dvitrāḥ pavitrāḥ param // 104 //
children.translated_text: O destroyer of <s>Kṣya</s> and <s>Śakra</s>, those who adopt the graceful course of valor and statecraft—there would not be in the three worlds more than two or three such pure ones as you. // 104 //
Here, the preeminence of valor is understood.

children.text: vibhaktiviśeṣasya yathā pradhanādhvani dhīradhanurdhvanibhṛti vidhuraraiyodhi tava divasam /
children.translated_text: Regarding a particular case ending, as [in the verse]: On the road of battle, O steadfast bearer of the bow's sound, in the turbulent combat, [it took] you a day;
But in a single day, O lord of men, you became, without battle, the object of praise ordained by fate. // 105 //
Here, 'divasena' ('in a day,' instrumental of completion) suggests the attainment of the result.

children.text: bhūyo bhūyaḥ savidhanagarīrathyayā paryaṭantaṃ dṛṣṭvā dṛṣṭvā bhavanavalabhītuṅgavātāyanasthā /
children.translated_text: [He], wandering again and again along the streets of the nearby city, being seen repeatedly by those stationed at the lofty windows of mansion parapets,
As if <s>Kāma</s> (the god of love) himself were new—<s>Mālatī</s> toward <s>Mādhava</s>—<s>Rati</s> (love), with deeply longing, trembling, quivering limbs, faints. // 106 //
Here, [this illustrates the suggestive power] of the <s>taddhita</s> (secondary derivative) suffix denoting compassionate nature.

children.text: paricchedātītaḥ sakalavacanānāmaviṣayaḥ punarjanmanyasminnanubhavapathaṃ yo na gatavān /
children.translated_text: Beyond measure, beyond the scope of all words, one who in this next birth has not entered the path of experience—

children.text: nivekapradhvaṃsādupacitamahāmohagahano vikāraḥ ko 'pyantarjaḍayati ca tāpaṃ ca kurute // 107 //
children.translated_text: From the destruction of discernment, dense with accumulated great delusion, some indescribable inner transformation both stupefies and causes anguish. // 107 //
Here, [this illustrates the suggestive power] of the prefix 'pra' and the <s>visarga</s> (final aspiration).

children.text: kṛtaṃ ca garvābhimukhaṃ manastvayā kimanyadevaṃ nihatāśva no dviṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: And your mind has been made to face pride—what else? Our enemies whose horses are slain;

children.text: tamāṃsi tiṣṭhanti hi tāvadaṃśumān na yāvadāyātyudayādrimaulitām // 108 //
children.translated_text: For darkness remains only so long as the sun has not reached the crest of the eastern mountain. // 108 //
Here, [this illustrates the suggestive power] of the particle 'ca' ('and'), which suggests <s>tulyayogitā</s> (equal conjunction).

children.text: rāmo 'sau bhuvaneṣu vikramaguṇaiḥ prāptaḥ prasiddhiṃ parā- masmadbhāgyaviparyayādyadi paraṃ devo na jānāti tam /
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> is he who has attained supreme fame in all the worlds through his qualities of valor—if, due to the reversal of our fortune, the Lord does not know him,

children.text: bandīvaiṣa yaśāṃsi gāyati sarudyasyaikabāṇāhati- śreṇībhūtaviśālatālavivarodgīrṇaiḥ svaraiḥ saptabhiḥ // 109 //
children.translated_text: This bard sings his glories, with tears, through the seven notes issuing from the hollows of the broad palm trees struck in a row by his single arrow. // 109 //

children.text: atrāsāviti bhuvaneṣviti guṇairiti sarvanāmaprātipadikavacanānāṃ na tvaditi na maditi, api, asmadityasya sarvākṣepiṇaḥ, bhāgyaviparyayādityanyathāsaṃpattimukhena na tvabhāvamukhenābhidhānasya /
children.translated_text: Here, 'asau' ('that one'), 'bhuvaneṣu' ('in the worlds'), 'guṇaiḥ' ('by qualities')—of pronouns, nominal stems, and number—not 'tvad' ('you') nor 'mad' ('I'), but 'asmad' ('we') which encompasses all; 'bhāgyaviparyayāt' ('from reversal of fortune')—expression through the mode of otherwise-occurrence, not through the mode of absence.
When youthfulness displays its art—of the bow of <s>Madana</s> (Cupid), namely the eyebrows—she recites first;
She dwells upon the crest of all beautiful women, this one with eyes darting like a startled deer. // 110 //

children.text:
atra, imanijavyayībhāvakarmabhūtādhārāṇāṃ svarūpasya taruṇatve, iti dhanuṣaḥ samīpe, iti maulau basatīti tvādibhistulye, eṣāṃ vācakatve, asti kaśvit svarūpasya viśeṣī yaśvamatkārakārī sa eva vyañjakatvaṃ prāpnoti /
evamanyeṣāmapi boddhavyam /
varṇaracanānāṃ vyañjakatvaṃ guṇasvarūpanirūpaṇe udāhariṣyate /
apiśabdāt prabandheṣu vājakādiṣu /
evaṃ rasādīnāṃ pūrvagaṇitabhedābhyāṃ saha ṣaḍbhedāḥ /
(sū- 62)
children.translated_text:
Here, of the <s>avyayībhāva</s> (indeclinable compound), <s>karma</s> (object), and <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (locus) [expressed by] 'ima-,' 'ni-,' 'ja-,'—the intrinsic nature being youthfulness, 'iti' meaning 'of the bow,' 'samīpe' meaning 'near,' 'iti' meaning 'on the crest,' 'vasati' meaning 'dwells'—though equivalent with 'tvādi' and the rest, when there is a particular form of the intrinsic nature that produces a special effect, that very form attains suggestive power.
The same should be understood for others as well.
The suggestive power of phonetic arrangement will be illustrated in the discussion of the nature of <s>guṇa</s> (poetic quality).
By the word 'api' ('also'), [this applies] in extended compositions such as the <s>Vājakādi</s> and others.
Thus, together with the previously enumerated varieties, there are six types of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) and the rest.
(Sūtra 62)
The varieties are thus fifty-one,
as explained.
(Sūtra 63)
And in the mutual combination of those: //43//
Through <s>saṃkara</s> (intermixture), which is of three forms, and through <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (fusion), which is of one form—

children.text:
na kevalaṃ śuddhā evaikapañcāśadbhedā bhavanti yāvatteṣāṃ svaprabhedairekapañcāśatā saṃśayāspadatvenānugrāhyānugrāhakatayaikavyañjakānupraveśena ceti trividhena saṃkareṇa parasparanirapekṣarūpayaikaprakārayā saṃsṛṣṭyā ceti caturbhirguṇane /
(sū- 64)
children.translated_text:
Not only are there fifty-one pure varieties, but their multiplication by four—through their own sub-varieties [combined] with the fifty-one, through being objects of doubt, through the relationship of supporter and supported, through the entry of a single suggestive element—thus threefold <s>saṃkara</s> (intermixture), and through <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (fusion), which has a single form independent of mutual relation.
(Sūtra 64)
Veda-sky-ocean-space-moon [= numerically encoded]:
(10,404) together with the pure varieties; (Sūtra 65)
Arrow-seasons-era-sky-moon [= numerically encoded] (10,455). //44//
Of these, only a sketch is illustrated:

children.text: khaṇapāhuṇiā deara jāāe suhaa kiṃpi de bhaṇiā /
children.translated_text: O dear brother-in-law, [you are but] a momentary guest; the beloved has said something to you;
In the house with a balcony facing the courtyard, reconcile her with gentle coaxing, O excellent one. // 111 //

children.text: atrānunayaḥ kimupabhogalakṣaṇe 'rthāntare saṃkramitaḥ kimanuraṇananyāyenopabhege, eva vyaṅgaye vyañjakaḥ, iti saṃdehaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, [there is] doubt: has the entreaty shifted to another meaning characterized by enjoyment, or does the suggestive element suggest through the principle of passionate attachment to enjoyment itself?

children.text: snigdhaśyāmalakāntiliptaviyato velladbalākā ghanāḥ vātāḥ śīkariṇaḥ payodasuhṛdāmānandakekāḥ kalāḥ /
children.translated_text: The clouds, their beauty smeared with glossy dark luster across the sky, with moving cranes, the winds sprinkle fine rain, the peacock-cries of the clouds' friends are melodious;

children.text: kāmaṃ santu dṛḍhaṃ kaṭhorahṛdayo rāmo 'smi sarvaṃ sahe vaidehī tu kathaṃ bhaviṣyati ha hā hā devi dhīrā bhava // 112 //
children.translated_text: Let them be as they may—I am firm, hard-hearted <s>Rāma</s>, I endure everything; but how will <s>Vaidehī</s> (<s>Sītā</s>) fare? Alas, alas! O queen, be steadfast! // 112 //

children.text: atra lipteti payodasuhṛdāmiti ca, atyantatiraskṛtavācyayoḥ saṃsṛṣṭiḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, 'liptā' ('smeared') and 'payodasuhṛdām' ('of the clouds' friends')—of these two, where the expressed meaning is completely concealed, there is <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (fusion).

children.text: tābhyāṃ saha rāmo 'smītyarthāntarasaṃkramitavācyasyānugrāhyānugrāhakabhāvena rāmapadalakṣaṇaikavyañjakānupraveśena cārthāntarasaṃkramitavācyarasadhvanyoḥ saṃkaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Together with those two, 'Rāmo 'smi' ('I am <s>Rāma</s>')—of the expressed meaning transferred to another sense—through the relationship of supporter and supported, and through the entry of the single suggestive element characterized by the word '<s>Rāma</s>'—there is <s>saṃkara</s> (intermixture) of the <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion) of transferred expressed meaning and <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment).
Other examples may also be cited.

children.text: iti kāvyaprakāśe dhvaninirṇayo nāma caturtha ullāsaḥ //4 // //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth <s>ullāsa</s> (chapter) named 'Determination of <s>Dhvani</s>' in the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>. //4//
// Now begins the fifth <s>ullāsa</s> (chapter). //

Having thus determined <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion), [the author] states the varieties of <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (subordinated suggestion).
(Sūtra 66)
<s>Agūḍham</s> (unconcealed), subordinate to another, established through the expressed meaning, unclear in suggestion,
Of doubtful equal prominence, implied by tone, and unattractive—//45//
The suggested meaning thus—the eight varieties of <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (subordinated suggestion) are recognized.

children.text: kāminīkucakalaśavat gūḍhaṃ camatkaroti, agūḍhaṃ tu sphuṭatayā vācyāyamānamiti guṇībhūtameva /
children.translated_text: Like the pitcher-shaped breasts of a beautiful woman, what is concealed produces wonder; but what is <s>agūḍha</s> (unconcealed), being manifest, is subordinated to the expressed meaning and thus becomes subordinated suggestion.

children.text: agūḍhaṃ yathā yasyāsuhṛtkṛtatiraskṛtiretya tapta- sūcīvyadhavyatikareṇa yunakti karṇau /
children.translated_text: <s>Agūḍha</s> (unconcealed suggestion) is illustrated as follows: He whose ears are pierced by the contempt inflicted by enemies, as if by the penetration of heated needles, returning—

children.text: kāñcīguṇagrathanabājanameṣa so 'smi jīvanna saṃprati bhavāmi kimāvahāmi // 113 //
children.translated_text: I am he who [once] fastened the string of the girdle—now, still alive, what do I bring? // 113 //
Here, of the expressed meaning that has been transferred to another meaning while still living (i.e., <s>jīvannityarthāntarasaṃkramitavācya</s>):
Their bodies tinged with the pollen of blooming lotuses, the bees sing sweetly in the garden pools;
And the orb of the sun, resembling the petals of fresh <s>bandhujīva</s> flowers, shines forth kissing the eastern mountain. (114)
Here, of the expressed meaning that is completely concealed by the act of kissing (<s>cumbanasya atyanta-tiraskṛta-vācya</s>):

children.text: atrāsīt phaṇipāśabandhanavidhiḥ śaktyā bhavaddevare gāḍhaṃ vakṣasi tīḍite hanumatā droṇādriratrāhṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here the serpent-noose binding was employed by your brother-in-law <s>Śakti</s>; here, when <s>Hanumān</s> was tightly pressed on the chest, <s>Droṇa</s> mountain was brought at night;

children.text: divyairindrajidatra lakṣmaṇaśarairlokāntaraṃ prāpitaḥ kenāpyatra mṛgākṣi rākṣasapateḥ kṛttā ca kaṇṭhāṭavī // 115 //
children.translated_text: Here <s>Indrajit</s> was sent to the other world by the divine arrows of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>; and here, O deer-eyed one, the forest of the neck of the lord of <s>Rākṣasas</s> was severed by someone. (115)
The reading 'his also here' (<s>tasyāpi atra</s>) is the correct one.

children.text: aparasya rasādervācyasya vā (vākyārthībhūtasya) aṅgaṃ rasādi, anuraṇanarūpaṃ vā /
children.translated_text: Of the other — the expressed meaning being <s>rasa</s> etc. (or what has become the sentence-meaning) — <s>rasa</s> etc. serves as a subordinate element, or it takes the form of suggestion (<s>anuraṇanarūpa</s>).
For example: This hand, which excels in the pleasure of touch, which presses the full breasts,
which touches the navel, thighs, and hips, and which loosens the girdle. (116)
(1) Here, the word 'by someone here' (<s>kenāpi atra</s>) represents suggestion rooted in the power of meaning (<s>arthaśaktimūlānuraṇanarūpa</s>).
Here, <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic sentiment) serves as a subordinate to <s>karuṇa</s> (the pathetic sentiment).

children.text: kailāsālayabhālalocanarucā nirvartitālaktaka- vyaktiḥ pādanakhadyutirgiribhuvaḥ sā vaḥ sadā trāyatām /
children.translated_text: May the radiance of the toenails of the daughter of the mountain, which produces the appearance of lac-dye through the lustre of the forehead-eye of the dweller of <s>Kailāsa</s>, always protect you;

children.text: spardhābandhasamṛddhayeva sudṛḍhaṃ rūḍhā yayā netrayoḥ kāntiḥ kokanadānukārasarasā sadyaḥ samutsāryate // 117 //
children.translated_text: by which the lustre of the eyes, as if enriched by the bond of rivalry, firmly established, fresh like lotuses, is immediately driven out. (117)
Here, the <s>bhāva</s> (transitory emotion) serves as a subordinate to <s>rasa</s> (the dominant sentiment).

children.text: atyuccāḥ paritaḥ sphuranti girayaḥ sphārāstathāmbhodhaya- stānetānapi bibhratī kimapi na klāntāsi tubhyaṃ namaḥ /
children.translated_text: Very lofty mountains tower on all sides, and likewise vast oceans — yet bearing all these, you are not in the least exhausted; salutations to you!

children.text: āśvaryeṇa muhurmuhuḥ stutimiti prastaumi yāvadbhuva- stāvadbibhradimāṃ smṛtastava bhujo vācastato mudritāḥ // 118 //
children.translated_text: With wonder, again and again, I begin to praise you thus — and as long as you bear this earth, the remembered arm of yours seals those words. (118)

children.text: atra bhūviṣayo ratyākhyo bhāvo rājaviṣayasya ratibhāvasya /
children.translated_text: Here, the <s>bhāva</s> (emotion) called <s>rati</s> (love) directed toward the earth serves as a subordinate to the <s>rati-bhāva</s> (emotion of love) directed toward the king.

children.text: bandīkṛtya nṛpa dviṣāṃ mṛgadṛśastāḥ paśyatāṃ preyasāṃ śliṣyanti praṇamanti lānti paritaścumbanti tesainikāḥ /
children.translated_text: O king, having captured the deer-eyed women of the enemies — while their lovers look on — those soldiers embrace, bow down, languish, and kiss them on all sides;

children.text: asmākaṃ sukṛtairdṛśornipatito 'syaucityavārāṃnidhe vidhvastā vipado 'khilāstaditi taiḥ pratyarthibhiḥ stūyase // 119 //
children.translated_text: By our good fortune your gaze has fallen upon us, O ocean of propriety — all calamities have been destroyed — thus you are praised by those very adversaries. (119)
Here, the <s>bhāva</s> serves as the subordinate: <s>rasābhāsa</s> (semblance of sentiment) and <s>bhāvābhāsa</s> (semblance of emotion) are suggested in the first half and second half respectively.
By the incessant trembling of the clusters of locks, by the frowning, threatening, and roaring again and again,

children.text: dadṛśe tava vairiṇāṃ madaḥ sa gataḥ kvāpi tavekṣaṇe kṣaṇāt // 120 //
children.translated_text: the pride of your enemies was seen — but it vanished somewhere in an instant at your glance. (120)
Here, the <s>bhāva</s> serves as <s>bhāvapraśama</s> (the subsidence of emotion).

children.text: sākaṃ kuraṅgakadṛśā madhupānalīlāṃ kartuṃ suhṛdbhirapi vairiṇi te pravṛtte anyābhidhāyi tava nāma vibho gṛhītaṃ kenāpi tatra viṣamāmakarodavasthām // 121 //
children.translated_text: When your enemy set out to engage in the sport of drinking wine (<s>madhupāna</s>) together with the doe-eyed one and with friends, someone uttered your name, O lord, and that created a terrible situation there. (121)
Here, there is the arising of <s>trāsa</s> (terror).

children.text: asoḍhā tatkālollasadasahabhāvasya tapasaḥ kathānāṃ viśrambeṣvatha ca rasikaḥ śailaduhituḥ /
children.translated_text: Unable to bear the <s>tapas</s> (penance) whose concurrent emotion was flashing at that moment, and then during the intimate narrations of the daughter of the mountain (<s>Śailaduhitu</s>),

children.text: pramodaṃ vo diśyāt kapaṭabaṭuveṣāpanayane tvarāśaithilyābhyāṃ yugapadabhiyuktaḥ smaraharaḥ // 122 //
children.translated_text: may <s>Smarahara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>, the destroyer of <s>Kāma</s>), who was simultaneously seized by haste and hesitation at the removal of the disguise of the false dwarf-student, grant you joy! (122)
Here, there is the conjunction (<s>saṃdhi</s>) of <s>āvega</s> (agitation) and <s>dhairya</s> (composure).

children.text: paśyetkaśviccala capala re kā tvarāhaṃ kumārī hastālambaṃ vitara ha ha hā vyutkramaḥ kvāsi yāsi /
children.translated_text: "Look at this — how unsteady! O fickle one, what is this haste? I am an unmarried girl! Give me a hand to hold! Ha ha ha, what transgression! Where are you going?"

children.text: itthaṃ pṛthvīparivṛḍha bhavadviṣo 'raṇyavṛtteḥ kanyā kaṃcit phalakisalayānyādadānābhidhatte // 123 //
children.translated_text: Thus, O lord of the earth, the daughter of your forest-dwelling enemy speaks to someone while gathering fruit and leaf-shoots. (123)

children.text: yadyapi bhāvodayabhāvasaṃdhibāvaśabalatvāni nālaṃkāratayā, uktāni tathāpi kaśvit brūyādityevamuktam /
children.translated_text: Although the arising of <s>bhāva</s>, the conjunction of <s>bhāvas</s>, and the variegation of <s>bhāvas</s> have not been stated as figures of speech, nonetheless, someone might say so — thus it has been stated.

children.text: yadyapi sa nāsti kaśvidviṣayaḥ, yatra dhvaniguṇībhūtavyaṅgyayoḥ svaprabhedādibhiḥ saha saṃkaraḥ saṃsṛṣṭirvā nāsti tathāpi pradhānyena vyapadeśā bhavantīti kvacitkenacidvacavahāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Although there is no subject matter in which there is not mixture or blending (<s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s>) with <s>dhvani</s> and <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> along with their own subdivisions, nevertheless, designation is based on predominance — thus somewhere there is usage by someone.

children.text: janasthāne bhrāntaṃ kanakamṛgatṛṣṇāndhitadhiyā vaco vaidehīti pratipadamudaśru pralapitam /
children.translated_text: Wandering in <s>Janasthāna</s> with mind deluded by the mirage of a golden deer, the word '<s>Vaidehī</s>' was tearfully uttered at every step;

children.text: kṛtālaṃkābharturvadanaparipāṭīṣu ghaṭanā mayāptaṃ rāmatvaṃ kuśalavasutā na tvadhigatā // 124 //
children.translated_text: Effort was made in arranging the features of the face of the husband who was adorned — I obtained the state of being <s>Rāma</s>, but the state of being the father of <s>Kuśa</s> and <s>Lava</s> was not attained. (124)

Here, there is a mixture (<s>śabalatā</s>) of <s>śaṅkā</s> (apprehension), <s>asūyā</s> (jealousy), <s>dhṛti</s> (fortitude), <s>smṛti</s> (recollection), <s>śrama</s> (fatigue), <s>dainya</s> (dejection), <s>vibodha</s> (awakening), and <s>autsukya</s> (eagerness). These are the figures of speech beginning with <s>rasavat</s> and others.

children.text: atra śabdaśaktimūlānuraṇanarūpo rāmeṇa sahopamānopameyabhāvo vācyāṅgatāṃ nītaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the relation of <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison) and <s>upameya</s> (object of comparison) with <s>Rāma</s>, which is suggestion rooted in the power of words (<s>śabdaśaktimūlānuraṇanarūpa</s>), has been subordinated to the expressed meaning.
Having come now to the lotus-pond whose body is distorted by separation, having spent the night somewhere,

children.text: etāṃ prasādayati pasya śanaiḥ prabhāte tanvaṅgi pādapatanena sahasraraśmiḥ // 125 //
children.translated_text: see how the thousand-rayed one (<s>Sahasraraśmi</s>, the sun) slowly appeases her at dawn by falling at her feet, O slender-limbed one! (125)

(2) Here, the story of the hero, rooted in the power of meaning (<s>arthaśaktimūla</s>), in the form of a real thing (<s>vasturūpa</s>), stands through the superimposition of the independent story of the sun and the lotus alone.

children.text: vācyasiddhyaṅgaṃ yathā bhramimaratimalasahṛdayatāṃ pralayaṃ mūrchāṃ tamaḥ śarīrasādam /
children.translated_text: The expressed meaning as a subordinate to the suggested: For example — delusion, the filth of passion, heartlessness, dissolution, swooning, darkness, bodily exhaustion,

children.text: maraṇaṃ ca jaladabhujagajaṃ prasahya kurute viṣaṃ viyoginīnām // 126 //
children.translated_text: and death — poison, like a cloud-serpent, forcibly inflicts all these upon women in separation. (126)

children.text: atra hālāhalaṃ vyaṅgyaṃ bhujagarūpasya vācyasya siddhikṛt /
children.translated_text: Here, <s>hālāhala</s> (deadly poison) is the suggested meaning, which brings about the establishment of the expressed meaning in the form of a serpent.

children.text: yathā vā gacchāmyacyuta darśanena bhavataḥ kiṃ tṛptirutpadyate kiṃ tvevaṃ vijanasthayorhatajanaḥ saṃbhāvayatyanyathā /
children.translated_text: For example: "I am going, <s>Acyuta</s>! Is there satisfaction from seeing you? But in this way, when we two are alone, a person who knows will imagine otherwise."

May <s>Hari</s>, whose body bristles with horripilation, protect you, as he embraces the <s>Gopī</s> who was languid with distress at the futile lingering indicated by the manner of that address! (127)
(3) Here, the suggestion through the words <s>Acyuta</s> etc. serves as a subordinate to the expressed meaning beginning with 'the manner of address' etc.
This distinction is that in one case it belongs to a single speaker, and in the other it belongs to different speakers.

children.text: asphuṭaṃ yathā adṛṣṭe darsanotkaṇṭhā dṛṣṭe vicchedabhīrutā /
children.translated_text: An unclear example: When you are unseen, there is longing for your sight; when seen, there is fear of separation;

children.text: nādṛṣṭena na dṛṣṭena bhavatā labhyate sukham // 128 //
children.translated_text: Neither when unseen nor when seen is happiness obtained from you. (128)

children.text: (4) atrādṛṣṭo yatā na bhavasi viyogabhayaṃ ca yathā notpadyate tathā kuryā iti kliṣṭam /
children.translated_text: (4) Here, the meaning is forced (<s>kliṣṭa</s>): 'Be unseen in such a way that there is no longing, and be seen in such a way that the fear of separation does not arise — do so.'
An example of doubtful predominance: <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), whose composure was somewhat disturbed, like the ocean at the onset of the rising of the moon,
directed his eyes upon the face of <s>Umā</s>, whose lower lip resembled a <s>bimba</s> fruit. (129)

children.text: (5) atra paricumbitumaicchaditi kiṃ pratīyamānam kiṃ vā vilocanavyāpāraṇaṃ vācyaṃ pradhānamiti saṃdehaḥ /
children.translated_text: (5) Here, there is doubt whether the suggested meaning is 'he desired to kiss,' or whether the expressed meaning — the directing of the eyes — is predominant.
An example of equal predominance: The abandonment of transgression against <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> is indeed for your welfare;
<s>Jāmadagnya</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>) is likewise a friend; otherwise, he becomes ill-disposed. (130)

children.text: (6) atra jāmadagnyaḥ sarveṣāṃ kṣatriyāṇāmiva rakṣasāṃ kṣaṇāt kṣayaṃ kariṣyatīni vyaṅgyasya vācyasya ca samaṃ prādhānyam /
children.translated_text: (6) Here, the suggested meaning — that <s>Jāmadagnya</s> will destroy all <s>Kṣatriyas</s> in an instant, just as he would <s>Rākṣasas</s> — and the expressed meaning have equal predominance.

children.text: kākvākṣiptaṃ yathā mathnāmi kauravaśataṃ samare na kopāta duḥśāsanasya rudhiraṃ na pibāmyurastaḥ //
children.translated_text: An example of meaning indicated by tone (<s>kākū</s>): "I will not churn the hundred <s>Kauravas</s> in battle! I will not drink the blood of <s>Duḥśāsana</s> from his chest!

children.text: saṃcūrṇayāmi gadayā na suyodhanorū saṃdhiṃ karotu bhavatāṃ nṛpatiḥ paṇena // 131 //
children.translated_text: I will not crush the thighs of <s>Suyodhana</s> with a mace! Let the king make peace with them through a wager!" (131)
(7) Here, the suggested meaning — 'I will indeed churn them' etc. — stands together with the negation of the expressed meaning.
An example of the inelegant (<s>asundara</s>): Hearing the commotion of the flock of <s>vāṇīra</s> birds flying up,
she who is occupied with household work — her limbs languish greatly. (132)

children.text: (8) atra dattasaṃketaḥ kaśvillatāgahanaṃ praviṣṭa iti vyaṅgyāt sīdantyahgānīti vācyaṃ sacamatkāram //
children.translated_text: (8) Here, from the suggested meaning — that someone who was given a rendezvous has entered a thicket of creepers — the expressed meaning 'her limbs languish' becomes charged with wonder (<s>sacamatkāra</s>).
(Sūtra 67)
The subdivisions of these are to be understood as appropriate, as before. (46)

children.text:
yathāyogamiti "vyajyante vastumātreṇa yadālaṃkṛtayastadā /
dhruvaṃ dhvanyaṅgatā tāsāṃ kāvyavṛttestadāśrayāt" iti dhvanikāroktadiśā vastumātreṇa yatrālaṃkāro vyajyate na tatra guṇībhūtavyaṅgyatvam /
(sū- 68)
children.translated_text: The phrase 'as appropriate' means: following the direction stated by the author of the <s>Dhvani</s> — 'When figures of speech are suggested by mere subject matter, then their subordination to <s>dhvani</s> is certain, because the poetic mode depends on that' — where a figure is suggested by mere subject matter alone, there is no <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (subordinated suggestion). (Sūtra 68)
The combination of <s>dhvani</s> with those very figures, and with them through blending (<s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s>) and mixture (<s>saṃkara</s>).
The phrase 'with figures' means: with those very figures of speech, and with those that are endowed with figures.

children.text: taduktaṃ dhvanikṛtā "sa guṇībhūtavyaṅgayaiḥ sālaṃkāraiḥ saha prabhedaiḥ svaiḥ /
children.translated_text: This has been stated by the author of the <s>Dhvani</s>: "With <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> and with figures of speech, together with its own subdivisions,
<s>dhvani</s> is further illuminated in many ways through mixture (<s>saṃkara</s>) and blending (<s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s>)."
Thus. (Sūtra 69)
Through mutual combination in this manner, the number of subdivisions becomes exceedingly great. (47)

children.text:
evam anena prakāreṇa, avāntarabhedagaṇane 'tiprabhūtatarā gaṇanā /
tathāhi--śṛṅgārasyaiva bhedaprabhedasaṇanāyāmānantyam /
kā gaṇanā tu sarvaiṣām /
saṃkalanena punarasya dhvanestrayo bhedāḥ /
vyahgyasya trirūpatvāt /
tathāhi--kiṃcidvācyatāṃ sahate kiṃcicvanyathā /
tatra vācyatāsahamavicitraṃ vicitraṃ ceti /
avicitraṃ vastumātram vicitraṃ tvalaṃkārarupam /
yadyapi prādānyena tadalaṃkāryam tathāpi brāhnaṇaśramaṇanyāyena tathocyate /
rasādilakṣaṇastvarthaḥ svapne 'pi na vācyaḥ /
sa hi rasādiśabdena śṛṅgārādiśabdena vābhidhīyeta /
na cābhidhīyate /
tatprayoge 'pi vibāvādyāprayoge tasyāpratipattestadaprayoge 'pi vibhāvādiprayoge tasya pratipatteśvetyanvayavyatirekābhyāṃ vibhāvādyabhidhānadvāreṇaiva pratīyate, iti niśvīyate tenāsau vyahgya eva /
mukhyārthabādhādyabhāvānna punarlakṣaṇīyaḥ /
arthāntarasaṃkramitātyantatiraskṛtavācyayorvastumātrarūpaṃ vyaṅgyaṃ vinā lakṣaṇaiva na bhavatīti prāk pratipāditam /
śabdaśaktimūle tu, abhidhāyā niyantraṇenanānabhidheyasyārthāntarasya tena sahopamāderalaṃkārasya ca nirvivādaṃ vyaṅgyatvam /
children.translated_text: In the case rooted in the power of words (<s>śabdaśaktimūla</s>), because denotation is restricted to what is denotable, the suggestiveness of figures like <s>upamā</s> (simile) etc., which pertain to a different meaning together with that, is beyond dispute.

children.text: arthaśaktimūle 'pi veśeṣe saṃketaḥ kartuṃ na yujyate, iti sāmānyarūpāṇāṃ padārthānāmākāṅkṣāsaṃnidhiyogyatāvaśātparasparasaṃsargo yatrāpadārtho 'pi viśeṣarūpo vākyārthastatrābhihitānvayavāde kā vārtā vyaṅgyasyābhidheyatāyām /
children.translated_text: Even in the case rooted in the power of meaning (<s>arthaśaktimūla</s>), convention cannot be established for particulars; thus, where there is mutual association of word-meanings of a general nature through expectancy, proximity, and compatibility, and where the sentence-meaning in its particular form is not itself a word-meaning — in the <s>abhihitānvayavāda</s> (theory of expressed-then-connected meaning), what need is there to speak of the suggestedness of the suggested meaning?
Those who also say: "The elders of language perceive the denotable portion directly;
and the apprehension by the listener is through inference and gesture; (1)

Thus, in this manner, in counting the sub-varieties, the enumeration becomes extremely prolific. For even in counting the varieties and sub-varieties of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> alone, there is infinity. What then of counting all of them? In summary, this <s>dhvani</s> has three divisions, because the suggested meaning has three forms. Namely: some tolerate being expressed, some do not. Of those that tolerate expression, there are the non-striking and the striking. The non-striking is mere subject matter; the striking is in the form of a figure of speech. Although that is primarily the object of ornamentation, nevertheless, by the analogy of 'the Brāhmaṇa and the ascetic,' it is so called. But meaning characterized as <s>rasa</s> etc. is never to be expressed even in a dream. For it would be denoted by the word <s>rasa</s> etc. or by the word <s>śṛṅgāra</s> etc. But it is not so denoted. Even when those terms are used, without the employment of <s>vibhāva</s> etc., there is no apprehension of it; and even without those terms, when <s>vibhāva</s> etc. are employed, there is apprehension — thus by positive and negative concomitance, it is understood only through the denotation of <s>vibhāva</s> etc. Therefore it is established that this is indeed suggested (<s>vyaṅgya</s>). Because there is no absence of the primary meaning etc., it is not figurative (<s>lakṣaṇīya</s>). That the suggested meaning in the form of mere subject matter does not exist without <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification) in the cases of meaning-transferred and completely-concealed expressed sense — this has been established earlier.
but through otherwise-inexplicability, the cognitive power, which is of two kinds,
through <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) one should understand the threefold connection based on three means of valid knowledge. (2)"

children.text:
iti pratipāditadiśā "devadatta gāmānaya'; ityādyuttamavṛddhavākyaprayogāddeśāddeśāntaraṃ sāsnādimantamarthaṃ madhyamavṛddhe nayati sati'; anenāsmādvākyādevaṃvidho 'rthaḥ pratipannaḥ'; iti tacceṣṭayānumāya tayorakhaṇḍavākyavākyārthayorarthāpacyā vācyavācakabhāvalakṣaṇaṃ saṃbandhamavadhārya bālastatra vyutpadyate /
parataḥ "caitra gāmānaya devadatta, aśvamānaya devadatta gāṃ naya'; ityādivākyaprayoge tasya tasya śabdasya taṃ tamarthamavadhārayatīti, anvayavyatirekābhyāṃ pravṛttinivṛttikāri vākyameva prayogayogyamiti vākyasthitānāmeva padānāpanvitaiḥ padārtheranvitānāmeva saṃketo gṛhyate, iti viśiṣṭā eva padārthā vākyārthaḥ /
na tu padārthānāṃ vaiśiṣṭyam /
yadyapi vākyāntaraprayujyamānānyapi pratyabhijñāpratyayena tānyenaitāni padāni niśvīyante, iti padārthāntaramātreṇānvitaḥ padārthaḥ saṃketagocaraḥ, tathāpi sāmānyāvacchādito viśeṣarūpa evāsau pratipadyate vyatiṣaktānāṃ padārthānāṃ tathābhūtatvādityanvitābhidhānavādinaḥ /
teṣāmapi mate sāmānyaviśeṣarūpaḥ padārthaḥ saṃketaviṣaya ityativiśeṣabhūto vākyārthāntargato 'saṃketitatvādavācya eva yatra padārthaḥ pratipadyate tatra dūre, arthāntarabhūtasya niḥśeṣacyutetyādau vidhyādeśvarcā /
ananvito 'rtho 'bhihitānvaye padārthāntaramātreṇānvitastvanvitābhidhāne, anvitaviśeṣastvavācya eva ityubhayanaye 'pyapadārtha eva vākyārthaḥ /
yadapyucyate "naimittikānusāreṇa nimittāni kalpyante'; iti /
tatra nimittatvaṃ kārakatvaṃ jñāpakatvaṃ vā śabdasya prakāśakatvānna kārakatvam /
jñāpakatvaṃ tu-ajñātasya katham jñātatvaṃ ca saṃketenaiva sa cānvitamātre /
evaṃ ca nimittasya niyatanimittatvaṃ yāvanna niśvitam tāvannaimittikasya pratītireva katham iti "naimittikānusāreṇa nimittāni kalpyante'; ityavicāritābhidhānam /
ye tvabhidadhati "so 'yamiṣoriva dīrghadīrghataro vyāpāraḥ'; iti "yatparaḥ śabdaḥ sa śabdārthaḥ'; iti ca vidhirevātra vācya iti /
te 'pyatātparyajñāstātparyavācoyukterdevānāṃpriyāḥ /
tathāhi "bhūtabhavyasamuccāraṇe bhūtaṃ bhavyāyopadiśyate'; iti kārakapadārthāḥ kriyāpadārthenānvīyamānāḥ pradhānakriyānirvartakasvakriyābhisaṃbandhāt sādhyāyamānatāṃ prāpnuvanti /
children.translated_text: For instance, "in the utterance of past and future, the past is taught for the sake of the future" — the meanings of <s>kāraka</s>-words (case-words), when being connected with the meaning of the verb, attain the state of being accomplished through their connection with their own subsidiary actions that bring about the principal action.
And from that, by the maxim of "unburned fire" — whatever has not yet been achieved, that much is enjoined.

children.text: yathā-ṛtvikpracaraṇe pramāṇāntarāt siddhe "lohitoṣṇīṣā ṛtvijaḥ pracaranti" ityatra lohitoṣṇīṣatvamātraṃ vidheyam /
children.translated_text: For example — when the movement of <s>ṛtvij</s>s (priests) is already established through another means of knowledge, in "the priests move about wearing red turbans," only the quality of wearing red turbans is what is to be enjoined.

children.text: havanasyānyataḥ siddheḥ "dadhnā juhoti" ityādau dadhyādeḥ karaṇatvamātraṃ vidheyam //
children.translated_text: Since the act of offering is established from elsewhere, in "one offers with curds" and similar [injunctions], only the instrumentality of curds and the like is what is to be enjoined.

In the manner thus established, when upon the command "<s>Devadatta</s>, bring the cow," an elder or middle person brings from one place to another an object possessing a dewlap and so forth, [the child understands] "from this very sentence, such-and-such a meaning has been grasped"; inferring this from that person's action, and ascertaining through <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) the relation of signifier and signified — which is the relation between the undivided sentence and sentence-meaning — the child thereby learns language.
Subsequently, in the use of sentences like "<s>Caitra</s>, bring the cow; <s>Devadatta</s>, bring the horse; <s>Devadatta</s>, take the cow," [the child] ascertains each word's particular meaning through <s>anvaya</s> (co-occurrence) and <s>vyatireka</s> (non-occurrence) — that only a sentence, which causes engagement and cessation, is fit for usage; and that convention is grasped only for words as situated in sentences, connected with their connected meanings — thus, only the qualified word-meanings constitute the sentence-meaning,
not the qualification of word-meanings [as something separate].
Although words used in other sentences too are recognized through the cognition of recognition as "these are the same words," and thus a word-meaning connected with merely another word-meaning falls within the scope of convention, nevertheless this is apprehended only in the form of the particular as delimited by the universal, since word-meanings that are intertwined are of such nature — so say the <s>anvitābhidhāna</s>-vādins (proponents of related designation).
In their view too, the word-meaning that is the object of convention has the form of both universal and particular; therefore, where a word-meaning is apprehended as an extreme particular contained within the sentence-meaning that is not the object of convention and hence inexpressible — there it is far-removed; of what belongs to another meaning, as in "<s>niḥśeṣacyuti</s>" (complete fall) and similar cases, <s>arcanā</s> (worship) in injunctions and the like.
The meaning that is unconnected [with other words] in the <s>abhihitānvaya</s> view, and connected with merely another word-meaning in the <s>anvitābhidhāna</s> view, while the specific connection is itself inexpressible — in both systems, the sentence-meaning is indeed a non-word-meaning [i.e., something beyond individual word-meanings].
As for what is said: "On the basis of the effect, the causes are postulated" —
there, the nature of being a cause means being either an agent (<s>kāraka</s>) or an informer; since a word is an illuminator, it is not an agent.
As for being an informer — how can what is unknown become known? And that [becoming known] is only through convention, and that [convention] is only regarding the connected [meaning].
And thus, until the fixed causal nature of the cause is established, how can there even be cognition of the effect? — therefore, the statement "on the basis of the effect, the causes are postulated" is an unconsidered declaration.
Those who declare "this very long, ever-longer operation is like an arrow" and "the meaning of a word is that which the word is directed toward" — meaning that only the injunction is the expressible meaning —
they too, being ignorant of <s>tātparya</s> (purport), are "beloved of the gods" [i.e., fools] because of the propriety of <s>tātparya</s> being the expressible.

kvacidubhayavidhiḥ /
kvacittrividhirapi /
yathā-"raktaṃ paṭaṃ vayaḥ'; ityādau, ekavidhirdvividhistrividhirvā tataśva "yadeva vidheyaṃ tatraiva tātparyam'; ityupāttasyaiva śabdasyārthe tātparyaṃ na tu pratītamātre /
evaṃ hi "pūrvo dhāvati'; ityādāvaparādyarthe 'pi kvacittātparyaṃsyāt /
