yadi ca vācyavācakatvavyatirekeṇa vyaṅgyavyañjakabhāvo nābhyupeyate tadāsādhutvādīnāṃ nityadoṣatvaṃ saṣṭatvādīnāmanityadoṣatvamiti vibhāgakaraṇamanupapannaṃ syāt /
na cānupapannam sarvasyaiva vibhaktatayā pratibhāsāt /
vācyavācakabhāvavyatirekeṇa vyaṅgyavyañjakatāśrayaṇe tu vyaṅgyasya bahuvidhatvāt kvacideva kasyacidevaucityenopapadyata eva vibhāgavyavasthā /
"dvayaṃ gataṃ saṃprati śocanīyatāṃ samāgamaprārthanayā kapālinaḥ /
'; ityādau pinākyādipadavailakṣaṇyena kimiti kapālyādipadānāṃ kāvyānuguṇatvam /
api ca vācyo 'rthaḥ sarvāna pratipattṭṭan prati, ekarūpa eveti niyato 'sau /
na hi "gato 'stamarkaḥ'ityādau vācyo 'rthaḥ kvacidanyathā bhavati /

children.translated_text: But the suggested meaning, aided by the specific context, speaker, hearer, and other particulars, takes on multiplicity.

children.text: tathā ca "gato 'stamarkaḥ'; ityataḥ sapatnaṃ pratyavaskandanāvasara iti, abhisaraṇamupakramyatāmiti prāptaprāyaste preyāniti karmakaraṇānnivartāmahe, iti sāṃdhyo vidhirupakramyatāmiti dūraṃ mā gā iti surabhayo gṛhaṃ praveśyantāmiti saṃtāpo 'dunā na bhavatīti vikreyavastūni saṃhriyantāmiti nāgato 'dyāpi preyānityādiranavadhirvyaṅgye 'rthaḥ, tatra tatra pratibhāti /
children.translated_text: Thus, from "the sun has set," [various suggested meanings arise:] "the opportunity for attack against the enemy [has come]"; "let the secret rendezvous begin"; "your beloved has nearly arrived"; "let us cease from our labor"; "let the <s>saṃdhyā</s> (twilight) ritual be commenced"; "do not go far"; "let the cows be brought home"; "there is no more heat now"; "let the merchandise be gathered in"; "my beloved has still not come" — thus the suggested meaning, being unlimited, is perceived differently in each context.

children.text: vācyavyaṅgyayoḥ niḥśeṣetyādau niṣedhavidhyātmanā, "mātsaryamutsārya vicārya kāryamāryāḥ samaryādamudāharantu /
children.translated_text: Regarding the expressible and the suggested, in passages like "<s>niḥśeṣa</s>" (completely) and so forth, [they appear] in the form of prohibition and injunction; [and in verses such as:] "Setting aside envy, having deliberated upon the matter, let the noble ones declare with proper decorum —
Should one resort to the slopes — of mountains, or of smiling beauties with lovely hips? (verse 133)"

Sometimes there is a twofold injunction, sometimes even a threefold one — as in "weave a red cloth" and similar cases. Whether it is a single, twofold, or threefold injunction, from that [it follows that] "the purport lies only in what is to be enjoined" — the <s>tātparya</s> (purport) of a word pertains only to its meaning as employed, not merely to what is cognized.
For otherwise, in "the first one runs" and similar cases, the purport would sometimes apply to the meaning of the latter part as well.
As for the argument that in "eat poison, and do not eat at his house," the purport is "one should not eat at that house" — and that this alone is the sentence-meaning — we reply: there, the particle "ca" (and) serves to indicate syntactic unity; and since two predicate-sentences do not stand in the relation of principal and subordinate, the sentence about eating poison, being identified as a friendly remark, is taken as subordinate — meaning "eating at this house is worse even than eating poison, therefore by no means eat at his house" — thus the purport pertains only to the meaning of the words actually employed.
Moreover, if the word's operation extends to whatever meaning is obtained immediately upon hearing the word, then how is it that in "O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, a son has been born to you" or "O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, your daughter is pregnant," joy, grief, and the like are not also expressible? And why should <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification) be needed, when even for the meaning requiring <s>lakṣaṇā</s>, cognition is accomplished by the ever-longer operation of <s>abhidhā</s> (primary signification) itself?
Furthermore, the principle that among <s>śruti</s> (direct statement), <s>liṅga</s> (indicative sign), <s>vākya</s> (sentence), <s>prakaraṇa</s> (context), <s>sthāna</s> (position), and <s>samākhyā</s> (name), each preceding one is stronger — even in the <s>anvitābhidhāna</s> view, the suggestive nature (<s>vyaṅgyatva</s>) of injunction is equally established.
Moreover, in "make a liking" — when the words are inverted within a poetic composition, how would there be a fault?
For the meaning here is not vulgar when connected with other word-meanings — thus it is indeed inexpressible. Such and similar [arguments] would be irrefutable.
And if, apart from the relation of expressible and expressor, the relation of suggested and suggestor is not accepted, then the classification whereby some faults like impropriety are permanent while others like harshness are non-permanent would be untenable.
Yet it is not untenable, since everything appears as distinctly classified.
But when the relation of suggested and suggestor is accepted as distinct from the expressible-expressor relation, then because the suggested is of many kinds, the classification is properly established — as propriety applies only to certain [suggested meanings] in certain cases.
In [the verse] "Two things have now become pitiable through the entreaty for union by <s>Kapālin</s> (Śiva)" — why is it that words like "<s>Kapālin</s>" are suited to poetry while words like "<s>Pinākin</s>" [referring to the same deity] would be incongruous?
Furthermore, the expressible meaning is uniform for all cognizers — it is fixed and the same.
For in "the sun has set" and similar [expressions], the expressible meaning never differs.

children.text: ityādau saṃśayaśāntaśaṅgāryantaragataniśvayarūpeṇa, "kathamavanipa darpo yanniśātāsidhārā- dalanagalitamūdhnā vidviṣāṃ svīkṛtā śrīḥ /
children.translated_text: In such cases, [the suggested meaning operates] in the form of resolution contained within doubt, tranquility, and the <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic) <s>rasa</s>; [and in the verse:] "How is it, O king, that the glory obtained by the sharp sword-edge splitting the heads of enemies has been claimed as your own?

children.text: nanu tava nihatārerapyasau kiṃ na nītā tridivamapagatāṅgairvallabhā kīrtirebhiḥ // 134" //
children.translated_text: Surely, even though your enemies are slain, could not that glory — the beloved fame — have been sent to heaven by these [elephants] whose limbs are removed? (verse 134)"

children.text: ityādau nindāstutivapuṣā svarūpasya, pūrvapaśvādbhāvena pratīteḥ kālasya śabdāśrayatvena śabdatadekadeśatadarthavarṇasaṃghaṭanāśayatvena ca, āśrayasya śabdānuśāsanajñānena prakaraṇādisahāyapratibhānairmalyasahitena tena cāvagama iti nimittasya boddhṛmātravidagdhavyapadeśayoḥ pratītimātracamatkṛtyośva karaṇāt kāryasya gato 'stamarka ityādau pradarśitanayena saṃkhyāyāḥ, "kassa va ṇa hoi roso daṭṭhūṇa piāi savvaṇaṃ aharaṃ /
children.translated_text: In such cases, [the suggested meaning operates] in the form of censure-within-praise (<s>nindāstuti</s>) regarding the essential nature; through the sequence of prior and subsequent occurrence, [the suggested meaning operates] regarding time; through dependence on words, parts of words, word-meanings, and arrangements of phonemes, [it operates] regarding the basis; through knowledge of <s>śabdānuśāsana</s> (grammar), the purity of intuition aided by context and similar factors, [it operates] regarding the cause; through the fact that only those addressed as learned comprehend it, and through the production of <s>camatkṛti</s> (aesthetic rapture) in mere cognition, [it operates] regarding the effect; through the method demonstrated in "the sun has set" regarding number; [and in the Prakrit verse:] "For whom does anger not arise upon seeing the beloved's face every day?
The garlands on the bed, fragrant with bees, are fresh on this side — come quickly! (verse 135)"

children.text:
ityādau sakhītatkāntādigatatvena viṣayasya ca bhede 'pi yadyekatvam tat kvacidapi nīlapītādau bhedo na syāt /
uktaṃ hi "ayameva hi bhedo bhedaheturvā yadviruddhadharmādhyāsaḥ kāraṇabhedaśva" iti /
vācakānāmarthāpekṣā vyañjakānāṃ tu na tadapekṣatvamiti na vācakatvameva vyañjakatvam /
kiṃ ca vāṇīrakuḍaṃgvityādau pratīyamānamarthamabhivyajya vācyaṃ svarūpe, eva yatra viśrāmyati tatra guṇībhūtavyaṅgye 'tātparyabhūto 'pyarthaḥ svaśabdānabhidheyaḥ pratītipathamavataran kasya vyāpārasya viṣayatāmavalambatāmiti /
nanu "rāmo 'smi sarvaṃ sahe'; iti "rāmeṇa priyajīvitena tu kṛtaṃ premṇaḥ priye nocitam'; iti "rāmo 'sau bhuvaneṣu vikramaguṇaiḥ prāptaḥ prasiddhiṃ parām'; ityādau lakṣaṇīyo 'pyartho nānātvaṃ bhajate viśeṣavyapadeśahetuśva bhavati tadavagamaśva śabdārthāyattaḥ prakaraṇādisavyapekṣaśveti ko 'yaṃ nūtanaḥ pratīyamāno nāma /
ucyate--lakṣaṇīyasyārthasya nānātve 'pi, anekārthaśabdābhidheyavanniyatatvameva /

children.translated_text: Indeed, what does not have a fixed relation with the primary meaning cannot be indicated through <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification).

children.text: pratīyamānastu prakaraṇādiviśeṣavaśena niyatasaṃbandhaḥ, aniyatasaṃbandhaḥ saṃbaddhasaṃbandhasva dyotyate /
children.translated_text: But the suggested meaning, by virtue of particular contextual factors, has both fixed relation and unfixed relation, and the relation of what is connected is indicated (<s>dyotya</s>).

children.text: na ca "attā ettha ṇimañjai ettha ahaṃ diahae paloehi /
children.translated_text: [In the Prakrit verse:] "The sun sinks here — here I spend the day, behold!

children.text: mā pahia rattiandhaa sejjāe maha ṇimajjahisi // 136" //
children.translated_text: O traveler, do not, blinded by the night, sink into my bed! (verse 136)"

In such cases, even though [the suggested meaning] takes on unity through belonging to a friend, her lover, and so forth regarding the domain — if there were unity despite difference [of properties], then even in blue, yellow, and similar [colors] there would be no distinction. For it has been said: "This very distinction, or the cause of distinction, is the superimposition of contradictory properties and the difference of causes."
The expressors require reference to meaning, but the suggestors do not depend on that — therefore suggestive power is not the same as expressive power.
Moreover, in expressions like "<s>vāṇīrakuḍaṅga</s>" and similar cases, where the suggested meaning manifests and the expressible rests in its own nature — there, in cases of subordinated suggestion (<s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>), even a meaning that is not the purport, being undesignated by its own word yet entering the path of cognition — whose operation does it become the object of?
Now, [one might object:] in "I am <s>Rāma</s>, I endure all," in "By <s>Rāma</s> who holds life dear, duty toward love was done but not what was fitting, O beloved," and in "That <s>Rāma</s> has attained supreme fame in the worlds through the qualities of his valor" — even the meaning requiring <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification) takes on multiplicity, becomes the basis for specific characterization, and its apprehension depends on word-meaning while requiring context and such — so what is this novel thing called "suggested meaning"?
We reply: even though the meaning requiring <s>lakṣaṇā</s> has multiplicity, it is fixed, just like the meaning of a polysemous word.

children.text:
ityādau vivakṣitānyaparavācye dhvanau mukhyārthabādhaḥ /
tatkathamatra lakṣaṇā /
lakṣaṇāyāmapi vyañjanamavaśyamāśrayitavyamiti pratipāditam /
yathā ca samayasavyapekṣā, abhidhā tathā mukhyārthabādhāditrayasamayaviśeṣasavyapekṣā lakṣaṇā, ata evābhidhāpucchabhūtā setyāhuḥ /
na ca lakṣaṇātmakameva dhvananam tadanugamena tasya darśanāt /
na ca tadanugatameva, abhidhāvalambanenāpi tasya bhāvāt /

na cobhayānusāryeva, avācakavarṇānusāreṇāpi tasya dṛṣṭeḥ, na ca śabdānusāryeva, aśabdātmakanetratribhāgāvalokanādigatatvenāpi tasya prasiddheriti, abhidhātātparyalakṣaṇātmakavyāpāratrayātivartī dhvananādiparyāyo vyāpāro 'napahnavanīya eva /
children.translated_text: Nor does it follow only both [<s>abhidhā</s> and <s>lakṣaṇā</s>], since it is observed even following non-expressive phonemes; nor does it follow only words, since it is well known to occur through non-verbal means such as glances, one-third glances, and the like. Therefore, <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion), also called <s>vyañjanā</s>, is an operation that transcends the three operations of <s>abhidhā</s> (primary signification), <s>tātparya</s> (purport), and <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification) — and is undeniable.

children.text: tatra "attā, ettha" ityādau niyatasaṃbandhaḥ "kassa va ṇa hoi roso" ityādau, aniyatasaṃbandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: There, in "the sun [sinks] here" and similar cases, the relation [between word and suggested meaning] is fixed; in "for whom does anger not arise" and similar cases, the relation is unfixed.
[In the Prakrit verse:] "Seeing <s>Brahman</s> (the creator) standing in the lotus of <s>Nābhi</s> (Viṣṇu's navel), <s>Lakṣmī</s>, with reversed passion,
Playfully strikes the right cheek of <s>Hari</s> (Viṣṇu) — she who delights in <s>rasa</s> (passion/aesthetic sentiment)! (verse 137)"

In such cases, in <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion) where the intended meaning is different from the literal while the unintended is expressed, there is no cancellation of the primary meaning. So how can there be <s>lakṣaṇā</s> here? It has been established that even in cases of <s>lakṣaṇā</s>, <s>vyañjana</s> (suggestion) must necessarily be resorted to.
Just as <s>abhidhā</s> (primary signification) depends on convention, so <s>lakṣaṇā</s> depends on the specific convention-conditions of the triad: cancellation of primary meaning and so forth. Therefore they say it is merely an appendage of <s>abhidhā</s>.
Nor is suggestion merely of the nature of <s>lakṣaṇā</s>, since suggestion is observed to follow it [only sometimes].
Nor does it always follow [<s>lakṣaṇā</s>], since suggestion can occur based on <s>abhidhā</s> as well.

children.text:
ityādau saṃbaddhasaṃbandhaḥ /
atra hi haripadena dakṣiṇanayanasya sūryātmakatā vyajyate tannimīlanena sūryāstamayaḥ, tena pajhasya saṃkocaḥ, tato brahnaṇaḥ sthagaman tatra sati gopyāṅgasyādarśanena, aniryantraṇaṃ nidhuvanavilasitamiti /
"akhaṇḍabuddhinirgrāhyo vākyārtha eva vācyaḥ, vākyameva ca vācakam'; iti ye 'pyāhuḥ, tairapyavidyāpadapatitaiḥ padapadārthakalpanā kartavyaiveti tatpakṣe 'pyavaśyamuktodāharaṇādau vidhyādirvyaṅgya eva /
nanu vācyādasaṃbaddhaṃ tāvanna pratīyate yataḥ kutaśvit yasya kasyacidarthasya pratīteḥ prasaṅgāt /
children.translated_text: Now, what is unrelated to the expressed meaning is never cognized, because there would be the unwanted consequence of the cognition of any meaning whatsoever from any source whatsoever.

children.text: evaṃ ca saṃbandhāt vyaṅgyavyañjakabhāvo 'pratibandhe 'vaśyaṃ na bhavatīti vyāptatvena niyatadharminiṣṭhatvena ca trirūpāllihgālliṅgijñānamanumānaṃ yat tadrūpaḥ paryavasyati /
children.translated_text: And thus, due to this relation, the status of suggested and suggestor, when there is no obstruction, necessarily does not obtain — and so it culminates in the form of inference, which is knowledge of the inferred from a logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>) possessing the three characteristics: pervasion, residence in the established subject, and invariable concomitance.

children.text: tathāhi-- "bhama dhammia vīsaddho so suṇao ajja mārio teṇa /
children.translated_text: For example — "O virtuous one, that dog of ours was killed today, trust me,
by <s>Dariasiṃha</s>, a resident of the village of <s>Golāṇa</s>" (138).

and so on, this is a connected relation. For here, by the word <s>Hari</s>, the solar nature of the right eye is suggested; by its closing, the setting of the sun; by that, the closing of the lotus; from that, the concealment of <s>Brahman</s>; and in that state, due to the invisibility of the <s>gopī</s>'s body, the unrestrained erotic play is suggested. Even those who say "The sentence-meaning alone, graspable only by undivided cognition, is the expressed meaning, and the sentence alone is the expressor" — even they, having fallen into the position of ignorance, must necessarily construct word and word-meaning analysis; and so even in their view, in the cited examples, the injunction and so forth are necessarily suggested meanings.

children.text:
atra gṛhe śvanivṛtyā bhramaṇaṃ vihitaṃ godāvarītīre siṃhopalabdherabhramaṇamanumāpayati /
yat yat bhīrubhramaṇaṃ tattadbhayakāraṇanivṛcyupalabdhipūrvakaṃ godāvarītīre ca siṃhopalabdhiriti vyāpakaviruddhopalabdhiḥ /
atrocyate--bhīrurapi guroḥ prabhorvā nideśena priyānurāgeṇa, anyena caivaṃbhūtena hetunā satyapi bhayakāraṇe bhramatītyanaikāntiko hetuḥ śuno bibhyadapi vīratvena siṃhānna bibhetīti viruddho 'pi godāvarītīre siṃhasadbhāvaḥ pratyakṣādanumānādvā na niśvitaḥ, api tu vacanāt na cavacanasya prāmāṇyamasti, arthenāpratibandhādityasiddhaśva tatkathamevaṃvidhāddhetoḥ sādhyasiddhiḥ /
tathā niḥśeṣacyutetyādau gamakatayā yāni candanacyavanādīnyupāttāni tāni kāraṇāntarato 'pi bhavanti, ataśvātraiva snānakāryatvenoktānīti nopabhoge, eva pratibaddhānītyanaikāntikāni /
children.translated_text: Similarly, in the verse beginning with "completely fallen" and so on, the things like the falling of sandal paste that are taken up as indicators can also arise from other causes; and moreover, they are mentioned here only as effects of bathing — thus they are not necessarily connected to enjoyment, and are therefore inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>).
And by the proponent of <s>vyakti</s> (manifestation), the suggestive power of these has been stated only in conjunction with inferior words.
And here, the inferiority is not established by any valid means — so how can there be inference?

children.text: evaṃvidhādarthādevaṃvidho 'rtha upapacyanapekṣatve 'pi prakāśate, iti vyaktivādinaḥ punastat adūṣaṇam //
children.translated_text: From such a meaning, such another meaning manifests even without the need for corroboration — this is again the position of the proponent of <s>vyakti</s>, which is not a refutation of our view.

Here, the roaming of the dog near the house is observed, and the non-roaming is inferred from the perception of a lion on the bank of the <s>Godāvarī</s>. Whatever roaming of a timid person occurs, that is preceded by the perception of the cessation of the cause of fear — and on the bank of the <s>Godāvarī</s> there is the perception of a lion — thus this is the apprehension of something contradictory to the pervader. To this it is replied: even a timid person may roam despite the cause of fear being present, due to the command of a guru or master, due to attachment to a beloved, or due to some other such reason — thus the reason is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>). Though fearing the dog, one may not fear the lion due to heroism — thus it is also contradictory. The existence of the lion on the bank of the <s>Godāvarī</s> is not established by perception or inference, but only by verbal testimony, and verbal testimony has no validity here since it is not unobstructed by the actual facts — thus it is also unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>). How then can the establishment of what is to be proved come from such a reason?

Thus ends the fifth <s>ullāsa</s> (chapter) of the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>, named the determination of the varieties of <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion), <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (subordinated suggestion), and <s>saṃkīrṇa</s> (mixed types). //5//
// Now begins the sixth <s>ullāsa</s> //
(<s>sūtra</s> 70)
The two kinds of poetry that were previously illustrated as ornamented in word and sense —
In them, the presence of word-ornament and sense-ornament is according to the predominance of one quality or the other. //48//

children.text: na tu śabdacitre 'rthasyācitratvam arthacitre vā śabdasya /
children.translated_text: But it is not that in word-ornament the sense is unornamented, nor in sense-ornament is the word unornamented.
And thus it has been said: "Figures of speech such as <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) and others constitute ornament, as has been stated by others in many ways;
Even a beautiful woman's face does not shine without adornment.
Others call <s>rūpaka</s> and similar figures external ornament;

children.text: supāṃ tiṅāṃ ca vyutpattiṃ vācāṃ vāñchantyalaṃkṛtim //
children.translated_text: They desire the etymological derivation of nominal and verbal suffixes as the ornamentation of speech.
This they call excellence of expression — etymological derivation is not of this kind;
But the twofold division into ornament of word and ornament of sense has been taught by us."
Thus.

children.text: śabdacitraṃ yathā prathamamaruṇacchāyastāvattataḥ kanakaprabha- stadanu virahottāmyattanvīkapolataladyutiḥ /
children.translated_text: An example of word-ornament: First there is a reddish hue, then a golden radiance, and after that the complexion of the cheek of a slender woman languishing in separation;
Then rises in the face of night one capable of destroying darkness, having the splendor of a freshly cut lotus stalk, marked with a deer — the moon. (139)

children.text: arthacitraṃ yathā te dṛṣṭimātrapatitā api kasya nātra kṣobhāya pakṣmaladṛśāmalakāḥ khalāśva /
children.translated_text: An example of sense-ornament: Even when merely glanced upon, whose agitation do they not cause, those with eyelash-adorned eyes, and the wicked too —

children.text: nīyāḥ sadaiva savilāsamalīkalagnā ye kālatāṃ kuṭilatāmiva na tyajanti // 140 //
children.translated_text: Those who are always playfully attached to deception, who never abandon their dark and crooked nature, like black bees. (140)

children.text: yadyapi sarvatra kāvye 'ntataḥ, vibhāvādirūpatayaiva paryavasānam tathāpi sphuṭasya rasasyānupalambhādavyaṅgyametatkāvyadvayamuktam /
children.translated_text: Although in all poetry there is ultimately a resolution into the form of <s>vibhāva</s> (determinants) and the like, nevertheless, because a manifest <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) is not apprehended, these two kinds of poetry are called <s>avyaṅgya</s> (without suggestion).

children.text: atra ca śabdārthālaṃkārabhedādbahavo bhedāḥ, te cālaṃkāranirṇaye nirṇeṣyante //
children.translated_text: And here, due to the distinction between ornaments of word and sense, there are many varieties; these will be determined in the section on the ascertainment of ornaments.

children.text: iti kāvyaprakāśe śabdārthacitranirūpaṇaṃ nāma ṣaṣṭha ullāsaḥ //6 //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixth <s>ullāsa</s> of the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>, named the examination of word-ornament and sense-ornament. //6//
// Now begins the seventh <s>ullāsa</s> //
Having examined the nature of poetry, he states the general definition of defects (<s>sū</s>. 71):
A defect is the diminishment of the principal meaning and <s>rasa</s>; and since it depends on that, it is to be called expressible;
Those pertaining to word and so forth are serviceable to both; therefore the defect applies to them as well. //49//
"Diminishment" means degradation. "Word and so forth" — the word "and so forth" includes verse-composition. He states the specific definitions (<s>sū</s>. 72):
A defective word is one that is harsh to the ear, that deviates from grammatical usage, that is unused,
That is incapable, that has a suppressed meaning, that has an inappropriate meaning, that is meaningless, that is non-denotative, and that is indecent in three ways. //50//
That is ambiguous, unfamiliar, vulgar, requiring interpretation, or that is forced;
That has an unexamined predicate, that is contradictory, and that which is defective only when occurring in a compound. //51//

(1) "Harsh to the ear" — defective due to the form of harsh syllables, as in: With the waves of sidelong glances from the eyes that are the auspicious abode of <s>Anaṅga</s> (the bodiless god of love),

children.text: āliṅgitaḥ sa tanvaṅgyā kārtārthyaṃ labhate kadā // 141 //
children.translated_text: When will he, embraced by that slender-limbed woman, attain fulfillment? (141)
Here the word <s>kārtārthya</s> (fulfillment) is the example.

children.text: (2) "cyutasaṃskṛti'; vyākaraṇalakṣaṇahīnaṃ yathā etanmandavipakvatindukaphalaśyāmodarāpāṇḍara- prāntaṃ hanta pulindasundarakarasparśakṣamaṃ lakṣyate /
children.translated_text: (2) "Deviating from grammatical usage" — that which lacks the characteristics prescribed by grammar, as in: This is seen to be dark-bellied like an unripe <s>tinduka</s> fruit, slowly ripening, with whitish edges, and fit for the touch of the beautiful hand of a <s>Pulinda</s> maiden.

children.text: tat pallīpatiputri kuñjarakulaṃ kumbhābhayābhyarthanā- dīnaṃ tvāmanunāthate kucayugaṃ patrāvṛtaṃ mā kṛthāḥ // 142 //
children.translated_text: O daughter of a village chief, this elephant herd, distressed by the prayer for fearlessness from their frontal globes, beseeches you — do not cover your pair of breasts with leaves! (142)

children.text:
atrānunāthate, iti /
"sarpiṣo nāthate'; ityādāvivāśiṣyeva nāthaterātmanepadaṃ vihitam "āśiṣi nāthaḥ" iti /
atra tu yācanamarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: Therefore it should be read as "<s>anunāthati stanayugam</s>" (with the <s>parasmaipada</s> ending).
(3) "Unused" — that which, though recorded in grammar, is not employed by poets.
As in: As this cruel conduct is always being manifested,

children.text: tathā manye daivato 'sya piśāco rākṣaso 'tha vā // 143 //
children.translated_text: So I think, by fate, he is either a <s>piśāca</s> (demon) or a <s>rākṣasa</s> (ogre). (143)

Here the form <s>anunāthate</s> is the example. Just as in "<s>sarpiṣo nāthate</s>" and such cases, the <s>ātmanepada</s> (middle voice) of the verb <s>nāth</s> is prescribed only in the sense of blessing, by the rule "<s>āśiṣi nāthaḥ</s>." But here the intended meaning is entreaty.

children.text: atra daivataśabdo "daivatāni puṃsi vā'; iti puṃsyāmnāto 'pi na kenacitprayujyate /
children.translated_text: Here the word <s>daivata</s>, though recorded in the masculine gender by the rule "<s>daivatāni puṃsi vā</s>," is not used by anyone in that form.

children.text: (4) "asamarthaṃ'; yattadarthaṃ paṭhyate na ca tatrāsya śaktiḥ /
children.translated_text: (4) "Incapable" — that which is used for a particular meaning but does not have the capacity to express it.
As in: Having accumulated merit by bathing at various pilgrimage sites,
She now respectfully approaches the beautiful river. (144)
Here <s>hanti</s> (strikes) is intended in the sense of going.
(5) "Suppressed meaning" — that which has two meanings but is used in the less well-known sense.
As in: With hair reddened by the blows of feet wet with lac-juice, by her beloved,
The innocent woman, trembling with modesty, was suddenly kissed upon seeing him. (145)
Here the meaning of the word <s>śoṇita</s> in the sense of "made brilliant" — referring to its nature as redness — is obstructed by its more common meaning of "blood."

children.text: (6) "anucitārthaṃ'; yathā tapasvibhiryā sucireṇa labyate prayatnataḥ sattribhiriṣyate ca yā /
children.translated_text: (6) "Inappropriate meaning" — as in: That state which ascetics obtain with great difficulty over a long time, and which enemies also seek —

children.text: prayānti tāmāśu gatiṃ yaśasvino raṇāsvamedhe paśutāmupāgatāḥ // 146 //
children.translated_text: The glorious ones who have become sacrificial victims in battle quickly attain that state, as in the <s>aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice). (146)
Here the word <s>paśu</s> (animal/victim) suggests cowardice — hence it is of inappropriate meaning.
(7) "Meaningless" — a word whose sole purpose is to fill the verse meter, an expletive.
As in: O <s>Gaurī</s>, with the radiance golden like the pollen of blossoming lotus filaments,
May my desire be fulfilled, O blessed one, by your grace! (147)
Here the particle <s>hi</s> is the example.

children.text: (8) "avācakaṃ'; yathā avandhayakopasya vihanturāpadāṃ bhavanti vaśyāḥ svayameva dehinaḥ /
children.translated_text: (8) "Non-denotative" — as in: Of one whose anger is not fruitless, of the destroyer of calamities, beings become obedient of their own accord;

children.text: amarṣaśūnyena janasya jantunā na jātahārdena na vidviṣādaraḥ // 148 //
children.translated_text: By a creature devoid of indignation, who has no heartfelt sympathy for people, no respect is shown to an enemy. (148)

children.text: atra jantupadamadātaryarthe vivakṣitam tatra ca nābhidhāyakam /
children.translated_text: Here the word <s>jantu</s> (creature) is intended in the sense of one who does not give, but it does not denote that meaning.

children.text: yathā vā hādhik sā kila tāmasī śaśimukhī dṛṣṭā mayā yatra sā tadvicchedarujāndhakāritamidaṃ dagdhaṃ dinaṃ kalpitam /
children.translated_text: Or as in: Alas, that dark-complexioned moon-faced woman was seen by me where she was; this day, blinded by the pain of separation from her, has been burnt and contrived.

children.text: kiṃ kurmaḥ kuśale sadaiva vidhuro dhātā na cettatkathaṃ tādṛgyāmavatīmayo bhavati me no jīvaloko 'dhunā // 149 //
children.translated_text: What shall we do? The Creator is always hostile to our welfare — but if that is not so, then how is it that such a terrible illness afflicts me, and the world of the living is no longer mine? (149)
Here <s>dina</s> (day) is non-denotative in the intended sense of "consisting of light."
And also that which, through association with a prefix, acquires a different meaning.
As in: With shanks for stems, thighs for stalks, nails for radiant filaments, arranged in rows, terrifying, with fresh lac-color spreading as tendrils, with beautiful anklets as bees,

children.text: bharturnṛttānukāre jayati nijatanusvacchalāvaṇyavāpī- saṃbhūtāmbhojaśobhāṃ vidadhadabhinavo daṇḍapādo bhavānyāḥ // 150 //
children.translated_text: In the imitation of dance by her lord, the novel raised foot of <s>Bhavānī</s> triumphs, creating the beauty of a lotus born from the pool of the natural grace and charm of her own body. (150)
Here the prefix <s>vi</s> in <s>vidadhad</s> is superfluous, since <s>dadhad</s> alone suffices for the meaning.
(9) "Indecent" — "in three ways" means through suggesting shame, disgust, or inauspiciousness.
As in: He whose instrument is so great that it is not seen in anyone else —
Who else but that wise man could endure the arching of her eyebrow? (151)

children.text: (1) līlātāmarasāhato 'nyavanitāniḥśahkadaṣṭādharaḥ kaśvitkesaradūṣitekṣaṇa iva vyāmīlya netre sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: (1) Struck by a playful lotus, with lower lip boldly bitten by another woman, with eyes as if sullied by some pollen, he stood with eyes half-closed;

children.text: mugdhā kuḍmalitānanena dadatī vāyuṃ sthitā tatra sā bhrāntyā dhūrtatayātha vā natimṛte tenāniśaṃ cumbitā // 152 //
children.translated_text: The innocent woman stood there with face bowed, offering him air, and he, out of confusion or roguishness, kissed her ceaselessly by way of bowing. (152)

children.text: (2) mṛdupavanavibhinno matpriyāyā nināśāt ghanarucirakalāpo niḥsapatno 'dya jātaḥ /
children.translated_text: (2) Split by the gentle breeze, from the destruction of my beloved's braid, the thick and beautiful peacock's tail has today become without a rival;

children.text: rativigalitabandhe keśapāśe sukeśyāḥ sati kusumasanāthe kaṃ haredeṣa barhī // 153 //
children.translated_text: When the beautiful-haired woman's hair-braid, loosened by passion, has flowers as its lord, whom would this peacock steal away? (153)
(3) In these, the words <s>sādhana</s> (instrument), <s>vāyu</s> (air), and <s>vināśa</s> (destruction) are suggestive of shame and the like.
(10) "Ambiguous" — as in: Your honor was embraced in battle by the goddess of victory;

children.text: āśīḥparaṃparāṃ vandyāṃ karṇe kṛtvā kṛpāṃ kuru // 154 //
children.translated_text: Having placed the succession of blessings at your ear, O venerable one, show mercy. (154)

children.text: atra vandyāṃ kiṃ haṭhahṛtamahilāyām kiṃ vā namasyāmiti saṃdehaḥ //
children.translated_text: Here there is doubt whether <s>vandya</s> means "a woman seized by force" or "one worthy of salutation."
(11) "Unfamiliar" — that which is well-known only in technical treatises.
As in: Right knowledge is declared to be the light for those who have dispelled the darkness of latent impressions;
Even action that is being performed would not become a cause of bondage for them. (155)
Here the word <s>āśaya</s> in the sense of <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impression) is used only in <s>Yoga</s>-<s>śāstra</s> and such texts.
(12) "Vulgar" — that which is current only in common usage.
As in: Your face has the radiance transferred from the beloved of the full-moon night;
And your waist, with the beauty of a golden slab, captivates the mind. (156)
Here the word <s>kaṭi</s> (waist) is the example.
(13) "Requiring interpretation" — "Some well-established <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary significations) function like direct denotation by virtue of capacity;
Some are made current at present, and some are never so, due to incapacity."
That which is a prohibited secondary signification (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>).
As in: Your face, O slender one, fond of the full-moon night shining in the autumn season,
Makes a guest of the slapping of cheeks. (157)
Here, by "slapping of cheeks," being defeated is secondarily signified.

children.text: atha samāsagatameva duṣṭamiti saṃbandhaḥ, anyat kevalaṃ samāsagataṃ ca //
children.translated_text: Now, "defective only in a compound" — this is the connection; otherwise individually it is [not defective], but in a compound it is.
(14) "Forced" — because the apprehension of meaning is obstructed.
As in: With those that shine with the rising of the light born from the eye of <s>Atri</s>,
Your conduct, O king, shines exceedingly in a manner resembling them. (158)
Here the meaning is: by the <s>kumuda</s> (night-lotuses) that shine with the rising light of the moon born from <s>Atri</s>'s eye.
(15) "With unexamined predicate" — that in which the predicate portion is not indicated with due prominence.

As in: Of those whose false glory, born in the world upon the attainment of victory, is washed away by the grace at the feet of <s>Īśa</s> (the Lord), anointed by the stream of blood flowing abundantly from the severed heads cut on the battlefield —

children.text: kailāsaullāsanecchāvyatikarapiśunotsarpidarpoddhurāṇāṃ doṣṇāṃ caiṣāṃ kimatat phalamiha nagarīrakṣaṇe yat prayāsaḥ // 159 //
children.translated_text: Of these arms, whose swelling pride betrays a mingling of desire to sport upon <s>Kailāsa</s>, what unexpected fruit is there — that the effort is in guarding the city? // 159 //

children.text: atra mithyāmahimatvaṃ nānuvādyam api tu vidheyam /
children.translated_text: Here, false grandeur is not the <s>anuvādya</s> (topic) but rather the <s>vidheya</s> (predicate);

children.text: yathā vā srastāṃ nitambādavaropayantī punaḥ punaḥ kesaradāmakāñcīm /
children.translated_text: Or, for example: She who repeatedly adjusts the girdle of filaments slipping from her hips,
as if it were a second bowstring placed there by <s>Smara</s> (the god of love), who knows the right spot. // 160 //
Here, only the quality of being a second is the subject of <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy);
The reading "a second bowstring" (<s>maurvīṃ dvitīyām</s>) is the correct one.

children.text: yathā vā vapurvirūpākṣaṇalakṣyajanmatā digambaratvena niveditaṃ vasu /
children.translated_text: Or, for example: A body whose birth is marked by the eye of <s>Virūpākṣa</s> (Śiva), wealth offered through <s>digambaratva</s> (nakedness),

children.text: vareṣu yadbālamṛgākṣi mṛgyate tadasti kiṃ vyastamapi trilocane // 161 //
children.translated_text: that which is sought in brides, O young doe-eyed one — does all that exist even separately in the three-eyed one (<s>Trilocana</s>, i.e., <s>Śiva</s>)? // 161 //
Here, what should be said is "unnoticed birth" (<s>alakṣitā janiḥ</s>);
Or, for example: She who was never released even for a moment from him whose mind is the sole abode of the chain of the ocean of bliss, whose heart is governed by extreme restlessness —

children.text: yā sarvadaiva bhavatā tadudantacintā tāntiṃ tanoti tava saṃprati dhigdhigasmān // 162 //
children.translated_text: that anxiety about his tidings, which is always with you, now causes you weariness — alas, shame on us! // 162 //
Here, the negation "not released" (<s>na muktā</s>) is the <s>vidheya</s> (predicate);

children.text: yathā navajaladharaḥ saṃnaddho 'yaṃ na dṛptaniśācaraḥ suradhanuridaṃ dūrākṛṣṭaṃ na tasya śarāsanam /
children.translated_text: For example: This is a fresh cloud armed for battle, not a proud demon of the night; this is a rainbow drawn from afar, not his bow;

children.text: ayamapi paṭurdhārāsāro na bāṇaparaṃparā kanakanikaṣasnigdhā vidyut priyā na mamorvaśī // 163 //
children.translated_text: this too is a dense shower of rain, not a volley of arrows; this is lightning, smooth as a touchstone of gold — not his beloved <s>Urvaśī</s>. // 163 //
In this verse —
nothing else is predicated here through the denial by way of <s>anuvāda</s> (reiteration) of what is not stated;
For example: He guarded himself without fear, he followed <s>dharma</s> without affliction,
without greed he acquired wealth, without attachment he experienced happiness. // 164 //
Here, through the <s>anuvāda</s> (reiteration) of fearlessness and other qualities, the guarding of the self and so on is expressed. //
(16) "Producing contradictory understanding" — for example: Skilled in activities resembling the rays of the moon,
that one alone is a friend without cause (<s>akāryamitra</s>) — what shall we say about him? // 165 //

children.text: atra "kārṃya vinā mitram'; iti vivakṣitam "akārye mitram iti'; tu pratītiḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the intended meaning is "a friend without any task [to accomplish]" (<s>kārya vinā mitram</s>), but the understanding produced is "a friend in wrongdoing" (<s>akārye mitram</s>);
Or, for example: Of the beloved who, after a long time, brings delight to the eyes,
the lover suddenly seizes his throat (<s>galagraha</s>). // 166 //
Here, what should be said is "embrace of the neck" (<s>kaṇṭhagraha</s>);

children.text: yathā vā na trastaṃ yadi nāma bhūtakaruṇāsaṃtānaśāntātmanaḥ tena vyārujatā dhanurbhagavato devādbhavānīpateḥ /
children.translated_text: Or, for example: If one is not frightened, since the Lord whose nature is pacified by the continuity of compassion for beings — by him who bent the bow of the blessed one, the lord of <s>Devās</s>, the husband of <s>Bhavānī</s>,

children.text: tatputrastu madāndhatārakavadhādviśvasya dattotsavaḥ skandaḥ skanda iva priyo 'hamatha vā śiṣyaḥ kathaṃ vismṛtaḥ // 167 //
children.translated_text: his son <s>Skanda</s>, who gave joy to the world by slaying the pride-blinded <s>Tāraka</s>, is dear like <s>Skanda</s> himself — or rather, how has this disciple been forgotten? // 167 //

children.text: atra bhavānīpatiśabdo bhavānyāḥ patyantare pratītiṃ karoti yathā vā gorapi yadvāhanatāṃ prāptavataḥ so 'pi girisutāsiṃhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the word <s>Bhavānīpati</s> (husband of <s>Bhavānī</s>) produces an understanding of another husband of <s>Bhavānī</s>. Or, for example: Even of the bull, which has attained the status of being a vehicle, that lion of the mountain's daughter (<s>Girisutā</s>) —
may that consort of <s>Ambikā</s>, who is without ego in the presence [of others], protect you. // 168 //
Here, the word <s>Ambikāramaṇa</s> (consort of <s>Ambikā</s>) produces a contradictory understanding. //

children.text: "śrutikaṭu'; samāsagataṃ yathā sā dūre ca sudhāsāndrataraṅgitavilocanā /
children.translated_text: "Harsh to the ear" — an example within a compound: She, at a distance, with eyes brimming with waves of nectar,
the season (<s>kāla</s>) worthy of the cry of peacocks has arrived. // 169 //
Thus other [examples] should also be understood. //
(Sūtra 47)
Setting aside that which has lost its grammatical form, that which is incapable, and that which is meaningless,
these defects exist in the sentence as well, and some also in parts of a word. // 52 //
Some [defects exist in parts of a word], but not all;
Examples in order: He studied the <s>Vedas</s>, worshipped the gods, satisfied the <s>Pitṛs</s> (ancestors), honored his kinsmen,
conquered the six groups [of enemies], delighted in statecraft, and completely destroyed his foes. // 170 //

children.text: sa rātu vo duśvyavano bhāvukānāṃ paraṃparām /
children.translated_text: May he, the dispenser of inauspicious conduct (<s>duśvyavana</s>), protect you and the lineage of the fortunate ones,
[protect them] from those condemned for faults such as being dumb and mute (<s>aneḍamūka</s>). // 171 //
Here, <s>duśvyavana</s> means <s>Indra</s>, and <s>aneḍamūka</s> means one who is dumb and deaf. //
Of him whose arm is accompanied by arrows, who has subdued the lord of the earth by the banner of <s>Makara</s> (the crocodile emblem of <s>Kāmadeva</s>),
your fame (<s>śloka</s>) shines more brilliantly, O lord of the earth, radiant as the lotus. // 172 //

children.text: atra sāyakādayaḥ śabdāḥ khaḍgābdhibhūcandrayaśaḥparyāyāḥ śarādyarthatayā prasiddhāḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, the words <s>sāyaka</s> (arrow) and others are well-known in the sense of arrow etc., [but are intended as] synonyms for sword, ocean, earth, moon, and fame. //

children.text: kuvindastvaṃ tāvatpaṭayasi guṇagrāmamabhito yaśo gāyantyete diśi diśi ca nagnāstava vibho /
children.translated_text: You are indeed a weaver (<s>kuvinda</s>), for you spread the multitude of virtues everywhere; and these naked ones sing your fame in every direction, O Lord;
yet your fame, beautiful in all its limbs, bright and vast like the moonlight of autumn, wanders about without any covering here. // 173 //
Here, the word <s>kuvinda</s> (weaver) and others, while conveying another meaning, reveal the disparagement of the one being praised — thus it has an inappropriate meaning (<s>anucitārtha</s>);
This one, having obtained the abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the chief of clouds, with uneven horses, causes
the sleep of the thousand-petaled ones, intent on flight. // 174 //

Here, the words <s>prābhrabhrāṭ</s>, <s>Viṣṇudhāma</s>, <s>viṣamāśva</s>, <s>nidrā</s>, and <s>parṇa</s> are non-denotative of [their intended meanings:] excellent cloud, sky, the seven horses, contraction, and petals. //
Approaching the king, <s>Kampanā</s>, the beautiful-eyed one,
enthusiastic with various weapons, caused bewilderment. // 175 //
Here, the words <s>upasarpaṇa</s> (approaching), <s>praharaṇa</s> (striking), and <s>mohana</s> (bewildering) are indelicate (<s>aślīla</s>) because they suggest shameful meanings;
They eat what has been vomited by others and consume what has been excreted;
those poets who would engage in appropriating the meaning of others. // 176 //
Here, the words <s>vānta</s> (vomited), <s>utsarga</s> (excretion), and <s>pravartana</s> (engaging) produce disgust (<s>jugupsā</s>);

children.text: pitṛvasatimahaṃ vrajāmi tāṃ saha parivārajanena yatra me /
children.translated_text: I go to my father's dwelling, there with my retinue, where, for me,
in the lineage of fire, the heart becomes free of all thorns of grief. // 177 //
Here, when the intended meaning is "father's house" etc., the understanding of "cremation ground" and such produces an inauspicious meaning (<s>amaṅgalārthatva</s>). //
Devoted to the splendor of the temple of the gods, having obtained full trembling,
inclined to seeking, this radiant glory — behold it! // 178 //

children.text: atra kiṃ surādiśabdā devasenāśaravibhūtyarthāḥ kiṃ madirādyarthāḥ, iti saṃdehaḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, the doubt is: do the words <s>surā</s> (gods/liquor) etc. mean deity, army, arrow, glory and radiance, or do they mean liquor and so on? //
Of that one who has extreme means, who possesses intense passion,

children.text: dṛḍhabhūmiḥ priyaprāptau yatnaḥ sa phalitaḥ sakhe // 179 //
children.translated_text: whose ground is firm — that effort in attaining the beloved has borne fruit, O friend. // 179 //
Here, words like <s>adhimātropāya</s> (extreme means) and others are not well-known (<s>apratīta</s>) because they are used only in the <s>Yogaśāstra</s> (science of yoga). //
This fellow with betel in his cheek (<s>tāmbūlabhṛtagalla</s>) babbles nonsense (<s>bhalla</s>),

children.text: karoti khādanaṃ pānaṃ sadaiva tu yathā tathā // 180 //
children.translated_text: and always eats and drinks however he pleases. // 180 //
Here, the words <s>galla</s> (cheek) and others are vulgar (<s>grāmya</s>). //
With cloth, lapis lazuli, and feet, she who is supreme in removing wounds and impurity,
motionless, fashioned — now announce the battle of the eyes! // 181 //

children.text: atrāmbāraratnapādaiḥ kṣatatamā, acalā bhūḥ kṛtā netradvandvaṃ bodhayeti neyārthatā //
children.translated_text: Here, the intended meaning is: by garments, gems, and feet, the supreme earth was made, motionless — "make known the pair of eyes" — thus it has a figurative meaning (<s>neyārthatā</s>);

children.text: dhammillasya na kasya prekṣya nikāmaṃ kuraṅgaśāvākṣyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing the braided hair of the doe-eyed maiden to one's heart's content, whose mind
does not become enamored of the beauty of a novel arrangement of skill? // 182 //

children.text: atra dhammillasya śobhāṃ prekṣya kasya mānasaṃ na rajyatīti saṃbandhe kliṣṭatvam //
children.translated_text: Here, in the construction "seeing the beauty of the braided hair, whose mind is not enamored" — there is awkwardness (<s>kliṣṭatva</s>). //

children.text: nyakkāro hyayameva me yadarayastatrāpyasau tāpasaḥ so 'pyatraiva nihanti rākṣasakulaṃ jīvatyahau rāvaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Indeed, this itself is my humiliation — that my enemies are there, and among them that ascetic; he too destroys the <s>Rākṣasa</s> clan right here — alas, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> lives!

children.text: dhigdhik śakrajitaṃ prabodhitavatā kiṃ kumbhakarṇena vā svargagrāmaṭikāviluṇṭhanavṛthocchūnaiḥ kimebhirbhujaiḥ // 183 //
children.translated_text: Shame, shame on <s>Śakrajit</s> (conqueror of <s>Indra</s>)! What was the use of awakening <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>? Of what use are these arms, swollen in vain from plundering the village-fort of heaven? // 183 //
and only the swelling is the <s>anuvādya</s> (topic), not what is qualified by "in vain";

children.text: atra ca śabdaracanā viparītā kṛteti vākyasyaiva doṣo na vākyārthasya /
children.translated_text: and here, since the word-arrangement is inverted, it is a defect of the sentence, not of the sentence-meaning;

children.text: yathā vā apāṅgasaṃsargi taraṅgitaṃ dṛśorbhruvorarālāntavilāsi vellitam /
children.translated_text: Or, for example: The sidelong glance that accompanies, the undulating movement of the eyes and brows, the curling grace at the tips,

children.text: visāri romāñcanakañcukaṃ tanostanoti yo 'sau subhage tavāgataḥ // 184 //
children.translated_text: the spreading goosebumps like an armor over the body — he who [caused all] that, O beautiful one, has arrived. // 184 //
Here, what should be said is "this itself is humiliation";
For indeed, a demonstrative pronoun (<s>tacchabda</s>) referring to a well-known, previously established, experienced object does not require the use of a relative pronoun (<s>yacchabda</s>);
Examples in order:
Cowardice is mere policy; valor is the behavior of wild beasts;
therefore, he sought success through both combined. // 185 //
Here, the two words "he who" (<s>yo 'sau</s>) are the <s>anuvādya</s> (topic) and produce a sense of contempt (<s>avajñā</s>);

children.text: dvayaṃ gataṃ saṃprati śocanīyatāṃ samāgamaprārthanayā kapālinaḥ /
children.translated_text: Two things have now become pitiable through the request for union with the skull-bearer (<s>Kapālin</s>, i.e., <s>Śiva</s>):

children.text: kalā ca sā kāntimatī kalāvatastvamasya lokasya ca netrakaumudī // 186 //
children.translated_text: that art, the luminous digit of the moon (<s>kalā</s>), and you, the moonlight (<s>kaumudī</s>) for the eyes of this world. // 186 //

children.text: utkampinī bhayapariskhalitāṃśukāntā te locane pratidiśaṃ vidhure kṣipantī /
children.translated_text: Trembling, with garments slipping due to fear, casting your distressed eyes in every direction,

children.text: krūreṇa dāruṇatayā sahasaiva dagdhā dhūmāndhitena dahanena na vīkṣitāsi // 187 //
children.translated_text: you were not even seen by the fire, blinded by smoke, which cruelly and harshly burned [everything] suddenly. // 187 //

However, the relative pronoun (<s>yacchabda</s>), being connected with the subsequent sentence, does not by its own capacity require the use of the correlative pronoun (<s>tacchabda</s>) connected with the prior sentence;

children.text: yathā sādhu candramasi puṣkaraiḥ kṛtaṃ mīlitaṃ yadabhirāmatādhike /
children.translated_text: For example: Well done by the lotuses against the moon — that they close when the exceedingly charming one [rises];

children.text: udyatā jayini kāminīmukhe tena sāhasamanuṣṭhitaṃ punaḥ // 188 //
children.translated_text: but the moon, rising triumphant, has again committed this audacity against the face of the beloved. // 188 //

children.text:
prāgupāttastu yacchabdastacchabdopādānaṃ vinā sākāṅkṣaḥ /
yathā atraiva śloke, ādyapādayorvyatayāse /

children.translated_text: When both are used, the absence of syntactic expectancy is well established;
Even when [the correlative] is not used, sometimes both are understood through context (<s>sāmarthya</s>);

children.text: yathā ye nāma kecidiha naḥ prathayantyavajñāṃ jānanti te kimapi tān prati naiṣa yatnaḥ /
children.translated_text: For example: Those who spread contempt toward us here, whoever they may be — they know something; this effort is not directed at them;

children.text: utpatsyate 'sti mama ko 'pi samānadharmā kālo hyayaṃ niravadhirvipulā ca pṛthvī // 189 //
children.translated_text: there will arise someone of the same nature as me — for this time is limitless and the earth is vast. // 189 //

However, the relative pronoun (<s>yacchabda</s>) used earlier, without the correlative (<s>tacchabda</s>), creates syntactic expectancy (<s>sākāṅkṣa</s>);
as in this very verse, in the first two <s>pādas</s> (quarters) there is transposition;
And thus, without the use of the correlative (<s>tacchabda</s>), there is syntactic expectancy (<s>sākāṅkṣatva</s>) here;
Nor does he [the poet] express the meaning of the correlative with "that one" (<s>asau</s>);
That one, with beautiful filaments kissed by the wind, the chief among the bright orbs of the serene lord of stars (the moon),
beheld by the anguished gaze of women separated [from their lovers], the spring season has arrived like <s>Hanumān</s>. // 190 //
Here, [the meaning is]: toward him who will arise;
For here, the meaning of the correlative pronoun (<s>tacchabda</s>) is not conveyed;

children.text: pratītau vā karakālakarāladoḥsahāyo yudhi yo 'sau vijayārjunaikamallaḥ /
children.translated_text: Or, if it were conveyed: He whose arms are terrible as death, accompanied by allies, who in battle is the sole champion like <s>Vijayārjuna</s> —

children.text: yadi bhūpatinā sa tatra kārye viniyujyeta tataḥ kṛtaṃ kṛtaṃ syāt // 191 //
children.translated_text: if he were employed by the king in that task, then the deed would be as good as done. // 191 //
Here, the word "he" (<s>sa</s>) would become redundant;
Now, he who sees this entire sphere of meaning without differentiation, O Lord, as your form —
for that one, eternally happy, in a world filled by his own side and [that of] the enemy, whence is there fear? // 192 //
then, it deserves to be used in another sentence here, not in that very sentence;

children.text: yacchabdasya hi nikaṭe sthitaḥ prasiddhiṃ parāmṛśati /
children.translated_text: for the relative pronoun (<s>yacchabda</s>), being situated nearby, refers to what is well-known;
For example: That formidable and exceedingly fierce <s>Kṣātra</s> (warrior) power of this king —
by that one playing with dice, surely even that has been lost. // 193 //
It is said that, like the word "this" (<s>idam</s>), the word "that" (<s>adaḥ</s>) also expresses the meaning of the correlative pronoun (<s>tacchabda</s>);
Here is the correlative pronoun (<s>tacchabda</s>);

children.text: nanu katham kalyāṇānāṃ tvamasi mahasāṃ bhājanaṃ viśvamūrte dhuryāṃ lakṣmīmatha mayi bhṛśaṃ dhehi deva prasīda /
children.translated_text: Now, how [can there be a fault]? "You are the vessel of great auspicious things, O universal form; then bestow upon me the foremost <s>Lakṣmī</s> (prosperity) abundantly, O Lord, be gracious;

children.text: yadyatpāpaṃ pratijahi jagannātha namrasya tanme bhadraṃ bhadraṃ vitara bhagavan bhūyase maṅgalāya // 194 //
children.translated_text: whatever sin there is, destroy it, O Lord of the world, for one who bows — grant me welfare upon welfare, O Blessed One, for greater auspiciousness." // 194 //
Here, having said "whatever" (<s>yadyad</s>), "that of mine" (<s>tanme</s>) is said;

children.text: ucyate--yadyaditi yena kenacidrūpeṇa sthitaṃ sarvātmakaṃ vastvākṣiptam tathābhūtameva tacchabdena parāmṛśyate /
children.translated_text: It is explained: by saying "whatever" (<s>yadyad</s>), the all-encompassing reality existing in whatever form is indicated, and it is referred to in that very form by the correlative pronoun (<s>tacchabda</s>);

children.text: yathā vā kiṃ lobhena vilaṅghitaḥ sa bharato yenaitadevaṃ kṛtaṃ mātrā strīlaghutāṃ gatā kimatha vā mātaiva me madhyamā /
children.translated_text: Or, for example: Has <s>Bharata</s> been overcome by greed that he has done this? Or has my mother gone to the lightness of women? Or is it that my mother is [merely] the middle one?

children.text: mithyaitanmama cintitaṃ dvitayamapyāryānujo 'sau gurur- mātā tātakalatramityanucitaṃ manye vidhātrā kṛtam // 195 //
children.translated_text: This is my false thought — both [are wrong]; that revered younger brother is the elder, the mother is the wife of the father — I think this was improperly done by the Creator. // 195 //

children.text: atrāryasyeti tātasyeti ca vācyam na tvanayoḥ samāse guṇībhāvaḥ kāryaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, what should be said is "of the noble one" (<s>āryasya</s>) and "of the father" (<s>tātasya</s>), and the subordination of these two in a compound should not be done;
Thus, examples should be given for other [incorrect] compounds as well. //
Producing contradictory understanding — for example: Those who have resorted to the earth, whose land is reddened, whose forms are embraced by <s>Śiva</s>,
having destroyed their bodies today, they lie having attained happiness (<s>gatāsukhāḥ</s>). // 196 //

children.text: atra kṣaṇādiguṇayuktāḥ sukhamāsate, iti vivakṣite hatā iti viruddhā pratītiḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, when the intended meaning is that they rest happily, endowed with qualities such as <s>kṣamā</s> (earth/patience) and others, the contradictory understanding is that they have been slain. //

An illustration is given in order for a part of a verse, as applicable: "Due to excessive fickleness, due to being like a dream or illusion, due to the insipidity of its outcome, from union with a woman—

children.text: iti yadi śatakṛtvastacvamālocayāma- stadapi na hariṇākṣīṃ vismaratyantarātmā // 197 //
children.translated_text: even if we reflect upon this a hundred times, still the inner self does not forget the doe-eyed one." (197)
Here, [the fault is in] 'tvā' and such [harsh sounds].

children.text: yathā vā tadgaccha siddhyai kuru devakāryamartho 'yamarthāntaralabhya eva /
children.translated_text: Or, for example: "Go forth for success, accomplish the task of the gods — this goal is attainable only through other means;
it awaits confidence born of auspicious attainment, like a seed-sprout awaits water before its rising." (198)
Here, [the sequences] 'ddhyai' and 'bdhyai' are harsh.
"[The mountain] which bears on its peaks her who is the accomplisher of the adornments and graceful movements of the <s>Apsaras</s> (celestial nymphs),
resplendent with mineral pigments, like an untimely twilight with colors distributed by the breaking of clouds." (199)
Here, the word 'mattā' in the sense of 'intoxicated' has its meaning suppressed [by the compound].

children.text: ādāvañjanapujjaliptavapuṣāṃ śvāsānillollāsita- protsarpadvirahānalena ca tataḥ saṃtāpitānāṃ dṛśām /
children.translated_text: "Of the eyes that were first anointed with collyrium on their surfaces, then heated by the rising fire of separation fanned by the wind of sighs,

children.text: saṃpratyeva niṣekamaśrupayasā devasya cetobhuvo bhallīnāmiva pānakarma kurute kāmaṃ kuraṅgekṣaṇā // 200 //
children.translated_text: now the doe-eyed woman performs the act of quenching with the water of tears — like [the tempering] of the arrows of <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love) in the mind." (200)

children.text:
atra dṛśāmiti bahuvacanaṃ nirarthakam /
kuraṅgekṣaṇāyā ekasyā evopādānāt /

children.translated_text: Nor can the plurality be justified by difference of function, as in 'alasavalitaiḥ' etc., since the [different] functions are not actually mentioned.
And the word 'dṛk' (eye) is not used here in the sense of function.
In this very [verse], the <s>ātmanepada</s> (middle voice) in 'kurute' is also purposeless,
because when the result of the principal action does not relate to the agent, there is no result of action intended by the agent.
Here, the plural 'of the eyes' is purposeless, since only one doe-eyed woman is being referred to.

children.text: cāpācāryastripuravijayī kārtikeyo vijeyaḥ śastravyastaḥ sadanamudadhirbhūriyaṃ hantakāraḥ /
children.translated_text: "The bow-master, the conqueror of <s>Tripura</s>, <s>Kārtikeya</s> is the one to be conquered, [<s>Paraśurāma</s>] whose weapons are scattered, the ocean is [his] abode, this earth is the slayer—

children.text: astyevaitat kimu kṛtavatā reṇukākaṇṭhabādhāṃ baddhaspardhastava paraśunā lajjate candrahāsaḥ // 201 //
children.translated_text: even granting all this, does your <s>Candrahāsa</s> (sword) not feel ashamed, competing with the axe of him who inflicted the wound on <s>Reṇukā</s>'s neck?" (201)
Here, the <s>kṛtya</s> suffix in 'vijeya' (to be conquered) does not properly convey the meaning of the <s>kta</s> (past participle) suffix.

Here, 'even a trace of offense' should be expressly stated.

children.text: (14) asthānasthapadaṃ yathā priyeṇa saṃgrathya vipakṣasaṃnidhānupāhitāṃ vakṣasi pīvarastane /
children.translated_text: (14) A word placed where it does not belong. As in: No woman discarded the garland, though wilted from water, that had been strung by her beloved and placed on her ample-bosomed chest despite the proximity of a rival;

children.text: srajaṃ na kācidvijahau jalāvilāṃ vasanti hi premṇi guṇā na vastuṣu // 236 //
children.translated_text: For love resides in virtues, not in objects. (verse 236)
Here, 'no one discarded' is what should be stated (rather than 'not any woman discarded').

children.text: yathā vā lagnaḥ kelikacagrahaślathajaṭālambena nidrāntare mudrāṅkaḥ śitikandharenduśakalenāntaḥ kapolasthalam /
children.translated_text: Or as in: Imprinted by the crescent moon of <s>Śitikaṇṭha</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), clinging to the inner cheek during sleep through the loosened matted locks caught in amorous play,

children.text: pārvatyā nakhalakṣmaśahkitasakhīnarmasmitahrītayā pronmṛṣṭaḥ karapallavena kuṭilātāmracchaviḥ pātu vaḥ // 237 //
children.translated_text: May it protect you—that mark, reddish and curved, which was wiped away by the sprout-like hand of <s>Pārvatī</s>, who was embarrassed by the playful smiles of her companions suspecting it to be a nail-mark! (verse 237)
Here, 'reddish and curved' (kuṭilatāmra) should be stated before 'nail-mark' (nakhalakṣma).

children.text: (15) asthānasthasamāsaṃ yathā adyāpi stanaśailadurgaviṣame sīmantinīnāṃ hṛdi sthātuṃ vāñchati māna eṣa dhigiti krodhādivālohitaḥ /
children.translated_text: (15) A compound placed where it does not belong. As in: Even today, pride, red with anger, wishes to remain in the hearts of women, which are as difficult to access as mountain fortresses of breasts—'shame on it!' (he says);
At that very moment, the moon, extending its far-reaching rays, draws out its sword of blade-like petals issuing from the blossoming white water-lily buds, roaring. (verse 238)

children.text: atra kruddhasyoktau samāso na kṛtaḥ kaveruktau tu kṛtaḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, in the speech of the angry one, no compound has been formed, but in the poet's speech it has been formed.
(16) Intermingled (<s>saṃkīrṇa</s>): where the words of one sentence enter into another sentence.

children.text: yathā kimiti na paśyasi kopaṃ pādagataṃ bahuguṇaṃ gṛhāṇemam /
children.translated_text: As in: Why do you not see—anger—fallen at your feet—of many virtues—accept this one;
Indeed, release—the lord of your heart—from the neck—the embodiment of darkness of the mind. (verse 239)

children.text: atra pādagataṃ bahuguṇaṃ hṛdayanāthaṃ kimiti na pasyasi, imaṃ kaṇṭhe gṛhāṇa manasastamorūpaṃ kopaṃ muñceti /
children.translated_text: Here the construction should be: 'Why do you not see the lord of your heart, fallen at your feet, of many virtues? Accept this one on your neck. Release the anger, which is the embodiment of the darkness of the mind.'
But if construed as a single sentence, it becomes forced—that is the distinction.
(17) Enveloped (<s>gārbhita</s>): where another sentence enters into the middle of a sentence.
As in: Association with the wicked who are devoted to harming others—
I tell you this—should never be undertaken. (verse 240)
Here, the third quarter has entered into the middle of another sentence.

children.text: yathā vā lagnaṃ rāgāvṛtāṅgyā sudṛḍhamiha yayaivāsiyaṣyārikaṇṭhe mātaṅgānāmapīhopari parapuruṣairyā ca dṛṣṭā patantī /
children.translated_text: Or as in: She who clung tightly, her body covered with passion (lac-dye), she who shall wield the sword at the enemy's throat, and who was seen by rival men falling from atop elephants;

children.text: tatsakto 'yaṃ na kiṃcidgaṇayati viditaṃ te 'stu tenāsmi dattā bhṛtyebhyaḥ śrīniyogādgaditumiva gatetyambudhiṃ yasya kīrtiḥ // 241 //
children.translated_text: He is attached to her and regards nothing else—let this be known to you—by his command I have been given to the servants, as if sent to speak, thus his fame has gone to the ocean. (verse 241)
Here, 'let this be known to you' is the embedded clause.
On the contrary, it creates a contrary impression—that <s>Lakṣmī</s> (prosperity) departs from him.
(18) "In anklets and such ornaments, sounds like 'raṇita' (tinkling) are conventional; in birds, 'kūjita' (cooing) and the like;
In lovemaking, 'stanita' (moaning) and 'bhaṇita' (murmuring) etc.; in clouds and such, 'garjita' (thundering) and the like."
This is the fault of transgressing established convention (<s>prasiddhi</s>).
As in: Imitating again and again the fierce thundering of the terrible dense clouds of the <s>Puṣkarāvartaka</s> type, agitated by the winds of the great dissolution;
This terrifying roar, filling the cavity of the sky, unprecedented until now, arose from the battlefield—from where? (verse 242)

children.text: atra ravo maṇḍūkādiṣu prasiddho na tūktaviśeṣe siṃhanāde //
children.translated_text: Here, 'rava' (roar) is conventionally associated with frogs and the like, not with the specific sense intended—namely, the lion's roar.
(19) Where the sequence (<s>prakrama</s>) or occasion (<s>prastāva</s>) is broken.

children.text: yathā nāthe niśāyā niyaterniyogādastaṃ gate hanta niśāpi yātā /
children.translated_text: As in: When the lord of the night departed by his nightly duty of setting—alas, the night too has passed;

children.text: kulāṅganānāṃ hi daśānurūpaṃ nātaḥ paraṃ bhadrataraṃ samasti // 243 //
children.translated_text: For the condition of noble women, nothing more auspicious than this exists. (verse 243)

children.text:
atra "gate'; iti prakrānte "yātā'; iti prakṛteḥ /
"gatā niśāpi'; iti tu yuktam /
nanu "naikaṃ padaṃ dviḥ prayojyaṃ prāyeṇa'; ityanyatra kathitapadaṃ duṣṭamiti cehaivoktam /
tatkathamekasya padasya dviḥprayogaḥ, /

children.translated_text: The answer is:

children.text: uddeśyapratinirdeśyavyatirikto viṣaya ekapadaprayoganiṣedhasya tadvati viṣaye pratyuta tasyaiva padasya sarvanāmno vā prayogaṃ vinā doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: The prohibition against using the same word applies to cases other than the subject and its predicate; in such cases, without using that very word or a pronoun, it would be a fault.
For example: The sun rises red, and red indeed it sets;
In prosperity and in adversity, great ones maintain the same form. (verse 244)

Here, after introducing 'gate' (having gone), 'yātā' (has passed) is used from the same root. 'Gatā niśāpi' (the night too has gone) would have been appropriate. Now, it has been stated elsewhere that 'generally, the same word should not be used twice'—this is the fault called 'kathita-pada' (repeated word). Then how can one word be used twice?

children.text: atra rakta evāstametīti yadi kriyeta tadā padāntarapratipāditaḥ sa evārtho 'rthāntaratayeva pratibhāsamānaḥ pratītiṃ sthagayati //
children.translated_text: Here, if one were to say 'it sets as red' (using a different word), then the same meaning conveyed by another word, appearing as if it were a different meaning, would obstruct the intended understanding.

children.text: yathā vā yaśo 'dhigantuṃ sukhalipsayā vā manuṣyasaṃkhyāmativartituṃ vā /
children.translated_text: Or as in: Whether to attain fame, or out of desire for happiness, or to transcend the count of mortals;
<s>Siddhi</s> (success) approaches those who are engaged in effort without attachment, as though it were eager. (verse 245)
Here, of the suffix (pratyaya)—
The reading 'sukham īhituṃ vā' (or to strive for happiness) would be correct.

children.text: te himālayamāmantrya punaḥ prekṣya ca śūlinam /
children.translated_text: They, having bid farewell to the <s>Himālaya</s>, having looked again at the <s>Śūlin</s> (Trident-bearer, <s>Śiva</s>),
And having reported to him the accomplished purpose, released by him, they ascended to the sky. (verse 246)
Here, of the pronoun—
The expression 'anena visṛṣṭāḥ' (released by him) should be stated.

children.text: mahībhṛtaḥ putravato 'pi dṛṣṭistasminnapabatye na jagāma tṛptim /
children.translated_text: The gaze of the mountain king, even though he had sons, did not reach satisfaction upon that daughter;
For upon a mango tree of inexhaustible blossoms and honey, the garland of bees has a special attachment. (verse 247)
The reading 'mahībhṛto 'patyavato 'pi' (of the mountain king, even though he had offspring) would be correct.

children.text: "atra satyapi putre kanyārūpe 'pyapatye sneho 'bhūt'; iti kecitsamarthayante /
children.translated_text: Here some explain: 'even though he had a son, there was affection for the daughter-like offspring as well.'
Misfortunes overpower the one who lacks valor; the future protects the one beset by calamity;
Diminution is certain for one without extent; one who is not weighty does not attain the position of royal fortune. (verse 248)
Here, of a synonym—
Here, of the prefix (upasarga) and the synonym—
"The misfortune overpowers, brings about a lack of extent;
One assumes diminution from lack of extent; one with diminution does not attain the position of royal fortune."
—this would be correct.

children.text: kācitkīrṇā rajobhirdivamanuvidadhau mandavaktrendulakṣmī- raśrīkāḥ kāśvidantardiśa iva dadhire dāhamudbhrāntasacvāḥ /
children.translated_text: Some, covered with dust, made the sky bear the beauty of a dim-faced moon; some, bereft of beauty, held a burning sensation within the directions, as if bewildered in spirit;

children.text: bhremurvātyā ivānyāḥ pratipadamaparā bhūmivatkampamānāḥ prasthāne pārthivānāmaśivamiti puro bhāvi nāryaḥ śaśaṃsaḥ // 249 //
children.translated_text: Others whirled like gusts of wind, still others trembled at every step like the earth—thus the women foretold the inauspiciousness that was to come before the departure of the kings. (verse 249)
Here, of the grammatical number—

children.text: "kāśvitkīrṇā rajobhirdivamanuvidadhurmandavaktrenaduśobhā niḥśrīkāḥ'; iti "kampamānāḥ'; ityatra "kampamāpuḥ'; iti ca paṭhanīyam /
children.translated_text: The readings should be 'kāścitkīrṇā rajobhirdivamanuvidadhuḥ' (some women made, plural) for 'mandavaktrenadu-śobhā niḥśrīkāḥ' (bereft of beauty), and 'kampamāpuḥ' (they trembled, plural) for 'kampamānāḥ' (trembling).

children.text: gāhantāṃ mahiṣā nipānasalilaṃ śṛṅgairmuhustāḍitaṃ chāyābaddhakadambakaṃ mṛgakulaṃ romanthamabhyasyatām /
children.translated_text: Let the buffaloes plunge into the water of the bathing pools, repeatedly striking it with their horns; let the herds of deer, gathered in clusters in the shade, practice rumination;

children.text: viśrabdhaiḥ kriyatāṃ varāhapatibhirmustākṣatiḥ palvale vikṣāntiṃ labhatāmidaṃ ca śithilajhyābandhamasmaddhanuḥ // 250 //
children.translated_text: Let the confident boar-chiefs make scratches with <s>mustā</s> grass roots in the marsh; and let this bow of ours, with its loosened bowstring-knot, obtain rest. (verse 250)
Here, of the <s>kāraka</s> (grammatical case)—
The expression 'viśrabdhāḥ racayantu sūkaravarāḥ mustākṣatim' (let the confident boar-chiefs make the mustā-scratches) would be faultless.
When the sage, a treasure of fame whose immeasurable glory of austerity, brilliance, and valor was beyond reckoning, and whose anger was truly aroused, approached;

children.text: aminavadhanurvidyādarpakṣamāya ca karmaṇe sphurati rabhasātpāṇiḥ pādopasaṃgrahaṇāya ca // 251 //
children.translated_text: The hand springs forth with impetuosity, both to show respect for the valor of his skill in the science of archery, and for the act of grasping his feet. (verse 251)
Here, of the sequence—
The expression 'for grasping the feet' should be stated first.
Similarly, other such cases should also be inferred.
(20) Where there is an absence of proper sequence.

children.text: yathā dvayaṃ gataṃ saṃprati śocanīyatāṃ samāgamaprārthanayā kapālinaḥ /
children.translated_text: As in: Two things have now gone to a state of being pitiable, due to the desire for union with <s>Kapālin</s> (<s>Śiva</s>):

children.text: kalā ca sā kāntimatī kalāvataḥ tavmasya lokasya ca netrakaumudū // 252 //
children.translated_text: That radiant digit of the moon-crested one, and this world's delight to the eyes (moonlight). (verse 252)
Here, the conjunction 'ca' (and) is appropriate after the word 'tvam' (you).

children.text: yathā vā śaktirnistriśajeyaṃ tava bhujayugale nātha doṣākaraśrī- rvaktre pārśve tathaiṣā prativasati mahākuṭṭanī khahgayaṣṭiḥ /
children.translated_text: Or as in: O lord, power—this sword—is victorious on your pair of arms; the beauty of the moon abides on your face; and this great procuress, the sword-staff, dwells at your side;

children.text: ājñeyaṃ sarvagā te vilasati ca puraḥ kiṃ mayā vṛddhayā te procyevetthaṃ prakopācchaśikarasitayā yasya kīrtyā prayātam // 253 //
children.translated_text: This omnipresent command of yours shines before you—what use am I, an old woman, to you?—having spoken thus in anger, his fame departed, whitened by the moon's rays. (verse 253)
Here, 'having spoken thus' (ittham procyeva) would be the proper sequence.
Likewise, in 'lagnaṃ rāgāvṛtāṅgyā—'
(verse 253a)
and such passages, the expression 'iti śrīniyogāt' should be stated.
(21) Where an unintended meaning contradicts the subject at hand.

children.text: yathā rāmamanmathaśareṇa tāḍitā duḥsahena hṛdaye niśācarī /
children.translated_text: As in: Struck in the heart by the arrow of <s>Kāma</s> (the god of love), which is unbearable, the demoness;
Anointed with blood that has the fragrance of sandal, she went to the abode of the lord of her life. (verse 254)

children.text:
atra prakṛte rase valiruddhasya śṛṅgārasya vyajjako 'paro 'rthaḥ /
arthadoṣānāha (sū- 76)
children.translated_text: Here, another meaning that reveals the <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic) sentiment, which contradicts the prevailing <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic mood), is expressed. Now he states the faults of meaning (sūtra 76):
Meaning that is unsupported, forced, contradictory, repetitious, having faulty sequence, or vulgar— (verse 55)
Ambiguous, without cause, contradicting established knowledge or learning,
Unexamined, having restrictions and non-restrictions, generalities and non-generalities, and circumlocutions— (verse 56)
Syntactically incomplete, having improper words, inconsistent with its companion, having a revealed contradiction,
Inappropriate in injunction and restatement, abandoned and then re-adopted, or obscene— (verse 57)
—these are to be understood as faults (of meaning).
Examples in order: (1) Whose joy, released from the expansive pathway spreading across the wide sky, is unimpeded;
The sun triumphs, creating laughter in the lotuses with his fragrance stirred by the wind. (verse 255)

children.text: atrātivitatatvādayo 'nupādāne 'pi pratipādyamānamarthaṃ na bādhanta ityapuṣṭāḥ, na tvasaṃgatāḥ punaruktā vā //
children.translated_text: Here, the qualifiers such as 'excessively extended' etc. do not obstruct the meaning being conveyed even if they are omitted—hence they are 'unsupported' (<s>apuṣṭa</s>), but not incoherent or repetitious.

children.text: (2) sadā madhye yāsāmiyamamṛtanisyandasurasā sarasvatyuddāmā vahati bahumārgā parimalam /
children.translated_text: (2) In the midst of which (literary tastes), this <s>Sarasvatī</s> (eloquence), unbounded, carrying fragrance through many paths, rich with the flow of nectar, always flows;

children.text: prasādaṃ tā etā ghanaparicitāḥ kena mahatāṃ mahākāvyavyomni sphuritamadhurā yāntu rucayaḥ // 256 //
children.translated_text: May these literary tastes, sparkling with sweetness in the sky of great poetry, deeply versed in profundity, attain clarity! (verse 256)

children.text: atra yāsāṃ kavirucīnāṃ madhye sukumāravicitramadhyamātmakatrimārgā bhāratī camatkāraṃ vahati tāḥ, gambhīrakāvyaparicitāḥ kathamitarakāvyavat prasannā bhavantu /
children.translated_text: Here, among the literary tastes of the poet, in the middle of which—the tender, the variegated, and the medium—the three-pathed <s>Bhāratī</s> (speech/eloquence) carries aesthetic delight; those tastes, being well-versed in profound poetry, how can they become clear like ordinary poetry?

children.text: yāsāmādityaprabhāṇāṃ madhye tripathagā vahatitāḥ, meghaparicitāḥ kathaṃ prasannā bhavantīti saṃkṣepārthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Among those rays of the sun, the <s>Tripathagā</s> (Ganges, flowing on three paths) flows; how can they, surrounded by clouds, become clear? This is the condensed meaning.

children.text: (3) jagati jayinaste te bhāvā navendukalādayaḥ prakṛtimadhurāḥ santyevānye mano madayanti ye /
children.translated_text: (3) In the world, victorious are those qualities — the crescent moon and the like, which are naturally sweet, and there are indeed others that intoxicate the mind;

children.text: mama tu yadiyaṃ yātā loke vilocanacandrikā nayanaviṣayaṃ janmanyekaḥ sa eva mahotsavaḥ // 257 //
children.translated_text: But for me, since this moonlight has gone forth in the world, that alone is the one great festival for the eyes in this life. (257)

children.text: atrendukalādayo yaṃ prati paspaśaprāyāḥ sa eva candrikātvamutkarṣārthamāropayatīti vyāhatatvam //
children.translated_text: Here, the crescent moon and the like, which are merely objects of touch for that person, he himself attributes the quality of being moonlight for the sake of exaltation — thus there is self-contradiction.
(4) 'What has been done, what has been approved' and so on. (258)

children.text: atrārjunārjuneti bhavadbhiriti cokte sabhīmakirīṭināmiti kirīṭipadārthaḥ punaruktaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, when '<s>Arjuna</s>, <s>Arjuna</s>' and 'by you all' have been said, in 'along with <s>Bhīma</s> and <s>Kirīṭin</s> (Arjuna),' the meaning of the word <s>Kirīṭin</s> is repeated.

children.text: yathā vā astrajvālāvalīḍhapratibalajaladherantaraurvāyamāṇe senānāthe sthite 'sminmama pitari gurau sarvadhanvīśvarāṇām /
children.translated_text: As for example: 'When the ocean of the opposing army is being consumed by the flames of weapons, when <s>Aurva</s> (submarine fire) is blazing within it, when this commander of armies, my father, the lord of all archers, stands —

children.text: karṇālaṃ kaṃbhrameṇa vraja kṛpa samaraṃ muñca hārdikya śaṅkāṃ tāte cāpadvitīye vahati raṇadhuraṃ ko bhayasyāvakāśaḥ // 259 //
children.translated_text: <s>Karṇa</s>, enough with confusion, go; <s>Kṛpa</s>, enter the battle; <s>Hārdikya</s> (son of <s>Hṛdika</s>), abandon your doubt — when my father, unrivaled with the bow, bears the burden of battle, where is there room for fear?' (259)
Here, the meaning of the fourth line's sentence is repeated.
(5) 'O jewel among kings, celebrated for the festival of bestowing freedom from poverty,

children.text: viśrāṇaya turaṅgaṃ me mātaṅgaṃ vā madālasam // 260 //
children.translated_text: Grant me a horse, or an elephant intoxicated with <s>mada</s> (rut).' (260)
Here, the elephant should have been mentioned first.

children.text: (6) svapiti yāvadayaṃ nikaṭe janaḥ svapimi tāvadahaṃ kimapaiti te /
children.translated_text: (6) 'As long as this person nearby sleeps, I too shall sleep for that long — do you know this?
Therefore, now, bring your elbow quickly; raise your thigh, bent.' (261)
This one is an unsophisticated speaker.
(7) 'Setting aside jealousy' and so on. (262)

children.text: atra prakaraṇādyabhāve saṃdehaḥ śāntaśṛṅgāryanyatarābhidhāne tu niśvayaḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, in the absence of context and other indicators, there is doubt; but when either <s>śānta</s> (tranquil) or <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic) <s>rasa</s> is expressed, there is certainty.

children.text: (8) gṛhītaṃ yenāsīḥ paribhavabhayānnocitamapi prabhāvādyasyābhūnna khalu tava kaśvinna viṣayaḥ /
children.translated_text: (8) 'That which was seized by him — even what was improper was not abandoned out of fear of humiliation; by whose power, indeed, nothing was beyond your reach;

children.text: parityaktaṃ tena tvamasi sutaśokānna tu bhayā- dvimokṣye śastra tvāmahamapi yataḥ svasti bhavate // 263 //
children.translated_text: Abandoned by him, you are [left] from grief for your son, not from fear — I too shall release the weapon against you, therefore farewell to you.' (263)
Here, the reason for releasing the weapon has not been stated.

children.text: (9) idaṃ te kenoktaṃ kathaya kamalātaṅkavadane yadetasmin hemnaḥ kaṭakamiti dhatse khalu dhiyam /
children.translated_text: (9) 'Who told you this? Tell me, O one whose face troubles the lotus; that upon this, you hold the notion that it is a bracelet of gold —

children.text: idaṃ tadduḥsādhākramaṇaparamāstraṃ smṛtibhuvā tava prītyā cakraṃ karakamalamūle vinihitam // 264 //
children.translated_text: This is the supreme weapon of <s>Smṛtibhū</s> (the god of love, born of memory), difficult to overcome in its advance, placed at the base of your lotus-hand out of love for you — the <s>cakra</s> (discus).' (264)
Here, the <s>cakra</s> (discus) of <s>Kāma</s> (the god of love) is not well-known in the world.

children.text: yathā vā (9 a) upaparisaraṃ godāvaryāḥ parityajatādhvagāḥ saraṇimaparo mārgastāvadbhavādbhirihekṣyatām /
children.translated_text: As for example: (9a) 'O travelers, abandon the vicinity of the <s>Godāvarī</s>; let another path be found by you for your road meanwhile;

children.text: iha hi vihito raktāśokaḥ kayāpi hatāśayā caraṇanalinanyāsodañcannavāṅkurakañcukaḥ // 265 //
children.translated_text: For here, by some despairing woman, a red <s>Aśoka</s> tree has been made to sprout new buds, encased in shoots, by the touch of her lotus-feet.' (265)
