children.text: atra pādāghātenāśokasya puṣpodghamaḥ kaviṣu prasiddho na punaraṅkurodgamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the blossoming of the <s>Aśoka</s> tree by the touch of a foot is well-known among poets, but not the sprouting of new shoots.

children.text: (susitavasanālaṃkārāyāṃ kadāyana kaumudī- mahasi sudṛśi svairaṃ yāntyāṃ gato 'stamabhūdvidhuḥ /
children.translated_text: ('When the beautiful woman adorned with white garments was going freely in the moonlight festival,

children.text: tadanu bhavataḥ kīrtiḥ kenāpyagīyata yena sā priyagṛhamagānmuktāśaṅkā kva nāsi śubhapradaḥ // 266 //
children.translated_text: The moon set; then your fame was sung by someone, whereby she went home free from apprehension — where were you not auspicious?' (266)

children.text: atrāmūrtāpi kīrtiḥ jyotsnāvatprakāśarūpā kathiteti lokaviruddhamapi kaviprasiddherna dupṭam //)//
children.translated_text: Here, though fame is formless, it has been described as having luminous form like moonlight — though contradicting common experience, it is not faulty because it is well-established among poets.)

children.text: (10) sadā snātvā niśīthinyāṃ sakalaṃ vāsaraṃ budhaḥ /
children.translated_text: (10) 'Having always bathed in the dead of night, the learned one throughout the entire day

children.text: nānāvidhāni śāstrāṇi vyācaṣṭe ca śṛṇoti ca // 267 //
children.translated_text: Expounds and listens to various <s>śāstras</s> (treatises).' (267)

children.text: grahoparāgādikaṃ vinā rātrau snānaṃ dharmaśāstreṇa viruddham /
children.translated_text: Bathing at night, except during eclipses of planets and the like, is contradicted by <s>dharmaśāstra</s> (legal scripture).

children.text: (10 a) ananyasadṛśaṃ yasya balaṃ bāhvoḥ samīkṣyate /
children.translated_text: (10a) 'Whose strength in both arms is seen to be unequaled by any other —
The pursuit of the sixfold policy for him is truly purposeless.' (268)
This [is contradicted] by <s>arthaśāstra</s> (treatise on statecraft).
(10ā) 'Having placed the armlet far away, the woman adorned as the playground of <s>Anaṅga</s> (the bodiless god of love)
Wore as a necklace the line of nail-marks made by her lover.' (269)

children.text: atra keyūrapade nakhakṣataṃ na vihitamiti, etatkāmaśāstreṇa /
children.translated_text: Here, the nail-scratch is not placed at the location of the armlet — this [is contradicted] by <s>kāmaśāstra</s> (treatise on erotics).
(10i) 'By the nail of practice of <s>aṣṭāṅgayoga</s> (eight-limbed yoga), making the hard-to-attain <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment) near,
Now attaining the desired <s>vivekakhyāti</s> (discriminative discernment), the crest-jewel of <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption) — liberated.' (270)

children.text: atra vivekakhyātistataḥ saṃprajñātasamādhiḥ paśvādasaṃprajñātastato muktirna tu vivekakhyātau etat yogaśāstreṇa /
children.translated_text: Here, <s>vivekakhyāti</s> (discriminative discernment) leads to <s>saṃprajñāta samādhi</s> (cognitive meditation); after that comes <s>asaṃprajñāta</s> (non-cognitive meditation), then liberation — not at the stage of <s>vivekakhyāti</s> itself. This [is contradicted] by <s>yogaśāstra</s> (treatise on yoga).
Similarly, contradictions with other branches of knowledge should also be illustrated.

children.text: (11) prāptāḥ śriyaḥ sakalakāmadughāstataḥ kiṃ dattaṃ padaṃ śirasi vidviṣatāṃ tataḥ kim /
children.translated_text: (11) 'Wealth fulfilling all desires has been obtained — then what? A place has been given upon the heads of enemies — then what?

children.text: saṃtarpitāḥ praṇayino vibhavaistataḥ kiṃ kalpaṃ sthitaṃ tanubhṛtāṃ tanubhistataḥ kim // 271 //
children.translated_text: Dear ones have been gratified with riches — then what? One has lived for an eon in these bodies — then what?' (271)

children.text:
atra tataḥ kimiti na navīkṛtam /
(tattu yathā yadi dahatyanalo 'tra kimadbhutaṃ yadi ca gauravamadriṣu kiṃ tataḥ /
lavaṇamambu sadaiva mahodadheḥ prakṛtireva satāmaviṣāditā // 272 //)//
children.translated_text:
Here, 'then what' has not been given fresh meaning.
(But as for example: 'If fire burns, what is wonderful in that? If there is gravity in mountains, what of it?
The ocean's water is always salty — the nature of the virtuous is indeed free from sorrow.' (272))

children.text: (12) yatrānullikhitārthameva nikhilaṃ nirmāṇametadvidhe- rutkarṣapratiyogikalpanamapi nyakkārakoṭiḥ parā /
children.translated_text: (12) 'Where all this creation merely sketches the intended meaning, where even the imagination of a rival in excellence is the ultimate in insignificance,

children.text: yātāḥ prāṇabhṛtāṃ manorathagatīrullahghya yatsaṃpada- stasyābhāsamaṇīkṛtāśmasu maṇeraśmatvamevocitam // 273 //
children.translated_text: Where the wealth surpasses the course of desires of living beings — for that gem, among stones made to resemble gems, the status of being merely a stone is indeed fitting.' (273)
Here, 'for that gem, among stones that merely shadow gems, the nature of being a stone is indeed fitting' — the restrictive sense should be stated.

children.text: (13) vaktrāmbhojaṃ sarasvatya dhivasati sadā śoṇa evādharaste bāhuḥ kākutsthavīryasmṛtikaraṇapaṭurdakṣiṇaste samudraḥ /
children.translated_text: (13) 'Your mouth is a lotus where <s>Sarasvatī</s> always dwells; your lower lip is indeed the <s>Śoṇa</s> river; your right arm, skilled in recalling the valor of <s>Kākutstha</s> (Rāma), is the ocean;

children.text: vāhinyaḥ pārśvametāḥ kṣaṇamapi bhavato naiva muñcantyabhīkṣṇaṃ svacche 'ntarmānase 'smin kathamavanipate te 'mbupānābhilāṣaḥ // 274 //
children.translated_text: These rivers at your sides never leave you even for a moment; in this clear inner mind of yours, O lord of the earth, how can there be desire for drinking water?' (274)

children.text: atra "śoṇa eva'; iti niyamo na vācyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, the restriction 'indeed the <s>Śoṇa</s>' should not be stated.

children.text: (14) śyāmāṃ śyāmalimānamānayata bhoḥ sāndrairmaṣīkūrcakair- mantraṃ tantramatha prayujya harata śvetotpalānāṃ śriyam /
children.translated_text: (14) 'Bring dark collyrium, O friends, with thick brush-strokes of ink; or employ a <s>mantra</s> (spell) or <s>tantra</s> (ritual device) and steal the beauty of white lotuses;

children.text: candraṃ cūrṇayata śraṇācca kaṇaśaḥ kṛtvā śilāpaṭṭake yena draṣṭumahaṃ kṣame daśa diśastadvakrmudrāṅkitāḥ // 275 //
children.translated_text: Grind the moon and, reducing it to particles on a stone slab — so that I may be able to see the ten directions stamped with the seal of that face.' (275)
Here, the specification of <s>śyāmā</s> (dark beauty) as 'moonlight' should be stated.
(15) 'O abode of <s>Makaras</s> (sea-creatures), do not despise these gems, struck by the harsh blows of rolling waves —

children.text: kiṃ kaustubhena vihito bhavato na nāma yācñāprasāritakaraḥ puruṣottamo 'pi // 276 //
children.translated_text: Is not even <s>Puruṣottama</s> (Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s>), from whom the <s>Kaustubha</s> gem was obtained, also one who extends his hand in supplication?' (276)

children.text: atra "ekena kiṃ na vihito bhavataḥ sa nāma'; iti sāmānyaṃ vācyam /
children.translated_text: Here, 'what has not been accomplished by that one alone for you?' — the general sense should be stated.

children.text: (16) arthitve prakaṭīkṛte 'pi na phalaprāptiḥ prabhoḥ pratyuta druhyan dāśarathirviruddhacarito yuktastayā kanyayā /
children.translated_text: (16) 'Even when the desire has been made manifest, there is no attainment of the fruit from the lord; rather, <s>Dāśarathi</s> (<s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>), acting contrary, is united with that maiden;

children.text: utkarphaṃ ca parasya mānayaśasorvisraṃsanaṃ cātmanaḥ strīratnaṃ ca jagatpatirdaśamukho devaḥ kathaṃ mṛṣyate // 277 //
children.translated_text: And the exaltation of the rival and the destruction of one's own honor and fame — and a jewel among women — how can the lord <s>Daśamukha</s> (ten-faced <s>Rāvaṇa</s>), a god, tolerate this?' (277)
Here, 'jewel among women' requires the complement 'to disregard';
For the connection with 'of the rival' through this [word] is not appropriate.

children.text: (17) ājñā śakraśikhāmaṇipraṇayinī śāsrāṇi cakṣurnavaṃ bhaktirbhūtapatau pinākini padaṃ laṅketi divyā purī /
children.translated_text: (17) 'His command courts the crest-jewel of <s>Śakra</s> (Indra); his weapons are a new eye; devotion is to the lord of beings, <s>Pinākī</s> (<s>Śiva</s>); his abode is <s>Laṅkā</s>, a divine city;

children.text: utpattirdruhiṇānvaye ca tadaho nedṛgvaro labhyate syāccedeṣa na rāvaṇaḥ kva nu punaḥ sarvatra sarve guṇāḥ // 278 //
children.translated_text: His birth is in the lineage of <s>Druhiṇa</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) — alas, such a bridegroom cannot be found! If only he were not <s>Rāvaṇa</s> — but where indeed are all virtues found in one place?' (278)

children.text: atra "syāccedeṣa na rāvaṇaḥ'; ityatra, eva samāpyam /
children.translated_text: Here, at 'if only he were not <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,' the sentence should indeed be concluded.

children.text: (18) śrutena buddhirvyasanena mūrkhatā madena nārī salilena nimnagā /
children.translated_text: (18) 'By learning, intelligence; by vice, foolishness; by intoxication, a woman; by water, a river;

children.text: niśā śaśāṅkena dhṛtiḥ samādhinā nayena cālaṃkriyate narendratā // 279 //
children.translated_text: By the moon, the night; by meditation, steadfastness; by statesmanship, kingship is adorned.' (279)
Here, vice and foolishness, being inferior, are incongruous when placed alongside superior companions such as learning and the rest.
(19) 'Attached, with limbs covered in passion —' (280)

children.text: ityatra viditaṃ te 'stvityanena śrīstasmādapasaratīti viruddhaṃ prakāśyate //
children.translated_text: Here, by the phrase 'let it be known to you,' it is revealed as contradictory that <s>Śrī</s> (the goddess of fortune) departs from him.

children.text: (20) prayatnaparibodhitaḥ stutibhiradya śeṣe niśā- makeśavamapāṇḍavaṃ bhubanamadya niḥsomakam /
children.translated_text: (20) 'Awakened with effort, through praises — today is the end of the night; without <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, the world today is without <s>Somaka</s>;

children.text: iyaṃ parisamāpyate raṇakathādya do 'śālinā- mapaitu ripukānanātigururadya bhāro bhuvaḥ // 281 //
children.translated_text: This battle-tale is concluded today — by one who has no portion, may the heavy burden of enemies upon the earth depart today.' (281)
Here, 'you have slept and are awakened with effort' — this should be the predicate.

children.text: yathā vā vātāhāratayā jagadviṣadharairāśvāsya niḥśeṣitaṃ tegrastāḥ punarabhratoyakaṇikātīvravratairbarhibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: As for example: 'Having been reassured by those who live on wind as food, the world was completely consumed by serpents; then those who had been devoured were [consumed] by peacocks observing the fierce vow of drinking only rain-drops;

children.text: te 'pi krūracamūrucarmavasanairnītāḥ kṣayaṃ lubdhakai- rdambhasya sphuritaṃ vidannapi jano jālmo guṇānīhate // 282 //
children.translated_text: Those too were brought to destruction by cruel hunters wearing hides and skins — even knowing the manifestation of deceit, the base person still strives for [false] virtues.' (282)
Here, the triad of 'living on wind' and the rest should be stated in reverse order.

(21) 'O ornament of the arm of <s>Rāmā</s> (the beloved), O refuge of the line of ashes, O subduer of the shame of <s>Smāra</s>'s (the god of love's) sport, O destroyer of the life-breath of the love-sick,

children.text: sarohaṃsottaṃsa pracaladala nīlotpala sakhe sakhedo 'haṃ mohaṃ ślathaya kathaya kvenduvadanā // 283 //
children.translated_text: O crest-ornament of the lake's swans, O friend of the trembling-petaled blue lotus — I am sorrowful; dispel my delusion; tell me, where is the moon-faced one?' (283)
Here, 'O destroyer of the life-breath of the love-sick' should not be the <s>anuvādya</s> (topic being discussed).
(22) 'Attached, with limbs covered in passion' and so on. (284)
Here, though 'let it be known to you' has concluded the thought, with 'by that one' and so on it is taken up again.
(23) 'Of one who has set out only to kill, who is obstinate, who seeks an opening —

children.text: yathāsya jāyate pāto na tatā punarunnatiḥ // 285 //
children.translated_text: As is his fall, so there is no subsequent rise for him.' (285)
Here, the meaning applicable to a man is also understood.

children.text: yatraiko doṣaḥ pradarśitastatra doṣāntarāṇyapi santi tathāpi teṣāṃ tatrāprakṛtatvātprakāśanaṃ na kṛtam //
children.translated_text: Where one fault has been demonstrated, other faults also exist there; nevertheless, since they are not the subject under discussion in that context, they have not been made explicit.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 77)
In compounds such as <s>karṇāvataṃsa</s> (ear-ornament), the sound <s>karṇa</s> (ear) and the like is produced
for the purpose of conveying proximity and the like.

<s>Avataṃsa</s> (crest-ornament) and similar terms refer to ornaments of the ear and so on; therein, words like <s>karṇa</s> (ear) are used for the comprehension of their location on the ear and so on.

children.text: yathā asyāḥ karṇāvataṃsena jitaṃ sarvaṃ vibhūṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: As for example: 'By the ear-ornament of hers, all adornments are surpassed;
Just so, the ear-ring of hers shines exceedingly.' (286)
'Then, delighting the directions with an unprecedented sweet fragrance,
There came bees buzzing loudly, adorned with head-crests.' (287)
Here, the words <s>karṇa</s> (ear), <s>śravaṇa</s> (ear), and <s>śiras</s> (head) serve the purpose of indicating proximity.
'In the midst of a terrible battle, facing the torn-apart enemies,
By your arm marked with the callus of the bowstring, there was a display of might.' (288)
Here, the word <s>dhanus</s> (bow) is for the comprehension that it is strung.
But elsewhere: 'By him whose arm was stiff from the binding of the bowstring, accompanied by a series of panting breaths,
By the lord of <s>Laṅkā</s> who had conquered <s>Vāsava</s> (Indra), the prison was inhabited until grace was shown.' (289)
Here, the word <s>jyā</s> (bowstring) stands alone.
'Through the delightful embraces of the lord of her life,
With the pearl necklace shining, the pair of breasts seems to laugh.' (290)
Here, the word <s>muktā</s> (pearl) is used to indicate that the pearls are not mixed with other gems.

children.text: saundaryasaṃpat tāruṇyaṃ yasyāste te ca vibhramāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The wealth of beauty, youth — those and their charms that belong to her —

children.text: ṣaṭpadān puṣpamāleva kān nākarṣati sā sakhe // 291 //
children.translated_text: Like a flower garland attracting bees, whom does she not attract, O friend?' (291)
Here, the word <s>puṣpa</s> (flower) refers to flowers of superior quality.
For the word <s>mālā</s> (garland), without a qualifying term, denotes only a garland of flowers.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 78)
When these are established, this is their justification. (58)
Indeed, compounds like <s>jaghanakāñcī</s> (hip-girdle) are not formed in the same way as <s>karṇāvataṃsa</s> (ear-ornament) and the like.
'She spoke sweet words adorned with clear syllables.' (292)

children.text: ityādau kriyāviśeṣaṇatve 'pi vivakṣitārthapratītisiddhau "gatārthasyāpi viśeṣyasya viśeṣaṇadānārṃtha kvacitprayogaḥ kāryaḥ" iti na yuktam /
children.translated_text: Here, even when serving as a qualifier of the action, since the intended meaning is already established, the argument that 'the use of a qualifier for a subject whose meaning is already understood should sometimes be employed' is not proper.
Or, if it were proper, then even with feet devoid of sandals, quickly —
'Traveling a long distance on foot, this one is not wearied.' (293)
This should be cited as an example.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 79)
When the meaning is well-known, without reason, there is no fault.

children.text: yathā candraṃ gatā pajhaguṇānna bhuhkte pajhāśritā cāndramasīmabhikhyām /
children.translated_text: Just as the lotus (<s>pajha</s>), having gone to the moon, does not enjoy its qualities, and having resorted to the lotus, does not enjoy the lunar radiance,

children.text: umāmukhaṃ tu pratipadya lolā dvisaṃśrayāṃ prītimavāpa lakṣmīḥ // 294 //
children.translated_text: But <s>Lakṣmī</s> (beauty), having reached the face of <s>Umā</s>, being fickle, attained a twofold delight. (294)

children.text: atra rātrau pajhasya saṃkocaḥ, divā candaramasaśva niṣprabhatvaṃ lokaprasiddhamiti "na bhuṅkte'; iti hetuṃ nāpekṣate //
children.translated_text: Here, the closing of the lotus at night and the loss of luster of the moon during the day are well-known in the world, so "does not enjoy" does not require a reason.
(Sūtra 80)
But in imitation, of all [faults].
Of all faults beginning with <s>śrutikaṭu</s> (harsh to the ear) and so forth.
For example: "I saw the doe-eyed one" — thus this one narrates,

children.text: paśyaiṣa ca gavityāha sutrāmāṇaṃ yajeti ca // 295 //
children.translated_text: "Look, this one says 'a cow'" and "he worships <s>Sutrāmān</s> (Indra)." (295)
(Sūtra 81)
A fault may sometimes become a merit due to the propriety of the speaker and so forth, and sometimes neither. (59)

children.text: vaktṛpratipādyavyaṅgyavācyaprakaraṇādīnāṃ mahimnā doṣo 'pi kvacidguṇaḥ kvacinna doṣo na guṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Due to the greatness of the speaker, the subject matter, the suggested meaning, the denoted meaning, the context, and so forth, a fault sometimes becomes a merit, and sometimes is neither a fault nor a merit.

children.text: tatra vaiyākaraṇādau vaktari pratipādye ca raudrādau ca rase vyaṅgye kaṣṭatvaṃ guṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: In this regard, harshness is a merit when the speaker is a grammarian and the like, when the subject is the <s>Raudra</s> (furious) and other <s>rasas</s>, and when it is suggested.
Examples in order: "Who is equal to <s>dīdhīṅ</s> and <s>vevīṅ</s>, not subject to <s>guṇa</s> and <s>vṛddhi</s> [vowel alternations],
Who resembles a <s>kvip</s> suffix — where you are not present? (296)
When I saw you, learned in the science of words,
I remembered my teacher and felt great joy. (297)
With ornaments mostly consisting of intestine-strung large skull-garlands and fiercely jangling bangles, filling the sky with their terrible sounds,
With a terrifying body stout with swaying breasts smeared thickly with a muddy mixture of drink, vomit, and blood, she runs with arrogant pride. (298)

children.text: vācyavaśādyathā mātaṅgāḥ kimu valgitaiḥ kimaphalairāḍambarairjambukāḥ sāraṅgā mahiṣā madaṃ vrajatha kiṃ śūnyeṣu śūrā na ke /
children.translated_text: Due to the denoted meaning, as in: "O elephants, what use is your prancing? O jackals, what use are your fruitless displays? O deer and buffaloes, why do you go mad? Who are the brave ones in empty places?

children.text: kopāṭopasamudbhaṭotkaṭasaṭākoṭeribhāreḥ puraḥ sindhudhvānini huṅkṛte sphurati yat tadgarjitaṃ garjitam // 299 //
children.translated_text: Before the lion whose mane bristles fierce and terrible with the swelling of rage, when he roars with a thunderous sound like the ocean — that indeed is a roar!" (299)
Here, when a lion is the subject, harsh words [are appropriate].

children.text: prakaraṇavaśādyathā raktāśoka kṛśodahī kva nu gatā tyaktvānuraktaṃ janaṃ no dṛṣṭeti mudhaiva cālayasi kiṃ vātāvadhūtaṃ śiraḥ /
children.translated_text: Due to the context, as in: "O red <s>Aśoka</s> tree, where has the emaciated one gone, abandoning her beloved? 'Not seen' — why do you vainly shake your wind-blown head?
Without the striking of your feet by the bees that clash against the cluster of bees gathering in longing, how can this blossoming of yours come about?" (300)
Here, in the speech of one angered by the shaking of the head.
Sometimes, in the absence of <s>rasa</s>, it is neither a merit nor a fault.

children.text: yathā śīrṇagrāṇāṅgripāṇīn vraṇibhirapaghanairghargharāvyaktaghoṣān dīrghāghrātānaghaughaiḥ punarapi ghaṭayatyeka ullāghayan yaḥ /
children.translated_text: As in: "He who, with noses, limbs, hands, and feet fallen off, with open wounds devoid of flesh, with indistinct guttural sounds, long-smelled by hosts of sins, yet reunites them again, uplifting them,

children.text: gharmāṃśostasya vo 'ntardviguṇaghanaghṛṇānighnanirvighnavṛtter- dattārghāḥ siddhasaṃgharvidadhatu ghṛṇayaḥ śīghramaṃhovighātam // 301 //
children.translated_text: May the compassions of that sun, whose inner doubled dense mercy destroys obstacles unimpeded, who is worshipped by the assembly of <s>Siddhas</s> (perfected ones) to whom offerings have been given, quickly destroy sin." (301)
<s>Aprayukta</s> (unusual usage) and <s>nihatārtha</s> (obscured meaning) are not faults in <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia) and the like.

children.text: yathā yena dhvastamanobhavena balijitkāyaḥ purā strīkṛto yaśvodvṛttabhujaṅgahāravalayogaṅgāṃ ca yo 'dhārayat /
children.translated_text: As in: "He by whom the body of <s>Indra</s>, the conqueror of <s>Bali</s>, was formerly made into a woman, who destroyed <s>Manobhava</s> (Kāma),

children.text: yasyāhuḥ śaśimacchirohara iti stutyaṃ ca nāmāmārāḥ pāyātsa svayamandhakakṣayakarastvāṃ sarvadomādhavaḥ // 302 //
children.translated_text: Whose praiseworthy name the gods call 'Bearer of the moon on his head' — may that <s>Mādhava</s> (Śiva/Viṣṇu), the destroyer of <s>Andhaka</s>, himself protect you, the giver of all." (302)
Here, in the reading referring to <s>Mādhava</s>, the words <s>śaśimat</s> and <s>andhakakṣaya</s> have unusual usage and obscured meaning [but this is not a fault due to the double meaning].
<s>Aślīla</s> (indecent expression) is sometimes a merit.

children.text: yathā suratārambhagoṣṭyām "vdyarthaiḥ padaiḥ piśunayecca rahasyavastu" iti kāmaśāstrasthitau karihastena saṃbādhe saṃbādhe praviśyāntarviloḍite /
children.translated_text: As in the context of lovemaking: "one should indicate secret matters through words with double meanings" — according to the <s>Kāmaśāstra</s>: "When the elephant's trunk has entered the narrow space and churns within,
The man's banner, advancing, shines with another instrument." (303)
In narratives of tranquility: "In the woman's wound, swollen and bloated like a split frog's belly,
Moist and oozing — what creature other than a worm could find attachment?" (304)

children.text: nirvāṇavairadahanāḥ praśamādarīṇāṃ nandantu pāṇḍutanayāḥ saha mādhavena /
children.translated_text: "May the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, whose fire of enmity is extinguished, rejoice in the caves of peace together with <s>Mādhava</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>),

children.text: raktaprasādhitabhuvaḥ kṣatavigrahāśva svasthā bhavantu kururājasutāḥ sabhṛtyāḥ // 305 //
children.translated_text: And may the sons of the <s>Kuru</s> king, whose land is adorned with blood and whose bodies bear wounds, be well along with their servants." (305)
Here it indicates future auspiciousness.
Even the ambiguous, by the greatness of the denoted meaning, sometimes produces a definite understanding through culmination in <s>vyājastuti</s> (ironic praise), and is a merit.
As in: "O lord, with vessels of thin gold, with all your attendants adorned,
With magnificent she-elephants abounding — now our homes are equal." (306)
When both the subject and the means of expression are known, the unfamiliar [usage] is a merit.

children.text: yathā ātmārāmā vihitaratayo nirvikalpe samādhau jñānodrekādvighaṭitatamogranthayaḥ sacvaniṣṭhāḥ /
children.translated_text: As in: "Those who delight in the Self, whose pleasures are directed toward the unchanging <s>Samādhi</s>, whose knots of darkness are unraveled by the abundance of knowledge, steadfast in truth,

children.text: yaṃ vīkṣante kamapi tamasāṃ jyotiṣāṃ vā parastā- ttaṃ mohāndhaḥ kathamayamamuṃ vetti devaṃ purāṇam // 307 //
children.translated_text: Whom they behold as something beyond both darkness and light — how can this one, blinded by delusion, know that ancient deity?" (307)
Or in self-reflection:

children.text: yathā ṣaḍadhikadaśanāḍīcakramadhyasthitātmā hṛdi vinihitarūpaḥ siddhidastadvidāṃ yaḥ /
children.translated_text: As in: "The Self situated in the center of the wheel of sixteen <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels), with form established in the heart, who grants <s>siddhi</s> (perfection) to those who know him,

children.text: avicalitamanobhiḥ sādhakairmṛgyamāṇaḥ sa jayati pariṇaddhaḥ śaktibhiḥ śaktināthaḥ // 308 //
children.translated_text: Sought by practitioners with unwavering minds — he who is endowed with <s>Śaktis</s> (powers), the Lord of <s>Śakti</s>, triumphs." (308)
In the speech of lowly characters, <s>grāmya</s> (vulgar language) is a merit.

children.text: yathā phullukkaraṃ kalamakūraṇihaṃ vahanti je sindhuvāraviḍavā maha vallahā de /
children.translated_text: As in: "Those who carry the full-blooming <s>kalama</s> rice and <s>kūraṇi</s> — the <s>sindhuvāra</s> plants are your great beloveds,

children.text: je gālidassa mahisīdahiṇo saricchā de kiṃ ca muddhaviaillapasūṇapuñjā // 309 //
children.translated_text: Those which are the right of <s>Gālida</s>'s (the cowherd's) buffalo-curd — what more, heaps of flowers from the <s>mudda</s> creeper?" (309)
Here, the words <s>kalama</s> (rice), <s>bhakta</s> (food), <s>mahiṣī</s> (buffalo), and <s>dadhi</s> (curd) are vulgar, yet appropriate in the speech of the <s>Vidūṣaka</s> (jester).
<s>Nyūnapada</s> (ellipsis) is sometimes a merit.
As in: "With the rising of hair-bristles from breasts compressed by tight embrace, with garments slipping from her beautiful hips due to the excess of dense affection,

children.text: mā mā mānada māti māmalamiti kṣāmākṣarollāpinī suptā kiṃ nu mṛtā nu kiṃ manasi me līnā vilīnā nu kim // 310 //
children.translated_text: 'No, no, O proud one, no more, no, hold me' — murmuring thus with languid eyes, is she sleeping? Or dead? Or absorbed in my mind? Or dissolved?" (310)
Sometimes it is neither a merit nor a fault.

children.text: yathā tiṣṭhetkopavaśātprabhāvapihitā dīrghaṃ na sā kupyati svargāyotpatitā bhavenmayi punarbhāvārdramasyā manaḥ /
children.translated_text: As in: "Let her remain hidden by the power of her anger — she does not stay angry long; having risen to heaven, her mind would again become moist with love toward me;

children.text: tāṃ hartuṃ vibudhadviṣo 'pi na ca me śaktāḥ purovartinīṃ sā cātyantamagocaraṃ nayanayoryāteti ko 'yaṃ vidhiḥ // 311 //
children.translated_text: Even the enemies of the gods are unable to take her from before me — yet she has gone utterly beyond the reach of my eyes — what fate is this!" (311)

children.text: uttarā pratipattiḥ pūrvāṃ pratipattiṃ bādhate, iti na doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: The later understanding cancels the earlier understanding, so it is not a fault.
<s>Adhikapada</s> (redundancy) is sometimes a merit.

children.text: yathā yadvañcanāhitamatirbahu cāṭugarbhaṃ kāryonmukhaḥ khalajanaḥ kṛtakaṃ bravīti /
children.translated_text: As in: "When the wicked person, with mind intent on deception and speech full of flattery, eager for his purpose, speaks falsely,

children.text: tatsādhavo na na vidanti vidanti kiṃtu kartuṃ vṛthā praṇayamasya na pārayanti // 312 //
children.translated_text: The virtuous do not not know it — they know it indeed — but they are unable to render his affection fruitless." (312)
Here, after 'hidden,' the ellipsis of words like 'this is not possible because' does not produce a specific understanding, so it is not a merit.
Here the second 'they know' serves to exclude any other interpretation.

children.text: yathā vā vada vada jitaḥ sa śatrurna hato jalpaṃśva tava tavāsmīti /
children.translated_text: Or as in: "Speak, speak! That enemy is conquered, not killed! Boast on: 'I am yours, I am yours!'

children.text: citraṃ citramarodīddhā heti paraṃ mṛte putre // 313 //
children.translated_text: Wonder, wonder! Alas, she wept loudly" — thus when the son has died. (313)
Thus in such cases where the speaker is filled with joy, fear, and the like.

children.text: kathitapadaṃ kvacidguṇaḥ, lāṭānuprāse, arthāntarasaṃkramitavācye vihitasyānuvādyatve ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Kathitapada</s> (repetition of what has been said) is sometimes a merit — in <s>Lāṭānuprāsa</s> (a figure of repetition), when the denoted meaning has shifted to another sense, and when what has been stated becomes the subject of predication.
Examples in order: "Your fame, O mountain-bearer, has the radiance of white camphor-dust-rays, has the form of the moon-maker,
<s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) of manly valor, that <s>Kamalā</s> too belongs to you alone, not to another." (314)

children.text: tālā jāaṃti guṇā jālā de sahiaehiṃ dheppanti /
children.translated_text: "Garlands are born, and qualities — garlands for you with companions produce,
Grasped by the rays of the sun, there arise lotuses, lotuses." (315)
"Mastery of the senses is the cause of humility; excellence of qualities is obtained through humility;
Through excellence of qualities, people become devoted; for prosperity arises from the devotion of people." (316)
<s>Patatprakarṣa</s> (falling climax) is sometimes a merit.
As in the previously cited example beginning with 'that which has not been attained.' (317)
<s>Samāptapunarātta</s> (resumption after completion) is sometimes neither a merit nor a fault.

children.text: yatra na viśeṣaṇamātradānārthaṃ punargrahaṇam api tu vākyāntarameva kriyate /
children.translated_text: Where the repetition is not merely for providing a qualifier, but rather constitutes a separate sentence altogether.
As in the same previously cited example beginning with 'that which has not been attained.' (318)
<s>Apadasthasamāsa</s> (compound not in a [single] word) is sometimes a merit, as in the previously cited example beginning with 'red Aśoka.' (319)
<s>Garbhita</s> (parenthetical insertion) is likewise [sometimes a merit].

children.text: yathā humi avahatthiareho ṇiraṃkuso aha vivearahio vi /
children.translated_text: As in: "Even in sleep, even though humble, uncontrolled, and separated from experience,

children.text: siviṇe vi tumammi puṇo pattihi bhattiṃ ṇa pasumarāmi // 320 //
children.translated_text: Even in dreams, again toward you, O beloved, I cannot perceive devotion." (320)
Here 'believe me' [is inserted] in the middle to generate firm conviction.
Thus other [examples] too should be understood from the observed instances.
(Sūtra 82)
The expression of <s>vyabhicāri</s> (transitory) emotions, <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment), and <s>sthāyibhāva</s> (dominant emotions) through explicit words,
The forced attribution through strained imagination of <s>anubhāva</s> (consequent) and <s>vibhāva</s> (determinant), (60)
The employment of adverse <s>vibhāvas</s> and the like, repeated brilliance,
Untimely expansion, cessation, and excessive extension of a limb [of rasa], (61)
Non-coordination of the principal [rasa], reversal of natural dispositions,
And the mention of what is not a limb [of rasa] — such are the faults in <s>rasa</s>. (62)

children.text: (1) svaśabdopādānaṃ vyabhicāriṇo yathā savrīḍā dayitānane sakaruṇā mātaṅgacarmāmbare satrāsā bhūjage savismayarasā candre 'mṛtasyandini /
children.translated_text: (1) Naming a <s>vyabhicārin</s> (transitory emotion) by its own word, as in: "Bashful toward the beloved's face, compassionate toward the elephant-hide garment, fearful of the serpent, filled with wonder at the moon dripping nectar,

children.text: serṣyā jahnusutāvalokanavidhau dīnā kapālodare pārvatyā navasaṃgamapraṇayinī dṛṣṭiḥ śivāyāstu vaḥ // 321 //
children.translated_text: Jealous at the sight of <s>Jāhnavī</s> (<s>Gaṅgā</s>), pitiful toward the skull-bowl — may the glance of <s>Pārvatī</s>, full of love at the new union, be auspicious for you!" (321)
Here, of shame and the rest [the explicit naming is the fault].

children.text: "vyānamrā dayitānane mukulitā mātaṅgacarmāmbare sotkampā bhujage nimeṣarahitā candre 'mṛtasyandini /
children.translated_text: "Downcast toward the beloved's face, half-closed toward the elephant-hide garment, trembling at the serpent, unblinking at the moon dripping nectar,

children.text: mīladbhrūḥ surasindhudarśanavidhau mlānā kapālodare'; ityādi tu yuktam //
children.translated_text: With furrowed brows at the sight of the celestial river, withered at the skull-bowl" — this and the like would be appropriate.
(2) Or the expression of <s>rasa</s> itself by its own word.
Examples in order: "Having brought that auspicious beauty of victory over <s>Anaṅga</s> (Kāma) within the range of his eyes, with a slightly raised glance from the base of the arm,

children.text: netrayoḥ kṛtavato 'sya gocare ko 'pyajāyata raso nirantaraḥ // 322 //
children.translated_text: Some continuous <s>rasa</s> arose in him." (322)
"Having beheld the beautiful form graced with manifest love anointing her tender cheek,
See, this one, having surpassed boyhood, having turned, extends waves at the boundary of <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment)." (323)

children.text: (3) sthāyino yathā saṃprahāre praharaṇaiḥ prahārāṇā parasaparam ṭhaṇatkāraiḥ śrutikatairutsāhastasta ko 'pyabhūt // 324 //
children.translated_text: (3) Of the <s>sthāyin</s> (dominant emotion), as in: "In the clash, from the blows of weapons upon one another, from the clashing sounds harsh to the ear, some <s>utsāha</s> (enthusiasm) arose." (324)
Here, of <s>utsāha</s> [the explicit naming is the fault].
(4) "In the sky washed by the flood of radiance white as camphor-dust, when that moon shone cool,
Her manifest joy, the rising of her breasts, arose from the artful placing of a <s>tilaka</s> on her forehead — her eyes [were not the cause]." (325)

children.text: atroddīpanālambanarūpāḥ sṛṅgāyogyā vibhāvā anubhāvaparalapasācayinaḥ sthitā iti paṣṭakalpanā //
children.translated_text: Here, the <s>vibhāvas</s> in the form of <s>uddīpana</s> (excitants) and <s>ālambana</s> (substrata) appropriate for <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> are present as if yielding to the <s>anubhāva</s> — this is forced attribution.

children.text: (5) pariharati ratiṃ matiṃ lunīte skhalati bhṛśaṃ parivartate ca bhūyaḥ /
children.translated_text: (5) "She abandons love, her mind wavers, she stumbles greatly and turns again and again;

children.text: iti bata viṣamā daśāsya dehaṃ paribhavati prasabhaṃ kimatra kurmaḥ // 326 //
children.translated_text: Alas, thus this dire condition assaults her body forcibly — what can we do here?" (326)

children.text: atra ratiparihārādīnāmanubhāvānāṃ karuṇādāvapi saṃbhavātkāminīrūpo vibhāvo yatnataḥ pratipādyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, since abandonment of love and the like as <s>anubhāvas</s> are possible also in <s>Karuṇa</s> (compassionate) and other <s>rasas</s>, the <s>vibhāva</s> in the form of a woman [as beloved] must be carefully established.

children.text: (6) prasāde vartasva prakaṭaya mudaṃ saṃtyaja ruṣaṃ priye śuṣyantyaṅgānyamṛtamiva te siñcati vacaḥ /
children.translated_text: (6) "Remain in grace, show joy, abandon anger — O beloved, your words sprinkle my limbs like nectar as they wither;

children.text: nidhānaṃ saukhyānāṃ kṣaṇamabhimukhaṃ sthāpaya mukhaṃ na mugdhe pratyetuṃ prabhavati gataḥ kālahariṇaḥ // 327 //
children.translated_text: O treasure of happiness, turn your face toward me for a moment — O innocent one, the deer of time once gone cannot be made to return." (327)

children.text: atra śṛṅgāre pratikūlasya śāntasyānityatāprakāśanarūpo vibhāvastatprakāśito nirvedaśva vyabhicārī, upāttaḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, in <s>Śṛṅgāra</s>, the <s>vibhāva</s> consists of the manifestation of impermanence belonging to the adverse <s>Śānta</s> (quiescent) [rasa], and the <s>Nirveda</s> (world-weariness) thus manifested is a <s>vyabhicārin</s> that has been incorporated.
"Even when my dear husband is humbled, even when he is beyond the path of my eyes, even when he is free from restraint, even when separated from experience,
Even in dreams, the bride considers [going to] the forest as a complete renunciation, nothing more." (328)
Here, complete renunciation and going to the forest are <s>anubhāvas</s> of <s>Śānta</s> (quiescent rasa).
If the going to the forest is a pretext for fetching firewood and the like, for the purpose of enjoyment, then it is not a fault.
(7) <s>Dīpti</s> (illumination) again [occurs] through repetition, as in the lament of <s>Rati</s> in the <s>Kumārasaṃbhava</s>.

children.text: (8) akāṇḍe prathanaṃ yathā veṇīsaṃhāre dvitīye 'ṅke 'nekavīrakṣaye pravṛtte bhānumatyā saha duyārdhenasya śṛṅgāravarṇanam //
children.translated_text: (8) Untimely expansion, as in the second act of the <s>Veṇīsaṃhāra</s>, where while the destruction of many heroes is underway, there is a description of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment) with <s>Bhānumatī</s> through a half-verse of <s>Duryodhana</s>.

children.text: (9) akāṇḍe chedo yathā vīracarite dvitīye 'ṅke rāghavabhārgavayordhārādhirūḍhaṃ vīrarase "kaṅkaṇamojanāya gacchāmi'; iti rāghavasyoktau //
children.translated_text: (9) Untimely cessation, as in the second act of the <s>Vīracarita</s>, where the <s>vīra rasa</s> (heroic sentiment) between <s>Rāghava</s> and <s>Bhārgava</s> has reached its climax, and <s>Rāghava</s> says "I go to put on the bracelet."
(10) Excessively elaborate description of a subordinate element (<s>aṅga</s>),
as [the description] of <s>Hayagrīva</s> in the <s>Hayagrīvavadha</s>.
(11) Failure to follow through on the principal element (<s>aṅgin</s>),

children.text: yathā ratnāvalyāṃ caturthe 'ṅke bābhravyāgamane sāgarikāyā vismṛtiḥ //
children.translated_text: as in the fourth act of the <s>Ratnāvalī</s>, where <s>Sāgarikā</s> is forgotten upon the arrival of <s>Bābhravya</s>.

children.text:
(12) prakṛtayo divyā adivyā divyādivyāśva vīraraudraśṛṅgāraśāntarasapradhānā dhīrodāttadhīroddhatadhīralalitadhīrapraśāntāḥ, uttamādhamamadhmamāśva /
tatra ratihāsaśokādbhutāni, adivyāttamaprakṛtivat divyeṣvapi /
kiṃ tu ratiḥ saṃbhogaśṛṅgārarūpāṃ, uttamadevatāviṣayā na varṇanīyā /
children.translated_text: However, <s>rati</s> (love) in the form of <s>saṃbhoga śṛṅgāra</s> (love-in-union), when directed toward supreme deities, should not be described.
For describing that is as utterly improper as describing the sexual union of one's parents.

children.text: krodhaṃ prabho saṃhara saṃhareti yāvadgiraḥ khe marutāṃ caranti /
children.translated_text: "Withdraw your anger, O Lord, withdraw it!" — while such words of the <s>Maruts</s> (wind gods) resound in the sky,
that fire born from the eye of <s>Bhava</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) reduced <s>Madana</s> (the god of love) to ashes. (329)

(12) The characters (<s>prakṛti</s>) are divine, non-divine, and mixed divine-and-non-divine; they have the <s>vīra</s> (heroic), <s>raudra</s> (furious), <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic), and <s>śānta</s> (quiescent) sentiments as predominant; they are <s>dhīrodātta</s> (steadfast-exalted), <s>dhīroddhata</s> (steadfast-haughty), <s>dhīralalita</s> (steadfast-graceful), and <s>dhīrapraśānta</s> (steadfast-tranquil); and they are superior, inferior, and middling. Among these, <s>rati</s> (love), <s>hāsa</s> (laughter), <s>śoka</s> (grief), and <s>adbhuta</s> (wonder) [apply]; in non-divine superior characters as in divine ones.

children.text:
ityuktavat bhrukuṭhyādivikāravarjitaḥ krodhaḥ sadyaḥphaladaḥ svargapātālagaganasamudrollaṅghanādyutsāhaśva divyeṣveva /
adivyeṣu tu yāvadavadānaṃ prasiddhamucitaṃ vā tāvadevopanibanddhavyam /
adhikaṃ nibadhyamānamasatyapratibhāsena "nāyakavadvartitavyaṃ na pratināyakavat'; ityupadeśe na paryavasyet /

children.translated_text: In mixed divine-and-non-divine [characters], both ways [apply].

Just as the reversal of the propriety stated above for divine and other characters applies to <s>dhīrodātta</s> and other [hero-types], so too describing them otherwise is a defect (<s>viparyaya</s>).

children.text: tatrabhavan bhagavannityuttamena na, adhamena muniprabhṛtau na rājādau bhaṭṭāraketi nottameti nottamena rājādau prakṛtiviparyayāpattervācyam /
children.translated_text: There, [the address] "Bhagavan" is by the superior [form], not by "Bhaṭṭāraka" for a sage etc., nor "Uttama" for a king etc. — [otherwise] there would be the fault of reversal of character-type. This should be stated.
Similarly, what is appropriate regarding the dress, behavior, etc. of [characters according to their] country, time, age, caste, and so forth should alone be depicted.

As stated [in this verse], anger devoid of distortions like furrowing of brows, yielding immediate results, and valor such as leaping over heaven, the netherworld, sky, and ocean — these belong to divine characters alone. But for non-divine characters, only as much as is well-known and appropriate should be depicted. If more is depicted, due to the appearance of unreality, it would not conform to the instruction that "one should act like the hero, not like the antagonist."
(13) Description of what is not a subordinate element and does not serve the <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment),

children.text: yathā karpūramañjaryāṃ nāyikayā svātmanā ca kṛtaṃ vasantavarṇanamanādṛtya bandivarṇitasya rājñā praśaṃsanam //
children.translated_text: as in the <s>Karpūramañjarī</s>, where the king praises the spring-description composed by a bard, disregarding the one composed by the heroine herself.
"Such [are they]" — thus [he says].
Description of the hero's anger etc. caused by the heroine's kick and the like.

children.text: uktaṃ hi dhvanikṛtā "anaucityādṛte nānyad rasabhaṅgasya kāraṇam /
children.translated_text: For the author of the <s>Dhvani</s> [treatise] has said: "There is no other cause for the destruction of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) than impropriety (<s>anaucitya</s>);
propriety (<s>aucitya</s>) in composition is the supreme secret (<s>upaniṣat</s>) of <s>rasa</s>."
Thus.
Now it is stated that in some cases even these [faults] are not faults. (Sūtra 83)
The <s>sañcārin</s> (transitory emotion) is sometimes not a fault even when expressed by its own name,

children.text: yathā autsukyena kṛtatvarā sahabhuvā vyāvartamānā hriyā taistairbandhuvadhūjanasya vacanairnītābhimukhyaṃ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: as in: "Turning back with haste born of <s>autsukya</s> (eager longing), being restrained by her companion <s>Hrī</s> (modesty), brought face to face again by various words of the kinswomen,

children.text: dṛṣṭvāgre varamāttasādhvasarasā gaurī nave saṃgame saṃrohatpulakā hareṇa hasatā śliṣṭā śivāyāstu vaḥ // 330 //
children.translated_text: seeing the bridegroom before her and seized by <s>sādhvasa rasa</s> (tremulous agitation), <s>Gaurī</s> in [that] new union, with rising goosebumps, was embraced by <s>Hara</s> who was laughing — may she be for your welfare!" (330)
Here, unlike the word <s>autsukya</s> (eager longing), its <s>anubhāva</s> (consequent expression) does not produce such [an adverse] apprehension.

children.text: ata eva "dūrādutsukam'; ityādau vrīḍāpremādyanubhāvānāṃ vivalitatvādīnāmivapotsukatvānubhāvasya sahasāprasaraṇādirūpasya tathā- pratipattikāritvābhāvādutsukamiti kṛtam //
children.translated_text: Therefore, in [expressions like] "longing from afar" and the like, just as the <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents) of modesty, love, etc. such as becoming visibly agitated do not [harm the rasa], so too the <s>anubhāva</s> of eagerness — whose nature is a sudden rushing forth — does not cause such [adverse] apprehension; hence [the word] "eager" suffices.
(Sūtra 84)
The expression of a <s>sañcārin</s> (transitory emotion) that is contradictory [to the dominant rasa] but is being sublated, conduces to merit. (63)
Expression as something being sublated is not merely non-faulty — it actually nourishes the predominant <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: yathā "kvākāryaṃ śaśalakṣmaṇaḥ kva ca kulam'; ityādau // 331 //
children.translated_text: As in: "Where is the deed of the hare-marked [moon]? And where is [this noble] family?" and so on. (331)

children.text: atra vitarkādiṣu, udgateṣvapi cintāyāmeva viśrāntiriti prakṛtarasaparipoṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, among deliberation (<s>vitarka</s>) and other [transitory emotions], even when they arise, they ultimately rest in anxiety (<s>cintā</s>) alone — thus the predominant <s>rasa</s> is nourished.

children.text: pāṇḍu kṣāmaṃ vadanaṃ hṛdayaṃ sarasaṃ tavālasaṃ ca vapuḥ /
children.translated_text: "Your face is pale and emaciated, your heart is moist, and your body is languid;
O friend, [all this] declares emphatically that [you have] the hereditary disease (<s>kṣetriya roga</s>) within your heart." (332)
In verses like this, the commonality of pallor and the like [between love-sickness and disease] means there is no contradiction.

children.text: satyaṃ manoramā rāmāḥ satyaṃ ramyā vibhūtayaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Truly, women are delightful; truly, riches are enjoyable;
but life is as fickle as the rolling sidelong glances of an intoxicated woman." (333)
Here the first half [of the verse] is stated precisely as something being sublated.

children.text: jīvitādapi, adhikamapāṅgabhaṅgasyāsthiratvamiti prasiddhabhahguropamānatayopāttaṃ śāntameva puṣṇāti na punaḥ śṛṅgārasyātra pratītistadaṅgāpratipatteḥ /
children.translated_text: The instability of sidelong glances, being even greater than [the instability of] life, is taken up through the well-known fragile metaphor, and nourishes only the <s>śānta rasa</s> (quiescent sentiment); the <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment) is not apprehended here, because its subordinate elements are not grasped.
Nor is the explanation here that it serves to orient the student [toward renunciation], since there is no immediate connection between <s>śānta</s> and <s>śṛṅgāra</s>.
Nor does it merely produce poetic beauty through another <s>rasa</s> or mere cessation [of one rasa], for such is not the case.
(Sūtra 85)

children.text: āśrayaikye viruddho yaḥ sa kāryo bhinnasaṃśrayaḥ /
children.translated_text: When there is identity of locus, the contradictory [rasa] should be assigned to a different locus;
a <s>rasa</s> that stands in immediate succession [to a contradictory one should be] separated by an intervening <s>rasa</s>. (64)

children.text: vīrabhayānakayorekāśrayatvena virodha iti pratipakṣagatatvena bhayānako niveśayitavyaḥ /
śāntaśṛṅgārayostu nairantaryeṇa virodha iti rasāntaramantare kāryam yathā nāgānande śāntasya jīmūtavāhanasya "aho gītam aho vāditram'; ityadbhutamantarniveśya malayavatīṃ pratiśṛhgāro nibaddhaḥ /
children.translated_text: But since the contradiction between <s>śānta</s> (quiescent) and <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic) is one of immediate succession, another <s>rasa</s> should be interposed between them; as in the <s>Nāgānanda</s>, where for the tranquil <s>Jīmūtavāhana</s>, the <s>adbhuta</s> (wondrous) is interposed through "Ah, what singing! Ah, what music!" and then the <s>śṛṅgāra</s> toward <s>Malayavatī</s> is composed.

children.text: na paraṃ prabandhe yāvadekasminnapi vākye rasāntaravyavadhinā virodho nivartate /
children.translated_text: Not only in the whole composition, but even within a single sentence, the contradiction is removed by the intervention of another <s>rasa</s>.
As in: "Smeared with abundant dust, their arms fragrant with the pollen of fresh <s>pārijāta</s> garlands,
tightly embraced by the <s>Śivās</s> (jackals/auspicious ones), their arm-interstices clasped by celestial women" — (334)
Since there is contradiction between the <s>vīra</s> (heroic) and <s>bhayānaka</s> (terrible) when they share a single locus, the <s>bhayānaka</s> should be placed in the opposing party.
"fanned by the blood-stained, quivering wings of carrion-eating birds,
and [also] fanned with fragrant sandal-water sprinklings and garments of wish-fulfilling creepers" — (334a)
"Seated upon the couches of aerial chariots, at that time filled with curiosity,
the heroes, being pointed out by the fingers of women, beheld their own fallen bodies." (335)
Here, between the <s>bībhatsa</s> (disgusting) and <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic), the <s>vīra rasa</s> (heroic sentiment) is interposed. (Sūtra 86)
Even a contradictory [rasa] when being recalled, or intended through similarity,

children.text: aṅginyaṅgatvamāptau yau tau na duṣṭau parasparam //65//
children.translated_text: or when the principal and subordinate relationship is attained — those two do not vitiate each other. (65)
"This is that [very hand] which used to loosen the girdle, which pressed against the full breasts,
which touched the navel, thighs, and hips, and which loosened the knot of the undergarment." (336)

children.text: etat bhūriśravasaḥ samarabhuvi patitaṃ hastamālokya tadvadhūrabhidadhau /
children.translated_text: This was said by the wife of <s>Bhūriśravas</s> upon seeing his hand fallen on the battlefield.
Here, the recollection of the former state, though an element of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, nourishes <s>karuṇa</s> (the pathetic sentiment).

children.text: dantakṣatāni karajaiśva vipāṭitāni prodbhinnasāndrapulake bhavataḥ śarīre /
children.translated_text: "The tooth-marks and nail-scratches on your body, with its dense goosebumps standing erect,
were given by a lioness with passionate heart, and were gazed upon with longing even by the sages." (337)

children.text: atra kāmukasya dantakṣatādīni yathā camatkārakārīṇi tathā jinasya /
children.translated_text: Here, the tooth-marks and the like produce the same aesthetic delight (<s>camatkāra</s>) for the <s>Jina</s> as for a lover.

children.text: yathā vā paraḥ śṛṅgārī tadavalokanātsaspṛhastadvat etaddṛśo munaya iti sāmyavivakṣā //
children.translated_text: Or, just as one who is amorous [would delight in them], so too the sages who behold them become desirous — thus the intention is similarity.

children.text: krāmantyaḥ kṣatakomalāṅguligaladraktaiḥ sadarbhāḥ sthalīḥ pādaiḥ pātitayāvakairiva galadbāṣpāmbudhautānanā /
children.translated_text: "Treading the ground strewn with <s>darbha</s> grass with feet whose tender toes drip blood, their faces washed by flowing tears,

children.text: bhītā bhartṛkarāvalambitakarāstvacchatrunāryo 'dhunā dāvāgriṃ parito bhramanti punarapyudyadvivāhā iva // 338 //
children.translated_text: frightened, their hands clinging to their husbands' hands — your enemy's women now wander about the forest fire, looking again as if they were newly wed brides." (338)
Here, in this flattering verse, <s>rati</s> (love) directed toward the king is apprehended.

children.text: tatra karuṇa iva śaṅgāro 'pyaṅgamiti tayorna virodhaḥ /
children.translated_text: There, just as <s>karuṇa</s> (the pathetic) is a subordinate element, so too is <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic) — hence there is no contradiction between them.

children.text: yathā ehi gaccha patottiṣṭa vada maunaṃ samācara /
children.translated_text: As in: "Come! Go! Fall! Rise! Speak! Observe silence!
Thus do the wealthy sport with supplicants who are seized by the grip of hope." (339)

children.text: ityatra, ehīti krīḍhanti gaccheti krīḍantīti krīḍanāpekṣayorāgamanagamanayorna virodhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, 'come' means 'they sport,' 'go' means 'they sport' — with respect to the play, the coming and going are not contradictory.

children.text: kṣipto hastāvalagraḥ prasabhamabhihato 'pyādadānoṃ'śukāntaṃ gṛhṇan keśeṣvapāstaśvaraṇanipatito nekṣitaḥ saṃbhrameṇa /
children.translated_text: "Pushed away while grasping [her] hand, struck forcibly yet seizing the edge of [her] garment, grasping [her] hair yet cast off, fallen at [her] feet yet not looked at in [her] agitation,

children.text: āliṅgan yo 'vadhūtastripurayuvatibhiḥ sāśrunetrotpalābhiḥ kāmīvārdrāparādhaḥ sa dahatu duritaṃ śāṃbhavo vaḥ śarāgniḥ // 340 //
children.translated_text: embracing yet shaken off by the women of <s>Tripura</s> whose lotus-eyes were filled with tears — may that fire of <s>Śambhu</s>'s arrow, like a lover guilty of a fresh offense, burn away your sins!" (340)

children.text: ityatra tripuraripuprabhāvātiśayasya karuṇo 'ṅgam tasya tu śṛṅgāraḥ, tathāpi na karuṇe viśrāntiriti tasyāṅgataiva /
children.translated_text: Here, <s>karuṇa</s> (the pathetic) is a subordinate element serving to highlight the supremacy of the destroyer of <s>Tripura</s>, and <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic) is subordinate to that; yet the apprehension does not rest in <s>karuṇa</s> — hence it remains subordinate.

children.text: athavā prāk yathā kāmuka ācarati sma tathā śarāgniriti śṛṅgārapoṣitena karuṇena mukhya evārtha upodbalyate /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, just as a lover formerly behaved, so does the arrow-fire — thus by the <s>karuṇa</s> nourished through <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, the principal meaning itself is strengthened.
For it has been said: "A subordinate quality, having refined itself,
attains the status of the principal; for it functions in great service to the principal."
Thus.

children.text: prāk pratipāditasya rasasya rasāntareṇa na virodhaḥ, nāpyaṅgāṅgibhāvo bhavati, iti rasaśabdenātra sthāyibhāva upalakṣyate //
children.translated_text: A <s>rasa</s> established earlier is not contradicted by a subsequent <s>rasa</s>, nor does the principal-subordinate relationship arise [between them]; here the word '<s>rasa</s>' figuratively denotes the <s>sthāyibhāva</s> (permanent emotional state).

children.text: iti kāvyaprakāśe doṣadarśano nāma saptama ullāsaḥ //7//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the seventh <s>ullāsa</s> (chapter), named 'Observation of Faults' (<s>Doṣadarśana</s>), in the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>. (7)
Now begins the eighth <s>ullāsa</s> (chapter).
Having thus described the faults, [the author] speaks of the distinction between <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) and <s>alaṃkāras</s> (ornaments). (Sūtra 87)
Those properties of <s>rasa</s> (the aesthetic sentiment), the principal [element], which are causes of its excellence — like valor and other [qualities] of the self —
and which are of stable nature, are [called] <s>guṇas</s> (qualities). (66)

children.text: ātmana eva hi yathā śauryādayo nākārasya tathā rasasyaiva mādhuryādayo guṇā na varṇānām /
children.translated_text: Just as valor and other [qualities] belong to the self alone, not to [its external] form, so too <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness) and other <s>guṇas</s> belong to <s>rasa</s> alone, not to the words (<s>varṇas</s>).

children.text: kvacitu śauryādisamucitasyākāramahacvāderdarśanāt "ākāra evāsya śūraḥ'; ityādervyavahārādanyatrāśūre 'pi vitatākṛtitvamātreṇa "śūraḥ'; iti kvāpi śūre 'pi mūrtilāghavamātreṇa "aśūraḥ'; iti, aviśrāntapratītayo yathā vyavaharanti tadvanmadhurādivyañjakasukumārādivarṇānāṃ madhurādivyavahārapravṛtteramadhurādirasāṅgānāṃ varṇānāṃ saukumāryādimātreṇa mādhuryādi madhurādirasopakaraṇānāṃ teṣāmasaukumāryāderamādhuryādi rasaparyantaviśrāntapratītivandhyā vyavaharanti, ata eva mādhuryādayo rasadharmāḥ samucitairvarṇairvyajyante na tu varṇamātrāśrayāḥ /
children.translated_text: However, since sometimes valor and the like are seen associated with [an impressive] form and stature, the usage "his very appearance is heroic" arises; and elsewhere, by mere extended physique, even a non-hero is [called] "heroic," while sometimes even a hero, by mere smallness of frame, [is called] "unheroic" — such usages do not lead to settled apprehension. Similarly, because words that are suggestive of sweetness etc. — being soft and the like — give rise to the usage of "sweet" etc., while words that are elements of non-sweet rasas, by mere softness alone, [are called] "sweet" etc., and words that are accessories of sweet rasas, by mere non-softness, [are called] "non-sweet" etc. — such usages are barren of settled apprehension that rests in <s>rasa</s>. Therefore, <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness) and other qualities, being properties of <s>rasa</s>, are manifested through appropriate words, but do not reside in the words alone.
How they serve as manifestors will be illustrated [below].
(Sūtra 88)
Those which sometimes assist that [rasa] when it is present, through the medium of its subordinate elements (<s>aṅgas</s>) —
like necklaces and the like [adorn the body], those are the <s>alaṃkāras</s> (ornaments): <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration), <s>upamā</s> (simile), and so forth. (67)

children.text: ye vācakavācyalakṣaṇāṅgātiśayamukhena mukhyaṃ rasaṃ saṃbhavinamupakurvanti te kaṇṭhādyaṅgānāmutkarṣādhānadvāreṇa śarīriṇo 'pi, upakārakā hārādaya ivālaṃkārāḥ /

children.translated_text: But where there is no <s>rasa</s>, they are confined to mere ingenuity of expression.
And sometimes they do not assist [the rasa] even when it is present.

children.text: yathākramamudāharaṇāni-- apasāraya ghanasāraṃ kuru hāraṃ dūra eva kiṃ kamalaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Examples in order — "Put away the camphor, keep the necklace at a distance, what use are lotuses?

children.text: alamalamāli mṛṇālaiḥ iti vadati divāniśaṃ bālā // 341 //
children.translated_text: Enough, enough with lotus stalks, O friend!" — thus speaks the young woman day and night. (341)

Those which assist the principal <s>rasa</s> that is capable of arising, through the excellence of the subordinate elements characterized as the expressed and the expressive — just as necklaces and the like [assist] the embodied soul through enhancing the excellence of the limbs like the neck — are <s>alaṃkāras</s> (ornaments).

children.text: ityādau vācakamukhena manorāgastīvraṃ viṣamiva visarpatyavirataṃ pramāthī nirdhūmaṃ jvalati vidhutaḥ pāvaka iva /
children.translated_text: In this and similar [verses], through the medium of the expressive: "The passion of the mind spreads ceaselessly like poison, overpowering; it burns like a smokeless fire when fanned;

children.text: hinasti pratyaṅgaṃ jvara iva garīyānita ito na māṃ trātuṃ tātaḥ prabhavati na cāmbā na bhavatī // 342 //
children.translated_text: it afflicts every limb like a severe fever — neither my father is able to save me, nor my mother, nor you, my lady." (342)
In this and similar [verses], through the medium of the expressed, the <s>alaṃkāras</s> (ornaments) serve the <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: citte vihaṭṭadi ṇa ṭuṭṭadi sā guṇesuṃ sejjāsu loṭṭadi visaṭṭadi dimmuhesuṃ /
children.translated_text: "[My heart] breaks in the mind, yet does not break; it rolls on the bed, yet comes apart in dark moments;

children.text: bolammi vaṭṭadi pavaṭṭadi kavvabandhe jhāṇeṇa ṭuṭṭadi ciraṃ taruṇī taraṭṭī // 343 //
children.translated_text: it turns in speech, yet revolves in poetic composition; through meditation it breaks for long" — [thus speaks] the young woman in agitation. (343)
In this and similar [verses], through the expressive alone —

children.text: mitre kvāpi gate saroruhavane baddhānane tāmyati krandatsu bhramareṣu vīkṣya dayitāsannaṃ puraḥ sārasam /
children.translated_text: When a friend had gone somewhere to a lotus pond, and [the <s>cakravāka</s> bird] was suffocating with its face confined, and the bees were crying, seeing a <s>sārasa</s> (crane) near the beloved before it,

children.text: cakrāhvena viyoginā bisalatā nāsvāditā nojjhitā kaṇṭhe kevalamargaleva nihitā jīvasya nirgacchataḥ // 344 //
children.translated_text: By the one separated [from its mate], the <s>cakrāhva</s> (cakravāka bird), a lotus stalk was neither tasted nor abandoned; it was merely placed on the neck like a bolt, of the life that was departing. (344)
In such cases, only the literal meaning is expressed, not <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment).

children.text: atra bisalatā na jīvaṃ roddhuṃ kṣameti prakṛtānanuguṇopamā //
children.translated_text: Here the lotus stalk is not capable of restraining the life-breath—thus it is a simile incongruent with the subject matter.
And this itself is the distinction between <s>guṇa</s> (quality) and <s>alaṃkāra</s> (ornament).

children.text: evaṃ ca "samavāyavṛcyā śauryādayaḥ saṃyogavacyātu hārādaya ityastu guṇālaṃkārāṇāṃ bhedaḥ, ojaḥprabhṛtīnāmanuprāsopamādīnāṃ cobhayeṣāmapi samabāyavṛcyā sthitiriti gaḍḍalikāpravāheṇaivaiṣāṃ bhedaḥ" ityabhidhānamasat //
children.translated_text: Thus, the statement that "the qualities like valor are expressed through inherent relation (<s>samavāyavṛttyā</s>), while ornaments like <s>hāra</s> are expressed through conjunction (<s>saṃyogavṛttyā</s>)—this is the difference between <s>guṇas</s> and <s>alaṃkāras</s>; both <s>ojas</s> and the rest as well as <s>anuprāsa</s>, <s>upamā</s> and the rest abide through inherent relation, so their distinction follows merely by the momentum of convention"—is false.

children.text: yadapyuktam "kāvyaśobhāyāḥ kartāro dharmā guṇāstadatiśayahetavastvalaṃkārāḥ" iti tadapi na yuktam /
children.translated_text: What has also been stated—"The qualities (<s>guṇas</s>) are those properties that produce the beauty of poetry, while the <s>alaṃkāras</s> are the causes of the excellence of those"—that too is not correct.

children.text: yataḥ kiṃ samastairguṇaiḥ kāvyavyavahāraḥ, uta katipayaiḥ /
children.translated_text: For is the designation 'poetry' dependent on all the <s>guṇas</s> together, or on only some of them?

children.text: yadi samastaiḥ, tatkathamasamastaguṇā gauḍī pāñcālī ca rītiḥ kāvyasyātmā /
children.translated_text: If on all of them together, then how can the <s>Gauḍī</s> and <s>Pāñcālī</s> <s>rītis</s> (styles), which do not possess all the <s>guṇas</s>, be the soul of poetry?

children.text: ata katipayaiḥ, tataḥ adrāvatra prajvalatyagniruccaiḥ prājyaḥ prodyannullasatyeṣa dhūmaḥ // 345 //
children.translated_text: If on only some, then [consider]: "The fire blazes aloft here brilliantly, not sluggishly, and this smoke rises abundantly." (345)
In such cases, even when <s>guṇas</s> like <s>ojas</s> and the rest are present, the designation 'poetry' is obtained.
"Attainment of heaven by this very body, O lady of beautiful complexion!
The juice of her lip utterly surpasses <s>sudhā</s> (nectar)." (346)
In such cases, <s>viśeṣokti</s> (specific statement) and <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast) are the activators of the designation 'poetry,' independent of <s>guṇas</s>.
Now he states the varieties of <s>guṇas</s> (<s>sūtra</s> 89):
<s>Mādhurya</s> (sweetness), <s>ojas</s> (vigor), and <s>prasāda</s> (clarity)—these three are they, not ten.
He states their definitions in order (<s>sūtra</s> 90):
The quality of producing delight is <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness); in <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment) it causes <s>druti</s> (melting). (68)
In <s>śṛṅgāra</s>—that is, in <s>saṃbhoga</s> (union).
<s>Druti</s> means a state as if melted.
However, the quality of being pleasant to hear belongs to <s>ojas</s> and <s>prasāda</s> as well.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 91)
In <s>karuṇa</s> (pathetic sentiment), in <s>vipralambha</s> (separation), and in <s>śānta</s> (quiescent sentiment), it is endowed with special intensity,
because it causes extreme <s>druti</s> (melting).
(<s>Sūtra</s> 92)
<s>Ojas</s> (vigor) is the cause of expansion through luminosity of the self; it has its abode in <s>vīra rasa</s> (heroic sentiment). (69)
<s>Ojas</s> is that which produces luminosity in the form of expansion of the mind.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 93)
In <s>bībhatsa</s> (disgusting) and <s>raudra</s> (furious) sentiments, its abundance increases progressively.
<s>Ojas</s> is greater in <s>bībhatsa</s> than in <s>vīra</s>, and still greater in <s>raudra</s>.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 94)
Like fire [consuming] dry fuel, like clear water, that which suddenly— (70)
(<s>Sūtra</s> 95)
<s>Prasāda</s> (clarity) is that which pervades the other [i.e., the mind]; it has its established place everywhere.
"The other" means—
What is pervaded here is the mind.
"Everywhere" means—
In all <s>rasas</s> (sentiments) and in all compositions.
The operation of these [<s>guṇas</s>] in words and meanings is understood through the operation of <s>guṇa</s> (quality). (71)
"Through the operation of <s>guṇa</s>" means through figurative usage (<s>upacāra</s>).
"Of those" means of the <s>guṇas</s>.
As in the case of valor being attributed to bodily form.
Why only three and not ten? He says (<s>sūtra</s> 96):
Some are subsumed within these; others are established through the absence of <s>doṣas</s> (faults);

children.text: anye bhajanti doṣatvaṃ kutracit na tato daśa //72//
children.translated_text: Yet others assume the nature of <s>doṣas</s> in certain contexts—therefore not ten. (72)

children.text:
bahūnāmapi padānāmekapadavadbhāsanātmā yaḥ śleṣaḥ, yaśvārohāvarohakramarūpaḥ samādhiḥ, yā ca vikaṭatvalakṣaṇā, udāratā yaśvaujomiśritaśaithilyātmā prasādaḥ, teṣāmojasyantarbhāvaḥ /
pṛthakpadatvarūpaṃ mādhuryaṃ bhaṅgyā sākṣādupāttam /
prasādenārthavyaktirgṛhītā /

children.translated_text: <s>Samatā</s> (uniformity), whose nature is absence of variation in the path, is sometimes a <s>doṣa</s> (fault).

children.text: tathāhi "mātaṅgāḥ kimu valgitaiḥ'; ityādau siṃhābhidhāne masṛṇamārgatyāgau guṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: For example, in "Are the elephants [impressive] merely by their gait?" and such cases, in the description of a lion, smoothness and deviation of path are <s>guṇas</s> (qualities).

Since <s>kaṣṭatva</s> (harshness) and <s>grāmyatva</s> (vulgarity) are designated as faults, by their removal, <s>saukumārya</s> (delicacy) in the form of non-harshness and <s>kānti</s> (brilliance) in the form of <s>aujjvalya</s> (lustre) are accepted.
Thus, the word-qualities are not ten.

<s>Śleṣa</s> (cohesion), whose nature is making many words appear as one; <s>samādhi</s> (appropriateness), which consists of a pattern of ascent and descent; the characteristic called <s>vikaṭatā</s> (roughness); and <s>prasāda</s> consisting of <s>udāratā</s> (elevation) mixed with <s>ojas</s> and looseness—these are subsumed under <s>ojas</s>. <s>Mādhurya</s> (sweetness) in the form of individual words has been directly adopted through implication. The manifestation of meaning is covered by <s>prasāda</s>.
"Constructing a sentence in the sense of a word, and expressing a word in the sense of a sentence,
<s>prauḍhi</s> (boldness), <s>vyāsa</s> (expansion) and <s>samāsa</s> (compression), and its purposefulness—

children.text:
'; iti yā prauḍhiḥ oja ityuktaṃ tat vaicitryamātram na guṇaḥ /
tadabhāve 'pi kāvyavyavahārapravṛtteḥ /
apuṣṭārthatvādhikapadatvānavīkṛtatvāmaṅgalarūpāślīlagrāmyāṇāṃ nirākaraṇena ca sābhiprāyatvarūpamojaḥ, arthavaimalyātmā prasādaḥ, uktivaicitryarūpaṃ mādhuryam apāruṣyarupaṃ saukumāryam agrāmyatvarupā, udāratā ca svīkṛtāni /
abhidhāsyamānasvabhāvoktyalaṃkāreṇa rasadhvaniguṇībhūtavyahgyābhyāṃ ca vastusvabhāvasphuṭatvarūpā, arthavyaktiḥ, dīptarasatvarupā kāntiśva svīkṛtā /

children.translated_text: <s>Śleṣa</s> (cohesion), whose nature is composition characterized by sequence, complexity, proportion, and fitness—is also merely variety.
<s>Samatā</s> (uniformity), whose nature is absence of disparity, is merely the absence of <s>doṣa</s> (fault), not a positive <s>guṇa</s>.
What sane person would express something other than what is relevant in another's topic?

children.text: arthasyāyoneranyacchāyāyonervā yadi na bhavati darśanaṃ tatkathaṃ kāvyam ityarthadṛṣṭirūpaḥ samādhirapi na guṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: If there is no perception of the meaning from its proper source or from another source of appearance, then how can it be poetry? Thus <s>samādhi</s> (propriety), which is the form of perceiving meaning, is also not a <s>guṇa</s>.

The <s>prauḍhi</s> that has been described is merely variety, as stated under <s>ojas</s>—it is not a separate <s>guṇa</s>, since the designation 'poetry' applies even in its absence. And by the removal of <s>apuṣṭārthatva</s> (unsupported meaning), <s>adhikapadatva</s> (excess of words), <s>anavīkṛtatva</s> (lack of refinement), <s>amaṅgala</s> (inauspiciousness), <s>aślīla</s> (impropriety), and <s>grāmya</s> (vulgarity), purposefulness is subsumed under <s>ojas</s>; clarity of meaning under <s>prasāda</s>; variety of expression under <s>mādhurya</s>; delicacy (<s>saukumārya</s>) in the form of non-harshness; and <s>udāratā</s> (elevation) are accepted. Through the figure of <s>svabhāvokti</s> (natural description) to be discussed later, and through <s>rasadhvani</s> (suggestive sentiment) and <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (subordinated suggestion), <s>arthavyakti</s> (clarity of meaning) in the form of manifest nature of things, and <s>kānti</s> (brilliance) in the form of luminous sentiment, are accepted.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 97)
Therefore, the meaning-qualities (<s>arthaguṇas</s>) need not be stated separately. "<s>Vācyāḥ</s>" means "to be stated."
(<s>Sūtra</s> 98)
Phonemes (<s>varṇas</s>), compounds (<s>samāsa</s>), and composition (<s>racanā</s>) are considered their means of expression. (73)
And those that have been described as word-qualities (<s>śabdaguṇas</s>)—
Which [expresses] which? He says (<s>sūtra</s> 99):

children.text: mūrdhni vargāntyagāḥ sparśā aṭavargā raṇau laghū /
children.translated_text: Consonants occurring at the head and end of groups (<s>vargas</s>), the <s>aṭavarga</s> (dental-labial group), <s>ra</s> and <s>ṇa</s>, short [vowels],
absence of compounds or moderate compounds, and such composition—these [are the means of expressing] <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness). (74)

children.text: ṭaṭhaḍaḍhavarjitāḥ kādayo māntāḥ śirasi nijavargāntyayuktāḥ, tathā rephaṇakārau hrasvāntaritāviti varṇāḥ samāsābhāvo madhyamaḥ samāso veti samāsaḥ, tathā mādhuryavatī padāntarayogena racanā mādhuryasya vyañjikā /
children.translated_text: Excepting <s>ṭa</s>, <s>ṭha</s>, <s>ḍa</s>, <s>ḍha</s>, the consonants from <s>ka</s> to <s>ma</s> joined with the finals of their own groups at the head [of words]; likewise <s>repha</s> and <s>ṇakāra</s> separated by short vowels—these are the phonemes. Absence of compounds or moderate compounds constitutes the compound [rule]. And composition endowed with <s>mādhurya</s> through the connection of individual words is the means of expressing <s>mādhurya</s>.
Example: "Those limbs, resembling the sport of <s>Anaṅga</s> (the bodiless god of love), made captive by the graceful movements of her whose body is the embodiment of beauty,

children.text: kurvanti yūnāṃ sahasā yathaitāḥ svāntāni śāntāparacintanāni // 347 //
children.translated_text: suddenly render the hearts of young men free from thoughts of anything else." (347)
(<s>Sūtra</s> 100)
The combination of the first and third [consonants of a group] with the finals, with <s>repha</s>, of two equal [consonants];

children.text: ṭādiḥ śaṣau vṛttidairdhyaṃ gumpha uddhata ojasi //75//
children.translated_text: The <s>ṭa</s>-group, <s>śa</s> and <s>ṣa</s>, length of compounds, rugged composition, and forceful [arrangement]—these [express] <s>ojas</s> (vigor). (75)

children.text: vargaprathamatṛtīyābhyāmantyayoḥ, dvitīyacaturthayoḥ, repheṇa, adha upari, ubhayatra vā yasya kasyacit tulyayoḥ, tena tasyaiva saṃbandhaḥ ṭavargo 'rthāt ṇakāravarjaḥ śakāraṣakārau dīrghasamāsaḥ, vikaṭā saṃghaṭanā, ojasaḥ /
children.translated_text: With the first and third of a group along with the finals, with the second and fourth, with <s>repha</s>, below and above, or in both positions, of any two equal [consonants]—hence, the <s>ṭa</s>-group except <s>ṇa</s>, <s>śa</s> and <s>ṣa</s>, long compounds, and rugged composition are [the means of expressing] <s>ojas</s>.
Example: "<s>mūrdhnāmudvṛttakṛttet</s>" and so forth. (348)
(<s>Sūtra</s> 101)
That by which, merely upon hearing the words, comprehension of meaning arises—

children.text: sādhāraṇaḥ samagrāṇāṃ sa prasādo guṇo mataḥ //76//
children.translated_text: That which is common to all [sentiments] is considered the quality called <s>prasāda</s> (clarity). (76)
"Of all" means of all <s>rasas</s> (sentiments) and all compositions.

children.text: udāharaṇam parimlānaṃ pīnastanajaghanasaṃgādubhayata- stanormadhyasyāntaḥ parimilanamaprāpya haritam /
children.translated_text: Example: "Wilted from the pressure of full breasts and hips on both sides, the middle of the chest not having attained freshness within,

children.text: idaṃ vyastanyāsaṃ śrlathabhujalatākṣepavalanaiḥ kṛśāhgyāḥ saṃtāpaṃ vadati bisinīpatraśayanam // 349 //
children.translated_text: this bed of lotus leaves, through the tossing and turning of slack vine-like arms, speaks of the anguish of the slender-limbed one." (349)
Although composition and the rest are dependent on <s>guṇas</s>, nevertheless (<s>sūtra</s> 102):
Through propriety (<s>aucitya</s>) with respect to the speaker, the subject matter, and the literary work, in various contexts,
a different arrangement of composition, compound style, and phonemes is also desired. (77)
In some cases, disregarding the subject matter and the literary work, composition and the rest follow solely from the propriety of the speaker.

As in: "That slow, deep sound of <s>Mandara</s> [mountain], whose caves are flooded by ocean waters, its body made sluggish by the reddish glow of dawn; fierce as the mutual collision of thunderclouds at the time of dissolution roaring at the striking of corners;

the foremost messenger of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s wrath, the hurricane of doom for the destruction of the <s>Kuru</s> dynasty—by whom was that drum struck, matching our lion-roar with its own resounding echo?" (350)
Here the subject matter does not suggest anger and such [sentiments].

children.text: abhineyārthaṃ ca kāvyamiti tatpratikūlā uddhatā racanādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: And since poetry is intended for dramatic representation, the forceful composition and the rest are contrary to that [subject].
And the speaker here is <s>Bhīmasena</s>.
In some cases, disregarding the speaker and the literary work, composition and the rest follow solely from the propriety of the subject matter.

As in: "Being gazed upon by <s>Aruṇa</s> (the charioteer of the Sun), whose horses, startled by the assault of <s>Saiṃhikeya</s> (<s>Rāhu</s>) manifesting as the surging waves appropriate to the grand cutting, were pulled aside causing the sun's chariot to swerve,

children.text: kurvat kākutsthavīryastutimiva marutāṃ kandharārandhrabhājāṃ bhāṃkārairbhīmametannipatati viyataḥ kumbhakarṇottamāhgam // 351 //
children.translated_text: this head of <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, as if composing a eulogy of the valor of <s>Kākutstha</s> (<s>Rāma</s>), falls from the sky with terrifying roars of 'bhāṃ' entering the hollows of the necks of the <s>Maruts</s> (wind-gods)." (351)
In some cases, disregarding both the speaker and the subject matter, they are suited only to the literary work.

children.text: tathāhi--ākhyāyikāyāṃ śṛṅgāre 'pi na masṛṇavarṇādayaḥ kathāyāṃ raudre 'pi nātyantamuddhatāḥ, nāṭakādau raudre 'pi na dīrghasamāsādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: For instance—in an <s>ākhyāyikā</s> (narrative), even in <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment), soft phonemes and the rest are not [necessarily used]; in a <s>kathā</s> (tale), even in <s>raudra</s> (furious sentiment), they are not extremely forceful; in a <s>nāṭaka</s> (drama) and the like, even in <s>raudra</s>, long compounds and the rest are not [used].
Thus other kinds of propriety (<s>aucitya</s>) should also be followed.

children.text: iti kāvyaprakāśe guṇālaṃkārabhedaniyataguṇanirṇayo nāma aṣṭama ullāsaḥ //8 // //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eighth <s>ullāsa</s> (chapter) of the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>, named "The Determination of <s>Guṇas</s> Fixed in the Distinction of <s>Guṇa</s> and <s>Alaṃkāra</s>." (8)
Now begins the ninth <s>ullāsa</s> (chapter).

children.text: guṇavivecane kṛte 'laṃkārāḥ prāptāvasarāḥ, iti saṃprati śabdālaṃkārānāha (sū- 103)
children.translated_text: Having discussed the <s>guṇas</s>, the <s>alaṃkāras</s> (ornaments) have arrived at their proper occasion; accordingly, he now speaks of the <s>śabdālaṃkāras</s> (verbal ornaments) (<s>sūtra</s> 103):
When a statement made in one sense is construed differently by another,

children.text: śleṣeṇa kākvā vā jñeyā sā vakroktistathā dvidhā //78//
children.translated_text: through <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning) or through <s>kāku</s> (tone of voice)—that is to be known as <s>vakrokti</s> (oblique expression), and it is thus of two kinds. (78)
"Thus" means <s>śleṣa-vakrokti</s> (oblique expression through double meaning) and <s>kāku-vakrokti</s> (oblique expression through tone).

children.text: tatra padabhaṅgaśleṣeṇa yathā nārīṇāmanukūlamācarasi cejjānāsi kaśvetano vāmānāṃ priyamādadhāti hitakṛnnaivābalānāṃ bhavān /
children.translated_text: Of these, with <s>śleṣa</s> involving word-splitting (<s>padabhaṅga</s>): "If you act favorably toward women, you know who is thin; it is the delight of the perverse that you establish, O benefactor, you are never [the benefactor] of the weak.

children.text: yuktaṃ kiṃ hitakartanaṃ nanu balābhāvaprasiddhātmanaḥ sāmarthyaṃ bhavataḥ purandaramatacchedaṃ vidhātuṃ kutaḥ // 352 //
children.translated_text: Is benefaction appropriate? Indeed, for one whose nature is known to be devoid of strength, where is the capacity of yours, O <s>Purandara</s> (<s>Indra</s>), to inflict destruction?" (352)

children.text: abhaṅgaśleṣeṇa yathā aho kenedṛśī buddhirvāruṇā tava nirmitā /
children.translated_text: With <s>śleṣa</s> without word-splitting (<s>abhaṅga</s>): "Ah, by whom was such an intellect fashioned for you—an intellect that is <s>vāruṇī</s> (made of liquor / belonging to <s>Varuṇa</s>)?

children.text: triguṇā śrūyate buddhirna tu dārumayī kvacit // 353 //
children.translated_text: Intellect is heard to be threefold (<s>triguṇā</s>), but never made of wood (<s>dārumayī</s>)." (353)

children.text: kākvā yathā gurujanaparatantratayā dūrataraṃ deśamudyato gantum /
children.translated_text: With <s>kāku</s> (tone of voice): "Being under the control of elders, he is about to depart for a very distant land.
O friend, he will not return in the lovely springtime adorned with swarms of bees and cuckoos." (354)
(<s>Sūtra</s> 104)
<s>Anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) is the similarity of phonemes.

children.text:
svaravaisādṛśye 'pi vyañjanasadṛśatvaṃ varṇasāmyam /
rasādyanugataḥ prakṛṣṭo nyāso 'nuprāsaḥ /
(sū- 105)
children.translated_text: Even when vowels differ, the similarity of consonants constitutes phonemic similarity. An excellent placement that follows the <s>rasa</s> (sentiment) and other [aesthetic elements] is <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration). (<s>Sūtra</s> 105)
It is of two kinds, based on <s>cheka</s> (elegant) and <s>vṛtti</s> (recurrent).

children.text:
chekāḥ, vidagdhāḥ /
vṛttirniyatavarṇagato rasaviṣayo vyāpāraḥ /
gata iti chekānuprāso vṛcyanuprāsaśva /
kiṃ tayoḥ svarūpam, ityāha--
(sū- 106)
children.translated_text: <s>Cheka</s> means "elegant" or "clever." <s>Vṛtti</s> is an operation directed toward a specific phoneme and concerned with <s>rasa</s> (sentiment). "Based on" indicates <s>chekānuprāsa</s> (elegant alliteration) and <s>vṛttyanuprāsa</s> (recurrent alliteration). What is the nature of these two? He says— (<s>Sūtra</s> 106)
The former is the single occurrence of many [consonants],

children.text: anekasya, arthāta vyañjanasya sakṛdekavāraṃ sādṛśyaṃ chekānuprāsaḥ /
children.translated_text: "of many"—that is, of consonants—the similarity occurring once (<s>sakṛt</s>) is <s>chekānuprāsa</s> (elegant alliteration).
Example: "Then the moon, whose body was made languid by the faintly reddish trembling,
assumed the pallor of the cheeks of women emaciated by <s>Kāma</s> (the god of love)." (355)
(<s>Sūtra</s> 107)
The latter is the repeated occurrence even of one [consonant]. (79)

children.text:
ekasya, apiśabdādanekasya vyajjanasya dvirbahukṛtvo vā sādṛśyaṃ vṛcyanuprāsaḥ /
tatra (sū- 108)
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛttyanuprāsa</s> (recurrent alliteration) is the similarity of even one—or, by the word "also," of many—consonants occurring twice or more times. In that regard (<s>sūtra</s> 108):
When expressed through phonemes that manifest <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness), it is called <s>upanāgarikā</s> (refined/urbane).
(<s>Sūtra</s> 109)
Through those [phonemes] that manifest <s>ojas</s> (vigor), it is <s>paruṣā</s> (harsh).
Examples of both have been given earlier. (<s>Sūtra</s> 110)
<s>Komalā</s> (soft) [is expressed] through the remaining [phonemes]. (80)
"The remaining" means other [phonemes].
