Some call this very [type] <s>grāmyā</s> (rustic).

children.text: udāharaṇam apasāraya ghanasāraṃ kuru hāraṃ dūra eva kiṃ kamalaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Example: "Remove the camphor, put on the necklace, keep the lotuses far away!
Enough, enough of lotus stalks, O garland-maker!"—thus speaks the young woman day and night. (356)
(<s>Sūtra</s> 111)
For some, these are regarded as the <s>rītis</s> (styles) headed by <s>Vaidarbhī</s>.

children.text: etāstisro vṛttayaḥ, vāmanādīnāṃ mate vaidarbhīgauḍīpāñcālyākhyā rītayo matāḥ //
children.translated_text: These three <s>vṛttis</s> (modes), in the view of <s>Vāmana</s> and others, are regarded as the <s>rītis</s> named <s>Vaidarbhī</s>, <s>Gauḍī</s>, and <s>Pāñcālī</s>.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 112)
The verbal [alliteration] is <s>lāṭānuprāsa</s>, based merely on a difference of purport. (81)

<s>Lāṭānuprāsa</s> is alliteration pertaining to words—even when there is no difference in word and meaning, [it arises] merely from a difference in syntactic connection; and it is so called because it is favored by the <s>Lāṭa</s> people.
Others call this <s>padānuprāsa</s> (word-alliteration).
(<s>Sūtra</s> 113)
It [pertains] to words (<s>padānām</s>),
"It" refers to <s>lāṭānuprāsa</s>.

children.text: udāharaṇam yasya na savidhe dayitā davadahanastuhinadīdhitistasya /
children.translated_text: Example: 'For one whose beloved is not near, the forest fire is like the moon;
and for one whose beloved is near, the forest fire is like the moon.' (357)
(<s>sūtra</s> 114)
Of a word also,
by the word 'also' (<s>api</s>), 'that' (<s>sa</s>) is conjoined.
Example: 'The face of that lady of excellent complexion is truly the moon (<s>sudhākara</s>);

children.text: sudhākaraḥ kva nu punaḥ kalaṅkavikalo bhavet // 358 //
children.translated_text: but where indeed could a moon deficient in its blemish be found?' (358)
(<s>sūtra</s> 115)
In inflection or elsewhere, there,
of the noun, in the declinable and indeclinable,

children.text: ekasmin samāse bhinne vā samāse samāsāsamāsayorvā nāmnaḥ prātipadikasya na tu padasya sārūpyam /
children.translated_text: in a single compound, in a split compound, or in both compound and non-compound — the formal identity (<s>sārūpya</s>) is of the nominal stem (<s>prātipadika</s>), not of the inflected word (<s>pada</s>).
Example: 'O mountain (<s>dharaṇidhara</s>), your fame has a splendor adorned with white-rayed moonbeams, having the form of the moon (<s>vibhākara</s>);
heroic valor and <s>Kamalā</s> (Lakṣmī) — she too belongs only to you, not to another.' (359)
(<s>sūtra</s> 116)
Thus it is considered fivefold. (82)
(<s>sūtra</s> 117)

children.text:
arthe satyarthabhinnānāṃ varṇānāṃ sā punaḥśrutiḥ /
yamakam
children.translated_text: When meaning exists, the repetition of phonemes (<s>varṇa</s>) that are different in meaning — that is <s>yamaka</s> (paronomasia/rhyme).

children.text:
samarasamaraso 'yamityādāvekeṣāmarthavacve, anyeṣāmanarthakatve bhinnārthānāmiti na yujyate vaktum iti, arthe satītyuktam /
seti sarorasa ityādivailakṣaṇyena tenaiva krameṇa sthitā /
(sū- 118)
children.translated_text: In [the example] 'samarasamarasa' and the like, since for some the syllables are meaningful and for others they are not meaningful, it is not appropriate to say 'of different meanings' — therefore it is said 'when meaning exists.' 'That' (<s>sā</s>) refers to [the repetition] established in the same sequence, by the distinctness of [sounds like] 'sarorasa' and the like. (<s>sūtra</s> 118)
Operating in a quarter-verse, a part thereof, it attains multiplicity. (83)

children.text:
prathamo dvitīyādau dvitīyastṛtīyādau tṛtīyaśvaturthe prathamastriṣvapīti sapta /
prathamo dvitīye tṛtīyaśvaturthe prathamaśvaturthe dvitīyastṛtīye, iti dve /
tadevaṃ pādajaṃ navabhedam /
ardhāvṛttiḥ ślokāvṛttiśveti dve /
dvidhā vibhakte pāde prathamādipādādibhāgaḥ pūrvavat dvitīyādipādādibhāgeṣu, antabhāgo 'ntabhāgeṣviti viṃśatirbedāḥ ślokāntare hi nāsau bhāgāvṛttiḥ /
trikhaṇḍe triṃśat catuḥkhaṇḍe catvāriṃśat /
prathamapādādigatāntyārdhādibhāgo dvitīyapādādigate, ādyārdhādibhāge yamyate, ityādyanvarthatānusaraṇenānekabhedam antādikam ādyantikam tatsamuccayaḥ, madhyāṃdikam ādipadhyam antamadhyam madhyāntikaṃ teṣāṃ samuccayaḥ /
tathā tasminneva pāde, ādyādibhāgānāṃ madhyādibhāgeṣu,aniyate ca sthāne, āvṛttiriti prabhūtatamabhedam /
children.translated_text: Likewise, within the same quarter-verse, the repetition of initial-parts in middle-parts, and in indeterminate positions — thus extremely numerous varieties.
All this is submerged within the poem — therefore no definition of its varieties has been made.
A sample is cited: 'Having propitiated <s>Vidhushekhara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), the wearer of the moon-crest, [he became] a lord of women's ornaments, free from deceit;
free from deceit, a lord of women's ornaments — therefore conquer the earth.' (360)

The first [repeating] in the second [quarter] and so on, the second in the third and so on, the third in the fourth, and the first in [all] three — thus seven. The first in the second, the third in the fourth, the first in the fourth, the second in the third — thus two [more]. Thus from the quarter-verses, nine varieties. Half-verse repetition and whole-verse repetition — two [more]. When a quarter-verse is divided in two, the first half-part in the second half-parts, and the end-part in the end-parts — twenty varieties. In another verse, the part-repetition does not [apply]. With three divisions, thirty; with four divisions, forty. The end-half-part of the first quarter in the second quarter, the initial-half-part is rhymed — and so forth, following the logical possibilities, many varieties: end-initial, initial-terminal, their combination; middle-initial, initial-middle, terminal-middle, middle-terminal, and their combinations.
'By him who leads without sin, with happiness and the like; without <s>Yama</s>, by the leader with happiness and the like;
the great people were given respect of mind; the great people gave, with minds striving respectfully.' (361)
'He, delighting in undertakings, necessarily [produced] a feeble, faint sound;
always desiring battle, standing like a forest fire.' (362)
'He, delighting in undertakings, necessarily supported a faint sound;
always desiring battle, standing like a forest fire.' (363)
'Whose infinite glory pervades the universe — <s>Brahmā</s> (the creator) does not know her;

children.text: yā ca māteva bhajate praṇate mānave dayām // 364 //
children.translated_text: and she who, like a mother, bestows compassion on the person who bows down.' (364)
'When he bows, when he does not bow, he leads this [world], he does not pass away;

children.text: śivehitāṃ śive hitāṃ smarāmitāṃ smarāmi tām // 365 //
children.translated_text: the auspicious one, beneficial, I remember her — I remember her.' (365)
'O <s>Sarasvatī</s>, grant me favor; O <s>Sarasvatī</s> of the mind, grant me steadiness;
Flow, O powerful one; O <s>Sarasvatī</s> of <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, make [it] a field.' (366)
'She traveled together with pride, with <s>Kandarpa</s> (the god of love), she who is of the essence of <s>saṃsāra</s>;
she who was a refuge, bearing autumn-freshness, bearing [all], she who was a refuge of autumn.' (367)
'Bees defeated, the pride of proud women conquered, the world bore the fragrance of the flowers of [their] minds;
it bore [a beauty with] the disturbance of lotuses restrained, with copper-colored petals blossomed and coppery complexion.' (368)
Thus, established with thousands of varieties — the rest is to be inferred by others.
(<s>sūtra</s> 119)

Words that, being different through difference of expressed meaning, yet touch upon simultaneous utterance, coalesce — that is <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia/double entendre), eightfold through phonemes and the like. (84)

children.text: "arthabhedena śabdabhedaḥ'; iti darśane "kāvyamārge svaro na gaṇyate'; iti ca naye vācyabhedena bhinnā api śabdā yat yugapaduccāraṇena śliṣyanti bhinnaṃ svarūpamapahnuvate sa śleṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: According to the doctrine that 'difference of meaning entails difference of word,' and the principle that 'in the way of poetry, accent is not counted,' words that are different through difference of expressed meaning, yet through simultaneous pronunciation coalesce — concealing their distinct forms — that is <s>śleṣa</s>.

And it is eightfold through the distinction of phoneme (<s>varṇa</s>), word (<s>pada</s>), gender (<s>liṅga</s>), language (<s>bhāṣā</s>), stem (<s>prakṛti</s>), suffix (<s>pratyaya</s>), case-ending (<s>vibhakti</s>), and number (<s>vacana</s>).

children.text: krameṇodāharaṇam-- alaṃkāraḥ śaṅkākaranarakapālaṃ parijano viśīrṇāṅgo bhṛṅgī vasu ca vṛṣa eko bahuvayāḥ /
children.translated_text: Examples in order: 'His ornament is <s>Śaṅkā</s>-kara (fear-producing / <s>Śaṅkara</s>), his retinue is <s>Narakapāla</s> (skull-bowls / hell-protector), his body is broken-limbed, <s>Bhṛṅgī</s> [is his attendant], his wealth is a bull (<s>vṛṣa</s>), he is one, advanced in age;

children.text: avastheyaṃ sthāṇorapi bhavati sarvāmaraguro- rvidhau vakre mūrdhni sthitavati vayaṃ ke punaramī // 369 //
children.translated_text: this is the state even of <s>Sthāṇu</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), [who is] the teacher of all the gods — when fate is crooked, resting on the head, what then of us, and what of these?' (369)
'A vessel of broad gold (<s>kārtasvara</s>), adorned with all retinue, O Lord (<s>deva</s>);
radiant with a multitude of female elephants (<s>kareṇu</s>) — now our two dwellings are equal.' (370)
'Inclined toward glances bowed with devotion, rivaling the blue lotus, [serving as] the object of meditation, devoted to <s>samādhi</s>, attained through righteous conduct;

children.text: lāvaṇyasya mahānidhī rasikatāṃ lakṣmīdṛśostanvatī yuṣmākaṃ kurutāṃ bhavārtiśamanaṃ netre tanurvā hareḥ // 371 //
children.translated_text: a great treasure of charm (<s>lāvaṇya</s>), producing connoisseurship — may the eye / slender form of <s>Hari</s>, bestowing the pacification of worldly suffering upon you, [be gracious].' (371)
This is also an example of <s>śleṣa</s> through number (<s>vacana</s>).
'In the great assembly of gods and the righteous (<s>dharma</s>), in the gathering of darkness, in the collection of scriptures (<s>āgama</s>),
with many refuges of <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), endure that delusion of mind, at the time of opportunity, [with] the great [one].' (372)

children.text: ayaṃ sarvāṇi śāstrāṇi hṛdi jñeṣu ca vakṣyati /
children.translated_text: 'He will recite all the <s>śāstras</s> in his heart and among the learned;
this prince, creating power for his enemies and friends alike.' (373)
'At the moment of gazing at the foot of the tree / the lotus feet of the lord whose crest-jewel is the night / moon, a thousand unprecedented fortunes attained at the proper time;

children.text: pramathanivahamadhye jātucicvatprasādādahamucitaruciḥ syānnanditā sā tathā me // 374 //
children.translated_text: amidst the host of <s>Pramathas</s> (attendants of <s>Śiva</s>), through the grace of <s>Cit</s> / at any time, may I have the fitting radiance — may she be thus delighted for me.' (374)
'Take the everything of everyone, you who are devoted to cutting the existence / the bondage;
you approach friendliness toward guidance / you practice bodily restraint.' (375)
(<s>sūtra</s> 120)
Because of the absence of distinction, the distinction of stem and the like may also be a ninth [type].
'Also a ninth' — 'also' (<s>api</s>) indicates a different sequence.
Example: 'He who is repeatedly capable of cutting the wings of those of other lineages at the proper moment,
bearing gifts measured in hundreds of crores — that lord of the wise (<s>vibudhendra</s>) shines.' (376)
Here, because of the absence of restriction by context and the like, both meanings are expressed.

children.text: nanu svaritādiguṇabhedāt bhinnaprayatnoccāryāṇāṃ tadabhāvādabhinnaprayatnoccāryāṇāṃ ca śabdānāṃ bandhe 'laṃkārāntarapratibhotpattihetuḥ śabdaśleṣo 'rthaśleṣaśveti dvividho 'pyarthālaṃkāramadhye parigaṇito 'nyairiti kathamayaṃ śabdālaṃkāraḥ /
ucyate--iha doṣaguṇālaṃkārāṇāṃ śabdārthagatatvena yo vibhāgaḥ saḥ, anvayavyatirekābhyāmeva vyavatiṣṭhate /
children.translated_text: It is replied: Here, the classification of faults, qualities, and ornaments as pertaining to word and meaning is established solely through the method of agreement and difference (<s>anvayavyatireka</s>).

Thus: harshness and the like, denseness and the like, <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) and the like [pertain to word]; meaninglessness and the like, maturity and the like, <s>upamā</s> (simile) and the like [pertain to meaning] — they are established as pertaining to word and meaning precisely because they follow the presence and absence thereof.
'And she herself, radiant with the copper-red hue of sprouts, adorned by <s>karavīra</s> (oleander);
thus [read] without breaking — like the dawn, bestowing what is desired by one who craves the fruit of sleep.' (377)

Now, since words that are uttered with different effort due to the distinction of accent (<s>svarita</s>) and other qualities, and those uttered with the same effort due to the absence of that [distinction] — the verbal <s>śleṣa</s> in composition is a cause for the manifestation of other ornaments. And <s>śleṣa</s>, being twofold as verbal <s>śleṣa</s> and semantic <s>śleṣa</s>, is counted by others among the ornaments of meaning — then how is this a verbal ornament?

children.text: iti sabhaṅgaḥ iti dvāvapi śabdaikasamāśrayāviti dvayorapi śabdaśleṣatvamupapannam na tvādyasyārthaśleṣatvam /
children.translated_text: Thus [read] with breaking — both rest solely on the words. Thus the status of both as verbal <s>śleṣa</s> is established; but the first is not semantic <s>śleṣa</s>.

children.text: arthaśleṣasya tu sa viṣayaḥ, yatra śabdaparivartane 'pi na śleṣatvakhaṇḍanā /
children.translated_text: The domain of semantic <s>śleṣa</s>, however, is where even upon substitution of words, the status of <s>śleṣa</s> is not disrupted.
For example: 'With a little, it rises high; with a little, it goes downward;
how similar is the behavior of the tip of a balance and of a wicked person!' (378)

children.text: na cāyamupamāpratibhotpattihetuḥ śleṣaḥ, api tu śleṣapratibhotpattiheturupamā /
tathāhi--yathā "kamalamiva mukhaṃ manojñametatkacatitarām'; ityādau guṇasāmye kriyāsāmye, ubhayasāmye vā, upamā /
children.translated_text: Thus: just as in 'this face is charming like a lotus, even more so because of the hair' and the like — when there is similarity of quality, similarity of action, or similarity of both — there is <s>upamā</s>.

children.text: tathā "sakalakalaṃ purametañjātaṃ saṃprati sudhāśubimbamiva'; ityādau śabdamātrasāmye 'pi sāyuktaiva /
children.translated_text: So too in 'this was formerly the full-of-spots city, but now it has become like the orb of the nectar-rayed moon' and the like — even with mere verbal similarity, [<s>upamā</s>] is indeed appropriate.
Thus <s>Rudraṭa</s> has stated: 'These two are clearly ornaments of meaning — <s>upamā</s> and <s>samuccaya</s> (accumulation); however,
based merely on verbal similarity, they are also possible here.'
And this <s>śleṣa</s> is not a cause for the manifestation of <s>upamā</s> (simile); rather, <s>upamā</s> is a cause for the manifestation of <s>śleṣa</s>.
[End of quote.]

children.text: na ca "kamalamiva mukham'; ityādiḥ sādhāraṇadharmaprayogaśūnya upamāviṣaya iti vaktuṃ yuktam pūrṇopamāyā nirviṣayatvāpatteḥ //
children.translated_text: And it is not appropriate to say that 'a lotus-like face' and the like, being devoid of the employment of a common property, is [not] a domain of <s>upamā</s> — because the full <s>upamā</s> would then have no domain.
'O Lord, you alone are the netherworld; you are the foundation of the directions;
you are the immortal wind-region — one who embodies the three worlds.' (379)

children.text:
ityādiḥ śleṣasya copamādyalaṃkāravivikto 'sti viṣaya iti /
dvayoryoge, saṃkara eva /
upapattiparyālocane tu, upamāyā evāyaṃ yukto viṣayaḥ /
anyathā viṣayāpahāra eva pūrṇopamāyāḥ syāt /
na ca "abindusundarī nityaṃ galallāvaṇyabindukā'; ityādau virodhapratibhotpattihetuḥ śleṣaḥ, api tu śleṣapratibhotpattiheturvirodhaḥ /
na hyatrārthadvayapratipādakaḥ śabdaśleṣaḥ, dvitīyārthasya pratibhātamātrasya prarohābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: For here, the verbal <s>śleṣa</s> conveying two meanings [does not apply], since the second meaning, being merely flashed, does not take root.

children.text: na ca virodhābāsa iva virodhaḥ śleṣābhāsaḥ śleṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: And just as <s>virodha</s> (contradiction) is not a semblance of <s>virodha</s> (<s>virodhābhāsa</s>), so too <s>śleṣa</s> is not a semblance of <s>śleṣa</s> (<s>śleṣābhāsa</s>).
Thus in such sentences, another ornament is indeed the cause of the manifestation of <s>śleṣa</s>.
Likewise: 'Born of a good lineage, a pearl' (380).

And such is the domain of <s>śleṣa</s> distinct from ornaments like <s>upamā</s> and the like. When both are combined, there is indeed a <s>saṅkara</s> (mixture). But upon reflection on the logical grounds, this is a fitting domain of <s>upamā</s> alone. Otherwise, there would be a seizure of the domain of the full <s>upamā</s>. And in 'she who is always without a dot (<s>bindu</s>) is beautiful, with a dot of charm on the cheek' and the like, <s>śleṣa</s> is not a cause for the manifestation of <s>virodha</s> (contradiction); rather, <s>virodha</s> is a cause for the manifestation of <s>śleṣa</s>.

children.text: nālpaḥ kaviriva svalpaśloko deva mahān bhavān // 381 //
children.translated_text: 'Not small, not a poet of few verses — O Lord, you are great.' (381)
'The twilight (<s>sandhyā</s>) is full of passion (<s>anurāga</s>); the day (<s>divasa</s>) precedes it;
Ah, the course of fate is strange — yet still there is no union.' (382)
'Taking up his bow, making the mountain firm, with a string (<s>guṇa</s>) that is not inferior, with a terrible gaze;
with a white, unfallen arrow, he desired the target — salutation to him.' (383)

In such examples, what is appropriate is [respectively] the status of <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor), <s>śleṣa</s>, <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast), <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression), and <s>virodha</s> (contradiction) — not the status of <s>śleṣa</s> [alone].

children.text:
śabda śleṣa iti cocyate, arthālaṃkāramadhye ca lakṣyate, iti ko 'yaṃ nayaḥ /
kiṃ ca vaicitryamalaṃkāra iti ya eva kavipratibhāsaṃrambhagocarastatraiva vicitratā, iti saivālaṃkārabhūmiḥ /
arthamusvaprekṣitvameteṣāṃ śabdānāmiti cet anuprāsādīnāmapi tathaiveti te 'pyarthālaṃkārāḥ kiṃ necyante /

children.translated_text: Even though <s>anuprāsa</s> and the like are dependent on the particular expressed meaning that manifests <s>rasa</s> and the like, their ornamental status [remains as verbal ornaments].
Even the qualities and faults of words have their status as qualities and faults only in relation to meaning.
If the qualities, faults, and ornaments of meaning are established only in relation to words — then let them too be called 'pertaining to words.'

children.text: "vidhau vakre mūrdhni'; ityādau ca varṇādiśleṣe, ekaprayatnoccāryatve 'rthaśleṣatvaṃ śabdabhede 'pi prasajyatāmityevamādi svayaṃ vicāryam //
children.translated_text: And in 'when fate is crooked, resting on the head' and the like, in the phonemic and other types of <s>śleṣa</s>, even when there is unity of articulative effort, let the status of semantic <s>śleṣa</s> apply despite the difference of words — such matters and the like should be considered by oneself.

It is called 'verbal <s>śleṣa</s>' and yet is counted among the ornaments of meaning — what kind of system is this? Moreover, variety (<s>vaicitrya</s>) is the ornament — and wherever the poet's creative genius finds its scope, precisely there is variety, and that alone is the ground of the ornament. If one says that these words have a dependence on meaning, then [we reply:] <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) and the like also have exactly such [dependence on meaning] — why then are they not called ornaments of meaning?
(<s>sūtra</s> 121)
That is <s>citra</s> (visual poetry) where phonemes have the power to produce the shape of a sword and the like. (85)

children.text: saṃniveśaviśeṣeṇa yatra nyastā varṇāḥ khaḍgamurajapajhādyākāramullāsayanti taccitraṃ kāvyam /
children.translated_text: Where the phonemes, through a particular arrangement, are placed so as to manifest the form of a sword, a drum (<s>muraja</s>), a lotus (<s>padma</s>), and the like — that is <s>citra</s> (pictorial/figured) poetry.
This is difficult (<s>kaṣṭa</s>) poetry — a mere indication is shown.
Example: 'By <s>Māra's</s> enemy (<s>Śiva</s>), <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>), <s>Rāma</s>, and the elephant-faced one (<s>Gaṇeśa</s>), with the force of a rain-shower;
their praise of you, begun with substance, is eternal, capable of removing that suffering at the [right] moment.' (384)
'Mother of those who bow, collision of glories, one who has subdued confusion;

children.text: mānyātha sīmā rāmāṇāṃ śaṃ me diśyādumādimā // 385 //
children.translated_text: 'Venerable one, O boundary of <s>Rāmās</s> (beautiful women), may the first <s>Umā</s> grant me welfare.' (385)
(Sword-pattern) 'Straight, [yet] of abundant beginnings, trembling, with a stream of strength and beauty;
with an abundance of rays, abundant, spotless, with abundance of hands, pure.' (386)
(Drum-pattern) 'Shining, of substantial glory, of the essence of brilliance, struck, radiant;

children.text: bhāvitātmā śubhā vāde devābhā bata te sabhā // 387 //
children.translated_text: one whose self is realized, auspicious in speech, of divine radiance — ah, your assembly!' (387)
(<s>Padmabandha</s> [lotus-shaped composition]) <s>rasāsāra rasā sārasāyatākṣa kṣatāyasā</s> /
<s>sātāvāta tavātāsā rakṣatastvastvataṃkṣara</s> // 388 //

children.text: (sarvatobhadram) saṃbhavino 'pyante prabhedāḥ śaktimātraprakāśakā na tu kāvyarūpatāṃ dadhatīti na pradarśyante //
children.translated_text: (<s>Sarvatobhadra</s> [auspicious from all sides]) Though further subtypes are possible, they are merely displays of technical skill and do not partake of the nature of poetry — therefore they are not demonstrated.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 122)
That which appears like repetition (<s>punaruktavadābhāsa</s>) is [the figure] where words of different form convey a single meaning.

The appearance of a single meaning through words that are of different form, some meaningful and some meaningless — that is <s>punaruktavadābhāsa</s> (semblance of repetition). And it is: (<s>Sūtra</s> 123)
of words [alone],
that is, it pertains solely to words, whether with or without semantic distinction.
Example: 'The slayer of enemies, whose body and frame [are mighty], suddenly [appears] with charioteer, driver, horses, and foot-soldiers;
he shines, always generous, a <s>tilaka</s>-mark on the surface of the earth in steadfastness.' // 389 //
'The gardens of women shine forth, causes of curiosity and delight;
the wise courtiers, joyful-minded, attend upon that king.' // 390 //
(<s>Sūtra</s> 124)
Likewise, this [figure pertains] to both word and meaning. // 86 //
Example: 'He of slender body, last among the broad-hipped, with terrible sharp nails reddened by the blood of elephants,
a mass of splendor, great, broad-minded — he is <s>Indra</s>, <s>Hari</s>, the Victorious.' // 391 //

children.text: atraiksamin pade parivartiṃte nālaṃkāra iti śabdāśrayaḥ, aparasmistu parivartite 'pi sa na hīyate, ityarthaniṣṭha ityubhayālaṃkāro 'yam //
children.translated_text: Here, when one word is substituted, the figure is not [present] — hence it is word-based; but when another [word] is substituted and the figure is not diminished — hence it is meaning-based. Thus this is a figure of both [word and meaning].

children.text: iti kāvyaprakāśe śabdālaṃkāranirṇayo nāma navama ullāsaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus in the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>, the ninth <s>ullāsa</s> (chapter) named 'Determination of Verbal Figures' (<s>śabdālaṅkāranirṇaya</s>) [is concluded].
// Now the tenth <s>ullāsa</s> //
He states the figures of meaning (<s>arthālaṅkāra</s>): (<s>Sūtra</s> 125)
Similarity constitutes simile (<s>upamā</s>), [which exists] in [the context of] difference.

children.text: upamānopameyayoreva na tu kāryakāraṇādikayoḥ sādharmyaṃ bhavatīti tayoreva samānena dharmeṇa saṃbandha upamā /
children.translated_text: The similarity that exists between the object of comparison (<s>upamāna</s>) and the object compared (<s>upameya</s>) alone — not between cause and effect and the like — the connection through a common property between those two is simile (<s>upamā</s>).
The word 'difference' (<s>bheda</s>) is used to exclude [the figure of] non-distinction (<s>ananvaya</s>).
(<s>Sūtra</s> 126)
It is complete (<s>pūrṇā</s>) and elliptical (<s>luptā</s>).

children.text:
upamānopameyasādhāraṇadharmopamāpratipādakānumupādāne pūrṇā, ekasya dvayostrayāṇāṃ vā lope luptā /
(sū- 127)
children.translated_text: When the <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison), the <s>upameya</s> (object compared), the common property (<s>sādhāraṇadharma</s>), and the particle indicating comparison are all present, it is complete (<s>pūrṇā</s>). When one, two, or three of these are omitted, it is elliptical (<s>luptā</s>). (<s>Sūtra</s> 127)
The first [i.e., the complete simile] is complete.

children.text: śrautyārthī ca bhavedvākye samāse taddhite tathā //87//
children.translated_text: The <s>śrautī</s> (literal) and <s>ārthī</s> (implied) [similes] occur in sentences, compounds, and <s>taddhita</s> derivatives. // 87 //

children.text: yathevavādiśabdā yatparāstasyaivopamānatāpratītiriti yadyapyumānaviśeṣaṇānyete tathāpi śabdaśaktimahimnā śrutyaiva ṣaṣṭhīvat saṃbandaṃ pratipādayantīti tatsadbhāve śrautī, upamā /
children.translated_text: Words such as <s>iva</s> (like), <s>vat</s> (like), and the like — that to which they are appended is understood as the standard of comparison (<s>upamāna</s>). Although these are [grammatically] modifiers of the <s>upamāna</s>, through the power of the word itself they directly convey the relation, just like the sixth case-ending (<s>ṣaṣṭhī</s>). When these are present, it is a <s>śrautī</s> (literally expressed) simile.
Likewise, when the suffix <s>vat</s>, which is prescribed by the rule '<s>tatra tasyeva</s>' for expressing meaning, is employed —

children.text: "tena tulyaṃ mukham'; ityādāvupameye, eva "tattulyamasya'; ityādau copamāne, eva "idaṃ ca tacca tulyam'; ityubhayatrāpi tulyādiśabdānāṃ viśrāntiriti sāmyaparyālocanayā tulyatāpratītiriti sādharmyasyārthatvāttulyādiśabdopādāne, ārthī tadvat "tena tulyaṃ kriyā cedvatiḥ'; ityanena vihitasya vateḥ sthitau /
children.translated_text: In expressions like '<s>tena tulyaṃ mukham</s>' ('the face is equal to that'), the word <s>tulya</s> (equal) rests upon the <s>upameya</s>; in '<s>tattulyamasya</s>' ('that which is equal to this'), it rests upon the <s>upamāna</s>; and in '<s>idaṃ ca tacca tulyam</s>' ('this and that are equal'), it rests upon both. Through the consideration of equality, the cognition of similarity [arises] — and since the similarity is conveyed through the meaning, when words like <s>tulya</s> and the like are employed, it is <s>ārthī</s> (implied). Likewise, when the suffix <s>vat</s> prescribed by the rule '<s>tena tulyaṃ kriyā cedvatiḥ</s>' is in place —

children.text: "ivena nityasamāso vibhaktyalopaḥ pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ ca" iti nityasamāse, ivaśabdayoge samāsagā /
children.translated_text: According to the rule '<s>ivena nityasamāso vibhaktyalopaḥ pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ ca</s>' — when there is obligatory compounding with the word <s>iva</s>, it is a compound-based simile (<s>samāsagā</s>).

children.text: krameṇodāharaṇam-- svapne 'pi samareṣu tvāṃ vijayaśrīrna muñcati /
children.translated_text: Examples in order: 'Even in dreams, in battles, the goddess of victory (<s>Vijayaśrī</s>) does not leave you,
just as a <s>svādhīnapatikā</s> (a woman whose husband is under her control) [does not leave] her beloved, the source of [her] power.' // 392 //
'This lotus-face of hers, with trembling doe-like rolling eyes, with a beauty that steals away the fresh reddish stars,

children.text: sarasijamidamānanaṃ ca tasyāḥ samamiti cetasi saṃmadaṃ vidhatte // 393 //
children.translated_text: creates delight in the mind [with the thought:] "These two are equal."' // 393 //
'With exceedingly long, disciplined, upraised, divine rays of splendor — infallible means —

children.text: śaurirbhujairiva caturbhiradaḥ sadā yo lakṣmīvilāsabhavanairbhuvanaṃ babhāra // 394 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śauri</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) always bore the world with [his] four arms, as it were — mansions of the sport of <s>Lakṣmī</s>.' // 394 //
'In the spreading of the paths of unfailing desires, his fame of praised weighty virtues is well-strung;

children.text: suratarusadṛśaḥ sa bhavānabhilaṣaṇīyaḥ kṣitīśvara na kasya // 395 //
children.translated_text: like a divine wish-fulfilling tree (<s>surataru</s>), you, O lord of the earth, are desirable to whom not?' // 395 //
'The gravity of his depth is truly like that of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and the serpent;
he is difficult to behold in battle, like a midday jewel of the sky.' // 396 //

children.text: svādhīnapatikā kāntaṃ bhajamānā yathāṃ lokottaracamatkārabhūḥ, tathā jayaśrīstvadāsevanenetyādinā pratīyamānena vinā yadyapi noktervaicitryam, vaicitryaṃ cālaṃkāraḥ, tathāpi na dhvaniguṇībhūtavyaṅgyavyavahāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Although without the suggested meaning (<s>pratīyamāna</s>) — such as 'just as a <s>svādhīnapatikā</s> attends upon her beloved, so the goddess of victory [attends upon you] through devotion' and the like — there would be no charm of expression (<s>vaicitrya</s>), and charm is [what constitutes] a figure of speech (<s>alaṅkāra</s>), nevertheless this is not classified under <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion), subordinated suggestion (<s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>), or the like.

children.text: na khalu vyaṅgyasaṃsparśaparāmarśādatra cārutāpratītiḥ, api tu vācyavaicitryapratibhāsādeva /
children.translated_text: For here the perception of beauty does not arise from the apprehension of contact with the suggested meaning, but rather from the very appearance of charm in the expressed meaning.

children.text: rasādistu vyaṅgyo 'rtho 'laṃkārāntaraṃ ca sarvatrāvyabhicārītyagaṇayitvaiva tadalaṃkārā udāhṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: But <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) and other suggested meanings, as well as other figures, are invariably present everywhere — therefore, disregarding them, the figures are illustrated [as such].

children.text: tadrahitatvena tu, udāhriyamāṇā virasatāmāvahantīti pūrvāparaviruddhābhidhānamiti na codanīyam //
children.translated_text: If illustrated without them, they would bring about insipidity — but this is not a charge of self-contradiction, [since they are merely not foregrounded].
(<s>Sūtra</s> 128)

children.text: tadvat dharmasya lope syāt na śrautī taddhite punaḥ /
children.translated_text: When the common property (<s>dharma</s>) is omitted with the particle (<s>vat</s>), it would not be <s>śrautī</s>; in <s>taddhita</s> [derivatives], however, it is <s>ārthī</s> alone.
The 'property' (<s>dharma</s>) is the common attribute.
In <s>taddhita</s> [formations] such as <s>kalpa</s> and the like, it is <s>ārthī</s> (implied) alone.
Thus there are five [varieties of complete simile].

children.text: udāharaṇam-- dhanyasyānanyasāmānyasaujanyotkarṣaśālinaḥ karaṇīyaṃ vacaśvetaḥ satyaṃ tasyāmṛtaṃ yathā // 397 //
children.translated_text: Example: 'The speech of the blessed one, who is distinguished by the excellence of a generosity unmatched by any other — his word is truly like nectar (<s>amṛta</s>).' // 397 //
'That lord, with drawn sword, moving about in battle,
was seen by the enemy army as equal to <s>Kṛtānta</s> (Death).' // 398 //
'His conduct is like a sword; his speech is like nectar.

children.text: viṣakalpaṃ mano vetsi yadi jīvasi tatsakhe // 399 //
children.translated_text: If you know [his] mind to be like poison, then live, O friend!' // 399 //
(<s>Sūtra</s> 129)
When the <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison) is not employed, [the simile is] sentence-based or compound-based. // 88 //
'The adornment of ornaments, the glory of hosts of enemies, the spreading of fame — this is not [the work] of a tasteful poem;

children.text: dīsai aha va ṇisammai sarisaṃ aṃsaṃsametteṇa // 400 //
children.translated_text: or rather, consider! It is equal in some portion.' // 400 //

children.text: kavvassetyatra kavvasamamiti sarisamityatra ca ṇūṇamiti pāṭhe, eṣaiva samāsagā //
children.translated_text: In '<s>kavvassa</s>' here [meaning] 'equal to a poem,' and in '<s>sarisam</s>' [meaning] 'similar,' in the reading with '<s>ṇūṇam</s>' — this very [example] is the compound-based [simile].
(<s>Sūtra</s> 130)

children.text:
vāderlope samāse sā karmādhārakyaci kyaṅi /
karmakartrorṇamuli
children.translated_text: When <s>vā</s> and the like are omitted, in a compound, [the simile occurs] with <s>kyac</s>, <s>kyaṅ</s>, [as applied to] object and agent, and with <s>ṇamul</s>.

children.text: vāśabdaḥ, upamādyotaka iti vāderupamāpratipādakasya lope ṣaṭ samāsena sarmaṇo 'dhikaraṇāccotpannena kyacā kartuḥ kyaṅā karmakartrorupapadayorṇamulā ca bhavet //
children.translated_text: The word <s>vā</s> [stands for] the indicator of simile. When <s>vā</s> and the like — the conveyers of simile — are omitted, [the simile occurs] in six ways: through a compound, through <s>kyac</s> derived from the object or the locative, through <s>kyaṅ</s> [derived from] the agent, and through <s>ṇamul</s> [applied to] the object or agent.
Example: 'Then, by [the moon] which is the lord of [the goddess] <s>Sumukhā</s>, pale like the cheeks of beautiful women,
a delight to the eyes — by that moon, the eastern direction was adorned.' // 401 //
Likewise: 'With a terrifying sword-blade like a black serpent, with swiftly moving mind intent on the destruction [of foes],
with hair standing on end and cheek-beauty resplendent — such was he at the sight of the enemy's valor.' // 402 //

children.text: pairaṃ sutīyati janaṃ samarāntare 'sāvantaḥ purīyati vicitracaritracuñcuḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He makes the enemy behave like footsoldiers in battle; in the inner chambers, he acts like a city of wonders;

children.text: nārīyate samārasīmni kṛpāṇapāṇerālokya tasya caritāni sapatnasenā // 403 //
children.translated_text: at the boundary of battle, seeing the deeds of the one with sword in hand, the enemy army acts like women.' // 403 //
'In battle, the enemies see him as having the appearance of the fierce rays of the summer sun;
that king, however, moves with the movement of <s>Pārtha</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>).' // 404 //
(<s>Sūtra</s> 131)
When both of these are omitted, [the simile is] compound-based with <s>kvip</s>. // 89 //
Of both of these — the common property (<s>dharma</s>) and the particle (<s>vā</s>) and the like.

children.text: udāharaṇam-- savitā vidhavati vidhurapi savitarati tathā dinanti yāminyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Example: 'The sun widens [like a widower]; the widower too suns [i.e., shines]; thus the days night,
and the nights day [i.e., pass like each other], when the mind is subject to pleasure and pain.' // 405 //
'Difficult to assail even by hundreds of imaginations of rivals,
that elephant among kings shines forth in the conduct of battle.' // 406 //
(<s>Sūtra</s> 132)
When the common property and the <s>upamāna</s> are omitted, [the simile] is seen in verbal forms and in sentences.
'O buzzing bee, roaming around the clusters of thorny flowers,
wandering like flowers of the <s>mādhuka</s> tree, you do not attain [your goal].' // 407 //
In the reading '<s>kusumeṇa samam</s>' ('equal to a flower'), it is sentence-based. (<s>Sūtra</s> 133)
With <s>kyac</s>, when the particle and the <s>upameya</s> [are omitted] —
'<s>āse</s>' means 'without hope' (<s>nirāśe</s>).
'With eyes blossoming wide at the sight of the enemy's valor,
with upraised staff-like arm bearing a sword — he acts like <s>Sahasrāyudha</s> (the Thousand-armed one).' // 408 //
Here the self (<s>ātman</s>) is the <s>upameya</s> (object compared). (<s>Sūtra</s> 134)
And when three are omitted, it is compound-based. // 90 //
Of the three — the particle (<s>vā</s>) and the like, the common property (<s>dharma</s>), and the <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison).
Example: 'Casting a glance at youth, with a graceful form extended in charming play,
her interior pierced by the arrows of <s>Smara</s> (Love) — the doe-eyed one steals the sage's mind.' // 409 //

children.text: atra saptamyupamānetyādinā yadā samāsalopau bhavataḥ, tadedamudāharaṇam //
children.translated_text: Here, when by the rule 'the seventh case-ending [denotes] the <s>upamāna</s>' and the like, both compound and omission occur, then this is the example.

children.text: krūrasyācārasyāyaḥśūlatayādhyavasāyāt ayaḥśūlenānvicchati "āyaḥśūlikaḥ'; ityatiśayoktirna tu krūrācāropameyataikṣṇyadharmavādīnāṃ lope trilopeyamupamā /
children.translated_text: 'Because of the ascertainment of the cruel conduct as being an iron-stake, "he is like an iron-stake" — this is <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole), not simile with triple omission of the <s>upameya</s>'s cruelty as the common property and the particle.
Thus there are nineteen elliptical [varieties]; together with the complete [varieties], there are twenty-five.
'With this demeanor the glory of kingship, with this humility the dignity of the noble-minded —
she wilted with despondency, like a lotus with frost-water.' // 410 //

children.text: ityabhinne sādhāraṇe dharme, jyotsneva nayanānandaḥ sureva madakāraṇam /
children.translated_text: This is [an example] when the common property is undivided. 'A delight to the eyes like moonlight, a cause of intoxication like a <s>Surā</s> (divine liquor),
the broad-hipped woman who attracts all people like sovereignty.' // 411 //

children.text: iti bhenne ca tasmin ekasyaiva bahūpamānopādāne mālopamā /
children.translated_text: This is [an example] when the common property is divided, and when multiple <s>upamānas</s> are employed for a single <s>upameya</s> — that is <s>mālopamā</s> (garland simile).

When the <s>upameya</s> successively becomes the <s>upamāna</s>, with common properties both undivided and divided — 'Of him whose flood of suppliant-streams is agitated by the hand perpetually bestowing waves of gold:"
'His speech is like his intellect; his intellect is like his conduct; his conduct is like his fame — exceedingly pure.' // 412 //
'His form is sweet like [his] intellect; his court is adorned with splendor like [his] form;

children.text: tasya sabheva jayaśrīḥ śakyā jetuṃ nṛpasya na pareṣām // 413 //
children.translated_text: his victory-glory is like his court — conquerable by this king alone, not by others.' // 413 //

children.text: ityādikā raśanopamā ca na lakṣitā, evaṃvidhavaicitryasahasrasaṃbhavāt uktabhedānatikramācca //
children.translated_text: And the like — the chain simile (<s>raśanopamā</s>) too is not separately classified, because of the possibility of thousands of such varieties of charm, and because they do not transgress the [already] stated categories.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 135)
When a single [entity serves as] both <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> within a single sentence, [that is] <s>ananvaya</s> (non-sequential simile).
<s>Ananvaya</s> is the absence of connection with another standard of comparison.

children.text: udāharaṇam-- na kevalaṃ bhāti nitāntakāntirniṃtambinī saiva nitambinīva /
children.translated_text: Example: 'Not only does the woman of perfect beauty shine — that very woman shines like a woman of perfect beauty;
so far as [her] graces are the weapons of <s>Vilāsa</s> (Sport) — those very graces are like those graces.' // 414 //
(<s>Sūtra</s> 136)
The reversal [of <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s>] is <s>upameyopamā</s> (reciprocal simile). // 91 //
The reversal — that is, in two sentences.
The simile by the <s>upameya</s>, which is directed toward the exclusion of any other standard of comparison — that is <s>upameyopamā</s> (simile where the compared becomes the standard).

children.text: udāharaṇam-- kamaleva matirmatiriva kamalā tanuriva vibhā vibheva tanuḥ /
children.translated_text: Example: 'His intellect is like a lotus; the lotus is like his intellect. His body is like radiance; radiance is like his body.

children.text: dharaṇīva dhṛcirdhṛtiriva dharaṇī satataṃ vibhāti bata yasya // 415 //
children.translated_text: The earth is like his steadfastness; his steadfastness is like the earth — thus he always shines!' // 415 //
'Of both' means: of the <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s>.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 137)
The imaginative identification (<s>saṃbhāvanā</s>), also known as poetic fancy (<s>utprekṣā</s>), is [the identification] of the subject with something equal [to it].
'Equal' means: with the standard of comparison (<s>upamāna</s>).

children.text: udārahaṇam-- unmeṣaṃ yo mama na sahate jātivairī niśāyām intorintīvaradaladṛśā tasya saundaryadarpaḥ /
children.translated_text: Example: 'He who cannot tolerate my blossoming, an enemy by birth, in the night — his pride in beauty by the dark iris-petal eyes of hers

children.text: nītaḥ śāntiṃ prasabhamanayā vaktrakāntyeti harṣā- llagrā manye lalitatanu te pādayoḥ pajhalakṣmīḥ // 416 //
children.translated_text: has been forcibly brought to peace by the radiance of her face — therefore, with joy, I think, O slender one, the lotus-beauty has alighted at your feet.' // 416 //
'Darkness smears the limbs, as it were; the sky rains down collyrium, as it were;
like the service of a wicked person, one's vision has gone to futility.' // 417 //
In such [examples], spreading and the like are imaginatively identified as smearing and the like.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 138)
When with doubt and the difference is stated, [it is <s>saṃdeha</s>]; when [the difference is] not stated, [it is] <s>saṃśaya</s> (uncertainty). // 92 //

children.text: bhedīktau yathā ayaṃ mārtaṇḍaḥ kiṃ sa khalu turagaiḥ saptabhiritaḥ kṛśānuḥ kiṃ sarvāḥ prasarati diśo naiṣa niyatam /
children.translated_text: When the difference is stated, as in: 'Is this the sun? For he [comes] from there with seven horses. Is he fire? For he spreads in all directions — no, that is not certain.

children.text: kṛtāntaḥ kiṃ sākṣānmahiṣavahano 'sāviti ciraṃ samālokyājau tvāṃ vidadhati vikalpān pratibhaṭāḥ // 418 //
children.translated_text: Is he <s>Kṛtānta</s> (Death) himself, riding a buffalo?' — Thus, seeing you in battle for a long time, the enemies deliberate alternatives.' // 418 //

children.text: bhedhoktāvityanena na kevalamayaṃ niśvayagarbho yāvannisvayānto 'pi saṃdehaḥ svīkṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: By the phrase 'when the difference is stated' — not only is [the figure of] doubt with an embedded certainty accepted, but also doubt ending in certainty.

children.text: yathā induḥ kiṃ kva kalaṅkaḥ sarasijametat kimambu kutra gatam /
children.translated_text: As in: 'Is it the moon? Where then is the spot? Is it a lotus? Where then has the water gone?
It is her face! — with charming and playful words, O doe-eyed one, this is ascertained at last.' // 419 //

children.text: kiṃ tu niśvayagarbha iva nātra niśvayaḥ pratīyamāna iti, upekṣito bhaṭṭodbhaṭena /
children.translated_text: However, unlike [doubt] with embedded certainty, here no certainty is apprehended — therefore it was disregarded by <s>Bhaṭṭodbhaṭa</s>.

children.text: tadanuktau yathā asyāḥ sargavidhau prajāpatirabhūccandro nu kāntipradaḥ śṛṅgāraikarasaḥ svayaṃ nu madano māso nu puṣpākaraḥ /
children.translated_text: When it [the standard of comparison] is left unstated, an example: 'Was <s>Prajāpati</s> the moon that grants radiance in the creation of her? Was <s>Madana</s> (the god of love) himself, being the sole <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic essence) of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment)? Was the month <s>Puṣpākara</s> (the flower-bearing spring)?

children.text: vedābhyāsajaḍaḥ kathaṃ nu viṣayavyāvṛttakautūhalo nirmātuṃ prabhavenmanoharamidaṃ rūpaṃ purāṇo muniḥ // 420 //
children.translated_text: How could the ancient sage, dulled by the study of the <s>Vedas</s>, with his curiosity turned away from worldly objects, have the power to create this enchanting form?' (420)
(<s>Sūtra</s> 139)
That [figure] is <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) — which is the non-difference of the object of comparison (<s>upamāna</s>) and the subject of comparison (<s>upameya</s>).
Because of extreme similarity, it is the non-difference of those whose distinction is not concealed. (<s>Sūtra</s> 140)
When the expressed [metaphorical identifications] have all entities as their scope, [they are] heard [directly stated] and superimposed. (93)

children.text: āropaviṣayā iva āropyamāṇāḥ, yadā śabdopāttāḥ, tadā samastāni vastūni viṣayo 'syeti samastavastuviṣayam /
children.translated_text: Those that are being superimposed — as if they were the objects of superimposition — when they are conveyed by the words, then 'all entities are their scope' means that all things are their domain.
The plural in 'superimposed' (<s>āropitā</s>) is not intended [as grammatically significant].

children.text: yathā jyotsnābhasmacchuraṇadavalā bibhratī tārakāsthī- nyantardhānavyasanarasikā rātrikāpālikīyam /
children.translated_text: An example: 'Whitened by the scattering of moonlight-ash, bearing the bones of stars, addicted to the vice of disappearing — this night is a female ascetic of the <s>Kāpālika</s> order.

children.text: dvīpāddvīpaṃ bhramati dadhatī candarmudrākapāle nyastaṃ siddhāñjanaparimalaṃ lāñchanasya cchalena // 421 //
children.translated_text: She wanders from island to island, holding the moon-marked skull-bowl in which, under the pretext of [its] dark mark, is placed the fragrance of <s>siddhāñjana</s> (magical collyrium).' (421)

children.text: atra pādatraye, antardhānavyasanarasikatvamāropitadharma eveti rūpakaparigrahe sādhakamastīti tatsaṃkarāśaṅkā na kāryā //
children.translated_text: Here, in three of the four lines, the 'addiction to the vice of disappearing' is itself a property of the superimposed [metaphorical identification] — thus there is evidence for classifying it as <s>rūpaka</s>, and doubt about its being a mixture [with another figure] should not be entertained.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 141)

[When the superimposed identifications are both] directly expressed (<s>śrautā</s>) and implied (<s>ārthā</s>), and in which there is variation in one part — that is [<s>rūpaka</s> of the type called] <s>ekadeśavivarti</s> (partially varied).

Some [identifications] being superimposed are conveyed by the words; others are to be inferred through the power of the meaning — therefore, because of the variation in one part, it is <s>ekadeśavivarti</s>.

children.text: yathā jassa raṇanteurae kare kuṇantassa maṇḍalaggalaam /
children.translated_text: An example [in Prakrit]: 'Of him who is making the circular tip [of his sword] dance at the frontier of battle,

children.text: rasasaṃmuhī vi sahasā paraṃmuhī hoi riuseṇā // 422 //
children.translated_text: the enemy army, as if intoxicated by <s>rasa</s> (sentiment/flavor), suddenly turns its face away.' (422)

children.text:
atra raṇasyāntaḥpuratvamāropyamāṇaṃ śabdopātm maṇḍalāgralatāyāḥ nāyikātvam ripusenāyāśva pratināyikātvam arthasāmarthyādavasīyate, iti, ekadeśe viśeṣeṇa vartanādekadeśavivarti /
(sū- 142)
children.translated_text: Here, the superimposition that the battle is a harem (<s>antaḥpura</s>) is conveyed by the words; but the superimposition that the 'circular-tipped vine' is a heroine (<s>nāyikā</s>) and that the enemy army is a rival woman (<s>pratināyikā</s>) is inferred through the power of the meaning. Thus, because of the special variation in one part, it is <s>ekadeśavivarti</s>. (<s>Sūtra</s> 142)
<s>Sāṅga</s> (with subsidiary parts) — this [<s>rūpaka</s>]
of the two kinds previously stated, is <s>sāvayava</s> (having components).
(<s>Sūtra</s> 143)
But <s>niraṅga</s> (without subsidiary parts) is <s>śuddha</s> (pure).

children.text: yathā kuraṅgīvāṅgāni stimitayati gītadhvaniṣu yat sakhīṃ kāntodantaṃ śrutamapi punaḥ praśrayati yat /
children.translated_text: An example: 'That which stiffens the limbs like a doe when songs are heard, that which makes even a friend bend down upon hearing a message from the beloved,

children.text: anidraṃ yaccāntaḥ svapiti tadaho vedmyabhinavāṃ pravṛtto 'syāḥ sektuṃ hṛdi manasijaḥ premalatikāma // 423 //
children.translated_text: that which, though sleepless, sleeps within — ah, I perceive that <s>Manasija</s> (the god of love) has set about watering a fresh creeper of love in her heart.' (423)
(<s>Sūtra</s> 144)
A garland [of <s>rūpakas</s>] (<s>mālā</s>) is as previously [described for <s>upamā</s>]. (94)
As in the garland of similes, so too [in the garland of metaphors] — in a single [verse], many [identifications] are superimposed.

children.text: yathā saundaryasya taraṅgiṇī taruṇimotkarṣasya harṣodgamaḥ kānteḥ kārmaṇakarma narmarahasāmullāsanāvāsabhūḥ /
children.translated_text: An example: 'The river of beauty, the surge of the excellence of youth, the rise of delight from loveliness, the dwelling-place for the display of playful secrets,

children.text: vidyā vakragirāṃ vidheranavadhiprāvīṇyasākṣātkriyā bāṇāḥ pañcaśilīmukhasya lalanācūḍāmaṇiḥ sā priyā // 424 //
children.translated_text: the learning of crooked words of <s>Vidhi</s> (Brahmā), the direct manifestation of boundless skill, the arrows of the five-faced archer (<s>Kāma</s>) — the crest-jewel of women is that beloved.' (424)
(<s>Sūtra</s> 145)
[That figure] whose means of superimposition is determined, and which is the superimposition of another [entity] —

children.text: tat paraṃparitaṃ śliṣṭe vācake bhedabhāji vā //95//
children.translated_text: that is <s>paraṃparita</s> (chained), either in <s>śliṣṭa</s> (cohesive) form with a single expression, or with separation of [the two] identities. (95)

An example: 'O swan of the lake of the learned, O radiance blazing with the closing of the lotuses of enemies, O red-and-blue, O <s>Vaiśvānara</s> (fire) that elicits the sound "svāhā" from the sacrificial sticks of battle,

children.text: satyaprītividhānadakṣa vijayaprāgbhāvabhīma prabho sāmrājyaṃ varavīra vatsaraśataṃ vairiñcamuccaiḥ kriyāḥ // 425 //
children.translated_text: O you skilled in bestowing affection for truth, O <s>Bhīma</s> who is the precursor of victory, O Lord — may [your] sovereignty be supreme over the world for a hundred years, like the deeds of <s>Brahmā</s>!' (425)

children.text: atra mānasameva mānasam kamalāyāḥ saṃkoca eva kamalānāmasaṃkocaḥ, durgāṇāmamārgaṇameva durgāyāḥ mārgaṇam samitāṃ svīkāra eva samidhāṃ svīkāraḥ satye prītireva satyāmaprītiḥ, vijayaḥ paraparābhava eva vijayo 'junaḥ, evamāropaṇanimitto haṃsāderāropaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, '<s>mānasa</s>' (of the mind) is itself '<s>mānasa</s>' (the lake <s>Mānasa</s>); the closing of lotuses (<s>kamalā</s>) is itself the closing-in on [the goddess] <s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>); the seeking of difficult [places] (<s>durga</s>) is itself the seeking of [the goddess] <s>Durgā</s>; the acceptance of sacrificial sticks (<s>samit</s>) is itself the acceptance of battles (<s>samit</s>); affection for truth (<s>satya</s>) is itself non-affection for <s>Satyā</s> (a woman's name); victory over the other (<s>parābhava</s>) is itself <s>Vijaya</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>) — thus the superimposition of the swan and the rest is occasioned by the [determined means of] superimposition.

children.text: yadyapi śabdārthālaṃkāro 'yamityuktam vakṣyate ca tathāpi prasiddhyanurodhādatroktaḥ, ekadeśavivarti hīdamanyairabhidhīyate /
children.translated_text: Although it has been said that this is a figure of both word and meaning, and will be so stated [later], nevertheless, in accordance with established convention, it is stated here; for this is called <s>ekadeśavivarti</s> by others.

children.text: bhedabhāji yathā ālānaṃ jayakuñjarasya dṛṣadāṃ seturvipadvāridheḥ pūrvādriḥ karavālacaṇḍhamahaso līlopadhānaṃ śriyaḥ /
children.translated_text: With separation [of identities], an example: 'The tethering-post of the victory-elephant, the bridge of stones over the ocean of calamity, the eastern mountain of the sword-fierce sun, the cushion of <s>Śrī</s>'s play,

children.text: saṃgrāmāmṛtasāgarapramathanakrīḍāvidau mandaro rājan rājati vīravairivanitāvaidhavyadasate bhujaḥ // 426 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Mandara</s> (mountain) for the churning-sport of the ocean of battle-nectar — O king, the arm shines, which is the widowhood-bestower of the wives of heroic enemies.' (426)

children.text: atra jayoderbhinnaśabdavācyasya kujjaratvādyārope bhujasya, ālānatvādyāropo yujyate /
children.translated_text: Here, since the elephant-nature and the like are superimposed onto the arm — which is denoted by a different word from 'victory-elephant' — the superimposition of being a tethering-post and the like is appropriate.
'O you who have illuminated the three worlds with an extraordinary, great light,
O Lord, who does not praise you, the jewel released from the lineage of the good?' (427)

children.text: niravadhi ca nirāśrayaṃ ca yasya sthitamanivartitakautukaprapañcam /
children.translated_text: 'He whose limitless and supportless [splendor] abides, with the display of unwavering wonder,

children.text: prathama iha bhavān sa kūrmamūrtirjayati caturdaśalokavallikandaḥ // 428 //
children.translated_text: he, the first one here in the form of <s>Kūrma</s> (the Tortoise), is victorious — the root-bulb of the creeper of the fourteen worlds.' (428)
And thus, even a non-garland <s>rūpaka</s> should be seen as <s>paraṃparita</s> (chained).
'With the sprout-hands of creepers, with the lotus-hands of lovely women, [love] conquers the mind.
Of lotuses — with their own lotuses; of women — with their moon-faces: <s>Madana</s> (the god of love) [conquers].' (429)

children.text: ityādi raśanārūpakaṃ na vaicitryavaditi na lakṣitam //
children.translated_text: And such [examples] — the garland-<s>rūpaka</s> (<s>raśanārūpaka</s>) is not noted [as a separate type] since it is not [sufficiently] varied.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 146)
<s>Apahnutī</s> (concealment) is that [figure] in which the subject at hand (<s>prakṛta</s>) is denied and another [thing] is established.

children.text: upameyam asatyaṃ kṛtvopamānaṃ satyatayā yat sthāpyate sā tu, apahnutiḥ /
children.translated_text: That in which the subject of comparison (<s>upameya</s>) is made unreal and the standard of comparison (<s>upamāna</s>) is established as real — that is <s>apahnutī</s>.

children.text: udāharaṇam-- avāptaḥ prāgalbhyaṃ pariṇatarucaḥ śailatanaye kalaṅko naivāyaṃ vilasati śaśāhkasya vapuṣi /
children.translated_text: An example: 'Having attained boldness, with matured radiance, O daughter of the mountain (<s>Śailatanayā</s> / <s>Pārvatī</s>) — this is not at all a blemish that shines on the body of the moon.

children.text: amuṣyeyaṃ manye vigaladamṛtasyantaśiśire ratiśrāntā śete rajaniramaṇī gāḍhamurasi // 430 //
children.translated_text: I think this is the beloved <s>Rajanī</s> (Night), weary from lovemaking, who in the inner cold of dripping nectar, sleeps deeply on the chest of [her] lover.' (430)

children.text: itthaṃ vā bata sakhi kiyadetat paśya vairaṃ smarasya priyavirahakṛśe 'smin rāgiloke tathā hi /
children.translated_text: 'Alas, O friend, how much of this enmity of <s>Smara</s> (the god of love) should one witness — in this passionate world made thin by the separation from the beloved! For:
Under the guise of bees shining on the mango trees of the garden, <s>Kālakūṭa</s> (deadly poison) has been inscribed [on them] arrow by arrow by this one (Kāma).' (431)

children.text: atra hi na sabhṛṅgāṇi sahakārāṇi, api tu sakālakūṭāḥ śarā iti pratītiḥ /
children.translated_text: Here the cognition is: these are not mango trees with bees, but rather arrows with <s>kālakūṭa</s> poison.

children.text: evaṃ vā amuṣmiṃllāvaṇyāmṛtasarasi nūnaṃ mṛgadṛśaḥ smaraḥ śarvapluṣṭaḥ pṛṣujaghanabhāge nipatitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Or thus: 'Surely in that lake of the nectar of beauty of the doe-eyed one, <s>Smara</s> (Kāma), burned by <s>Śarva</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), has fallen upon the region of her hips and buttocks.

children.text: yadaṅgāṅgārāṇāṃ pratamapiśunā nābhikuhare śikhā dhūmasyeyaṃ pariṇamati romāvalivapuḥ // 432 //
children.translated_text: For this, betraying the initial [presence of] embers of the body, is a plume of smoke in the hollow of the navel that takes the form of a line of body-hair.' (432)
Here the cognition is: this is not a line of body-hair, but a plume of smoke.
Thus this [figure] should be understood through other modes as well.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 147)

children.text: śleṣaḥ sa vākye, ekasmin yatrānekārthatā bhavet //96//
children.translated_text: <s>Śleṣa</s> (paronomasia/pun) is that in which, in a single utterance, there is multiplicity of meaning. (96)
Where words that convey a single meaning [also] have multiple meanings — that is <s>śleṣa</s>.

children.text: udāharaṇam-- udayamayate diṅbhālinyaṃ nirākurutetarām nayati nidhanaṃ nidrāmudrāṃ pravartayati kriyāḥ /
children.translated_text: An example: 'He rises on the forehead of the directions / rises in the horizon of the army; he removes the other / he dispels the rival; he brings about the destruction / he destroys the sleep-seal; he sets activities in motion.

children.text: racayatitarāṃ svairācārapravartanakartanam vata bata lasattejaḥpuñjo vibhāti vibhākaraḥ // 433 //
children.translated_text: He intensely fashions the cutting of free-willed conduct. Alas, alas — the blazing mass of radiance, <s>Vibhākara</s> (the Sun / the King), shines forth!' (433)
Here, because the denotation is unrestrained, both the sun and the king are denoted.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 148)
<s>Parokti</s> (indirect speech) [combined] with differentiating [words] that are <s>śliṣṭa</s> (having double meaning) is <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression).

children.text: prakṛtārthapratipādakavākyena śliṣṭaviśeṣaṇamāhātmayāt na tu viśeṣyasya sāmarthyādapi yat aprakṛtasyārthasyābhidhānam sā samāsena saṃkṣepeṇārthadvayakathanāt samāsoktiḥ /
children.translated_text: When, through the power of the <s>śliṣṭa</s> qualifiers (double-meaning adjectives) in a sentence that conveys the subject at hand — not through the power of the qualified noun — there is also the expression of a meaning not at hand: that is <s>samāsokti</s>, because it tells two meanings in a condensed (<s>samāsa</s>) form.

children.text: udāharaṇam--lahiūṇa tujjha bāhuphphaṃsaṃ jīe sa ko vi ullāso /
children.translated_text: An example [in Prakrit]: 'Having obtained the touch of your arm, O life / O <s>Jayā</s>, there is some elation.

children.text: jaalacchī tuha virahe ṇa hūjjalā dubbalā ṇaṃ sā // 434 //
children.translated_text: Without you, O [my] separation, the water-born <s>Lakṣmī</s> / that one is not radiant — she is weak indeed.' (434)
Here, the word '<s>Jayalakṣmī</s>' (the goddess of victory) does not function merely as a term for the beloved.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 149)
<s>Nidarśanā</s> (illustration).
[It is] the construction of a simile involving a relation with a non-existent entity. (97)
<s>Nidarśana</s> is the making of an example (<s>dṛṣṭāntakaraṇa</s>).

children.text: udāharaṇam-- kvasūryaprabhavo vaṃśaḥ kva cālpaviṣayā matiḥ /
children.translated_text: An example: 'Where is the lineage born of the Sun, and where is my intellect of limited scope?
Out of delusion, I wish to cross an uncrossable ocean with a raft.' (435)

children.text: atra, uḍupena sāgarataraṇamiva manmatyā sūryavaṃśavarṇanamityupamāyāṃ paryavasyati /
children.translated_text: Here, it resolves into a simile: 'Just as the crossing of the ocean with a raft, so is my description of the Solar dynasty by my intellect.'

children.text: yathā vā udayati vitatordhvaraśmirajjāvahimarucau himadhāmni yāti cāstam /
children.translated_text: Or thus: 'When the cold-rayed [moon] rises with the extended net of upward rays, and the sun sets,
this mountain bears the sport of a lordly elephant adorned with two hanging bells.' (436)

children.text: atra kathamanyasya līlāmanyo vahatīti tatsadṛśīmityupamāyāṃ paryavasānam /
children.translated_text: Here, [the question arises:] how does one bear the sport of another? It resolves into a simile: '[He bears a sport] similar to that.'
'He wishes to cross the river with his arms, he wishes to seize the moon-disc with his hand,

children.text: meruṃ lilaṅghayiṣati dhruvameṣa deva yaste guṇān gaditumudyamamādadhāti // 437 //
children.translated_text: he will surely leap over <s>Meru</s> — O Lord, this person who undertakes the effort to narrate your virtues.' (437)
And in such [examples], this should be seen as a garland-form of this [figure].
(<s>Sūtra</s> 150)
The statement of the connection between each [thing] and its own cause, and that [connection being expressed] through action alone — that is the other [type of <s>nidarśanā</s>].

children.text: kriyayaiva svasvarūpasvakāraṇayoḥ saṃbandho yadavagamyate sā, aparā nidarśanā /
children.translated_text: When the connection between each thing's own nature and its own cause is understood through action alone — that is the other <s>nidarśanā</s>.

children.text: yathā unnataṃ padamavāpya yo laghurhelayaiva sa patediti bruvan /
children.translated_text: An example: 'One who is light, having attained an elevated position, falls down by the slightest provocation — so saying,
a pebble, having reached the peak of the mountain, blown by the wind, falls downward.' (438)

children.text: atra pātakriyayā patanasya lāghave sati, unnatapadaprāptirūpasya ca saṃbandhaḥ khyāpyate //
children.translated_text: Here, through the action of falling, the connection is made known: that of falling with lightness, and with having attained an elevated position.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 151)
<s>Aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (praise of the irrelevant) — that [figure] which itself has its basis in the relevant subject. (98)
<s>Aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> is the suggestion of the relevant (<s>prākaraṇika</s>) through the expression of the irrelevant (<s>aprākaraṇika</s>). (<s>Sūtra</s> 152)

children.text: kārye nimitte sāmānye viśeṣe prastute sati /
children.translated_text: [It occurs] when the effect, the cause, the general, the particular, or the relevant is at hand,
and the other [i.e., of these], or what is equal in speech, or what is equal [in nature is expressed] — thus it is fivefold. (99)
'The other' means the cause and so forth [of those listed].

children.text: krameṇodāharaṇam-- yātā kiṃ na milanti sundari punaśvintā tvayā matkṛte no kāryā nitarāṃ kṛśāsi kathayatyevaṃ sabāṣpe mayi /
children.translated_text: Examples in order: 'Have those who left not returned, O beautiful one? Or have you been thinking about me? You should not [worry] at all — you have become very thin.' While he was saying thus to me, with tears,

children.text: lajjāmantharatārakeṇa nipatatpītāśruṇā cakṣuṣā dṛṣṭvā māṃ hasitena bhāvimaraṇotsāhastayā sūcitaḥ // 439 //
children.translated_text: she looked at me with eyes bashful, with slowly moving pupils, from which tears of yellow hue fell — and through a smile, she indicated her readiness for the coming death.' (439)

children.text: atra prasthānātkimiti nivṛtto 'sīti kārye pṛṣṭe kāraṇamabhihitam /
children.translated_text: Here, when asked about the effect — 'Why have you not returned from the journey?' — the cause is stated.

children.text: rājantarājasutā na pāṭhayati māṃ devyo 'pi tūṣṇīṃ sthitāḥ kubje bhojaya māṃ kumārasacivairnādyāpi kiṃ bhujyate /
children.translated_text: 'The queen, the daughter of the king, does not feed me. The goddesses too remain silent. O hunchback, feed me! With the ministers of the prince, is there still no eating?'

children.text: ityaṃ nātha śukastāvāribhavane mukto 'dhvagaiḥ pañjarāt citrasthānavalokya śūnyavalabhāvekaikamābāṣate // 440 //
children.translated_text: Thus, O lord, a parrot released from its cage by travelers at the gate of your enemy's house, seeing the painted figures and the empty balconies, addresses each one.' (440)

children.text: atra prasthānodyataṃ bhavantaṃ jñātvā sahasaiva tvadarayaḥ palāyya gatāḥ, iti kāraṇe prastute kāryamuktam /
children.translated_text: Here, when the cause is the subject — namely, 'knowing that you were prepared for departure, your enemies suddenly fled in terror' — the effect is stated.

children.text: etattasya mukhātkiyat kamalinīpatre kaṇaṃ vāriṇo yanmuktāmaṇirityamaṃsta sa jaḍaḥ śṛṇvanyadasmādapi /
children.translated_text: 'How much [worth] is this from his mouth: a drop of water on a lotus leaf — which that fool took to be a pearl! Now hear something even [more foolish] than this:

children.text: aṅgulyagralaghukriyāpravilayinyādīyamāne śanaiḥ kutroḍḍīya gato mametyanudinaṃ nidrāti nāntaḥśucā // 441 //
children.translated_text: When it was gently lifted by the tip of a finger, dissolving into a light-playing [drop], every day he sleeps not, grieving inwardly: "Where has my [pearl] flown?"' (441)

children.text: atrāsthāne jaḍānāṃ mamatvasaṃbhāvanā bhavatīti sāmānye prastute viśeṣaḥ kathitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, when the general is the subject — namely, that fools are capable of attachment to unworthy things — the particular is stated.
'He who wipes away the tear-water of a friend's wife through retaliation against the enemy —

children.text: sa eva pūjyaḥ sa pumānsa nītimānsujīvitaṃ tasya sa bhājanaṃ śriyaḥ // 442 //
children.translated_text: he alone is worshipful, he is a [true] man, he is wise, his life is well-lived, he is the vessel of <s>Śrī</s> (prosperity).' (442)

children.text: atra "kṛṣṇaṃ nihatya narakāsuravadhūnāṃ yadi duḥkhaṃ praśamayasi tat tvameva ślāghyaḥ'; iti viśeṣe prakṛte sāmānyamamihitam /

children.translated_text: When the equal (<s>tulya</s>) is the subject and an equal [thing] is expressed, there are three varieties.

children.text: śleṣaḥ samāsoktiḥ sādṛśyamātraṃ vā tulyāt tulyasya hyākṣepe hetuḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Śleṣa</s> (pun), <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression), or mere similarity — for each of these is a basis for the suggestion of the equal from the equal.

children.text: krameṇodāharaṇam-- puṃstvādapi pravicalet yadi yadyadho 'pi yāyāt yadi praṇayane namahānapi syāt /
children.translated_text: Examples in order: 'Even if one were to deviate from manliness, even if one were to go downward, even if through entreaty one were to become the greatest [humbled one],

children.text: abhyuddharettadapi viśvamitīdṛśīyaṃ kenāpi dik prakaṭitā puruṣottamena // 443 //
children.translated_text: even then, this person would raise up the whole [world] — such a direction was revealed by a certain <s>Puruṣottama</s> (Supreme Person / <s>Viṣṇu</s>).' (443)
Here, when the particular is the subject — 'If you slay <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and pacify the sorrow of the wives of <s>Narakāsura</s>, then you alone are praiseworthy' — the general is stated.

children.text: yenāsyabhyuditena candra gamitaḥ klāntiṃ ravau tatra te yujyeta pratikartumeva na punastasyaiva pādagrahaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'O Moon, by his rising, you have been brought to exhaustion. It would be fitting for you to retaliate against him (the Sun), but instead you grasp his very feet [i.e., set in the west].

children.text: kṣīṇenaitadanuṣṭhitaṃ yadi tataḥ kiṃ lajjase no manāg astvenaṃ jaḍadhāmatā tu bhavato yad vyāmni visphūrjase // 444 //
children.translated_text: If, diminished, you have done this — then why are you not ashamed even a little? Let it be so — but it is the dullness of your nature, O dim one, that you blaze [only] in the sky.' (444)

children.text: ādāya vāri paritaḥ saritāṃ mukhebhyaḥ kiṃ tāvadarjitamanena durarṇavena /
children.translated_text: Having taken the waters from the mouths of rivers on all sides, what has this wretched ocean gained?

children.text: kṣārīkṛtaṃ ca vaḍavādahane hutaṃ ca pātālakukṣikuhare viniveśitaṃ ca // 445 //
children.translated_text: It has been turned salty, offered into the <s>vaḍavāgni</s> (submarine fire), and deposited in the hollow belly of the netherworld. (445)

children.text: iyaṃ ca kācit vācye pratīyamānārthānadhyāropeṇaiva bhavati /
children.translated_text: And this [figure] is a certain one that occurs in the expressed meaning, through the superimposition of the suggested meaning upon the literal meaning.

children.text: yathā abdherambhaḥ sthagitabhuvanābogapātālakukṣeḥ potopāyā iha hi bahavo laṅghane 'pi kṣamante /
children.translated_text: For example: 'The waters of the ocean, whose expanse covers the worlds and whose belly is the netherworld — even the many boats here are capable of crossing it;

children.text: āho riktaḥ kathamapi bhavedeṣa daivāt tadānīṃ ko nāma syādavaṭakuharālokane 'pyasya kalpaḥ // 446 //
children.translated_text: or, if by fate it were to become empty somehow, then who indeed would be competent even to behold the cavity of that abyss?' (446)
Sometimes through superimposition alone.

children.text: yathā kastvaṃ bhoḥ kathayāmi daivahatakaṃ māṃ viddhi śākhoṭakaṃ vairāgyādiva vakṣi sādhu viditaṃ kasmādidaṃ kathyate /
children.translated_text: For example: 'Who are you, sir?' 'I'll tell you — know me as a wretched <s>śākhoṭaka</s> tree, cursed by fate.' 'You speak as if from detachment — well said! But why is this told?'

children.text: vāmenātra vaṭastamadhvagajanaḥ sarvātmanā sevate na cchāyāpi paropakārakaraṇe mārgasthitasyāpi me // 447 //
children.translated_text: 'By this left-hand [side], a <s>vaṭa</s> (banyan) tree — travelers serve it with their whole being; yet not even a shadow of mine, standing by the road, serves the purpose of helping others.' (447)
Sometimes through superimposition in parts.

children.text: yathā so 'pūrvo rasanāviparyayavidhiḥ tat karṇayośvāpalaṃ dṛṣṭiḥ sā madavismṛtasvaparadik kiṃ bhūyakoktena vā /
children.translated_text: For example: 'That unprecedented reversal of the tongue's [function]! That restlessness of the ears! That gaze, confused about its own and others' directions through intoxication — but what more need be said?

children.text: sarvaṃ vismṛtavānasi bhramara he yadvāraṇo 'dyāpyasau antaḥśūnyakaro niṣevyata iti bhrātaḥ ka eṣa grahaḥ // 448 //
children.translated_text: You have forgotten everything, O bee! Yet still today that elephant, with an empty interior of his hand, is being served — brother, what is this seizure [of delusion]?' (448)

children.text: atra rasanāviparyāsaḥ śūnyakaratvaṃ ca bhramarasyāsevane na hetuḥ karṇacāpalaṃ tu hetuḥ, madaḥ pratyuta sevane nimittam //
children.translated_text: Here, the reversal of the tongue and the emptiness of the hand are not the cause of the bee's non-attendance; rather, the restlessness of the ears is the cause — while intoxication is in fact the reason for attendance.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 153)
But [when there is] the determination of the subject through absorption into another,
[or when] the subject is [presented as] something other, or [when] in the statement of meaning there is supposition — (100)
and [when there is] a reversal of the natural sequence between cause and effect — this is to be known as <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole).
When the <s>upameya</s> (comparandum), which is internally absorbed by the <s>upamāna</s> (comparans), is determined [as identical with the latter] — that is the first [type].

children.text: yathā kamalamanambhasi kamale ca kuvalaye tāni kanakalatikāyām /
children.translated_text: For example: '[Her face is] a lotus in water, and upon the lotus are <s>kuvalaya</s> (water-lily) [eyes]; those are upon a golden creeper;
and she [herself] is delicate and beautiful' — thus [they exclaim], 'What chain of portents is this?' (449)
Here, the face and other [features] are determined as having the form of a lotus and so forth.
And when that very [subject] is determined as something other — that is the second [type].

children.text: yathā aṇṇaṃ laḍahattaṇaaṃ aṇṇā via kā vi vattaṇacchāā /
children.translated_text: For example [in Prākrit]: 'Another is the beloved's manner, another indeed is some special conduct-shadow;

children.text: sāmā sāmaṇṇapaāvaiṇo reha ccia ṇa hoī // 450 //
children.translated_text: dark, with the gait of an ordinary [woman] — this line indeed does not appear [to be her].' (450)

children.text: "yadyarthasya'; yadiśabdena cecchabdena vā, uktau yat kalpanam (arthāt asaṃbhavino 'rthasya) sā tṛtīyā /
children.translated_text: 'When in the statement of meaning there is supposition' — with the word 'if' (<s>yadi</s>) or the word 'if' (<s>cet</s>), when there is supposition of an impossible meaning — that is the third [type].
For example: 'If on the full-moon night the body of the <s>amṛtāṃśu</s> (moon) were spotless,
then her face would attain the degradation of [mere] equality [with it].' (451)

children.text: kāraṇasya śīghrakāritāṃ vaktuṃ kāryasya pūrvamuktau caturthī /
children.translated_text: To express the swiftness of the cause, [when] the effect is stated first — that is the fourth [type].
For example: 'First, the heart of <s>Mālatī</s> was occupied by the arrow of the flower-bowed [<s>Kāma</s>];
afterwards, O beloved of the beautiful one, you entered the range of her eyes.' (452)
(<s>Sūtra</s> 154)
<s>Prativastūpamā</s> (counter-substantive simile) is that — (101)
where a single common [property] abides in two sentences.

children.text: sādhāraṇo dharmaḥ, upameyavākye, upamānavākye ca kathitapadasya duṣṭatayābhihitatvāt śabdabhedena yat upādīyate sā vastuno vākyārthasyopamānatvāt prativastūpamā /
children.translated_text: A common quality, [present] in the sentence of the <s>upameya</s> (comparandum) and the sentence of the <s>upamāna</s> (comparans), is expressed with different words because expressing it with the same word would be faulty — since the substantive, i.e. the sentence-meaning, serves as the comparans, it is <s>prativastūpamā</s>.

children.text: yathā devībhāvaṃ gamitā parivārapadaṃ kathaṃ bhajatveṣā /
children.translated_text: For example: 'She who has been elevated to the status of a goddess — how can she assume the role of an attendant?
Surely, a gem marked with the form of a deity is not fit for [ordinary] enjoyment.' (453)

children.text: yadi dahatyanalo 'tra kimadbhutaṃ yadi ca gauravamadriṣu kiṃ tataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'If fire burns here, what is so wondrous? If there is weightiness in mountains, what of it?
The water of the great ocean is always salty — the nature of the noble is ever unperturbed.' (454)
And so forth — the <s>mālā-prativastūpamā</s> (garland counter-substantive simile) should be observed.
Similarly, this should be applied in other cases as well.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 155)
<s>Dṛṣṭānta</s> (illustration) is the reflection of all these [figures]. (102)

children.text: eteṣāṃ sādhāraṇadharmādīnāma dṛṣṭo 'ntaḥ niśvayo yatra sa dṛṣṭāntaḥ /
children.translated_text: Where there is a perceived conclusion (<s>dṛṣṭo 'ntaḥ</s>) regarding the common properties and so forth of these — that is <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (illustration).

children.text: tvayi dṛṣṭa eva tasyā nirvāti mano manobhavajvalitam /
children.translated_text: 'Upon seeing you, her mind, burning with the fire of <s>Manobhava</s> (Love), is extinguished;
just as in the moonlight, the flower of the <s>kumud</s> (night-lotus) blooms.' (455)
This is [an illustration] by similarity.

children.text: vaidharmyeṇa tu tavāhave sāhasakarmaśarmaṇaḥ karaṃ kṛpāṇāntikamāninīṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: By dissimilarity, however: 'When [the hero], whose valor in battle brings delight, stretches his hand toward the sword,

children.text: bhaṭāḥ pareṣāṃ viśarārutāmaguḥ, dadhatyavāte sthiratāṃ hi pāṃsavaḥ // 456 //
children.translated_text: the warriors of the enemy attain the state of trembling — for dust particles maintain their steadiness [only] in the absence of wind.' (456)
(<s>Sūtra</s> 156)
When a single occurrence of a property applies to both the principal and the non-principal subjects,
that same [property] across many actions, of an agent — this is <s>dīpaka</s> (illuminator). (103)

children.text: prākaraṇikāprākaraṇikānāma arthāt upamānopameyānām dharmaḥ kriyādiḥ, ekavārameva yat upādīyate tat ekasthasyaiva samastavākyadīpanāt dīpakam /
children.translated_text: Of the contextual and non-contextual [subjects] — that is, of the <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> — when a property such as an action is employed only once, that is <s>dīpaka</s>, because the one [property] stationed in a single [subject] illuminates the entire sentence.

children.text: yathā kivaṇāṇaṃ dhaṇaṃ ṇāāṇaṃ phaṇamaṇī keśarāiṃ sīhāṇaṃ /
children.translated_text: For example [in Prākrit]: 'The wealth of merchants, the hood-jewels of serpents, the manes of lions,
the breasts of well-born girls — from where do these fall for the ignoble?' (457)
And when a single agent occurs once across many actions — that too is <s>dīpaka</s>.

children.text: yathā svidyati kūṇati vellati vicalati nimiṣati vilokayati tiryak /
children.translated_text: For example: 'She perspires, squints, trembles, fidgets, blinks, looks sideways,
inwardly delights, and wishes to be kissed — the newly-wed bride in bed.' (458)
(<s>Sūtra</s> 157)
<s>Mālādīpaka</s> (garland-illuminator) is the first if each successive [element] brings a higher quality.

children.text: pūveṃṇa pūrveṇa vastunā, uttaramuttaraṃ cedupakriyate tat mālādīpakam /
children.translated_text: When each preceding thing supports the next succeeding one — that is <s>mālādīpaka</s>.

children.text: yathā saṃgrāmāṅgaṇamāgatena bhavatā cāpe samāropite devākarṇaya yena yena sahasā yadyatsamāsāditam /
children.translated_text: For example: 'When you arrived at the battlefield and strung the bow — hear, O gods, what was swiftly accomplished with each:

children.text: kodaṇḍena śarāḥ śarairariśirastenāpi bhūmaṇḍalaṃ tena tvaṃ bhavatā ca kīrtiratulā kīrtyā ca lokatraḍalaṃ tena tvaṃ bhavatā ca kīrtiratulā kīrtyā ca lokatrayam // 459 //
children.translated_text: with the bow came arrows, with arrows the heads of enemies, with those the earth, with that you, with you incomparable fame, and with fame the three worlds.' (459)
(<s>Sūtra</s> 158)
When a single property applies to fixed [subjects] — that is <s>tulyayogitā</s> (equal conjunction). (104)
Of fixed subjects — either only the contextual ones, or only the non-contextual ones.

children.text: krameṇodāharaṇam-- pāṇḍu kṣāmaṃ vadanaṃ hṛdayaṃ sarasaṃ tavālasaṃ ca vapuḥ /
children.translated_text: Examples in order: 'Pale, emaciated is [your] face; the heart is moist, and the body languid;
O friend, the interior of the heart reveals most intensely a chronic disease.' (460)
'Before those two [eyes], playful and charming, lined with <s>kumuda</s> (white lotus), <s>kamala</s> (lotus), and dark <s>nīraja</s> (water-lily) [hues] —
the nectar, the nectar-rayed [moon], and the water-born [lotus] are all defeated at once by your face.' (461)
(<s>Sūtra</s> 159)
<s>Vyatireka</s> (distinction) is the superiority of something other than the <s>upamāna</s> (comparans) and so forth.
The distinction, i.e., the superiority, of the other — the <s>upameya</s> (comparandum).

children.text: kṣīṇaḥ kṣīṇo 'pi śaśī bhūyo bhūyo 'bhivardhate satyam /
children.translated_text: 'Though the moon wanes and wanes, truly it waxes again and again;

children.text: virama prasīda sundari yauvanamanivarti yātaṃ tu // 462 //
children.translated_text: desist, be pleased, O beautiful one — youth, once gone, does not return.' (462)

children.text:
ityādānupamānasyopameyādādhikyamiti kenaciduktam tadayuktam atra yauvanagatāsthairyādhikyaṃ hi vivakṣitam /
(sū- 160)
children.translated_text:
And so forth. That the <s>upamāna</s> is superior to the <s>upameya</s>, as some have said — that is incorrect; for here, the superiority of the transitoriness of youth is what is intended.
