(<s>Sūtra</s> 160)
When among three [types] — statement, non-statement [of the cause] — the equality is expressed with the reason: (105)
both by word and meaning, or when implied, or when joined through <s>śleṣa</s> (double entendre) — thus three times eight, that [is <s>vyatireka</s>].

children.text: vyatirekasya hetuḥ, upameyagatamutkarṣanimittam upamānagatamapakarṣakāraṇam tayordvayoruktiḥ, ekatarasya dvayorvā, anuktirityanuktitrayam etadbhedacatuṣṭayamupamānopameyabhāve śabdena pratipādite, ārthena ca krameṇoktāśvatvāra eva bhedāḥ, ākṣipte caupamye tāvanta eva, evaṃ dvādaśa /
children.translated_text: The cause of <s>vyatireka</s> [consists of]: the reason for the superiority in the <s>upameya</s> and the reason for the inferiority in the <s>upamāna</s> — the statement of both, [or] the non-statement of one or both — thus the three [types of] non-statement; this fourfold distinction, when the <s>upamāna</s>-<s>upameya</s> relation is conveyed by word, and by meaning — in each case four varieties; and when the comparison is implied, just as many — thus twelve.
These occur also with <s>śleṣa</s> (double entendre), hence twenty-four varieties.
Examples in order: 'With only a sword as his companion, in the destruction of numerous enemies,
unlike other lowly people, there is no pride in this one of great fortitude.' (463)

children.text: atraiva tuccheti mahādhṛterityanayoḥ paryāyeṇa yugapadvānupādāne 'nyat bhedatrayam /

children.translated_text: Similarly, the same should be observed in the other [cases] as well.
Here, because of the presence of the word <s>iva</s> (like), the comparison is expressed verbally.
'Even with only a sword as companion, in the defeat of numerous enemies,
this man of great fortitude has no pride at all, unlike other lowly people.' (464)
In this very [verse], by alternately or simultaneously omitting the [words] 'lowly' (<s>tuccha</s>) and 'of great fortitude' (<s>mahādhṛteḥ</s>), three other varieties [are obtained].
Here, the particle <s>vat</s> (like) [is used] in the sense of equality — hence the comparison is conveyed by meaning.
'This <s>Sunayanā</s> (beautiful-eyed one), having reduced the beauty of lotuses to servitude,
conquers the spotty moon with her spotless face.' (465)
Here, in the absence of words like <s>iva</s> (like) and <s>tulya</s> (equal), the simile is merely implied.
'Of one who has conquered the senses, who properly attends upon the learned elders,
whose qualities are deeply rooted — his virtues are not fragile like those of a lotus.' (466)
Here, the particle <s>vat</s> in the sense [of comparison] and the word <s>guṇa</s> (quality/string) as a <s>śleṣa</s> (double entendre) — this is a verbal comparison.
'Behold this lord of the earth, resplendent, with an unbroken orb [of sovereignty];
unlike the moon, he has never attained any diminution of his digits [of excellence].' (467)

children.text:
a6 tulyārthe vatiḥ kalāśabdaḥ śliṣṭaḥ /
mālāpratikastūpamāvat mālāvyatireko 'pi saṃbhavati /

children.translated_text: Its varieties too should be inferred in the same manner.
Only a sample is illustrated.
For example: 'Not like <s>Hara</s> (Śiva) do you have a hostile gaze; not like <s>Hari</s> (Viṣṇu), O Lord, have you shaken off the great bull;
nor like <s>Ravi</s> (the Sun), have you ever scorched the earth with unbearably hot rays.' (468)

The particle <s>vat</s> is used in the sense of equality; the word <s>kalā</s> (digit/art) is a <s>śleṣa</s>.
Just as with <s>mālā-prativastūpamā</s> (garland counter-substantive simile), <s>mālā-vyatireka</s> (garland distinction) is also possible.

children.text: atra tulyārthe vatiḥ viṣamādayaśva śabdāḥ śliṣṭāḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the particle <s>vat</s> is in the sense of equality, and the words <s>viṣama</s> (hostile/odd) and others are <s>śleṣa</s> (double entendres).
'With eternally risen splendor, dimming the radiance of the three watches of the night,
the Sun (<s>Bhāsvat</s>) is vanquished by this king (<s>Bhūpa</s>).' (469)
Here, the simile is merely implied, and the word <s>bhāsvat</s> (radiant one) is a <s>śleṣa</s>.
Or for example: 'The moon-disc shining with the quality of pure-selfness, the naturally lovely fragrance [resembling] <s>bimba</s>-fruit-hued lips,

children.text: yūnāmatīva pibatāṃ rajanīṣu yatra tṛṣṇāṃ jahāra madhu nānanamaṅganānām // 470 //
children.translated_text: the nectar [of the wine that] on [those] nights, for young men drinking [it], completely removed the thirst — that was not the face of women.' (470)

children.text: atrevādīnāṃ tulyādīnāṃ ca padānāmabhāve 'pi śliṣṭaviśeṣaṇairākṣiptaivopamā pratīyate /
children.translated_text: Here, even in the absence of words like <s>iva</s> (like) and <s>tulya</s> (equal), the simile is perceived as implied through the <s>śleṣa</s>-qualified adjectives.

children.text: evaṃjātīyakāḥ śliṣṭoktiyogyasya padasya pṛthagupādāne 'nye 'pi bhedāḥ saṃbhavanti /
children.translated_text: Thus, when a word suitable for <s>śleṣa</s> (double entendre) expression is separately employed, other varieties too are possible.
These too should be understood in the same direction.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 161)
The negation of what one wishes to state, with the intention of expressing a distinction — (106)
having the domain of what is to be said and what has been said — that is known as <s>ākṣepa</s> (objection/ironic denial), of two kinds.

children.text: vivakṣitasya prākaraṇikatvādanupasarjanīkāryasya, aśakyavaktavyatvamatiprasiddhatvaṃ vā viśeṣaṃ vaktuṃ niṣedho niṣedha iva yaḥ sa vakṣyamāṇaviṣaya uktaviṣayaśveti dvidhā, ākṣepaḥ /
children.translated_text: The negation — or rather, what resembles negation — of what is intended [to be stated], which, being the principal topic, should not be subordinated, [done] in order to express a special distinction, [namely] the impossibility of adequate expression or the extreme familiarity — this is <s>ākṣepa</s>, of two kinds: having the domain of what is about to be said, and having the domain of what has been said.

children.text: krameṇodāharaṇam-- e ehi kiṃpi kīevi kaeṇa ṇikviva bhaṇāmi alamaha vā /
children.translated_text: Examples in order [in Prākrit]: 'Come, come! Shall I say something? No, enough, I shall not speak;
[for] speech becomes the initiator of tasks for the unfaithful — I shall not say it.' (471)

children.text: jyotsnā mauktikadāma candanarasaḥ śītāṃśukāntadravaḥ karpūraṃ kadalī mṛṇālavalayānyambhojinīpallavāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Moonlight, a pearl necklace, sandalwood paste, the cool liquid radiance of the moon, camphor, plantain, lotus-stalk bracelets, lotus leaves —

children.text: anyarmānasamāstvayā prabhavatā tasyāḥ sphuliṅgotkara- vyāpārāya bhavanti inta hanta kimanenoktena na brūmahe // 472 //
children.translated_text: all these become, for that proud woman of yours, O master, [mere] fuel for the work of sparks — alas, alas! What use is there in saying more? We shall not speak.' (472)
(<s>Sūtra</s> 162)
Even when the action [that is the cause] is negated, the manifestation of the result is <s>vibhāvanā</s> (causeless causation). (107)
Even when the action that has the form of a cause is negated, the manifestation of its result — that is <s>vibhāvanā</s>.
For example: 'Though not struck by flowering creepers, she suffered pain; though not bitten by swarms of bees,
she writhed; though not tossed by the waves of the lotus pond, she reeled and swayed.' (473)
(<s>Sūtra</s> 163)
<s>Viśeṣokti</s> (distinction-statement) is the non-statement of the effect when all the causes are present.
When the causes are all present yet the effect is not stated — that is <s>viśeṣokti</s>.
[It is of three kinds:] with unstated cause, with stated cause, and with inconceivable cause.

children.text: krameṇodārahaṇam-- nidrānivṛttāvudite dyuratne sakhījane dvārapadaṃ parāpte /
children.translated_text: Examples in order: 'When sleep had departed, when the day-jewel [sun] had risen, when the group of friends had arrived at the door,
when the serpent [of her braid] had loosened its coils — still that woman did not leave the embrace.' (474)

children.text: karpūra iva dagdho 'pi śaktimān yo jane jane /
children.translated_text: 'Like camphor, though burnt, he is potent among all people;
obeisance to that <s>Makaraketana</s> (Kāma, the god of love) whose valor is irresistible!' (475)
'He alone, the flower-weaponed [<s>Kāma</s>], conquers the three worlds;

children.text: haratāpi tanuṃ yasya śaṃbhunā na balaṃ hṛtam // 476 //
children.translated_text: even when <s>Śambhu</s> (Śiva) destroyed his body, his power was not taken away.' (476)
(<s>Sūtra</s> 164)
<s>Yathāsaṃkhya</s> (enumeration in order) is the sequential correlation of items arranged in order. (108)

children.text: yathā ekastridhā vasasi cetasi citramatra deva dviṣāṃ ca viduṣāṃ ca mṛgīdṛśāṃ ca /
children.translated_text: For example: 'O Lord, you dwell in three [kinds of] minds — how marvelous this is — in [the minds of] enemies, the learned, and the doe-eyed women;

children.text: tāpaṃ ca saṃmadarasaṃ ca ratiṃ ca puṣṇan śauryoṣmaṇā ca vinayena ca līlayā ca // 477 //
children.translated_text: nourishing heat, the sentiment of intoxication, and love respectively — through the fire of valor, through modesty, and through sportive grace.' (477)
(<s>sūtra</s> 165)

children.text: sāmānyaṃ vā viśeṣo vā tadanyena samarthyate /
children.translated_text: Whether the general or the particular is corroborated by another,
that is <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroboration) — through similarity or through dissimilarity. (109)

children.text: sādharmyeṇa vaidharmyeṇa vā sāmānyaṃ viśeṣeṇa yat samarthyate viśeṣo vā sāmānyena so 'rthāntaranyāsaḥ /
children.translated_text: Through similarity (<s>sādharmya</s>) or dissimilarity (<s>vaidharmya</s>), when a general [proposition] is corroborated by a particular, or a particular is corroborated by a general — that is <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s>.
Examples in order: 'For those whose minds are covered by their own faults, even what is exceedingly beautiful appears as the opposite;
one afflicted by bile sees even a conch shell white as the moon as yellow.' (478)

children.text: susitavasanālaṃkārāyāṃ kadācana kaumudī- mahasi sudṛśi svairaṃ yāntyāṃ gato 'stamabhūdvidhuḥ /
children.translated_text: 'On a certain moonlit night, when that lovely lady was strolling freely, adorned with white garments and ornaments, the moon set;

children.text: tadanu bhavataḥ kīrtiḥ kenāpyagīyata yena sā priyagṛhamagānmuktāśaṅkā kva nāsi śubhapradaḥ // 479 //
children.translated_text: thereafter, some person sang your fame — because of which she, freed from doubt, went to her beloved's house: "Where are you not present, O bestower of auspiciousness?"' (479)
'It is precisely because of its virtues that the foremost is yoked to the yoke;
the ox <s>Gali</s>, whose shoulder has not yet developed calluses, sleeps happily.' (480)

children.text: aho hi me bahvaparāddhamāyuṣā yadapriyaṃ vācyamidaṃ mayedṛśam /
children.translated_text: 'Alas, much has been offended by my life, in that such an unpleasant thing must be spoken by me;

children.text: ta eva dhanyāḥ suhṛdaḥ parābhavaṃ jagatyadṛṣṭvaiva hi ye kṣayaṃ gatāḥ // 481 //
children.translated_text: truly fortunate are those friends who, without having seen the humiliation of [their people] in the world, have passed away.' (481)
(<s>sūtra</s> 166)
<s>Virodha</s> (contradiction) is speech that [presents something] as contradictory even when there is no [actual] contradiction.
When there is no actual contradiction (<s>avirodha</s>) in the factual occurrence, yet the statement is as if of contradictory things — that is <s>virodha</s>. (<s>sūtra</s> 167)
A universal (<s>jāti</s>) is contradicted by four [means]; a quality (<s>guṇa</s>) by three among universals and the like. (110)

children.text: kriyā dvābhyāmapi dravyaṃ dravyeṇaiveti te daśa /
children.translated_text: An action (<s>kriyā</s>) by two; and a substance (<s>dravya</s>) by substance alone — thus they are ten.
Examples in order: 'Fresh lotus-bud, fiber-bracelet, and the like — [yet] a mass of forest fire;
O handsome one, for this doe-eyed [lady], by the power of fate in the calamity of separation from you.' (482)
'Mountains too are without loftiness, the wind too is unmoving, the oceans too are without depth;
the earth-bearer too is exceedingly light — O lord of men, certainly in your presence.' (483)

children.text: yeṣāṃ kaṇṭhaparigrahapraṇayitāṃ saṃprāpya dhārādhara- stīkṣṇaḥ so 'pyanurajyate ca kamapi snehaṃ parāpnoti ca /
children.translated_text: 'Upon receiving the embrace of the river of rut-water flowing from the temples of your rutting elephants,

children.text: teṣāṃ saṃgarasahgasaktamanasāṃ rājñāṃ tvayā bhūpate pāṃsūnāṃ paṭalaiḥ praśādhanavidhirnirvartyate kautukam // 484 //
children.translated_text: even the fierce [cloud] becomes affectionate and attains a certain love; O king, of those kings whose minds are absorbed in the encounter of battle, the toilette is accomplished by you with layers of dust — how marvelous!' (484)

children.text: sṛjati ca jagadidamavati ca saṃharati ca helayaiva yo niyatam /
children.translated_text: 'He who, with mere sport, always creates this world, protects it, and destroys it —
that <s>Janārdana</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), depending on the occasion, [becomes] a small fish (<s>śaphara</s>) — this is indeed wonderful!' (485)
'O king, always engaged with the pestle, occupied with abundant household work,

children.text: dvijapatnīnāṃ paṭhināḥ sati bhavati karāḥ sarojasukumārāḥ // 486 //
children.translated_text: the hands of <s>brāhmaṇa</s> wives are [as] hard as fish — yet, O lord, they are [still] tender as lotuses.' (486)
'Even pleasant speech of a wicked person burns the minds of the virtuous exceedingly;
but harsh speech of a good person, like sandalwood paste, delights.' (487)
'That <s>Bhārgava</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>), who was hard as the solid rock blocking the <s>Krauñca</s> mountain, through the fierce fall of his unstoppable arrows;
became [tender] as a fresh lotus petal — truly, he was a wondrous creation.' (488)

children.text: paricchedātītaḥ sakalavacanānāmaviṣayaḥ punarjanmanyasminnanubhavapathaṃ yo na gatavāt /
children.translated_text: 'Beyond the reach of measurement, beyond the scope of all words, not having entered the path of experience in this birth;

children.text: vivekapradhvaṃsādupacitamahāmohagahano vikāraḥ ko 'pyantarjaḍhayati ca tāpaṃ ca kurute // 489 //
children.translated_text: from the destruction of discernment, dense with accumulated great delusion — some inexplicable inner transformation both stupefies and causes anguish.' (489)

children.text: ayaṃ vārāmekī nilaya iti ratnākara iti śrito 'smābhistṛṣṇātaralitamanobhirjalanidhiḥ /
children.translated_text: '"This is our sole water-resource, this is the ocean of gems" — thus was the ocean resorted to by us whose minds are agitated by thirst;

children.text: ka evaṃ jānīte nijakarapuṭīkoṭaragataṃ kṣaṇādenaṃ tāmyattimimakaramāpāsyati muniḥ // 490 //
children.translated_text: who could know that this sage, with the ocean held in the hollow of his own palm, would instantly dry up this [ocean] with its suffering fish and sea-monsters?' (490)
'Through the embrace of the river of rut-water streaming from your rutting elephants in the equal [contest],
O ornament of the earth, when you stand on the bank, even the <s>Kālindī</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>) [becomes like] the river on <s>Śiva's</s> crest (<s>Gaṅgā</s>).' (491)
(<s>sūtra</s> 168)
<s>Svabhāvokti</s> (natural description) is the depiction of the characteristic action, form, and appearance of a child and the like. (111)
Of its own — the action and form belonging to one and the same [subject].
'Form' (<s>rūpa</s>) means color; 'appearance' (<s>saṃsthāna</s>) means shape.

children.text: udāharaṇam-- paśvādaṅghrī prasārya trikanativitataṃ drāghayitvāṅgamuccaiḥ āsajyābhugnakaṇṭho mukhamurasi saṭāṃ dhūlidhūmrāṃ vidhūya /
children.translated_text: Example: 'Stretching its legs first, extending its body high with its back arched threefold, pressing its crooked neck [down], shaking the dust-gray mane upon its chest;

children.text: ghāsagrāsābhilāṣādanavaratacalatprothatuṇḍasturaṅgo mandaṃ śabdāyamāno vilakhati śayanādutthitaḥ kṣmāṃ khureṇa // 492 //
children.translated_text: with its muzzle constantly moving from the desire of grasping a mouthful of grass, gently neighing, the horse, having risen from its bed, scratches the ground with its hoof.' (492)
(<s>sūtra</s> 169)
<s>Vyājastuti</s> (ironic praise) is [speech] where on the surface there is blame, but [the intent is] praise; or established otherwise.
That which is in the form of a pretext, or praise through a pretext.

children.text: krameṇodāharaṇam-- hitvā tvāmuparodhavanadhyamanasāṃ manye na mauliḥ paro lajjāvarjanamantareṇa na ramāmanyatra saṃdṛśyate /
children.translated_text: Examples in order: 'Having forsaken you, I think there is no other crest-jewel for those whose minds are engaged in the rivalry of obstruction; modesty is not seen in any other without the avoidance of shame;

children.text: yastyāgaṃ tanutetarāṃ mukhaśatairetyāśritāyāḥ śriyaḥ prāpya tyāgakṛtāvamānanamapi tvayyeva yasyāḥ sthitiḥ // 493 //
children.translated_text: who extends renunciation exceedingly, with a hundred faces — of that <s>Śrī</s> (Prosperity) who has sought refuge, even though insulted by the renunciation done [to her], her abode is in you alone.' (493)

children.text: he helājitabaudhisacva vacasāṃ kiṃ vistaraistoyadhe nāsti tvatsadṛśaḥ paraḥ parahitādhāne gṛhītavrataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'O you who have effortlessly conquered the wise, what use are elaborate words, O rain-cloud? There is no other equal to you, who has taken the vow of conferring benefit on others;
having gained disrepute through aversion to rendering service to thirsty travelers, you compassionately render assistance to the wind (<s>Maru</s>) in bearing the burden of that infamy.' (494)
(<s>sūtra</s> 170)
<s>Sahokti</s> (combined expression) is where a single word, by the force of the meaning 'together with,' expresses both. (112)

children.text: ekārthābidhāyakamapi sahārthabalāt yat ubhayasyāpyavagamakaṃ sā sahoktiḥ /
children.translated_text: Even though denoting a single meaning, that which, by the force of the meaning of 'together with' (<s>saha</s>), conveys both — that is <s>sahokti</s>.

children.text: yathā saha diahaṇisāhiṃ dīharā sāsadaṇḍā saha maṇivalayehiṃ bāppadhārā galanti /
children.translated_text: For example: 'Together with long sighing, the long days; together with a stick, together with bangle-jewels, streams of tears flow;

children.text: tuha suhaa vioe tīa uvviggirīe saha a taṇuladāe dubbalā jīvidāsā // 495 //
children.translated_text: O friend, in separation from you, of the frightened woman, together with the slender creeper-[like body], the feeble hope of life [withers].' (495)

children.text: śvāsadaṇḍādigataṃ dīrgatvādi śābdam divasaniśādigataṃ tu sahārthasāmarthyātpratipadyate //
children.translated_text: The length and the like pertaining to sighing-stick and the like is verbal; but that pertaining to day-night and the like is understood through the force of the meaning of 'together with.'
(<s>sūtra</s> 171)

children.text: vinoktiḥ sā vinānyena yatrānyaḥ sanna netaraḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Vinokti</s> (expression of absence) is where, without one, another exists but is not [truly] the other.
In some cases, [the absent thing is] unattractive; in other cases, [it is] attractive.

children.text: krameṇodāharaṇam-- arucirniśayā vinā śaśī śaśinā sāpi vinā mahattamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Examples in order: 'The moon is without luster without the night; the night too without the moon is exceedingly dark;

children.text: ubhayena vinā manobhavasphuritaṃ naiva cakāsti kāminoḥ // 496 //
children.translated_text: without both, the stirring of the god of love (<s>Manmatha</s>) simply does not shine for lovers.' (496)
'Without the doe-eyed lady, [he is] bold in the brilliance of the genius of varied conduct;
this prince, of beautiful disposition like the nectar-rayed [moon], is without that friend [but still radiant].' (497)
(<s>sūtra</s> 172)
<s>Parivṛtti</s> (exchange) is the mutual exchange of meanings between equals or unequals. (113)
<s>Parivṛtti</s> is the ornament [of exchange].

children.text: udāharaṇam-- latānāmetāsāmuditakusumānāṃ marudayaṃ mataṃ lāsyaṃ datvā śrayati bhṛśamāmodamasamam /
children.translated_text: Example: 'The wind, having given to these creepers in bloom the dance of their blossoming flowers, takes on an incomparable fragrance;
but the creepers of the highways, alas, suddenly seizing the glance [of travelers], give in return a confusion of wandering, weeping, and delusion.' (498)

children.text: atra prathame 'rdhe samena samasya dvitīye, uttamena nyūnasya /
children.translated_text: Here, in the first half, of an equal with an equal; in the second, of an inferior with a superior.
'O king, in battle with various weapons, having received the blows accompanied by terrible sounds,
this earth has been bestowed by the host of your proud enemy-heroes — a mode of embrace without deception.' (499)
Here, of an inferior with a superior.
(<s>sūtra</s> 173)

children.text:
pratyakṣā iva yadbhāvāḥ kriyante bhūtabhāvinaḥ /
tadbhāvikam
children.translated_text: When past and future states are made as if directly present — that is <s>bhāvika</s> (vivification).
'Past and future' — this is a <s>dvandva</s> compound.
'There is a <s>bhāva</s> (intention) of the poet herein' — therefore it is called <s>bhāvika</s>.
Example: 'I see collyrium that was [applied] here in your eye;
I behold directly your form with its future array of ornaments.' (500)
In the first [line], the seeing of the past; in the second, of the future.
(<s>sūtra</s> 174)
<s>Kāvyaliṅga</s> (poetic reason) is where a reason has the status of a sentence or word-meaning. (114)

children.text: vākyārthatā yathā vapuḥprādurbhāvādanumitamidaṃ janmani purā purāre na prāyaḥ kvacidapi bhavantaṃ praṇatavān /
children.translated_text: As a sentence-meaning, for example: 'From the manifestation of [your] body, it is inferred that in a former birth, O enemy of <s>Pura</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), I had for the most part not bowed to you anywhere;

children.text: naman muktaḥ saṃpratyahamatanuragre 'pyanatibhāk maheśa kṣantavyaṃ tadidamaparādhadvayamapi // 501 //
children.translated_text: now, bowing, liberated — though having no bowing even before a subordinate — O great lord, both these offenses should be forgiven.' (501)

children.text: anekapadārthatā yathā praṇayisakhīsalīlaparihāsarasādhigatai- rlalitaśirīṣapuṣpahananairapi tāmyati yat /
children.translated_text: As a multiple word-meaning, for example: 'That body which suffers even from the blows of delicate <s>śirīṣa</s> flowers, [delivered] in the playful jesting of loving companions;

children.text: vapuṣi vadhāya tatra tava śastramupakṣipataḥ patatu śirasyakāṇḍayamadaṇḍa ivaiṣa bhujaḥ // 502 //
children.translated_text: upon that [body], as you cast a weapon for the purpose of killing, may this arm fall upon your head like the staff of <s>Yama</s> appearing without warning.' (502)

children.text: ekapadārthatā yathā bhasmoddhūlana bhadramastu bhavate rudrākṣamāle śubhaṃ hā sopānaparaṃparāṃ girisutākāntālayālaṃkṛtim /
children.translated_text: As a single word-meaning, for example: 'May the smearing of ashes be auspicious for you; may the rosary of <s>rudrākṣa</s> beads be propitious; alas, the flight of steps, the ornament of the dwelling of the beloved of the daughter of the mountain (<s>Pārvatī</s>);

children.text: adyārādhanatoṣitena vibhunā yuṣmatsaparyāsukhā- lokocchedini mokṣanāmani mahāmohe nidhīyāmahe // 503 //
children.translated_text: today, by the Lord who is pleased through worship, we are being deposited in that great delusion called liberation, which cuts off the happiness of beholding your worship.' (503)

children.text: eṣu, aparādhadvaye pūrvāparajanmanoranamanam bhujapāte śastropakṣepaḥ, mahāmohe sukhāvalokoccheditvaṃ ca yathākramamuktarūpo hetuḥ //
children.translated_text: In these [examples], the reason is in the stated form — respectively: in the two offenses, the non-bowing in the former and latter births; in the falling of the arm, the casting of the weapon; and in the great delusion, the cutting off of the happiness of beholding.
(<s>sūtra</s> 175)
<s>Paryāyokta</s> (indirect expression) is speech that [conveys meaning] without the relation of expressed and expresser.

children.text: vācyavācakabhāvavyatiriktenāvagamanavyāpāreṇa yat pratipādanaṃ tat paryāyeṇa, bhaṅgyantareṇa kathanāt paryāyoktam /
children.translated_text: That which conveys [meaning] through a mode of apprehension other than the relation of expressed and expresser — that is <s>paryāyokta</s>, because of stating indirectly, by a different turn of phrase.
Example: 'Upon seeing which, even the long-established affection for one's dwelling was abandoned —
by intoxication on the face of <s>Airāvaṇa</s> (<s>Indra's</s> elephant), by pride in the heart of <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>).' (504)

children.text:
atra, airāvaṇaśakrau madamānamuktau jātāviti vyaṅgyamapi śabdenocyate tena yadevocyate tadeva vyaṅgyam /
yathā tu vyaṅgyaṃ na tathocyate /
yathā gavi śukle calati dṛṣṭe "gauḥ śuklaśvalati'; iti vikalpaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as when a white cow is moving and is perceived, there is the conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>): 'A white cow is moving.'

children.text: yadeva dṛṣṭaṃ tadeva vikalpayati na tu yathā dṛṣṭaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: One constructs conceptually precisely what is perceived — but not in the way it is perceived.
Because it is not perceived as undifferentiated and unblended.
One constructs conceptually through differentiation and combination.

Here, what is suggested (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) is that <s>Airāvaṇa</s> and <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>) abandoned their intoxication and pride respectively — and even the suggested is stated through words. Thus what is stated is itself the suggested. But it is not stated in the way the suggested [normally is].
(<s>sūtra</s> 176)
<s>Udātta</s> (the exalted) is the prosperity of a thing.
'Prosperity' (<s>saṃpat</s>) means endowment with affluence.

children.text: yathā muktāḥ kelivisūtrahāragalitāḥ saṃmārjanībhirhṛtāḥ prātaḥ prāṅgaṇasīmni mantharacaladbālāṅgrilākṣāruṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: For example: 'Pearls, fallen from the strings of playful necklaces, gathered by brooms, reddened with the lac from the slowly moving toes of children in the morning at the threshold of the courtyard —

children.text: dūrāddāḍimabījaśaṅkitadhiyaḥ karṣanti kelīśukāḥ yadvidvadbhavaneṣu bhojanṛpatestat tyāgalīlāyitam // 505 //
children.translated_text: the pet parrots, mistaking them from afar for pomegranate seeds, drag them away. In the houses of the learned, this is the mere play of the generosity of King <s>Bhoja</s>.' (505)
(<s>sūtra</s> 177)
And [it is also] the indication of the great. (115)
'Indication' (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>) means the state of being a subordinate element — [indicating] the indicated meaning from the [stated] meaning.
Example: 'This is that very forest, dwelling in which, <s>Rāma</s>, devoted to the observance of <s>Daśaratha's</s> word,
with his arms as his sole companion, accomplished the destruction of the <s>Rākṣasas</s>.' (506)
And here the heroic is not the [dominant] <s>rasa</s>, because it is subordinate to [the dominant rasa] here.
(<s>sūtra</s> 178)
When, for the accomplishment of that [result], where one [cause] exists, another that contributes to it also arises — that is <s>samuccaya</s> (accumulation).

children.text: tasya prastutasya kāryasya, ekasmin sādhake sthite sādhakāntarāṇi yatra saṃbhavanti sa samuccayaḥ /
children.translated_text: When one factor sufficient for [producing] that result of the subject at hand exists, and other contributing factors also arise — that is <s>samuccaya</s>.

children.text: udāharaṇam-- durvārāḥ smahamārgaṇāḥ priyatamo dūre mano 'tyutsukaṃ gāḍhaṃ preṇa navaṃ vayo 'tikaṭhināḥ prāṇāḥ kulaṃ nirmalam /
children.translated_text: Example: 'The arrows of the god of love are irresistible, the beloved is far away, the mind is exceedingly eager, love is intense, youth is fresh, the vital breaths are exceedingly obstinate, the family is pure,

children.text: strītvaṃ dhairyavirodhi manmathasuhṛt kālaḥ kṛtānto 'kṣamo no sakhyaśvaturāḥ kathaṃ nu virahaḥ soḍhavya itthaṃ śaṭhaḥ // 507 //
children.translated_text: womanhood is opposed to steadfastness, the season is a friend of <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love), time is pitiless, and friends are not alert — how indeed is this separation to be endured? Thus [speaks] the deceiver.' (507)

children.text: atra virahāsahatvaṃ smaramārgaṇā eva kurvanti tadupari priyatamadūrasthityādi, upāttam /
children.translated_text: Here, the arrows of the god of love alone produce the inability to bear separation; on top of that, the distance of the beloved and the like are additionally introduced.

children.text: eṣa eva samuccayaḥ sadyoge 'sadyoge sadasadyoge ca paryavasyatīti na pṛthaklakṣyate /
children.translated_text: This very <s>samuccaya</s> culminates in [three cases:] the conjunction of [factors] that are [all] present, the conjunction of [factors] that are [all] absent, and the conjunction of present and absent [factors] — therefore it is not defined separately.

children.text: tathāhi-- kulamamalinaṃ bhadrā mūrtirmatiḥ śrutiśālinī bhujabalamalaṃ sphītā lakṣmīḥ prabhutvamakhaṇḍitam /
children.translated_text: Thus: 'The lineage is spotless, the form is gracious, the intellect is adorned with learning, the strength of arms is sufficient, prosperity is abundant, sovereignty is unbroken;

children.text: prakṛtisubhagā hyete bhāvā amībhirayaṃ jano vrajati sutarāṃ darpaṃ rājan ta eva tavāṅkuśāḥ // 508 //
children.translated_text: these qualities, naturally charming — O king, these same [qualities] by which this person attains excessive pride are your very goads [for controlling him].' (508)
Here, the conjunction is of [factors that are all] present.
In the previously stated example, the conjunction is of [factors that are all] absent.

children.text: śaśī divasadhūsaro galatayauvanā kāminī saro vigatavārijaṃ mukhamanakṣaraṃ svākṛteḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The moon [is] grey by day, the woman [is one] whose youth is fading, the lake [is one] without lotuses, the face [is one] without learning, of its own nature —

children.text: prabhurdhanaparāyaṇaḥ satatadurgataḥ sajjano nṛpāṅgaṇagataḥ khalo manasi sapta śalyāni me // 509 //
children.translated_text: 'The master is devoted to wealth; the good man is always in difficulty; the wicked man is in the king's court — seven thorns are in my mind.' // 509 //

children.text:
atra śaśini dhūsare śalye śalyāntarāṇīti śobhanāśobhanayogaḥ /
(sū- 179)
children.translated_text: Here, [when applying the figure of] 'the moon is dim,' then 'as a thorn [one thing leads to] other thorns' — this is the conjunction of the auspicious and the inauspicious. (Sūtra 179)
But that other [type], simultaneously, [involves] qualities and actions. // 116 //

children.text: guṇau ca kriye ca guṇakriye ca guṇakriyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Both qualities and actions, and qualities-and-actions [combined] — [these are] qualities-and-actions.

children.text: krameṇodāharaṇam-- vidalitasagalārikulaṃ tava balamidamabhavadāśu vimalaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Examples in order: 'This army of yours, having shattered the enemy hosts, quickly became bright;

children.text: prakhalamukhāni narādhipa malināni ca tāni jātāni // 510 //
children.translated_text: their faces, O lord of men, became clear in front — and those [enemy faces] became dim.' // 510 //

children.text: ayamekapade tayā viyogaḥ priyayā copanataḥ suduḥsaho me /
children.translated_text: 'This separation from my beloved, who has come near, is exceedingly difficult for me to bear;
and by the rising of new rain-clouds, the days must become lovely though without shelter.' // 511 //
'Your eye, suddenly [turned] upon your enemies — O sister of the white lotus in beauty —

children.text: patitaṃ ca mahīpatīndra teṣāṃ vapuṣi prasphuṭamāpadāṃ kaṭākṣaiḥ // 512 //
children.translated_text: has fallen, O lord of kings, upon their bodies through side-glances clearly [foretelling] calamities.' // 512 //

children.text: "dhunoti cāsiṃ tanute ca kīrtim'; ityādeḥ "kṛpāṇapāṇiśva bhavān raṇakṣitau sasādhuvādāśva surāḥ surālaye'; ityādeśva darśanāt "vyadhikaraṇe'; iti "ekasmin deśe'; iti ca na vācyam //
children.translated_text: From examples such as 'he wields the sword and extends his fame,' and 'you, with sword in hand, on the battlefield, and the gods, with words of praise, in the abode of the gods' — since such [examples] are visible, one should not say 'in different loci' or 'in one place.'
(<s>Sūtra</s> 180)
<s>Paryāya</s> (sequence) is [the figure where] a single [thing occurs] successively in many [loci].

children.text: ekaṃ vastu krameṇānekasmin bhavati kriyate vā sa paryāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Paryāya</s> is where a single entity successively exists in or is placed in many [locations].
Examples in order: 'O <s>Kālakūṭa</s> (deadly poison)! Who has instructed you in this course of residence — ever more distinguished in position?

children.text: prāgarṇavasya hṛdaye vṛṣalakṣmaṇo 'tha kaṇṭhe 'dhunā vasasi vāci punaḥ khalānām // 513 //
children.translated_text: First you dwelt in the heart of the ocean; then on the throat of <s>Vṛṣalakṣman</s> (<s>Śiva</s>); and now you reside in the speech of wicked people.' // 513 //
'O slender one, your redness (<s>rāga</s>) was previously seen only in your <s>bimba</s>-fruit lips;
now, O doe-eyed one, it is also perceived in your heart.' // 514 //
Although there is actually a difference in the redness (<s>rāga</s>), because it is determined as one, the oneness is not contradictory.
[In Prakrit:] 'With him — in the robbery of the companion of <s>Śrī</s> — of one essence, hidden in the heart,
the [redness/passion] of the beloved has been deposited on the <s>bimba</s>-fruit lips by the Flower-arrowed one (<s>Kāma</s>).' // 515 //
(<s>Sūtra</s> 181)
The other [type] is the reverse.

children.text: anekamekasmin krameṇa bhavati kriyate vā so 'nyaḥ /
children.translated_text: When many [things occur] successively in a single [locus], that is the other [type of <s>paryāya</s>].

children.text: krameṇodāharaṇam-- madhurimaruciraṃ vacaḥ khalānāmamṛtamaho prathamaṃ pṛthu vyanakti /
children.translated_text: Examples in order: 'The speech of the wicked, charming with sweetness — at first it widely reveals nectar, as it were;

children.text: atha kathayati mohahetumantargatamiva hālahalaṃ viṣaṃ tadeva // 516 //
children.translated_text: but then it reveals the <s>hālāhala</s> poison concealed within, a cause of delusion — that very same [speech].' // 516 //

children.text: tadgehaṃ natabhitti mandiramidaṃ labdhāvakāśaṃ divaḥ sā dhenurjaratī nadanti kariṇāmetā ghanābhā ghaṭāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'That house with its bending wall — this is a mansion that has obtained access to heaven. That cow — an aged one. Those [things that] thunder like elephants — these are cloud-like pots.

children.text: sa kṣudro mukaladhvaniḥ kalamidaṃ saṃgītakaṃ yoṣitām āśvaryaṃ divasairdvijo 'miyatīṃ bhūmiṃ samāropitaḥ // 517 //
children.translated_text: That meager sound of a flute — this is the sweet music of women. Wonder! By days, the twice-born (<s>dvija</s>) has been elevated to this [sad] state of affairs.' // 517 //
Here, because the taking up and giving up of one and the same [thing] is not intended, it is not <s>parivṛtti</s> (exchange).
(<s>Sūtra</s> 182)
<s>Anumāna</s> (inference) is that statement which involves the <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved) and the <s>sādhana</s> (means of proof). // 117 //

The <s>sādhana</s> (means of proof) is a reason possessing three characteristics — being a property of the subject (<s>pakṣadharma</s>), positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>), and negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>).
In the subject (<s>dharmin</s>), the exclusion of non-possession — the pervading [property] being the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum).

children.text: yathā yatraitā laharīcalācaladṛśo vyāpārayanti bhruvaṃ yat tatraiva patanti saṃtatamamī marmaspṛśo mārgaṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: Example: 'Where these women of rolling eyes trembling like waves ply their eyebrows, there these arrows that pierce the vital parts constantly fall.

children.text: taccakrīkṛtacāpamañcitaśarapreṅkhatkaraḥ krodhano dhāvatyagrata eva śāsanadharaḥ satyaṃ sadāsāṃ smaraḥ // 518 //
children.translated_text: He runs ahead — the angry bearer of authority, with bow turned into a wheel, arrows fitted, and hand swinging — truly, <s>Smara</s> (Love) is always their commander.' // 518 //

children.text: sādhyasādhanayoḥ paurvāparyavikalpe na kiṃcidvaicitryamiti na tathā darśitam //
children.translated_text: When there is no fixed order between the <s>sādhya</s> and <s>sādhana</s>, there is no particular charm — therefore it is not demonstrated thus.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 183)
<s>Parikara</s> (circumscription) is the statement with purposeful qualifiers (<s>sākūta viśeṣaṇa</s>).
[These are qualifiers] of the qualified subject, by implication.

children.text: udāharaṇam-- mahaujaso mānadhanā dhanārcitā dhanurbhṛtaḥ saṃyati labdhakīrtayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Example: 'Of great vigor, rich in honor, worshiped for their wealth, bow-bearers who have gained fame in battle —

children.text: na saṃhatāstasya na bhedavṛttayaḥ priyāṇi vāñchantyasubhiḥ samīhitum // 519 //
children.translated_text: his [warriors] are neither united [by force] nor given to treacherous conduct; with their lives they desire to accomplish what is dear [to their lord].' // 519 //

children.text: yadyapyapuṣṭārthasya doṣatābhidhānāttannirākaraṇena puṣṭārthasvīkāraḥ kṛtaḥ, tathāpyekaniṣṭhatvena bahūnāṃ viśeṣaṇānāmevamupanyāse vaicitryamityalaṃkāramadhye gaṇitaḥ //
children.translated_text: Although, through the statement that an unsupported meaning is a fault, the acceptance of a supported meaning has been made [i.e., superfluous adjectives are normally a defect], nevertheless, when many qualifiers are applied to a single subject in this manner, there is charm — therefore it is counted among the figures.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 184)
<s>Vyājokti</s> (pretextual speech) is the concealment of the true nature of a thing that has become manifest through some pretext. // 118 //

children.text: nigūḍhamapi vastuno rūpaṃ kathamapi prabhinnaṃ kenāpi vyapadeśena yadapahnūyate sā vyājoktiḥ /
children.translated_text: When the true nature of a thing, though hidden, has somehow become manifest, and is then denied by means of some excuse — that is <s>vyājokti</s>.
This is not <s>apahṇuti</s> (denial), because the similarity based on both the relevant and the irrelevant, which [is required for <s>apahṇuti</s>], is impossible here.

Example: '<s>Śiva</s>, with bristling hair and the like all visibly erect from the joyful embrace of <s>Girijā</s>'s hand being placed [in his] as she was given away by the Lord of Mountains, was confused by the disruption of the arrangements of all the rites —

children.text: hā śaityaṃ tuhinācalasya karayorityūcivān sasmitaṃ śailāntaḥpuramātṛmaṇḍalagaṇairdṛṣṭo 'vatādvaḥ śivaḥ // 520 //
children.translated_text: "Alas, the coldness of <s>Himācala</s>'s hands!" he said with a smile, being watched by the groups of mothers of the mountain's inner chambers — may that <s>Śiva</s> protect you!' // 520 //

children.text: atra pulakavepathū sācikarūpatayā prasṛtau śaityakāraṇatayā prakāśitatvādapalapitasvarūpau vyājoktiṃ prayojayataḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, the bristling of hair and trembling, which had spread in the form of involuntary reactions, being presented as caused by coldness — having their true nature denied — give rise to <s>vyājokti</s>.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 185)

children.text: kiṃcit pṛṣṭamapṛṣṭaṃ vā kathitaṃ yat prakalpate /
children.translated_text: <s>Parisaṃkhyā</s> (enumeration) is where something asked or unasked, being stated, is understood
as being for the purpose of excluding [something] else of a similar kind. // 119 //

children.text: pramāṇāntarāvagatamapi vastu śabdena pratipāditaṃ prayojanāntarābhāvāt sadṛśavastvantaravyavacchedāya yat paryavasyati sā bhavetparisaṃkhyā /
atra ca kathanaṃ praśnapūrvakaṃ tadanyathā va paridṛṣṭam /
children.translated_text: Here, the statement is observed either preceded by a question or otherwise.

children.text: tathā, ubhayatra vyapohyamānasya pratīyamānatā vācyatvaṃ ceti catvāro bhedāḥ /
children.translated_text: Likewise, in both [cases], the excluded thing may be either suggested or explicitly stated — thus there are four varieties.

children.text: krameṇodāharaṇam-- kimāsevya puṃsāṃ savidhamanavadyaṃ dyusaritaḥ kimekānte dhyeyaṃ caraṇayugalaṃ kaustubhabhṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: Examples in order: 'What should a man resort to as blameless in proximity? The heavenly river (<s>Gaṅgā</s>). What should be meditated upon in solitude? The two feet of the bearer of the <s>Kaustubha</s> [gem] (<s>Viṣṇu</s>).

children.text: kimārādhyaṃ puṇyaṃ kimabilaṣaṇīyaṃ ca karuṇā yadāsaktyā ceto niravadhivimuktyai prabhavati // 521 //
children.translated_text: What is meritorious and worthy of worship? What is desirable? Compassion — for devotion of mind to it avails for boundless liberation.' // 521 //

Even a thing that is known through another means of knowledge, when expressed by words — because there is no other purpose — comes to culminate in the exclusion of similar other things. That is <s>parisaṃkhyā</s>.

children.text: kiṃ bhūṣaṇaṃ sudṛḍhamatra yaśo na ratnaṃ kiṃ kāryamāryacaritaṃ sukṛtaṃ na doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'What is firm adornment here? Fame, not jewels. What is the [proper] action? Noble conduct, not a good deed [that is] a fault.

children.text: kiṃ cakṣurapratihataṃ dhiṣaṇā na netraṃ jānāti kastvadaparaḥ sadasadvivekam // 522 //
children.translated_text: What is the eye that is unobstructed? Intellect, not the [physical] eye. Who other than you knows the discrimination of the real and the unreal?' // 522 //
'Crookedness resides in your locks of hair; redness (<s>rāga</s>) in your hands, feet, and lips;
hardness in the pair of your breasts; fickleness in your eyes.' // 523 //

children.text: bhaktirbhave na vibhave vyasanaṃ śāstre na yuvatikāmāstre /
children.translated_text: 'Devotion to existence, not to wealth; passion for the <s>śāstra</s>, not for the weapons of young women's desire;

children.text: cintā yaśasi na vapuṣi prāyaḥ paridṛśyate mahatām // 524 //
children.translated_text: concern for fame, not for the body — these are mostly seen among the great.' // 524 //
(<s>Sūtra</s> 186)

children.text:
yathottaraṃ cet pūrvasya pūrvasyārthasya hetutā /
tadā kāraṇamālā syāt
children.translated_text: <s>Kāraṇamālā</s> (chain of causes) is when successively the prior meaning is the cause of the subsequent.
'Successive' means: each one in relation to the one following it.

children.text: udāharaṇam-- jitendriyatvaṃ vinayasya kāraṇaṃ guṇaprakarṣo vinayādavāpyate /
children.translated_text: Example: 'The mastery of the senses is the cause of discipline; through discipline, excellence of virtue is attained;
through excellence of virtue, people become devoted; for prosperity arises from the devotion of the people.' // 525 //
The figure of <s>hetu</s> is not [separately] classified.

children.text: āyurghṛtamityādirūpo hyeṣa na bhūṣaṇatāṃ kadācidarhati vaicitryābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: For an instance of the form 'life is ghee' and the like can never deserve the status of an ornament, because of the absence of charm.
'The season of dense lotus-blossoms, intoxication of all bees, and delight of cuckoos —
this delightful [season] now causes longing among the people.' // 526 //
'The statement of a cause together with what possesses that cause — because of non-difference — is [the figure called] <s>hetu</s> (cause).'

children.text: ityatra kāvyarūpatāṃ komalānuprāsamahimnaiva samāmnāsiṣurna punarhetvalaṃkārakalpanayeti pūrvoktakāvyaliṅgameva hetuḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, the status of poetry is attributed solely to the glory of the soft <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) — not through the construction of the figure of <s>hetu</s>. Therefore, <s>hetu</s> is just the previously mentioned <s>kāvyaliṅga</s> (poetic sign).
(<s>Sūtra</s> 187)
But through action, mutually — // 120 //
of two entities, in the generation of each other —

children.text: arthayorekakriyāmukhena parasparaṃ kāraṇatve sati, anyonyanāmā, alaṃkāraḥ /
children.translated_text: when through the medium of a single action, two entities are mutually causes of each other, the figure named <s>anyonya</s> (mutual [causation]) [is present].

children.text: udāharaṇam-- haṃsāṇaṃ sarohiṃ sirī sārijjai aha sarāṇa haṃsehiṃ /
children.translated_text: [In Prakrit:] 'The <s>Śrī</s> (beauty) of swans [is enhanced] by the lake; then the [beauty] of the lake [is enhanced] by the swans.'

children.text: aṇṇoṇṇaṃ via ee appāṇṇaṃ ṇavara garuanti // 527 //
children.translated_text: 'As if they mutually honor each other, indeed — they honor only themselves.' // 527 //
Here, the mutual generation of both is through the medium of mutually conferring beauty and essence upon each other.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 188)
<s>Uttara</s> (response) — merely from hearing the response,

children.text: praśnasyonnayanaṃ yatra kriyate tatra vā sati //121//
children.translated_text: where the question is inferred — or when [the question] is present, // 121 //
[and the response] is repeatedly of an inconceivable nature — that would be <s>uttara</s>.

children.text: prativacanopalambhādeva pūrvavākyaṃ yatra kalpyate tadekaṃ tāvaduttaram /
children.translated_text: Where the preceding statement is constructed solely from hearing the reply — that is the first [type of] <s>uttara</s>.

children.text: udāharaṇam-- vāṇiaa hatthidantā kutto amhāṇa vagghakittī a /
children.translated_text: [In Prakrit:] 'O merchant, whence have you come, to have elephant-tusks and tiger-skins?'
'So long as the daughter-in-law, with face turned away in bashfulness, busies herself in the house.' // 528 //

children.text:
hastidantavyādhrakṛttīnāmahamarthī tāḥ, mūlyena prayaccheti kreturvacanam amunā vākyena samunnīyate /
na caitat kāvyaliṅgam uttarasya tādrūpyānupapatteḥ /
nahi praśnasya prativacanaṃ janako hetuḥ /
nāpīdamanumānam ekadharminiṣṭhatayā sādhyasādhanayoranirdeśādityalaṃkārāntarāmevottaraṃ sādhīyaḥ /
praśnādanantaraṃ lokātikrāntagocaratayā yat asaṃbhāvyarūpaṃ prativajanaṃ syāt tat aparamuttaram /
children.translated_text: When, immediately after a question, a reply of an inconceivable form — surpassing worldly expectation — is given, that is the other [type of] <s>uttara</s>.
If presented only once, there is no perception of beauty — therefore 'repeatedly' is stated.

children.text: udāharaṇam-- kā visamā devvagaī kiṃ laddhaṃ jaṃ jaṇo guṇaggāhī /
children.translated_text: [In Prakrit:] 'What is an uneven destiny? When the people are appreciative of virtues [yet fortune is unjust].

children.text: kiṃ sokhkhaṃ sukalattaṃ kiṃ dukkhaṃ jaṃ khalo loo // 529 //
children.translated_text: What is happiness? Good reputation. What is suffering? That the wicked are [found in] the world.' // 529 //

The speech of the buyer — 'I want elephant-tusks and tiger-skins; give them for a price' — is inferred from this statement. This is not <s>kāvyaliṅga</s> (poetic sign), because such a nature of the response is inappropriate [for that figure]. For the reply to a question is not a generating cause. Nor is this <s>anumāna</s> (inference), because the <s>sādhya</s> and <s>sādhana</s> are not indicated as pertaining to a single subject. Therefore <s>uttara</s> is more properly a separate figure.
In the <s>parisaṃkhyā</s> (enumeration) that involves a question and the exclusion of the other, the purport is simply the [word] 'only' (<s>eva</s>).
But here, the word 'only' rests in the expressed meaning — this is the distinction between the two.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 189)
<s>Sūkṣma</s> (the subtle) — when an extremely subtle meaning, perceived from some [indication], is revealed to another // 122 //

children.text: dharmeṇa kenacid yatra tat sūkṣmaṃ paricakṣate /
children.translated_text: through some property — that they call <s>sūkṣma</s>.
'From some [source]' — from a gesture, a glance, or the like. 'Subtle' means perceptible only to one of keen intellect.

children.text: udāharaṇam-- vaktrasyandisvedabinduprabandhairdṛṣṭvā bhinnaṃ kuṅkumaṃ kāpi paṇṭhe /
children.translated_text: Example: 'Seeing the vermilion (<s>kuṅkuma</s>) on her path broken by the streams of drops of sweat flowing from her face, some friend, revealing the masculinity of the slender one,

children.text: puṃstvaṃ tanvyā vyajjayantī vayasyā smitvā pāṇau khaḍgalekhāṃ lilekha // 530 //
children.translated_text: smiled and drew the outline of a sword on her palm.' // 530 //

children.text: atra, ākṛtimavalokya kayāpi vitarkitaṃ puruṣāyitam asilatālekhanena vaidagdhyādabhivyaktimupanītam /
children.translated_text: Here, someone, observing the form, inferred the masculine disguise, and through the cleverness of drawing a sword-outline, brought it to manifestation.
Because bearing a sword in hand is appropriate only for men.

children.text: yathā vā saṃketakālamanasaṃ viṭaṃ jñātvā vidagdhayā /
children.translated_text: Or thus: 'Knowing the gallant (<s>viṭa</s>) to have missed the appointed time, the clever woman,
with a hint cast through a slight glance, playfully closed a lotus.' // 531 //

children.text: atra jijñāsitaḥ saṃketakālaḥ kayācidiṅgitamātreṇa vidito niśāsamayaśaṃsinā kamalanimīlanena līlayā pratīpāditaḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, the appointed time was inquired about by someone, understood merely through a gesture, and playfully conveyed by the closing of a lotus — which indicates the time of night.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 190)
<s>Sāra</s> (quintessence) is progressive excellence, with an ultimate limit. // 123 //

children.text: paraḥ paryantabhāgaḥ, avadhiryasya dhārādhirohitayā tatraivotkarṣasya viśrānteḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Ultimate' means the final portion — the limit — because through the mode of ascending, the excellence comes to rest there.

children.text: udāharaṇam-- rājye sāraṃ vasudhā vasudhāyāṃ puraṃ pure saudham /
children.translated_text: Example: 'In the kingdom, the essence is the earth; on the earth, the city; in the city, the palace;
in the palace, the bed; on the bed, a beautiful woman — the totality of <s>Anaṅga</s> (Love).' // 532 //
(<s>Sūtra</s> 191)
<s>Asaṃgati</s> (incongruity) — where two properties that are cause and effect, being in entirely different locations,
are simultaneously manifested — that is <s>asaṃgati</s>. // 124 //

children.text: iha yaddeśaṃ karaṇam taddeśameva kāryamutpadyamānaṃ dṛṣṭam yathā dhūmādi /
children.translated_text: In this world, the effect is seen to arise in the very same location as the cause — as in the case of smoke and the like.

children.text: yatra tu hetuphalarūpayorapi dharmayoḥ kenāpyatiśayena nānādeśatayā yugapadavabhāsanam sā tayoḥ svabhāvotpannaparasparasaṃgatityāgāt asaṃgatiḥ /
children.translated_text: But where two properties that are in the form of cause and effect, through some extraordinary [means], are simultaneously manifested in different locations — that is <s>asaṃgati</s>, because of the abandonment of the naturally arisen mutual connection between them.

children.text: udāharaṇam-- jassea vaṇo tassea veaṇā bhaṇai taṃ jaṇo aliaṃ /
children.translated_text: [In Prakrit:] 'Whose complexion — [from it] whose feeling! — the people call that [feeling] false.'
'[But] the biting of the lip, O silent one — that is the feeling of many, bearing fruit.' // 533 //

children.text: eṣā ca virodhabādhinī na virodhaḥṣa bhinnādhāratayaiva dvayoriha virodhitāyāḥ pratibhāsāt /
children.translated_text: This [figure] supersedes <s>virodha</s> (contradiction). It is not <s>virodha</s>, because here the appearance of contradiction arises precisely from the two [properties] having different substrata.

children.text: virodhe tu virodhitvam ekāśrayaniṣṭhamanuktamapi paryavasitam apavādaviṣayaparihāreṇotsargasya vyavasthiteḥ /
children.translated_text: In [the case of] <s>virodha</s>, however, the contradictoriness is concluded as pertaining to a single substratum — even though not stated [explicitly] — because the general rule is established with the exception of the special case being excluded.
And thus it has been demonstrated.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 192)
<s>Samādhi</s> (accomplishment) is a task easily accomplished through the employment of another means.

children.text: sādhanāntaropakṛtena kartrā yad akleśena kāryamārabdhaṃ samādhīyate sa samādhirnāma /
children.translated_text: When a task is undertaken without difficulty by an agent who is aided by another means (<s>sādhanāntara</s>) — that is called <s>samādhi</s>.
An example: 'My feet are about to fall [at hers] in order to remove her pride.
Fortunately, this rising thunder of the clouds is of assistance.' (534)
(<s>Sūtra</s> 193)

children.text: samaṃ yogyatayā yogo yadi saṃbhāvitaḥ kvacit //125//
children.translated_text: When the conjunction of what is equal is somewhere perceived as [having] fitness — (125)

children.text: idamanayoḥ ślāghyamiti yogyatayā saṃbandhasya niyataviṣayamadhyavasānaṃ cettadā samam tat sadyoge 'sadyoge ca /
children.translated_text: When there is a determinate ascertainment of the relation — that 'this is praiseworthy for both of them' — through fitness, then it is <s>sama</s> (congruence), whether the conjunction actually exists or does not exist.

children.text: udāharaṇam-- dhātuḥ śilpātiśayanikaṣasthānameṣā mṛgākṣī rūpe devo 'pyayamanupamo dattapatraḥ smarasya /
children.translated_text: An example: 'This doe-eyed one is the touchstone for the supreme skill of the Creator in [making] form; and this one (the man) too is unparalleled, the decorated leaf-drawing of <s>Smara</s> (the god of love).

children.text: jātaṃ daivātsadṛśamanayoḥ saṃgataṃ yat tadeta- cchṛṅgārasyopanatamadhunā rājyamekātapatram // 535 //
children.translated_text: That their union has come about by fate as something fitting — this is now the sole-umbrella kingdom of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment) that has presented itself.' (535)

children.text: citraṃ citraṃ bata bata mahaccitrametadvicitraṃ jāto daivāducitaracanāsaṃvidhātā vidhātā /
children.translated_text: 'Wonderful, wonderful! Alas, alas! A great wonder, this extraordinary [thing] — that <s>Vidhātā</s> (the Creator) has, by fate, become the arranger of fitting arrangements!
For the ripened fruits of the <s>nimba</s> (neem) trees are abundantly ready to be tasted, and the crow-folk are expert in the art of devouring them!' (536)
(<s>Sūtra</s> 194)
When, somewhere, because of extreme disparity, the conjunction (<s>śleṣa</s>) would not achieve a fitting combination,
and when the agent does not obtain the fruit of the action, and indeed the undesired result occurs — (126)
when the qualities and actions of the effect contradict the qualities and actions of the cause,

children.text: krameṇa ca viruddhe yat sa eṣa viṣamo mataḥ //127//
children.translated_text: in sequence — that is regarded as <s>viṣama</s> (incongruity). (127)

children.text: dvayoratyantavilakṣaṇatayā yat anupapadyamānatayaiva yogaḥ pratīyatejhr1ṭa yacca kiṃcidārabhamāṇaḥ kartā kriyāyāḥ praṇāśāt na kevalamabhīṣṭaṃ yat phalaṃ na labheta yāvadaprārthitamapyanarthaṃ viṣayamāsādayet jhr2ṭa tathā satyapi kāryasya kāraṇarūpānukāre tat tayorguṇau kriye ca parasparaṃ viruddhatāṃ vrajataḥ jhr3kṣ4ṭa sa samavipayaryātmā catūrūṣo viṣamaḥ /
children.translated_text: When, because of the extreme dissimilarity of the two, the conjunction is perceived as precisely impossible; and when someone undertaking some activity, because of the destruction of the action, not only does not obtain the desired fruit, but even encounters an undesired calamity; and likewise when, even though the effect resembles the cause in form, the qualities and actions of both become mutually contradictory — this <s>viṣama</s>, consisting of congruence-and-its-reversal, is fourfold.
Examples in order: 'Where is this girl with limbs softer than the <s>śirīṣa</s> flower, with long eyes?
And where is this fire of <s>Madana</s> (the god of love), harsh as the fire of a charcoal pit?' (537)
'The hare (the mark on the moon), frightened by the son of <s>Siṃhikā</s> (<s>Rāhu</s>), took refuge in the cool-rayed [Moon].
But there, that other son of <s>Siṃhikā</s> (<s>Rāhu</s>) swallowed him together with his refuge.' (538)

children.text: sadyaḥ karasparśamavāpya citraṃ raṇe raṇe yasya kṛpāṇalekhā /
children.translated_text: 'It is a wonder — upon obtaining the touch of the hand in battle after battle, the line of his sword,
dark as a <s>tamāla</s> leaf, gives birth to fame, white as the autumn moon, the ornament of the three worlds.' (539)
'O one with eyes [like] blue lotus petals, you bestow this abundant bliss,
yet it is separation, caused by you alone, that exceedingly scorches my body.' (540)
Here, the bestowing of bliss contradicts the torment of separation.

children.text: evam vipulena sāgaraśayasya kukṣiṇā bhuvanāni yasya papire yugakṣaye /
children.translated_text: Likewise: 'By whose vast belly, as he reclined on the ocean, the worlds were drunk up at the end of the age,

children.text: madavibhramāsakalayā pape punaḥ sa purastriyaikatamayaikayā dṛśā // 541 //
children.translated_text: he was again drunk up by a single glance — a glance incomplete in its intoxicating charm — of a single city-woman.' (541)
And in such [examples] too, the incongruity should be understood as appropriate to each case.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 195)
When, of a great [thing], ones even greater become, in order, the supported and the support,
and even in smallness it is greater — that [is called <s>adhika</s>]. (128)

children.text: āśritam ādheyam āśrayastadādhāraḥ, tayormahatorapi viṣaye tadapekṣayā tanū, apyāśrayāśrayiṇau prastutavastuprakarṣavivakṣayā yathākramaṃ yat adhikataratāṃ vrajataḥ, tadidaṃ dvividham adhikaṃ nāma /
children.translated_text: 'Supported' means what is placed upon; 'support' means its substratum. Of both of these, even when their scope is great, they are, relative to [the subject], small; yet they successively become the support and the supported — with the intention of expressing the excellence of the subject at hand, they progressively become greater and greater. This twofold [figure] is called <s>adhika</s> (excess).
Examples in order: 'O King, vast indeed is the belly of the three worlds,
yet your mass of fame, which cannot be contained, shines even within it.' (542)
'The worlds resided expansively within the body (<s>tanu</s>) of him (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) who had withdrawn himself at the time of the dissolution of the age.
Yet even in that body, the joys arising from the visit of the ascetics did not find room for the enemy of <s>Kaiṭabha</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>).' (543)
(<s>Sūtra</s> 196)
The disparagement of what belongs to an adversary, by one who is unable to retaliate against the adversary [directly],
for the purpose of praising that [adversary] — that is called <s>pratyanīka</s> (counter-attack). (129)

children.text: nyakkṛtiparamapi vipakṣaṃ sākṣānnirasitumaśaktena kenāpi yat tameva pratipakṣamutkarṣayituṃ tadāśritasya tiraskaraṇam tat anīkapratinidhitulyatvāt pratyanīkamabhidhīyate /
children.translated_text: When someone, unable to directly repudiate an adversary who is supremely belittling, disparages something belonging to that very adversary in order to exalt the adversary himself — that, because of its similarity to [attacking] a substitute in [the adversary's] army, is called <s>pratyanīka</s>.

children.text: yathā, anīke, abhiyojye tatpratinidhībhūtamaparaṃ mūḍhatayā kenacidabhiyujyate tatheha pratiyogini vijeye tadīyo 'nyo vijīyate, ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: just as in an army (<s>anīka</s>), when unable to attack the [main] adversary, another who has become that adversary's substitute is, out of confusion, attacked by someone — so here, when unable to defeat the rival, someone else belonging to [the rival] is defeated.

children.text: udāharaṇam-- tvaṃ vinirjitamanobhavarūpaḥ sā ca sundara bhavatyanuraktā /
children.translated_text: An example: 'You have conquered [even] the form of <s>Manobhava</s> (the god of love), and she, O handsome one, is devoted [to you].
Yet <s>Kāma</s>, as if out of remorse, torments her simultaneously with [his] five arrows.' (544)
Or thus: 'Unable to do the slightest harm to him, who has undertaken bodily discipline and assumed a warlike form,
<s>Rāhu</s>, the skilled one, now assails the moon — which resembles the face of that beloved.' (545)
Here, the moon's 'belonging to him' is through the relation of a relative's relative [i.e., the beloved's face resembles the moon].
(<s>Sūtra</s> 197)
When an entity is concealed by another entity having the same characteristic (<s>lakṣmaṇā</s>),
whether innate or adventitious — that is known as <s>mīlita</s> (concealment). (130)

children.text: sahajam āgantukaṃ vā kimapi sādhāraṇaṃ yat lakṣaṇam taddvāreṇa yat kiṃcit kenacidvastu vastusthityaiva balīyastāyā tirodhīyate tat mīlitamiti dvidhā smaranti /
children.translated_text: Whether innate or adventitious, some common characteristic — through the medium of that, when some entity is concealed by another entity simply by the force of its greater presence, that is known as <s>mīlita</s>, twofold [according to whether the characteristic is innate or adventitious].

children.text: krameṇodāharaṇam-- apāṅgatarale dṛśau madhuravakravarṇā giro vilāsabharamantharā gatiratīva kāntaṃ mukham /
children.translated_text: Examples in order: 'Restless side-glances, sweet and curved speech, a gait slow with the weight of coquetry, an exceedingly beautiful face —

children.text: iti sphuritamaṅgake mṛgadṛśaḥ svato līlayā tadatra na madodayaḥ kṛtapado 'pi saṃlakṣyate // 546 //
children.translated_text: thus the limbs of the doe-eyed one radiate by their own natural play. Herein, though the onset of intoxication has entered, it is not perceived.' (546)

children.text: atra dṛktaralatādikamaṅgasya liṅgaṃ svābhāvikam sādhāraṇaṃ ca mahodayena tatrāpyetasya darśanāt /
children.translated_text: Here, the restlessness of the glance and the like is a sign of the body that is both natural and common — since it is observed even in the onset of intoxication.

children.text: ye kandarāsu nivasanti sadā himādrestvatpātaśaṅkitadhiyo vivaśā dviṣaste /
children.translated_text: 'Those enemies of yours who dwell always in the caves of the <s>Himālaya</s>, with minds terrified by fear of your assault —

children.text: apyaṅgamutpulakamudvahatāṃ sakampaṃ teṣāmaho bata bhiyāṃ na budho 'pyabhijñaḥ // 547 //
children.translated_text: although they bear limbs bristling with horripilation and trembling — alas, no wise person can discern [whether this is from] their fears.' (547)

children.text: atra tu sāmarthyādavasitasya śaityasya, āgantukatvāttatprabhavayorapi kampapulakayostādrūpyaṃ samānatā ca bhayeṣvapi tayorupalakṣitatvāt //
children.translated_text: Here, because the cold is inferred through contextual power, and because the trembling and horripilation produced by it are adventitious [yet] identical in appearance [to those produced by fear], and because trembling and horripilation are observed in cases of fear too — there is commonality.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 198)
Where one entity after another is either established or negated with respect to each preceding one,
in the capacity of a qualifier — that is <s>ekāvalī</s> (single strand), and it is twofold. (131)

children.text: pūrva pūrvaṃ prati yathottarasya vastuno vīpsayā viśeṣaṇabhāvena yat sthāpanaṃ niṣedho vā saṃbhavati sā dvidhā budhairekāvalī bhaṇyate /
children.translated_text: When, with respect to each preceding [entity], the successive establishment or negation of the next entity as a qualifier occurs by means of repetition — that twofold [figure] is declared by the wise to be <s>ekāvalī</s>.

children.text: krameṇodāharaṇam-- purāṇi yasyāṃ savarāṅganāni varāṅganā rūpapūraskṛtāṅgyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Examples in order: 'In her cities, the beautiful women; of the beautiful women, their limbs preceded by beauty;
beauty, with fully unfolded graceful charm; and charm is the weapon of the flower-armed (<s>Kāma</s>).' (548)

children.text: na tajjalaṃ yanna sucārupaṅkajaṃ na paṅkajaṃ tat yadalīnaṣaṭpadam /
children.translated_text: 'That water is not [truly water] which does not have a beautiful lotus; that lotus is not [truly a lotus] in which no bee resides;

children.text: na ṣaṭmado 'sau kalaguñjito na yo na guñjitaṃ tanna jahāra yanmanaḥ // 549 //
children.translated_text: that bee is not [truly a bee] which does not hum melodiously; and that humming is not [truly humming] which does not captivate the mind.' (549)

children.text: pūrvatra purāṇāṃ varāṅganāḥ tāsāmaṅgaviśeṣaṇamukhena rūpam tasya vilāsāḥ, teṣāmapyastramityamunā krameṇa viśeṣaṇaṃ vidhīyate /
children.translated_text: In the first [example], beautiful women are [qualifiers] of the cities; then beauty, in the form of a qualifier by way of particular limbs, belongs to those [women]; then charm belongs to that [beauty]; then these [charms] function as the weapon [of Kāma] — thus qualification is established in this progressive order.
In the latter [example], the same should be construed with negation.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 199)
<s>Smaraṇa</s> (recollection) is the remembrance of a thing as it was experienced, when something similar to it is seen.

children.text: yaḥ padārthaḥ kenacidākāreṇa niyataḥ, yadā kadācit anubhūto 'bhūt sa kālāntare smṛtipratibodhādhāyini tatsamāne vastuni dṛṣṭe sati yat tathaiva smaryate tat bhavet smaraṇam /
children.translated_text: When an object, determined by some particular mode, was once experienced at some time, and at a later time, upon seeing a similar object that awakens the memory, it is remembered in just that way — that is <s>smaraṇa</s>.

children.text: udāharaṇam-- nimnanābhikuhareṣu yadambhaḥ plāvitaṃ caladṛśāṃ laharībhiḥ /
children.translated_text: An example: 'The water that was flooded into the low hollows of the navel by the waves of the moving-eyed [river-women],
reminded the divine women, through the gurgling sounds produced from it, of the throat-sounds of lovemaking.' (550)
Or thus [in Prakrit]: 'Of him (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) whose fame, obtained by hand, is established at the mouth of <s>Jaśodā</s> (i.e., in <s>Yaśodā</s>'s telling),
who has remembered the five-fold (<s>Pañcajanya</s>) — pay homage to the horripilation of <s>Kaṇha</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>).' (551)
(<s>Sūtra</s> 200)
<s>Bhrāntimat</s> (delusion-based) [is that figure arising from] the cognition of another, when something equal to it is seen. (132)

children.text:
taditi anyat aprākaraṇikaṃ nirdiśyate /
tena samānam arthādiha prākaraṇikam āśrīyate /
tasya tathāvidhasya dṛṣṭau satyāṃ yat aprākaraṇikatayā saṃvedanam sa bhrāntimān /
children.translated_text: When, upon the seeing of such a [similar] thing, there is a cognition of it as the irrelevant [thing] — that is <s>bhrāntimat</s>.

children.text: na ceṣa rupakaṃ prathamātiśayoktirvā tatra vastuto bhramasyābhāvāt iha ca, arthānugamanena saṃjñāyāḥ pravṛtteḥ tasya spaṣṭameva pratipannatvāt /
children.translated_text: And this is not <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) or the first [type of] <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) — because in those, there is actually no delusion, whereas here there is. And because the designation applies by following the meaning; and because that [delusion] is clearly established.

children.text: udāharaṇam-- kapāle mārjāraḥ paya iti karān leḍhi śaśina- starucchidraprotān bisamiti karī saṃkalayati /
children.translated_text: An example: 'The cat licks its paws thinking "milk!" at [the sight of] the rays of the moon streaming through holes in the skull-cup. The elephant gathers [them] thinking "lotus-fibers!"

children.text: ratānte talpasthān harati vanitāpyaṃśukamiti prabhāmattaśvandro jagadidamaho viplavayati // 552 //
children.translated_text: And the woman in bed after lovemaking snatches at them thinking "a garment!" — Alas, the moon, intoxicated by [its own] radiance, throws this world into confusion!' (552)
'That' refers to another, i.e., what is not the subject at hand. 'Equal to that' — here what is the subject at hand is relied upon.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 201)
<s>Pratīpa</s> (inverse comparison): the rejection of the standard of comparison, or the [standard's] being made the subject of comparison;
or if the [subject of comparison] itself is to be imagined [as the standard] — the basis being disdain. (133)

children.text: asya dhuraṃ sutarāmupameyameva voḍhuṃ prauḍhamiti kaimarthyena yat upamānamākṣipyate yadapi tasyaivopamānatayā prasiddhasya, upamānāntaravivakṣayānādarārthamupameyabhāvaḥ kalpyate tat upameyasyopamānapratikūlavartitvāt ubhayarūpaṃ pratīpam /
children.translated_text: When, [arguing that] the subject of comparison is far more capable of bearing the burden, the standard of comparison is rejected through [a sense of] futility; or when that which is well-known as the standard of comparison is, through the desire to posit another standard, treated as the subject of comparison out of disregard — both forms constitute <s>pratīpa</s>, because the subject of comparison stands contrary to the standard.

children.text: krameṇodāharaṇam-- lāvaṇyaukasi sapratāpagarimaṇyagresare tyāgināṃ deva tvayyavanībharakṣamabhuje niṣpādite vedhasā /
children.translated_text: Examples in order: 'O Lord, who are the abode of beauty, distinguished by the weight of majesty, the foremost among the generous, upon whom <s>Vedhas</s> (Brahmā) has fashioned arms capable of bearing the burden of the earth —

children.text: induḥ kiṃ ghaṭitaḥ kimeṣa vihitaḥ pūṣā kimutpāditaṃ cintāratnamado mudhaiva kimamī sṛṣṭāḥ kulakṣmābhṛtaḥ // 553 //
children.translated_text: what was the purpose of creating the moon? Why was this sun made? Why was the <s>Cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling jewel) produced? And why were these mountains of noble lineage needlessly created?' (553)

children.text: e ehi dāva sundari kaṇṇaṃ dāūṇa suṇasū vaaṇijjaṃ /
children.translated_text: [In Prakrit:] 'Come here, O beautiful one, give [me your] ear and listen to the gossip.

children.text: tujjha muheṇa kisoari caṃdo ubhamijjai jaṇeṇa // 554 //
children.translated_text: By your face, O young woman, the moon is outrivaled by the people.' (554)

children.text: atra mukhenopamīyamānasya śaśinaḥ svpataraguṇatvāt upamityaniṣpacyā "vaaṇijjam'; iti vacanīyapadābhivyaṅgyastiraskāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, because the moon, being compared with the face, has inferior qualities, the comparison cannot be completed — and the disdain suggested by the word 'gossip' (<s>vacanīyam</s>) [is expressed].
But sometimes the act of comparison is fully accomplished — the basis being disregard.

children.text: yathā garvamasaṃvāhyamimaṃ locanayugalena kiṃ vahasi mugdhe /
children.translated_text: An example: 'Why do you carry, O innocent one, with your pair of eyes, this pride that cannot be massaged away?

children.text: santīdṛśāni diśi diśi saraḥsu nanu nīlanalināni // 555 //
children.translated_text: Are there not, everywhere, in ponds in every direction, blue lotuses like these?' (555)
Here, the very making of the lotuses into the subject of comparison is the disregard [of them].

children.text: anayaiva rītyā yat asāmānyaguṇayogāt nopamānabhāvamapi, anubhūtapūrvi tasya tatkalpanāyāmapi bhavati pratīpamiti pratyetavyam /
children.translated_text: By this same method, it should be understood that when, because of the possession of extraordinary qualities, something does not even accept the status of a standard of comparison — and it was previously experienced [as such] — even in the imagining of it [as a standard], there is <s>pratīpa</s>.

children.text: yathā ahameva guruḥ sudāruṇānāmiti hālāhala tāta mā sma dṛpyaḥ /
children.translated_text: An example: 'I alone am the teacher of terrible things' — O <s>Hālāhala</s> (deadly poison), father, do not be proud!

children.text: nanu santi bhavādṛśāni bhūyo bhuvane 'smin vacanāni durjanānām // 556 //
children.translated_text: Surely there are in this world more things like you — namely, the words of wicked people.' (556)
Here, the status of <s>hālāhala</s> as a standard of comparison is precisely what is deemed inconceivable, and yet it is established [in the verse].
(<s>Sūtra</s> 202)
When, of the subject at hand, through the desire to express similarity of quality with another,
an identity is established through conjunction — that is known as <s>sāmānya</s> (generality). (134)

children.text: atādṛśamapi tādṛśatayā vivakṣituṃ yat aprastutārthena saṃpṛktamaparityakranijaguṇameva tadekātmatayā nibadhyate tat samānaguṇanibandhanāt sāmānyam /
children.translated_text: When something, though not actually of such a nature, is desired to be spoken of as such, and is connected with an irrelevant meaning without abandoning its own qualities — and is bound together as identical with it — that, because it is based on common qualities, is <s>sāmānya</s>.
An example: 'With bodies anointed with sandalwood paste, adorned with fresh garlands, with faces brightened by very white tooth-leaf [ornaments], wearing beautiful clean garments —
when the moon spreads its full radiance and whitens the earth, they have gone beyond perception;
the <s>abhisārikās</s> (women going to meet their lovers), free from fear, proceed happily to the abode of the beloved.' (557)

children.text: atra prastutatadanyayoranyūnānatiriktatayā nibaddhaṃ dhavalatvamekātmatāhetuḥ, ata eva pṛthagbhāvena na tayorupalakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: Here, the whiteness, bound together in neither deficiency nor excess between the subject and the other, is the cause of identity. For that very reason, there is no discernment of them as separate.

children.text: yathā vā vetratvacā tulyarucāṃ vadhunāṃ karṇāgrato gaṇḍatalāgatāni /
children.translated_text: Or thus: 'Had the bees not playfully alighted upon the cheek-surfaces near the ears of the brides, whose luster is equal to that of a cane-bark,
who would have recognized [them as] fresh <s>campaka</s> flowers?' (558)

children.text: atra nimittāntarajanitāpi nānātvapratītiḥ prathamapratipannamabhedaṃ na vyudasitumutsahate pratītatvāttasya pratīteśva bādāyogāt //
children.translated_text: Here, even though the perception of difference is produced by another cause, it is unable to dislodge the non-difference that was first apprehended — because of that [non-difference] having been cognized, and because there is no annulment of what has been cognized.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 203)
Without a well-known substratum, the establishment of that which is superimposed;
a single entity simultaneously functioning, and one entity having multiple objects — (135)
when something accomplishes a task of another thing that is impossible [for that other thing];
and such an instrumentality — thus <s>viśeṣa</s> (distinction) is declared to be of three kinds. (136)

children.text: prasiddhādhāraparihāreṇa yat ādheyasya viśiṣṭā sthitirabhidhīyate sa prathamo viśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: When, setting aside the well-known substratum, a distinctive establishment of the superimposed is described — that is the first <s>viśeṣa</s>.
Example: 'Of those whose multitude of no small virtues, even for those who have ascended to heaven, until the end of the <s>kalpa</s>,

children.text: ramayanti jaganti giraḥ kathamiha kavayo na te vandyāḥ // 559 //
children.translated_text: whose words delight the worlds — how are those poets not worthy of reverence here?' (559)

children.text: ekamapi vastu yat ekenaiva svabhāvena yugapadanekatra vartate sa dvitīyaḥ /
children.translated_text: When a single entity, by its very own nature, simultaneously exists in many places — that is the second [<s>viśeṣa</s>].

children.text: udāharaṇam-- sā vasai tujjha hiae sā ccia acchīsu sā a vaaṇeśu /
children.translated_text: Example: 'She dwells in your heart, she indeed in your eyes, and she in your words;
O beautiful one of visible form, where can the breath find [any other] refuge?' (560)

children.text: yadapi kiṃcidrabhaseta, ārabhamāṇastenaiva yatnenāśakyapari kāryāntaramārabhate so 'paro viśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: And when someone, while eagerly undertaking something, with that very same effort also undertakes another task that is impossible [for the original effort] — that is the other <s>viśeṣa</s>.
Example: 'You of marvelous blazing form, radiant with the fire of valor, you of blameless wisdom — while creating you,

children.text: vidhinā sasṛje navo manobhūrbhuvi satyaṃ savitā bṛhaspatiśva // 561 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vidhi</s> (Brahmā) simultaneously created a new <s>Manobhū</s> (Kāmadeva); truly, upon the earth, <s>Savitṛ</s> and <s>Bṛhaspati</s> as well.' (561)

children.text: yathā vā gṛhiṇī sacivaḥ sakhī mithaḥ priyaśiṣyā lalite kalāvidhau /
children.translated_text: Or, as: 'Mistress of the house, minister, friend, mutual beloved pupil in the graceful art of arts,

children.text: karuṇāvimukhena mṛtyunā haratā tvāṃ bata kiṃ na me hṛnam // 562 //
children.translated_text: by merciless <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death), who took you away — alas! what has not been taken from me?' (562)

children.text: sarvatra, evaṃvidhaviṣaye 'tiśayoktireva prāṇatvenāvatiṣṭhate tāṃ vinā prāyeṇālaṃkāratvāyogāt /
children.translated_text: Everywhere, in such subjects, <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) alone stands as the vital force, since without it there is generally no qualification as an ornament.
Hence it has been said: 'This very <s>vakrokti</s> (indirect speech) is present everywhere; through it the meaning is illuminated.
A poet must exert effort in this; what ornament is there without it?'
Thus.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 204)
When a thing, abandoning its own quality, through association with one of exceedingly brilliant quality,

children.text: vastu tadguṇatāmeti bhaṇyate sa tu tadguṇaḥ //137//
children.translated_text: attains the quality of that [other thing] — that is called <s>tadguṇa</s> (taking on another's quality). (137)

children.text: vastu tiraskatanijarūpaṃ kenāpi samīpagatena praguṇayā svaguṇasaṃpadoparaktaṃ tatpratibhāsamevayatsamāsādayati sa tadguṇaḥ, tasyāprakṛtasya guṇo 'trāstīti /
children.translated_text: <s>Tadguṇa</s> is when an object, its own form eclipsed, being colored by the superior excellence of qualities of something in its vicinity through close association, assumes merely the appearance of that [neighboring thing] — [so called] because the quality of that extraneous thing is present here.

children.text: udāharaṇam-- viminnavarṇā garuḍāgrajena sūryasya rathyāḥ paritaḥ sphurantyā /
children.translated_text: Example: 'By <s>Garuḍa</s>'s elder brother [<s>Aruṇa</s>], the chariot-paths of the sun shine all around with variegated colors;

children.text: ratnaiḥ punaryatra rucā rucaṃ svāmāninyire vaṃśakarīranīlaiḥ // 563 //
children.translated_text: the gems in turn, dark-blue as bamboo shoots, transferred their luster to his [the sun's] luster.' (563)

children.text: atra ravituragāpekṣayā garuḍāgrajasya tadapekṣayā ca harinmaṇīnāṃ praguṇavarṇatā //
children.translated_text: Here, the superior color belongs to <s>Garuḍa</s>'s elder brother relative to the sun's horses, and to the green gems relative to him [<s>Aruṇa</s>].
(<s>Sūtra</s> 205)
When there is no imitation of that [other's] form, it would be <s>atadguṇa</s> (not taking on another's quality).

children.text: yadi tu tadīyaṃ varṇaṃ saṃbhantyāmapi yogyatāyām idaṃ nyūnaguṇaṃ na gṛhṇīyāt tadā bhavedatadguṇo nāma /
