children.translated_text: If, even when there is fitness for association, this [object] of lesser quality does not assume the color of that [superior thing] — then it would be [the figure] called <s>atadguṇa</s>.

children.text: udāharaṇam-- dhavalosi jaha vi sundara taha vi tue majjha rañjiaṃ hiaaṃ /
children.translated_text: Example: 'Though you are white, O beautiful one, yet you have reddened my heart;

children.text: rāabharapie vi hiae suhaa ṇihitto ṇa rattosi // 564 //
children.translated_text: O beloved, though lodged in a heart brimming with passion — you are not red.' (564)

children.text: atrātiraktenāpi manasā saṃyukto na raktatāmupagata ityatadguṇaḥ /
kiṃca taditi aprakṛtam asyeti ca prakṛtamatra nirdiśyate /
children.translated_text: Moreover, 'that' (<s>tat</s>) here designates the extraneous, and 'this' (<s>asya</s>) the intrinsic.

children.text: tena yat aprakṛtasya rūpaṃ prakṛtena kuto 'pi nimittāt nānuvidhīyate so 'tadguṇa ityapi pratipattavyam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, when the form of the extraneous thing is not conformed to by the intrinsic for whatever reason — that too should be understood as <s>atadguṇa</s>.

children.text: yathā gāṅgamambu sidamambu yāmunaṃ kajjalābhamubhayatra majjataḥ /
children.translated_text: For example: 'The water of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> is clear, the water of the <s>Yamunā</s> is dark as collyrium; for one who plunges into both,

children.text: rājahaṃsa tava saiva śubhratā cīyate na ca na cāpacīyate // 565 //
children.translated_text: O royal swan, your whiteness alone — it neither increases nor decreases.' (565)
Here, [the moon], though united even with the intensely reddened mind, does not assume redness — thus it is <s>atadguṇa</s>.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 206)
What has been accomplished in a certain way by someone, [and then] by another, differently — (131)

children.text: tathaiva yadvidhīyeta sa vyāghāta iti smṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: when that very thing is contrarily effected — that is known as <s>vyāghāta</s> (contradiction).

children.text: yenopāyena yat ekenopakalpitam tasyānyena jigīṣutayā tadupāyakameba yat anyathākaraṇam sa sādhitavastuvyāhatihetutvāt vyāghātaḥ /
children.translated_text: When what has been brought about by one person through a certain means is contrarily undone by another who desires to overcome it, using that very same means — that is <s>vyāghāta</s>, because it causes the frustration of the accomplished thing.

children.text: udāharaṇam-- dṛśā dagdhaṃ manasijaṃ jīvayanti dṛśaiva yāḥ /
children.translated_text: Example: 'Those who revive <s>Manasija</s> (Kāmadeva), burned by their glance, with their glance alone —
I praise those doe-eyed women who are victorious over <s>Virūpākṣa</s> (Śiva).' (566)
(<s>Sūtra</s> 207)
The desirable combination of these, when they exist distinctly, is <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (combination). (139)

children.text: eteṣāṃ samanantaramevoktasvarūpāṇāṃ yathāsaṃbhavamanyonyanirapekṣatayā yat ekatra śabdabhāge eva, arthaviṣaye, eva, ubhayatrāpi vā, avasthānam sā, ekārthasamavāyasvabhāvā saṃsṛṣṭiḥ /
children.translated_text: When these [ornaments] whose natures have just been described, as far as possible, independently of one another, have their presence in a single portion of expression alone, or in the domain of meaning alone, or in both — that, having the nature of co-occurrence in a single meaning, is <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s>.
There, combination of word-ornaments is as follows: 'With her beauty enhanced by the agitation of bees wandering in desire for the fragrance of her face,
she with her tinkling girdle, with the soft sound of her curls, with her tremulous-glanced one, brought about [delight].' (567)
Combination of sense-ornaments, in turn: 'The darkness smears the limbs, as it were; the sky rains collyrium, as it were;
like the service of a wicked person, [my] sight has gone to fruitlessness.' (568)

children.text: pūrvatra parasparanirapekṣau yamakānuprāsau saṃsṛṣṭiṃ prayojayataḥ, uttaratra tu tathāvidhe, upamotprekṣe /
children.translated_text: In the former, <s>yamaka</s> (chiming) and <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration), mutually independent, produce the combination; in the latter, similarly, <s>upamā</s> (simile) and <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy).
And the combination of word-ornaments and sense-ornaments [is as follows]:

children.text: so ṇatthi ettha gāme jo eaṃ mahamahantalāaṇṇaṃ /
children.translated_text: 'There is no one in this village who, [seeing] this great and magnificent display,
could restrain [her] as she wanders about, churning the hearts of young men.' (569)
Here, <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) and <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) are mutually independent.

children.text: saṃsargaśva tayorekatra vākye chandasi vā samavetatvāt //
children.translated_text: And their conjunction is due to their co-occurrence in a single sentence or meter.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 208)
When those that have not attained independence have a principal-subordinate relationship among themselves — that is <s>saṃkara</s> (intermixture).

children.text: ete, eva yatrātmani, anāsāditasvatantrabhāvāḥ parasparam anugrāhyānugrāhakatāṃ dadhati sa eṣāṃ saṃkīryamāṇasvarūpatvāt saṃkaraḥ /
children.translated_text: When these very [ornaments], not having attained an independent status within a [passage], mutually assume the relation of supporter and supported — that is their <s>saṃkara</s>, because their natures are being intermixed.

children.text: udāharaṇam-- ātte sīmantaratne marakatini hṛte hematāṭaṅkapatre luptāyāṃ mekhalāyāṃ jhaṭiti maṇitulākoṭiyugme gṛhīte /
children.translated_text: Example: 'When the emerald crest-jewel of the parting was seized, when the golden earring-leaf was taken, when the girdle was suddenly snatched, when the pair of jeweled pendants at the waist were grasped —

children.text: śoṇaṃ bimboṣṭhakāntyā tvadarimṛgadṛśāmitvarīṇāmaraṇye rājan guñjāphalānāṃ sraja iti śabarā naiva hāraṃ haranti // 570 //
children.translated_text: O king, the <s>Śabara</s> women do not at all take the necklace, [saying] "these are but garlands of <s>guñjā</s> berries," [mistaking it] because of the red luster of your enemies' doe-eyed wives' berry-like lips in the forest.' (570)

children.text: atra tadguṇamapekṣya bhrāntimatā prādurbhūtam tadāśrayeṇa ca tadguṇaḥ sacetasāṃ prabhūtacamatkṛtinimittamityanayoraṅgāṅgibhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, <s>bhrāntimat</s> (delusion) has arisen with reference to <s>tadguṇa</s>, and through its support, <s>tadguṇa</s> [in turn arises] — since the delusion of sentient beings is the cause of abundant wonder, there is a principal-subordinate relationship between these two.

children.text: yathā vā jaṭābhābhirmābhiḥ karadhṛtakalaṅkākṣavalayo viyogivyāpatteriva kalitavairāgyaviśadaḥ /
children.translated_text: Or, as: 'With matted-hair-like rays, with the disc of the stain held in hand like a rosary,

children.text: paripreṅkhattārāparikarakapālāṅkitatale śaśī bhasmāpāṇḍuḥ pitṛvana iva vyomni carati // 571 //
children.translated_text: as if having assumed dispassion's pallor through the affliction of separation — the moon, pale as ashes, wanders in the sky as if in a cremation ground.' (571)

children.text:
upamā rūpakam utprekṣā śleṣaśveti catvāro 'tra pūrvavat aṅgāṅgitayā pratīyante /
kalaṅka evākṣavalayamiti rūpakaparigrahe karadhṛtatvameva sādhakapramāṇatāṃ pratipadyate /
asya hi rūpakatve tirohitakalaṅkarūpam akṣavalayameva mukhyatayāvagamyate tasyaiva ca karagrahaṇayogyatāyāṃ sārvatrikī prasiddhiḥ /
śleṣacchāyayā tu kalaṅkasya karadhāraṇam asadeva pratyāsacyā, upacarya yojyateśaśāṅkena kevalaṃ kalaṅkasya mūrtyaiva, udvahanāt /
kalaṅko 'kṣavalayamiveti tu, apamāyāṃ kalaṅkasya, utkaṭatayā pratipattiḥ /
children.translated_text: But 'the stain is like a rosary' — in the case of <s>upamā</s> (simile), the perception of the stain is through its prominence.

children.text: na cāsya karadhṛtatvaṃ tacvato 'stīti mukhye 'pyupacāra eva śaraṇaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: And since its being held in the hand does not actually exist, even in the literal sense, figurative usage alone would be the recourse.
Such <s>saṃkara</s> (intermixture) is also observed between word-ornaments.

children.text: yathā rājati taṭīyamabhihatadānavarāsātipātisārāvanadāḥ gajatā ca yūthamaviratadānavarā sātipāti sārā vanadā // 572 //
children.translated_text: For example: 'The banks shine, struck by excellent torrential rains, with a succession of uninterrupted showers from the forest; and the herd moves in elephant-fashion, with excellent uninterrupted showers, exceedingly hostile, in the forest.' (572)

<s>Upamā</s> (simile), <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor), <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy), and <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning) — these four are perceived here, as before, in a principal-subordinate relationship.
When <s>rūpaka</s> is applied such that the stain itself is the rosary, the very fact of being held in the hand serves as the probative evidence.
For in the metaphorical reading, what is apprehended as primary is the rosary in the concealed form of the stain, and for that very [rosary], the fitness for being grasped by the hand is universally well known.
But through the shade of <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning), the holding of the stain by the hand is simply impossible — it is applied through figurative transfer and superimposition, since the moon merely bears the stain by its very form.

Here, <s>yamaka</s> (chiming) and <s>citra</s> (visual pattern) of the anuloma-pratiloma (forward-reverse) type, occurring in two quarters, are mutually dependent.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 209)
And when in grasping one [ornament], there is neither logical ground nor fault [to decide] — that is uncertainty. (140)

children.text: dvayorbahūnāṃ vā, alaṃkārāṇāmekatra kamāveśe 'pi virodhāt na yatra yugapadavasthānam na caikatarasya parigrahe sādhakam taditarasya vā parihāre bādhakamasti yainaikatara eva parigṛhyeta sa niśvayābhāvarūpo dvitīyaḥ saṃkaraḥ samuccayena saṃkarasyaivākṣepāt /
children.translated_text: When, even though two or many ornaments may be simultaneously present in one place, there is a conflict — where there is no simultaneous existence, and where there is neither a probative ground for accepting one nor a prohibitive ground for rejecting the other by which one alone might be accepted — that indeterminacy constitutes the second [type of] <s>saṃkara</s>, since it is a challenge to <s>saṃkara</s> by way of accumulation.

children.text: udāharaṇam-- jaha gahiro jaha raaṇaṇibbharo jaha a ṇimmalacchāo /
children.translated_text: Example: 'Just as [the ocean] is deep, just as it is heavy with passion, just as its splendor is spotless —

children.text: taha kiṃ vihiṇā eso sarasavāṇīo jalaṇihī ṇa kio // 573 //
children.translated_text: so why was this ocean of <s>Sarasvatī</s>'s speech not made [directly] by <s>Vidhi</s> (Brahmā) as a reservoir of water?' (573)

children.text: atra samudre prastute viśeṣaṇasāmyādaprastutārthapratīteḥ kimasau samāsoktiḥ kim abdheraprastutasya mukhena kasyāpi tatsamaguṇatayā prastutasya pratīteḥ, iyamaprastutapraśaṃsā, iti saṃdehaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, since in the context of the ocean, due to the similarity of qualifying attributes, the meaning of an unintended subject is perceived — the doubt arises: is this <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression), or is it <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (praise of the irrelevant), since through the medium of the unintended ocean, one whose qualities are similar is perceived as the intended subject?
Or, as: 'This disc of the moon, which delights the eyes, is shining;
even now, this darkness, though obstructed, has not been dispelled.' (574)

children.text: atra kiṃ kāmasyoddīpakaḥ kālo vartate, iti bhahgyantareṇābhidhānāt paryāyoktam uta vadansyendubimbatayā, adhyavasānāt atiśayoktiḥ kiṃ vā, etaditi vaktraṃ nirdiśya tadrūpāropavaśāt rūpakam atha vā tayoḥ samuccayavivakṣāyāṃ dīpakam atha vā tulyayogitā kimupradeṣasamaye viśeṣaṇasāmyādānanasyāvagatau samākoktiḥ, āhosvit mukhanairmalyaprastāvāt aprastutapraśaṃsā, iti bahūnāṃ saṃdehādayameva saṃkaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Here [the doubt is]: is it <s>paryāyokta</s> (circumlocution), since the time that excites passion is being indicated by an indirect expression? Or is it <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole), since the face is metaphorically identified as the moon's disc? Or is it <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor), since [the face] is indicated by 'this' and there is a superimposition of that form? Or, when a simultaneous expression of both is intended, is it <s>dīpaka</s> (illuminator)? Or is it <s>tulyayogitā</s> (equal conjunction)? Or is it <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression), since at the time of moonrise, through similarity of qualifying attributes, the perception of [her] face is obtained? Or is it <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (praise of the irrelevant), occasioned by the spotlessness of the face? — Due to this doubt among many [possibilities], this is precisely [the type of] <s>saṃkara</s> [called uncertainty].

children.text: yatra tu nyāyadoṣayoranyatarasyāvatāraḥ, tatra, ekatarasya niśvayāt na saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: But where either a logical ground or a fault [for deciding] is present — there, due to the determination of one [reading], there is no doubt.

children.text: nyāyaśva sādhakatvam anukūlatā doṣo 'pi bādhakatvaṃ pratikūlatā /
children.translated_text: 'Logical ground' (<s>nyāya</s>) means probative force, i.e. favorability; 'fault' (<s>doṣa</s>) also means prohibitive force, i.e. unfavorability.

children.text: tatra saubhāgyaṃ vitanoti vaktraśaśino jyotsneva hāsadyutiḥ // 575 //
children.translated_text: There [as an example]: 'The radiance of laughter, like the moonlight of the face-moon, spreads charm.' (575)

children.text: ityatra mukhyatayā, avagamyamānā hāsadyutirvaktre, evānukūlya bhajate, ityūpamāyāḥ sādhakam śaśinā tu na tathā pratikūleti rūpakaṃ prati tasyā abādhakatā /
children.translated_text: Here, the radiance of laughter, being apprehended as primary, is favorable to the face alone — hence it is a probative ground for <s>upamā</s> (simile); but the moon does not enjoy such favorability — hence there is no prohibition against <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) either.
'That this other cool-rayed [moon] has risen, [proves that] your face is indeed a moon.' (576)

children.text: ityātrāparatvamindoranuguṇaṃ na tu vaktrasya pratikūlamiti rūpakasya sādhakatāṃ pratipadyate na tūpamāyā bādhakatām /
children.translated_text: Here, the 'otherness' is compatible with the moon, not contrary to the face — hence it serves as a probative ground for <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) and does not prohibit <s>upamā</s> (simile).
'O King <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Lakṣmī</s> embraces you tightly.' (577)

children.text: ityatra punarāliṅganamupamāṃ nirasyati sadṛśaṃ prati parapreyasīprayuktasyāliṅganasyāsaṃbhavāt /
children.translated_text: Here, the embrace rules out <s>upamā</s> (simile), since it is impossible for [<s>Lakṣmī</s>] to embrace a [mere] likeness — she being the beloved of another [<s>Viṣṇu</s>].

children.text: pādāmbujaṃ bhavatu no vijayāya mañju- majjīraśijjitamanoharamambikāyāḥ // 578 //
children.translated_text: 'May the lotus-foot of <s>Ambikā</s>, charming with the tinkling of its beautiful anklets, be for our victory.' (578)

children.text: ityatra mañjīraśiñjitam ambuje pratikūlam asaṃbhavāditi rūpakasya bādhakam na tu pāde 'nukūlamityupamāyāḥ sādhakamamidhīyate vidhyupamardino bādhakasya tadapekṣayotkaṭatvena pratipatteḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the tinkling of anklets is contrary to a lotus, due to its impossibility — hence it prohibits <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor); but it is not favorable to the foot, hence it is not stated as a probative ground for <s>upamā</s> (simile) — because the prohibitive factor, being more powerful relative to that [metaphor], is perceived as predominant over the prescriptive factor.
Thus in other cases too, it should be examined by the discerning.
(<s>Sūtra</s> 210)
When clearly in a single locus, both word-ornament and sense-ornament

children.text: abhinne, eva pade sphuṭatayā yat ubhāvapi śabdārthālaṃkārau vyavasthāṃ samāsādayataḥ so 'pyaparaḥ saṃkaraḥ /
children.translated_text: are established — [this means:] when, in an undivided word itself, both word-ornament and sense-ornament clearly attain establishment — that too is another [type of] <s>saṃkara</s>.
Example: 'The day-lotus, with the sun-disc as its wide pericarp, its rays as clearly radiant filaments,
with the cluster of eight directions as petals, its opening-mouths the points of the compass, its bound darkness like a swarm of bees — contracted.' (579)
Here, <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) and <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration), both entering into a single quarter, [coexist].
(<s>Sūtra</s> 211)
Thus this [<s>saṃkara</s>] is declared to be of three forms. (141)

children.text: tadayamanugrāhyānugrāhakatayā saṃdehena, ekapadapratipādyatayā ca vyavasthitatvāttriprakatāra eva saṃkaro vyākṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus this <s>saṃkara</s>, being established through the relation of supporter and supported, through doubt, and through co-expression in a single word, has been analyzed as having three varieties.

children.text: prakārāntareṇa tu na śakyo vyākartum ānantyāttatprabhedānāmiti pratipāditāḥ śabdārthomayagatatvena traividhyajuṣo 'laṃkārāḥ //
children.translated_text: But it cannot be analyzed in any other manner, since the varieties of those [sub-types] are infinite — thus the ornaments, being of three kinds as pertaining to word, sense, and both, have been expounded.

children.text:
kutaḥ punareṣa niyamo yadeteṣāṃ tulye 'pi kāvyaśobhātiśayahetutve kaśvidalaṃkāraḥ śabdasya kaśvidarthasya kaśviccobhayasya, iti cet uktamatra yathā kāvye doṣaguṇālaṃkārāṇāṃ śabdārthobhayagatatvena vyavakthāyāmanvayavyatirekāveva prabhavataḥ, nimittāntarasyābhāvāt tataśva yo 'laṃkāro yadīyānvayavyatirekāvanuvidhatte sa tadalaṃkāro viyavasthāpyate, iti /
evaṃ ca yathā punaruktavadābhāsaḥ paraṃparitarūpakaṃ cobhayorbhāvābhāvānuvidhāyitayā, ubhayālaṃkārau tathā śabdahetukārthāntaranyāsaprabhṛtayo 'pi draṣṭavyāḥ /
arthasya tu tatra vaicitryam utkaṭatayā pratibhāsate, iti vācyālaṃkāramadhye vastusthitimanapekṣyaiva lakṣitāḥ /
children.translated_text: However, the variety of meaning manifests prominently therein — therefore they have been classified among the ornaments of the expressed meaning, without considering the actual state of the matter.

children.text: yo 'laṃkāro yadāśritaḥ sa tadalaṃkāra ityapi kalpanāyām anvayavyatirekāveva samāśrayitavyau /
children.translated_text: The notion that 'whichever ornament resides in whatever [entity], it is an ornament of that [entity]' — even in this conception, one must resort to agreement and difference alone.
Because without that resort, the specific relation of substrate and superstratum would not exist — therefore the stated criterion alone governs the [classification of] ornaments.
Mutual exclusion alone is predominant.

Whence then this rule that, even though these [ornaments] are equal in being causes of the excellence of poetic beauty, some are ornaments of word, some of meaning, and some of both? It has been stated here that, just as in the classification of faults, qualities, and ornaments of poetry as pertaining to word, meaning, and both, only agreement and difference (<s>anvayavyatireka</s>) are operative — because no other criterion exists — accordingly, whichever ornament conforms to the agreement and difference of a given [category], that is established as an ornament of that [category]. Thus, just as <s>punaruktavadābhāsa</s> (semblance of redundancy) and <s>paramparitarūpaka</s> (extended metaphor) are ornaments of both [word and meaning] because they follow the presence and absence of both, so too should <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroboration) and the like, which are caused by verbal [factors], be viewed [in the same way].
(<s>sūtra</s> 212)
Certain faults of these [ornaments], though possible according to circumstance,
are subsumed within the [faults] already stated — therefore they have not been treated separately. (142)

children.text: tathāhi--anuprāsasya prasiddhyabhāvo vaiphalyaṃ vṛttivirodha iti ye trayo doṣāḥ, te prasiddhiviruddhatām apuṣṭārthatvam pratikūlavarṇatāṃ ca yathākramaṃ na vyatikrāmanti tatsvabhāvatvāt krameṇodāharaṇam-- cakrī cakrārapaṅktiṃ harirapi ca haran dhūrjaṭirdhūrdhvajāgrā- nakṣaṃ nakṣatranātho 'rūṇamapi varuṇaḥ kūbarāgraṃ kuberaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus: the three faults of <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) — namely, absence of established usage, purposelessness, and conflict with the mode of expression — do not exceed, respectively, the [general faults of] contrariety to established usage, unsupported meaning, and incongruent phonemes, because they are of the same nature as those. Examples in order: 'The disc-bearer (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), bearing the row of discus-enemies, <s>Hari</s> too bearing them; <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), at the tip of the yoke-pole of the chariot-flag;

children.text: raṃhaḥ saṃghaḥ surāṇāṃ jagadupakṛtaye nityayuktasya yasya stauti prītiprasanno 'nvahamahimaruceḥ so 'vatātsyandano vaḥ // 580 //
children.translated_text: the constellationless lord of constellations (<s>Candra</s>), <s>Varuṇa</s> even at the tip of the yoke, <s>Kubera</s> — the host of gods in their swiftness, ever yoked for the benefit of the world, whose glory and radiance are praised with joy day after day — may that chariot (<s>Syandana</s>) protect you!' (580)

children.text: atra kartṛkarmapratiniyamena stutiḥ, anuprāsānurodhenaiva kṛtā na purāṇetihāsādiṣu tathā pratīteti prasiddhivirodhaḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, the praise through the fixed assignment of agents and objects has been made solely for the sake of the alliteration, and is not so understood in the <s>Purāṇas</s>, <s>Itihāsas</s>, and the like — therefore it is contrary to established usage.
'Speak, O young woman, O moon-faced one from whose face flows joy, O beautiful one;

children.text: yadi sallīlollāpini gacchasi tat kiṃ tvadīyaṃ me // 581 //
children.translated_text: if you go playfully conversing, then what is yours to me?' (581)
'The fine-sounding jeweled girdle-belt, the anklet ceaselessly jingling, beautiful, melodious —
the strolling about, at the time of the cessation of battle, the tinkling without cause, it makes.' (582)

children.text: atra vācyasya vicintyamānaṃ na kiṃcidapi cārutvaṃ pratīyate, ityapuṣṭārthataivānuprāsasya vaikalyam //
children.translated_text: Here, upon reflection, not even the slightest charm of the expressed meaning is perceived — therefore the deficiency of <s>anuprāsa</s> is simply unsupported meaning.
'<s>akuṇṭhotkaṇṭhayā</s>' (582a) [is cited as another example].

children.text: atra śṛṅgāre paruṣavarṇāḍambaraḥ pūrvoktarītyā virudhyate, iti paruṣānuprāso 'tra pratikūlavarṇataiva vṛttivirodhaḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, the clamor of harsh phonemes in the context of the erotic sentiment (<s>śṛṅgāra</s>) conflicts in the manner previously stated — therefore the harsh <s>anuprāsa</s> here is precisely the [fault of] incongruent phonemes, which is conflict with the mode of expression.
The fault of <s>yamaka</s> (paronomasia) is [the defect of] being improper through being confined to three quarter-verses.

children.text: yathā bhujaṅgamasyeva maṇiḥ sadambhā grāhāvakīrṇeva nadī sadambhāḥ /
children.translated_text: For example: 'Like the jewel of a serpent, deceptive (<s>sadambhā</s>); like a river infested with crocodiles, deceptive (<s>sadambhā</s>);

children.text: durantatāṃ nirṇayato 'pi jantoḥ karṣanti cetaḥ prasabhaṃ sadambhāḥ // 583 //
children.translated_text: even when determining the endless [nature] of a being, those deceptive ones (<s>sadambhāḥ</s>) forcibly attract the mind.' (583)

children.text: upamāyām upamānasya jātipramāṇagatanyūnatvam adhikatā vā tādṛśī, anucitārthatvaṃ doṣaḥ, dharṇāśraye tu nyūnādhikatve yathākramaṃ hīnapadatvamadhikapadatvaṃ ca na vyabhicarataḥ //
children.translated_text: In <s>upamā</s> (simile), the fault is the inappropriateness of the comparandum (<s>upamāna</s>) — being inferior or excessive in terms of class or measure, or of such a nature. Regarding the substrate of the property (<s>dharma</s>), inferiority or excess does not differ, respectively, from the [general faults of] deficient expression (<s>hīnapadatva</s>) and excessive expression (<s>adhikapadatva</s>).

children.text: krameṇodāharaṇam-- caṇḍālairiva yuṣmābhiḥ sāhasaṃ paramaṃ kṛtam // 584 //
children.translated_text: Examples in order: 'By you, like <s>Caṇḍālas</s> (outcasts), the greatest violence has been committed.' (584)
'This sun shines like a spark of fire.' (585)
'This one, seated on a lotus, shines like a <s>cakravāka</s> (ruddy goose);
like the Blessed <s>Brahmā</s> at the beginning of the age, as if he had created the creatures.' (586)
'Your navel is like the netherworld; your breasts are like the mountains that support the earth;
and this rod of your braid resembles the fall of the <s>Kālindī</s> (Yamunā) river.' (587)
Here, through comparanda such as <s>Caṇḍāla</s> and the like, the subject at hand is exceedingly disparaged — thus it is inappropriateness of meaning.
'That sage, marked with the <s>mauñjī</s> (grass girdle), wearing a garment of black antelope skin,
shone like the sun embraced by the edge of a dark cloud.' (588)

children.text: atropamānasya mauñjīsthānīyastaḍillakṣaṇo dharmaḥ kenāpi padena na pratipādita iti hīnapadatvam //
children.translated_text: Here, the property of lightning, which corresponds to the <s>mauñjī</s> of the comparandum, is not conveyed by any word — therefore it is deficient expression.

children.text: sa pītavāsāḥ pragṛhītaśārṅgo manojñamīmaṃ vapurāpa kṛṣṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, wearing yellow garments, holding the <s>Śārṅga</s> bow, attained this charming form —
like a cloud at night, bearing a rainbow with a hundred flashes, combined with the moon.' (589)
Here, without specifying the conch and the like of the comparandum, the inclusion of the moon is superfluous — therefore it is excessive expression.

children.text: liṅgavacanabhedo 'pi, upamānopameyayoḥ sādhāraṇaṃ cet dharmamanyarūpaṃ kuryāt tadā, ekatarasyaiva taddharmasamanvayāvagateḥ saviśeṣaṇasyaiva tasyopamānatvamupameyatvaṃ vā pratīyamānena dharmeṇa pratīyate, iti prakrāntasyārthasya sphuṭamanirvāhādasya bhagnaprakramarūpatvam /
children.translated_text: Difference of gender and number too — if the comparandum and comparatum share a common property yet render it in a different form, then the connection of the property applies to only one of them. The one with the qualifying attribute is perceived as comparatum or comparandum through the perceived property — thus, because of the manifest failure to carry through the intended meaning, this constitutes the defect of broken construction.

children.text: yathā-- cintāratnamiva cayuto 'si karato dhiṅbhandabhāgyasya me // 590 //
children.translated_text: For example: 'You have fallen from my hand like a wish-fulfilling gem — curse the fate of this wretch!' (590)
'Grain has been consumed, O Lord, pure like family brides.' (591)

children.text: yatra tu nānātve 'pi liṅgavacanayoḥ sāmānyābhidhāyi padaṃ svarupabhedaṃ nāpadyate na tatraitaddūṣaṇāvatāraḥ, ubhayathāpi, asya, anugamakṣamasvabhāvatvāt /
children.translated_text: But where, despite difference in gender and number, the word expressing the general [property] does not undergo change of form — there this fault does not enter, because in both cases its nature is capable of being consistently maintained.
For example: 'Celebrated through priceless virtues, like the great ocean through gems.' (592)
'Her costume, unlike others, endowed with sweetness by those women —

children.text: dadhate sma parāṃ śobhāṃ tadīyā vibhramā iva // 593 //
children.translated_text: bore supreme beauty, like her own charming gestures.' (593)

children.text: kālapuruṣavidhyādibhede 'pi na tathā pratītiraskhalitarūpatayā viśrāntimāsādayatītyasāvapi bhagnaprakramatayaiva vyāptaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even in the difference of time, person, mode (<s>vidhi</s>), and the like — since the perception does not rest in an unimpaired form — that too is encompassed by the defect of broken construction.

children.text: yathā atithiṃ nāma kākutsthāt putramāpa kumudvatī /
children.translated_text: For example: '<s>Kumudvatī</s> obtained from <s>Kākutstha</s> a son named <s>Atithi</s>,
like consciousness [obtaining] serenity from the last watch of the night.' (594)

children.text: atra cetanā prasādamāpnoti na punarāpeti kālabhedaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, consciousness 'obtains' serenity, but does not 'obtain [a child]' — this is a difference of time.
'With a form made distinct by the special [effect] of a fresh bath, beautiful with a shimmering garment in the splendor of <s>kusumbha</s> (safflower) dye,
you shine, worshiping the god <s>Makaraketu</s> (Kāma), like a creeper born from a shoot of young sprouts.' (595)

children.text: atra latā vibhrājate na tu vibhrājase, iti saṃbodhyamānaniṣṭhasya parabhāgasya, asaṃbodhyamānaviṣayatayā vyatyāsāt puruṣabhedaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, a creeper 'shines' (<s>vibhrājate</s>), but not 'you shine' (<s>vibhrājase</s>) — because the second-person ending of the addressed [subject] is transferred to the domain of the non-addressed [comparatum], this constitutes a difference of person.
'May your fame flow forever like the <s>Gaṅgā</s>.' (596)

children.text: ityādau ca gaṅgā pravahati na tu pravahatu, iti, apravṛttapravartanātmano vidheḥ /
children.translated_text: And in such cases, the <s>Gaṅgā</s> 'flows' (<s>pravahati</s>), not 'may it flow' (<s>pravahatu</s>) — because the injunctive (<s>vidhi</s>), whose nature is to initiate what has not been initiated, [applies to the subject but not the comparatum],
and because such and other kinds of meaning are impossible as pertaining to the comparatum — this constitutes a difference of mode and the like.

children.text: nanu samānam uccāritaṃ pratīyamānaṃ vā dharmāntaramupādāya paryavasitāyām upamāyām upameyasya prakṛtadhamābisaṃbandhānna kaśvitkālādibhedo 'sti /
children.translated_text: Now, [one might argue that] when the simile is completed by adopting a common or a perceived property that is different, there is no difference of time and the like, because the comparandum is connected with its own stated property.

children.text: yatrāpyupāttenaiva sāmānyadharmeṇa, upamā, avagamyate yathā "yudhiṣṭhira ivāyaṃ satyaṃ vadati'; iti tatra yudhiṣṭhira iva satyavādyayaṃ satyaṃ vadatīti pratipatsyāmahe /
children.translated_text: And where the simile is understood through the very stated common property — as in 'this one speaks the truth just like <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>' — there we would understand: 'This one, a truth-speaker like <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, speaks the truth.'

children.text: satyāvādī satyaṃ vadatīti ca na paunaruktayam āśaṅkanīyam raipoṣaṃ puṣṇātītivat yudhiṣṭhira iva satyavadanena satyavādyayamityarthāvagamāt /
children.translated_text: And one should not suspect redundancy in 'the truth-speaker speaks the truth,' just as [there is none in] 'he who nourishes nourishes (<s>raipoṣaṃ puṣṇāti</s>)' — because the meaning is understood as: 'This one is a truth-speaker by truth-speaking, like <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>.'

children.text: satyametat kiṃ tu sthiteṣu prayogeṣu samarthanamidaṃ na tu sarvathā niravadyam prastutavastupratītivyāghātāditi sacetasa evātra pramāṇam //
children.translated_text: This is true; however, this justification [works only] for established usages, but is not in every respect faultless — because it obstructs the perception of the intended subject matter. Therefore, only the discerning are the authority here.
Dissimilarity and impossibility too, in the case of simile, culminate simply in inappropriateness of meaning.
For example: 'I compose a poetry-moon with extended meaning-rays.' (597)

children.text: atra kāvsya śaśinā, arthānāṃ ca raśmibhiḥ sādharmyaṃ kutrāpi na pratītamityanucitārthatvam /
children.translated_text: Here, the similarity of poetry with the moon, and of meanings with rays, is not perceived anywhere — therefore it is inappropriateness of meaning.
'Blazing arrows fell from his face, occupying the center of the bow's arc —
like blazing streams of water, occupying the mid-day, from the solar disc with its halo.' (598)

children.text: atrāpi jvalantyo 'mbudhārāḥ sūryamaṇḍalāt niṣpatantyo na saṃbhavantītyupanibadhyamāno 'rtho 'naucityameva puṣṇāti //
children.translated_text: Here too, blazing streams of water falling from the solar disc are impossible — therefore the composed meaning nourishes only impropriety.

children.text: utprekṣāyāmapi saṃbhāvanaṃ dhruvevādaya eva śabdā vaktuṃ sahante na yathāśabdo 'pi kevalasyāsya sādharmyameva pratipādayituṃ paryāptatvāt tasya cāsyāmavivakṣitatvāditi tatrāśaktirasyāvācakatvaṃ doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: In <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) too, only words such as '<s>dhruva</s>' ('certainly'), '<s>iva</s>' ('as if') and the like are able to express the imagined identification, not the word <s>yathā</s> ('just as') — because that is adequate only for conveying the similarity of this [subject] alone, and because that [similarity] is not intended in <s>utprekṣā</s>. Therefore, the inability of that [word] amounts to its non-expressiveness — this is the fault.
For example: 'A dark blue lotus bud arose from the womb of the pool,
contracted as if (<s>yathā</s>) by suspicion of the coquetry of a woman's eye.' (599)

children.text: utprekṣitamapi tācvikena rupeṇa parivarjitatvāt nirupākhyaprakhyam tatsamarthanāya yat arthāntaranyāsopādānam tat ālokhyamiva gaganatale 'tyantamasamīcīnamiti nirviṣayatvametasya, anucitārthataiva dauṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even though imagined, because it is devoid of the proper form, [the <s>utprekṣā</s>] is without a recognizable semblance. The introduction of <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroboration) to support it is like drawing [a picture] on the sky — utterly inappropriate. Therefore this [type of utprekṣā] is without domain, and the fault is simply inappropriateness of meaning.

children.text: yathā divākarādrakṣati yo guhāsu līnaṃ divā bhītamivāndhakāram /
children.translated_text: For example: 'He who protects the darkness hiding in caves from the sun during the day, as if frightened —

children.text: kṣudre 'pi nūnaṃ śaraṇaṃ prapanne prapanne mamatvamuccaiḥ śirasāmatīva // 600 //
children.translated_text: surely, even toward a lowly being who has sought refuge, a great being's sense of protectorship rises with head held high.' (600)

children.text: atrācetanasya tamaso divākarāttrāsa eva na saṃbhavatīti kuta eva tatprayojitamadriṇā paritrāṇam /
saṃbhāvitena tu rūteṇa pratibhāsamānasyāsya na kācidanupapattiravataratīti vyartha eva tatsamarthanāyāṃ yatnaḥ /
children.translated_text: But through the imagined form as it appears, no impossibility whatsoever enters — therefore the effort to justify it is simply pointless.

children.text: sādhāraṇaviśeṣaṇavaśādeva samāsoktiranuktamapi, upamānaviśeṣaṃ prakāśayatīti tasyātra punarupādāne prayojanābhāvāt anupādeyatvaṃ yat tat apuṣṭārthatvaṃ punaruktaṃ vā doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Because <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression), through the force of the shared qualifier alone, reveals even the unstated comparandum — in repeating its introduction there is no purpose, and that [redundancy] is the fault of unsupported meaning or repetition.

children.text: yathā spṛśati tigmarucau kakubhaḥ karairdayitayeva vijṛmbhitatāpayā /
children.translated_text: For example: 'The fierce-rayed [sun] touches the quarters with his rays, [as though] yawning with spreading heat, like a beloved;
standing with a beautiful embrace of no small magnitude, with the charm of the day's beauty even for a long time.' (601)
Here, the fear of the inanimate darkness from the sun is itself impossible — so how much more the protection afforded by the mountain motivated by that [fear]?

children.text: atra tigmaruceḥ kakubhāṃ ca yathā sadṛśaviśeṣaṇavaśena vyaktiviśeṣaparigraheṇa ca nāyakatayā nāyikātvena ca vyaktiḥ, tathā grīṣmadivasaśriyo 'pi pratīnāyikātvena bhaviṣyatīti kiṃ dayitayeti svaśabdopādānena //
children.translated_text: Here, just as the specific identification of the fierce-rayed [sun] and the quarters as hero and heroine respectively is effected through shared qualifying attributes and specification of individuals — so too will the beauty of the summer day be perceived as the counter-heroine. Then what is the purpose of introducing the word 'beloved' (<s>dayitā</s>) explicitly?

children.text: śleṣopamāyāstu sa viṣayaḥ, yatropamānasyopādānamantareṇa sādhāraṇeṣvapi viśeṣaṇeṣu na tathā pratītiḥ /
children.translated_text: But the domain of <s>śleṣopamā</s> (simile through double entendre) is where, without the introduction of the comparatum, even in the shared qualifiers, the perception is not similarly [possible].
For example: 'And she herself, radiant with the copper-red hue of sprouts, adorned by <s>karavīra</s> (oleander);
like the dawn, bestowing what is desired by one who craves the fruit of sleep.' (602)
[End of discussion.]

children.text: aprastutapraśaṃsāyāmapi upameyam anayaiva rītyā pratītaṃ na punaḥ prayogeṇa kadarthatāṃ neyam /
children.translated_text: In <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (praise of the irrelevant) too, the comparandum, being perceived through this very method, should not be debased again through [explicit] usage.

children.text: yathā āhūteṣu vihaṃgameṣu maśako nāyān puro vāryate madhyevāridhi vāvasaṃstṛṇamaṇirdhatte maṇīnāṃ rucam /
children.translated_text: For example: 'When the birds are summoned, the mosquito is not prevented from going first; in the midst of the ocean, even a blade of grass bears the luster of gems;

children.text: khadyoto 'pi na kampate pracalituṃ madhye 'pi tejasvināṃ dhik sāmānyamacetanaṃ prabhumivānāmṛṣṭatacvāntaram // 603 //
children.translated_text: the firefly too does not hesitate to move even amidst the luminous — shame on the common, inanimate [thing that], like a master, has not scrutinized its own inner [worth]!' (603)

children.text: a6, acetanasya prabhoraprastutaviśiṣṭasāmānyadvāreṇābhivyaktau na yuktameva punaḥ kathanam //
children.translated_text: When the inanimate [thing], like a master, is already made manifest through the medium of the irrelevant-yet-qualified general [subject] — the explicit re-statement is not at all appropriate.

children.text: tadete 'laṃkāradoṣāḥ, yathāsaṃbhavino 'nye 'pyevaṃjātīyakāḥ pūrvoktayaiva doṣajātyā, antarbhāvitāḥ, na pṛthak pratipādanamarhantīti saṃpūrṇamidaṃ kāvyalakṣaṇam //
children.translated_text: These are the faults of the ornaments. Other faults of this kind too, wherever they may possibly occur, are subsumed under the very classes of faults previously stated — they do not merit separate treatment. Thus this definition of poetry (<s>kāvyalakṣaṇa</s>) is complete.

children.text: ityeṣa mārgo viduṣāṃ vibhinno 'pyabhinnarūpaḥ pratimāsate yat /
children.translated_text: This path of the learned, though varied, appears as one in form;

children.text: na tadvicitraṃ yadamutra samyagvinirmitā saṃghaṭanaiva hetuḥ //1//
children.translated_text: that is not surprising, for herein the well-constructed arrangement alone is the cause. (1)
Thus ends the tenth <s>ullāsa</s> (chapter), entitled 'Determination of Figures of Meaning' (<s>arthālaṃkāranirṇaya</s>), in the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>.
And this <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s> is completed.
